First, we prove that explicit folded Reed--Solomon codes of rate arbitrarily close to $\tfrac{a-1}{a+\ell-2}$ are $(0,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, which confirms the conjecture in the special case $\rho=0$ and $\ell=2$. Second, we show that for any $R\in(0,\tfrac{a-1}{a})$, there are rates arbitrarily close to $R$ at which attaining the conjectured bound requires exponentially large alphabets. This mirrors the phenomenon observed by Alrabiah--Guruswami--Li (SODA 2024), where achieving the generalized Singleton bound in the list-decoding setting also necessitates exponential alphabet size.

papers.title: An Exact Vertex Localization of Zykov's Theorem
papers.abstract: We establish a vertex-based localization of the exact form of Zykov's theorem. For a graph $G$ of order $n\geq1$, let $N(G,K_t)$ denote its number of copies of $K_t$, and let $c(v)$ be the order of a largest clique containing $v$. Write $Z_t(n,s)=N(T_s(n),K_t)$, where $T_s(n)$ is the balanced complete $s$-partite graph on $n$ vertices. We prove that, for every integer $t\geq2$, \[ N(G,K_t)\leq \frac1n\sum_{v\in V(G)}Z_t(n,c(v)). \] Equality holds if and only if $G$ is $K_t$-free or $G\cong T_s(n)$ for some $t\leq s\leq n$. Moreover, the coefficients $Z_t(n,s)$ are pointwise best possible among all bounds of this form. Our result strengthens the previous vertex-localized bound \[ N(G,K_t)\leq n^{t-1} \sum_{v\in V(G)} \frac{\binom{c(v)}{t}}{c(v)^t} \] by accounting for the integer part sizes of Turán graphs. The comparison between the two upper bounds is strict precisely when some vertex $v$ satisfies $c(v)\geq t$ and $c(v)\nmid n$. As consequences, we recover the exact Zykov and Turán bounds without divisibility assumptions.

papers.title: Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA) for Energy Market Settlements: A Machine and Reinforcement Learning-Based Approach
papers.abstract: The integration of segmented energy markets into Independent System Operators (ISOs) like CAISO and MISO has increased settlement complexity. Automated transaction processing creates challenges for evaluating accuracy, compliance, and financial integrity. Traditional rule-based manual auditing is inefficient, error-prone, and cannot handle the data volume from automated this http URL research proposes Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA), a machine and reinforcement learning framework for settlement auditing via anomaly prioritization. ANNA integrates statistical anomaly detection, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), clustering, and Deep Q-Network (DQN) reinforcement learning to flag potentially anomalous transactions from historical market data. The approach is evaluated as an analyst-support tool for prioritizing transactions needing further audit this http URL was tested against traditional statistical methods, clustering-based techniques, and supervised/reinforcement learning models. The study used three years of CAISO settlement data over 63 million source records across 32 charge codes and multiple counterparties. After preprocessing, approximately 2.9 million labeled transactions formed the working dataset, with model-specific subsets used for training and evaluation. Performance was assessed using precision, recall, computational efficiency, and false-negative this http URL outperforms traditional methods by identifying hidden relationships in settlement data, while standard deviation thresholds, K-Means, KNN, and Q-Learning performed poorly across key metrics. The result is a scalable solution integrating machine and reinforcement learning for automated auditing of energy market settlements, contributing computationally efficient anomaly prioritization to settlement-auditing workflows.

papers.title: Optimization of a Solar-Grid Water Supply System with Hydraulic Energy Storage: A Case Study
papers.abstract: Given the high cost of grid-scale batteries, other energy storage approaches are needed for developing and low-income regions. Elevated volumes of water are often more economically feasible energy storage options than batteries in these contexts. This paper presents a dual-framework modeling approach for one such energy storage setup: a solar-grid hybrid water supply system in the arid Afar region of Ethiopia. By utilizing an elevated 1,900 m3 water reservoir as a "hydraulic battery," the system replaces traditional electrochemical storage, significantly reducing capital expenditures. Using Python for high-resolution technical simulation and Xendee for economic optimization, the study shows a 55.1% solar fraction and a 10% Internal Rate of Return (IRR). The results confirm that hybrid systems with hydraulic storage offer a financially viable and reliable solution for water access in energy-constrained regions.

papers.title: Radiation-Hydrodynamical Modeling of Accretion Columns in Ultraluminous X-ray Pulsars
Nonmonotonic In-Plane Thermal Transport in Metal-Embedded Graphitic Carbon Nitride
Hierarchical randomized neural networks for efficiently and accurately finding multiple solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
papers.abstract: Being able to find multiple solutions of a semilinear elliptic equation is a fundamental problem in scientific computing. In this paper, fully taking the advantages of randomized neural networks, we propose a new efficient and accurate method for identifying potentially as many solutions as possible. The new method is constructed from three aspects--initialization, optimization, a technique for acceleration and improving accuracy, two of which are innovative developments. Firstly, based on the basis functions of a randomized network and the sampling points, a characteristic matrix is introduced so that its singular value decomposition can be used to determine weakly variant search directions, followed by a newly developed algorithm to generate effective initial candidates. Then the good deflated Gauss-Newton method [see {\em A. Riley, et al., SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 47~(5) (2025) A2963-A2987}] using an exponential deflation operator is adapted as the optimization to search for all multiple solutions. Local error estimate of a particular solution under some proper condition is given in terms of the neurons in the hidden layer and the sampling points for this newly designed method. Furthermore, to accelerate the computation and improve the solution accuracy, a new multilevel method based on hierarchical networks is designed. Without using any {\em a priori} information, several numerical tests show together with the multilevel method, the new method can not only accurately find multiple solutions with relative errors reaching $10^{-16}$ only in less than one-tenth computational cost for the best case, but also preserve the inherent symmetries of multiple solutions.

papers.title: Tableau Consequence under Positive Contexts: A Reconstruction of Walukiewicz's Completeness Proof
papers.abstract: We establish a positive-context lifting theorem for tableau consequence in the modal $\mu$-calculus: under explicit syntactic hypotheses, $\mathcal T_B\Rightarrow\mathcal T_C$ induces $\mathcal T_{A(B)}\Rightarrow\mathcal T_{A(C)}$. The proof orders instances of the given relation by birth time and assigns overlapping formula occurrences to the oldest supporting instance. A corollary gives bidirectional replacement by automaton normal form inside positive contexts. Together with a separate unfolding consequence lemma and ANF bisimulation, the lifting theorem yields a self-contained reconstruction of Walukiewicz's completeness proof for Kozen's axiomatisation and makes its least-fixpoint step more transparent. We also give a finite parity-game proof of regular-refutation existence and a two-sided transfer from tableau consequence to thin refutations.

papers.title: SA-GLRT-D: Sidelobe-Aware GLRT-Based Detector for FMCW Radar
papers.abstract: This paper investigates adaptive detection for frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar in multi-target complex scenarios, where reference-cell contamination, spectral leakage from the cell under test (CUT), and the resulting sidelobe interference severely degrade detection performance. A sidelobe-aware detector based on the generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT), termed SA-GLRT-D, is proposed. Unlike conventional filtering-then-constant false alarm rate (CFAR) schemes, the proposed method explicitly accounts for the non-ideal frequency-domain energy spreading of the CUT induced by the finite-window effect. Accordingly, conventional single-cell target detection is extended to local-region detection, and decision statistic construction, CUT-related parameter estimation, and sidelobe interference suppression are jointly accomplished within a unified hypothesis-testing framework. Furthermore, to reduce computational complexity, a fast implementation of SA-GLRT-D is developed, together with a dedicated parameter initialization strategy to enhance the stability of numerical optimization. Simulation and real-measurement results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high-accuracy target detection while maintaining a constant false alarm rate, with favorable computational efficiency.

papers.title: Sequential Selection against an Adaptive Opponent
papers.abstract: Selecting a strategy by testing it against an opponent is common in game-playing AI, red-teaming of language models, and safety evaluations of AI agents. In many of these settings, the opponent adapts to what it observes, so a strategy that keeps winning in practice may already have stopped working by the time it is used. Motivated by these settings, we study a player who tries strategies in practice games against an adaptive opponent, decides when to stop, and then either selects one strategy for the next game or abstains. The goal is to select a strategy that meets a target win probability while rarely selecting one that has already fallen below it. For a single strategy, we propose the Sequential Private Accumulated-excess Rule (SPAR), which accumulates evidence through a capped likelihood ratio and selects the strategy once this evidence reaches a privately drawn uniform threshold. We show that the stopping time must involve such private randomness. The number of games SPAR needs is inversely proportional to the error tolerance, and this rate is optimal even when the opponent happens not to adapt. To select among multiple strategies, we introduce Screen-then-SPAR, which screens candidates in stages before applying SPAR. The procedure adapts to the best strategy's unknown initial margin above the target and achieves the minimax rate up to logarithmic factors. The performance of Screen-then-SPAR is demonstrated through simulations and two real-data studies, one using recorded coding-agent attacks from MonitoringBench and the other using rock-paper-scissors matches between human players and an adaptive bot.

papers.title: Statistically Optimal and Near Linear Time Hypothesis Selection
papers.abstract: In hypothesis selection we are given $n$ distributions $q_1,\dots,q_n$ on a countable domain $\mathcal{X}$ and samples from an unknown distribution $p$. The goal is a distribution $q$ with $\mathrm{TV}(p,q)\le\alpha\min_i\mathrm{TV}(p,q_i)+\epsilon$. The factor $\alpha=2$ is optimal for algorithms using a number of samples from $p$ that is independent of $|\mathcal{X}|$, and in general only improper learners achieve it. We give a learner that achieves $\alpha=2$ with $O(\log(n/\delta)/\epsilon^2)$ samples of $p$, with probability at least $1-\delta$. This matches the sample complexity of Yatracos's factor-$3$ estimator, and it removes the logarithmic factors in the factor-$2$ bound of Bousquet et al. (FOCS 2021). The learner accesses the $q_i$ only through sampling and pointwise comparisons. We measure its running time by its oracle complexity, the number of oracle calls. In expectation it makes $O((n\epsilon^{-2}+\epsilon^{-4}\log(1/\epsilon))\log(n/\delta))$ oracle calls, independent of $\mathcal{X}$. It runs multiplicative weights over the constraints $\mathrm{TV}(q,q_i)\le\mathrm{TV}(p,q_i)$ and uses at most one sample of $p$ per round.

papers.title: XRISM view of a featureless cluster Abell 1060: Revealing the advection of a diffuse radio source by ICM motions
A cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce a cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values. For a diagonally constant index on a periodically extended skew Young diagram, it is a sum over semi-standard cyclic Young tableaux. It includes the cyclic multiple zeta values of Hirose, Murahara and Murakami as a special case. The first two main results are a cyclic analogue of the Maesaka--Seki--Watanabe formula for truncated sums and an {integral--series identity} under an admissibility condition. As an application, we give a proof of $4^n\zeta(\{1,3\}^n)=\zeta(\{4\}^n)$ by counting linear extensions of a poset. The third main result expresses a cyclic Schur multiple harmonic sum as a finite signed sum of Schur multiple harmonic sums with the same number of boxes and the same multiset of exponents.

papers.title: Scalable Modal Analysis of the Imperial Front Wing Flow Field
papers.abstract: The aerodynamic performance of motorsport vehicles relies on understanding the unsteady flow dynamics around complex geometries at high Reynolds numbers. Extracting the dominant 3D coherent structures from high-fidelity simulations is often intractable due to the high dimensionality of the state-space, and standard modal decompositions, such as proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), do not give interpretable meaning to the temporal dynamics of the modes. This study demonstrates a scalable POD and Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) method, implemented in the open-source pyLOM framework, that can identify coherent structures and their temporal dynamics in high-fidelity simulations of Formula 1 aerodynamics, specifically the Imperial Front Wing (IFW), a publicly available benchmark based on the McLaren MP4-17D, at Reynolds number $Re = 2.2 \times 10^5$. DMD is applied to large eddy simulation (LES) results of the flow field that is resolved using spectral/hp element method via Nektar++, producing $49.72 \times 10^6$ degrees of freedom at polynomial order p=4. The simulation captures four dominant vortical structures (endplate, canard, main, and footplate), with time-averaged force coefficients showing 2.24% and 2.87% differences in $C_L$ and $C_D$ compared to the reference data. DMD extracts the frequencies, amplitudes and damping ratios of the coherent structures, and modes at chord-based Strouhal numbers of 5.1, 7.5 and 9.3 are associated, through point-probe spectra, with the main-element laminar separation bubble, canard vortex core pulsation and endplate vortex meander, respectively. The DMD allows for both a model reduction technique and a compression scheme, here reducing approximately 6 TB of snapshots to 200 GB of modal data.

papers.title: Orbital Integrals on Unitary Groups and Zeta Values
papers.abstract: We generalize Yun's interpolation formula for orbital integrals on $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in terms of Dedekind zeta functions to stable orbital integrals on unitary groups. Our approach combines Xiao's germ expansion of orbital integrals and the Jacquet-Rallis fundamental lemma.

papers.title: Wavelet determinantal samplers: Optimal approximation rates adapting to regularity
papers.abstract: We construct wavelet-based determinantal samplers on manifolds and geometric graphs whose approximation rates adapt to the regularity of the observable. On a Riemannian manifold of dimension $m$, our wavelet DPPs satisfy variance reduction of order $n^{1-2s/m}$ for linear statistics of both $s$-Hölder and $H^s$ observables, where $0<s\le1$. Using these samplers, we further construct unbiased quadrature rules with root mean square error $O(n^{-1/2-s/m})$ using at most $3n/2$ function evaluations, matching the classical optimal randomized integration exponent. For point clouds sampled from an $m$-dimensional manifold, we develop corresponding determinantal samplers on two standard classes of geometric random graphs: $\varepsilon$-graphs and symmetric $k$-nearest-neighbour graphs. These samplers satisfy the same variance reduction for linear statistics of $s$-Hölder observables and yield conditionally unbiased estimators of empirical averages with root mean square error $O(n^{-1/2-s/m})$, using at most $2n$ function evaluations. In both settings, the rates are governed by the intrinsic dimension $m$ and the regularity $s$ of the observable.

papers.title: Performance of attention-based deep-learning models in Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor measurements
Detection of a warm absorber in a highly variable low-redshift quasar
Complex structures on products with $S^4$
papers.abstract: The main theorem of the present paper is that $S^4\times P$ admits a complex structure whenever $P$ is the fibre product, over a compact complex manifold, of the unit circle bundles of an even number of holomorphic line bundles. This theorem has lots of significant applications. For example, $S^4\times G$ admits a complex structure for every compact Lie group $G$ of even dimension. The same holds for $S^4\times V_{2s}(C^n)$ and $S^4\times V_{2s}(H^n)$ when $n\geq 2s\geq2$, and for $S^4\times V_{4s}(R^n)$ when $n\ge4s\ge4$. The theorem also gives complex structures on the product of $S^4$ with any even number of odd-dimensional spheres. Moreover, complex structures exist on $S^4$ times some moment-angle manifolds, including certain connected sums of sphere products. The construction uses a holomorphic $(C^*)^2$-action on $S^4 \times T^2$ endowed with the complex structure we constructed in [Gao-Tang-Yan, arXiv:2610.06067v1 ] and a smooth splitting equivariant under the compact torus.

papers.title: Computable certificates for data-driven dimension reduction on reaction-diffusion lattices
papers.abstract: Data-driven methods recover low-dimensional coordinates from high-dimensional spatiotemporal data. Whether those coordinates track a genuine invariant object or a finite-resolution artifact is not settled. On reaction-diffusion lattices, the spectral-gap condition of inertial-manifold theory reduces to a critical lattice size $n_*$. Below $n_*$, the two-dimensional diffusion-map reading carries an existence guarantee; above $n_*$ the guarantee lapses, and this lapse does not rule out a slow manifold. The closed form for $n_*$ follows from the reaction Lipschitz constant and the slow-mode growth rate. The certificate is tested on a quadratic and a cubic model system. At the Brusselator boundary the existence sign is checked by interval enclosure, and the spectral margin decays as $n^{-4}$ across the transition. On strongly damped Hopf lattices the slow manifold collapses to the uniform limit cycle; this degeneracy, the trivial graph $\varphi\equiv0$, is reported directly rather than concealed. The boundary gives a PDE-side prior for data-driven reduction: it marks the resolution at which a recovered two-dimensional structure can be trusted.

papers.title: Self-similar solutions to the inverse mean curvature flow in the Lorentz--Minkowski plane
papers.abstract: We classify the self-similar solutions of the inverse mean curvature flow in the Lorentz--Minkowski plane $\mathbb{R}^{1,1}$. Using hyperbolic numbers, the self-similarity condition becomes a linear ODE system, and all solutions are obtained in closed form with explicit smoothness and completeness criteria. Translating solitons occur in three causal types, and dilation--rotation solitons are governed by the discriminant $\Delta=a^2-4(b-1)$, as in the Euclidean case. When $a^2=b^2$ the translation cannot be eliminated, owing to the zero divisors of the hyperbolic numbers, and a genuinely Lorentzian class of mixed solitons arises, whose complete smooth members form a one-parameter family. The planar classification is then extended to translationally invariant solutions in $\mathbb{R}^{n,1}$, and rotationally invariant solutions are reduced to an explicit ODE system.

papers.title: Separating Genetic and Protein Evidence in Open Targets: An Auditable Re-ranking Study
papers.abstract: Biomedical target-ranking platforms combine genetics, literature, experimental evidence, tractability, and clinical precedent because each is useful for target discovery. A single integrated score, however, can be awkward to reuse for a narrower question such as which genes have direct evidence for disease risk or etiology. We examine this issue in Open Targets associations for Alzheimer disease (AD) and Parkinson disease (PD). Genetics-linked evidence and protein-oriented evidence are scored in separate channels and combined only at the end. In AD, the Open Targets overall top 20 contains 7 curated genetics-supported genes and 10 symptomatic pharmacology controls; the default late fusion contains 15 curated genes and no symptomatic controls. In PD, late fusion retains 13 curated genes and removes the 5 symptomatic controls present in the platform top 20. A genetics-only ranking reaches similar curated recall (14 genes in AD, 13 in PD), so most of the gain over the platform score comes from emphasizing genetic evidence; the protein channel mainly raises the number of tractable targets in the shortlist (from 9 to 12 in AD and from 8 to 10 in PD) without readmitting symptomatic controls. These results are stable across fusion weights from 0.35 to 0.75, perturbed protein-channel weights, and rule thresholds. An optional post-ranking rule further lowers high-clinical/low-genetic targets such as ACHE and GRIN1 without changing top-20 curated recall. The procedure is deterministic and uses public Open Targets fields. Because the component scores remain available, individual rank changes can be inspected and the ranking can be reproduced from the same data snapshot.

papers.title: Pseudo-Altermagnetism in Non-Hermitian Systems
Global existence and large-time behavior of classical axisymmetric solutions to the two-dimensional viscous Saint-Venant equations and related models
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes system with density-dependent viscosity in a disk, subject to the no-slip boundary condition. We consider both the symmetric viscous stress and the stress written in terms of the full velocity gradient. In each case the coefficients satisfy the BD relation $\mu(\rho)=\rho^\alpha$ and $\lambda(\rho)=2(\alpha-1)\rho^\alpha$. For every $1/2<\alpha\le1$ and $\gamma>1$, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for arbitrarily large axisymmetric initial data with strictly positive density and possibly nonzero tangential velocity. Moreover, the density has upper and positive lower bounds independent of time, and the solution converges to the constant equilibrium. The two stresses give the same radial momentum equation, but require different estimates of the tangential velocity. The endpoint $\alpha=1$, $\gamma=2$ includes the viscous shallow-water equations.

papers.title: Space-Time Covariance with Screening Effects, Markov Property, and Long-Range Dependence
papers.abstract: Constructing space-time covariance models is an essential task to account for spatio-temporal dependence. However, there is a lack of practical guidance for constructing new covariance constructions. This paper focuses on studying the interplay among three statistical properties: screening effect, Markov property, and long-range dependence for constructing desirable parsimonious space-time covariance functions. While these properties imply seemingly conflicting statistical practice, it is shown in this paper that closed-form parsimonious covariance functions that simultaneously possess all these properties could be constructed and may be desirable for understanding space-time dependence. To examine these properties, this paper first shows that the confluent hypergeometric (CH) covariance function has asymptotic screening effect even in long-range dependent regime. Then this paper provides theoretical characterizations on Markov property for the hierarchical mixture construction including a necessary and sufficient condition. To account for more practical structures, this paper constructs a flexible Lagrangian CH model with the time-lag varying smoothness and tail decay parameters via a hierarchical mixture approach. These properties are illustrated via simulation studies. The practical performance under these models is evaluated for the Irish wind data and the sea surface temperature data.

papers.title: Selling Training Data
papers.abstract: This paper studies the sale of supplementary training dataset to improve predictive model. The buyer not only has private knowledge of its own dataset, but also can choose the way to merge these two datasets. This flexibility imposes a new constraint on the menu, requiring the buyer's total net utility be monotonic in the Blackwell order on private datasets. Given that, we show that a single posted price for a fully informative dataset is optimal in hypothesis testing, under differential virtual-value condition. The result extends to multi-class classification in which private datasets share a clean component but differ in how their labels are contaminated.

papers.title: A decomposition of Hamiltonian matrices with symplectic kernels and its application to Williamson's diagonal form
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a decomposition of Hamiltonian matrices with symplectic kernels, which extends the main result in [K. D. Ikramov, On the Symplectic Eigenvalues of Positive Definite Matrices. Moscow Univ. Comput. Math. Cybern., 42(2018)1-4]. As an application, we present another proof of Williamson's diagonal form for positive-semidefinite matrices with symplectic kernels.

papers.title: A Constrained Coupled Cluster Approach for Strongly Correlated Electrons
papers.abstract: We introduce constrained coupled cluster (cCC), a general framework for imposing arbitrary physical constraints on conventional single-reference coupled cluster amplitudes without rederiving or replacing the underlying coupled cluster residual equations. As a first application, we derive a constraint from the spin-symmetry requirement for an exact wavefunction and demonstrate the resulting approach on strongly correlated problems. Across benchmark Hubbard models, nitrogen and chromium bond breaking, and iron--sulfur cluster spin gaps, the constraint strongly suppresses spin contamination, repairs qualitative failures of conventional coupled cluster, and often brings CCSDT, and in several cases CCSD, into quantitative agreement with exact diagonalization or high-accuracy density matrix renormalization group calculations. The derived constraint adds only a mean-field cost contraction to the coupled cluster calculation and is compatible with any cluster truncation. These results identify numerical constraints as a promising route for extending single-reference coupled cluster machinery into strongly correlated regimes conventionally associated with more complicated electronic structure methods.

papers.title: Global Patterns and Drivers of Terrestrial Surface Albedo Dynamics from 2001 to 2025
papers.abstract: Terrestrial surface albedo is a fundamental determinant of the global radiative balance, yet a spatially integrated understanding of its long-term trajectories and multi-sphere environmental drivers remains lacking. Utilizing MODIS observations (2001-2025), this study integrates Theil-Sen trend analysis, standardized anomaly diagnostics, and a pixel-wise multiple linear regression framework to quantify global albedo dynamics and attribute them to biophysical drivers. Our results reveal that global albedo change is characterized by profound spatial heterogeneity rather than a uniform trend, with 23.3% of the land surface exhibiting significant brightening, while 18.9% showed significant darkening. Multi-driver attribution demonstrates a clear zonal organization of controls: snow cover dominates albedo variability in northern high latitudes (46.9% of classified area), while NDVI (41.0%) and soil moisture (12.1%) govern tropical vegetated regions and moisture-limited transitional zones, respectively. These findings underscore that while terrestrial albedo is a robust indicator of Earth system change, its interpretation depends strongly on regional cryospheric, biophysical, and hydrological contexts.

papers.title: Division rings of fractions of LV-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field and let $A=L_K(E,\omega)$ be an LV-algebra of a row-finite weighted graph. We prove that $A$ embeds in a division ring if and only if $E$ has one vertex and its ordered loop weights satisfy $w_n=n$ and $w_j>j$ for $1\le j<n$. Under these conditions, $A$ has a universal division ring of fractions, which we identify with the free field on $2\sum_{j=1}^n w_j-n^2$ generators over $K$. We construct a free generating set explicitly by factoring the matrix of generators. We classify the resulting division rings over $K$ and bound the stabilization required to recognize invertible matrices. These results include mixed weights, for which the LV-algebra need not be a semifir.

papers.title: Rayleigh's conjecture for clamped plates in dimensions four and five
papers.abstract: In 1877, Lord Rayleigh conjectured that the disk minimizes the fundamental frequency of a clamped plate of prescribed area. We prove the higher-dimensional conjecture in dimensions four and five by establishing a sharp comparison between the first clamped-plate eigenvalue and the square of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue on the same domain. The proof uses a nonlinear transformation built from the ball eigenfunctions. A local identity keeps all terms of the Hessian. Exact coefficient inequalities and bounds for the infinite remainders establish positivity, while a weak formulation handles sign changes and critical sets. We characterize equality in the volume inequality and identify an obstruction to this transformation in dimension six.

papers.title: Singularities of Mean Curvature Flow with Bounded Total Curvature II: Multiplicity One
papers.abstract: Let \(M_t^n\subset\mathbb R^{n+1}\) be a smooth mean curvature flow of closed embedded hypersurfaces, with \(n\ge3\), and let \(T\) be its first singular time. If the integral of \(|A|^n\) is uniformly bounded for \(t<T\), every nonzero tangent flow at time \(T\) has multiplicity one. At each singular point the tangent flow is unique, and the rescaled flow converges locally smoothly to a closed self-shrinker.

papers.title: From Low-Dimensional Chaos to High-Dimensional Dynamics in Self-Attention Systems
papers.abstract: Continuous-time particle models of self-attention are often studied under symmetry assumptions that yield a gradient structure and constrain the dynamics to convergence toward equilibria. We investigate the behavior of these systems beyond the gradient setting, considering autonomous projected self-attention models with constant query, key, and value matrices and particles constrained to an ellipse. For three particles, the equations define a vector field on the three-dimensional torus. We derive explicit synchronized periodic solutions and compute their Floquet multipliers, establishing the existence of non-gradient dynamics. Numerical explorations using bifurcation diagrams, Poincare sections, periodic-orbit continuation, a nd Lyapunov exponents reveal attracting periodic orbits, invariant-torus-like behavior, and strong evidence of chaos. We then construct higher-dimensional systems by coupling these low-dimensional building blocks through masked and multi-head attention mechanisms. We discuss the persistence of normally hyperbolic invariant manifolds under weak coupling and investigate how the coupling architecture influences the resulting dynamics. Numerical experiments reveal the emergence of additional expanding directions, including a 60-particle system in which 26 of the 40 computed Lyapunov exponents exceed 0.01. These results demonstrate the richness of the dynamical behavior possible in simplified self-attention systems and motivate further investigation of the invariant structures organizing their high-dimensional dynamics.

papers.title: Levi Dynamics and Largest Domains of Discontinuity on Flag Manifolds
papers.abstract: Divergent sequences in a semisimple Lie group have a bounded Levi part that is invisible to Cartan projections and limit flags. We show that this Levi part is a genuine dynamical invariant and determines much of the large-scale behaviour of discrete groups on flag manifolds. For every real flag manifold, we compute the complete moving-source destination relation of a divergent sequence, including the Levi contribution. This yields a stratified convergence principle, a boundary compactification encoding the relation, and an exact properness criterion. For discrete groups the relation organises the classical limit sets into a single flag, from Quint's limit set through the recurrent and Kulkarni sets to the Myrberg set, the complement of equicontinuity. Sequences with coalescing limit flags satisfy a diagonal formula, which gives a recurrence criterion for the largest domain of proper discontinuity. For compact twists of Kleinian groups, the criterion becomes an exact incidence condition on the twist closure on every Grassmannian and Lagrangian Grassmannian. Two strongly irreducible subgroups of $\mathrm{PGL}(8,\mathbb{C})$ with identical marked Cartan projections, limit flags and destination relations on $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^7$ are distinguished on $\operatorname{Gr}(4,\mathbb{C}^8)$ alone. We also show that marked boundary data recover the compact twist while unmarked data recover only its orbit partition. Further applications treat critical projective dynamics, cusped Hitchin groups and symmetric powers.

papers.title: Friendship paradoxes in networks
papers.abstract: Since Scott L. Feld's seminal paper entitled ``Why your friends have more friends than you do'' [Am.~J.~Sociol.~\textbf{96}, 1464 (1991)], the friendship paradox (FP) has been extensively studied in network science and related fields over the last decades. In this paper we survey the literature on the FP and its generalizations. We first introduce definitions and general results of the FPs defined in networks, and then overview their results on model networks. Empirical results using various social network data as well as applications to real-world problems, such as early detection of outbreaks and network sampling, are also summarized. Finally, we conclude by discussing several directions of possible future works.

papers.title: Several families of linear codes via weight functions of three-weight codes
papers.abstract: Recently, Huang et al. proposed a general framework for deriving new linear codes from a given code by applying weight functions to the set of codewords with a prescribed Hamming weight in [A structural theory of linear codes from weight functions: constructions, geometry and applications, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, DOI: https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.2026.3742840 , 2026]. While this method was systematically developed for two-weight codes and yielded several families of projective two-weight codes, extending it to codes with more weights remains an interesting and challenging problem. In this paper, we generalize this construction to three-weight codes by employing a well-known family of ternary three-weight cyclic codes. By determining the weight distribution of every codimension-one subcode, as well as the distribution of fixed-weight codewords across these subcodes, we completely characterize the behavior of the weight-function construction on this family. As a result, we obtain three classes of linear codes with four nonzero weights and explicitly determine their parameters. Furthermore, the results show that these obtained codes are self-orthogonal and minimal.

papers.title: First-Order Information from Noisy Comparison Oracles
papers.abstract: We study stochastic and deterministic smooth unconstrained optimization problems where neither the functions nor their derivatives can be computed or estimated and the only information about the objective is available via pairwise comparisons. We focus on a specific model of smooth comparison oracles, as in the Bradley-Terry and Thurstone models, in which the probability of a correct comparison depends smoothly on the function-value gap. We investigate what first-order information can be obtained from such comparisons in deterministic and stochastic settings, and how many comparisons are needed to estimate it. We show that the first-order information that such comparisons provide is a fixed positive multiple of the gradient of the objective. We propose a random-direction estimator of the comparison gradient and analyze its bias and variance. It reaches mean-squared error $\varepsilon^2$ with $O(d^2\varepsilon^{-4})$ comparisons when the sample functions have Lipschitz gradients, and $O(d^2\varepsilon^{-3})$ when their Hessians are also Lipschitz. We prove lower bounds of the same order in $d$ and $\varepsilon$ for all comparison-based estimators, so these numbers are necessary and our estimator is optimal in $d$ and $\varepsilon$. As an application, we use it in a stochastic gradient method to find a point that is approximately stationary with respect to comparisons. We also extend the estimator to nonsmooth objectives, for which it estimates a smoothed comparison gradient.

papers.title: Stabilized Isogeometric Topology Optimization on Trimmed Geometries
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel stabilized isogeometric topology optimization method for complex design domains represented by trimmed geometries. Minimum compliance is taken as the model problem, where a generalized Cahn-Hilliard model, a time-dependent fourth-order partial differential equation, is solved and its steady-state solutions yield the optimized structures. This approach does not require sensitivity analysis and can naturally accommodate material constraints and complex topological changes. To impose Dirichlet boundary conditions and solve the instability issue caused by trimming, Nitsche's formulation with minimal stabilization is proposed for the high-order problem. Moreover, the immersed boundary-conformal method is extended to handle complex non-design domains, allowing material-void interfaces to be treated in a unified manner. Finally, a three-dimensional biharmonic problem and several two-dimensional topology optimization examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness, stability, and flexibility of the proposed method in dealing with complex design domains.

papers.title: China daily CO2 emission estimates 2019-2025
papers.abstract: Near-real-time CO2 estimates enable timely tracking of emission changes, but broad sectoral classifications limit their ability to resolve industrial dynamics across China's provinces. Here, we update Carbon Monitor to estimate daily CO2 emissions across five sectors in 31 mainland Chinese provinces during 2019-2025 and monthly emissions from 40 industrial and construction subsectors in 30 provinces, combining historical inventories with industrial production indicators. National emissions increased from 10.83 Gt CO2 in 2019 to 12.15 Gt CO2 in 2023, before declining slightly to 12.08 Gt CO2 in 2025. The 2024-2025 national reduction of 0.23% reflected opposing sectoral trends, with industrial emissions increasing by 48.8 Mt CO2 while power generation and ground transport emissions decreased by 46.6 Mt CO2 and 27.7 Mt CO2, respectively. Provincial trajectories also diverged, with emissions rising in 16 provinces and falling in 15. Industrial disaggregation revealed increases of 102.3 Mt CO2 in nonferrous-metal smelting and pressing and decreases of 108.1 Mt CO2 in nonmetal mineral products during 2019-2024. Comparison with a historical provincial inventory yielded a median absolute relative difference of 9.4%. These findings demonstrate that national emission stabilization masks divergent regional and industrial changes, highlighting the need for temporally updated, sector-specific evidence to assess progress toward sustained reductions and identify mitigation priorities.

papers.title: GABIF: An Adaptive Guided Graph Denoising Framework for Antibody Conditional Inverse Folding
papers.abstract: Antibodies play a central role in the human immune system, and their design is critical for vaccine development, therapeutic intervention, and improving human longevity. However, the vast combinatorial search space of antibodies poses a fundamental challenge for de novo discovery. Recent advances in deep learning, particularly denoising diffusion models, have demonstrated strong potential in protein inverse folding. Nevertheless, existing approaches are largely constrained to learning from natural antibody repertoires, thereby generating sequences that closely resemble natural antibodies. Such similarity, however, does not necessarily translate into improved functional performance in downstream applications. In this work, we develop a novel generative protein design model that enables the generation and optimization of antibody sequences tailored to specific downstream tasks and target metrics. Besides training on given an antibody dataset, we guide the generative model by an antibody-antigen binding affinity predictor for conditional discrete diffusion. The model is pre-trained on a given antibody dataset. Meanwhile, an antibody-antigen binding affinity predictor is incorporated as a conditional signal in a discrete diffusion framework, where a regressor serves as the conditional probability to guide the learning of the amino acid probability distribution of sequences under the objective of affinity optimization. In silico experiments demonstrate that our antibody design model achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art approaches, while the proposed regressor effectively improves binding affinity, as validated by an independent external predictor. Furthermore, our results highlight that the combination of finetuning and supervised guidance provides a powerful paradigm for adapting pretrained models to downstream tasks.

papers.title: Coarse Price Discrimination
papers.abstract: We study the revenue cost of limiting a seller to $L$ posted prices when heterogeneous buyers with independent values compete for scarce inventory. Our large-market assumption requires that removing any buyer have little effect on optimal revenue. We first make buyers arbitrarily replaceable at each fixed stock and then let stock grow. In this limit, one price guarantees half of optimal mechanism revenue and two guarantee $e/(e+1)$, approximately $73.1\%$. For $L\ge3$, the corresponding guarantee is a $1-1/(2L-1)$ fraction. The guarantees accommodate arbitrary differences in demand across buyers and do not require a separate price for each customer group.

papers.title: Space-time almost periodicity for the defocusing NLS hierarchy via local Toeplitz operators
papers.abstract: We study the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger hierarchy for reflectionless initial data with Dirac spectrum $E$. Under a gap moment condition of order $m$ and the assumption that $E$ is homogeneous, we prove existence and space-time almost periodicity of a global classical solution through order $m$ for every such initial datum. More generally, it suffices that $\mathbb C\setminus E$ be a Dirichlet regular Widom domain satisfying the direct Cauchy theorem and that the gap maxima of a weighted Green potential be summable, in addition to the gap moment condition. We obtain the frequencies by summing the upper and lower boundary values of the corrected powers $z^r$ on each gap and use local Toeplitz operators to reconstruct the potential from the gap phases. We also prove uniqueness under bounds on the spatial derivatives.

papers.title: Local Limits and Structures of Nearest-Predecessor Random Graphs
papers.abstract: We study the two-sided nearest-predecessor graph on $[n]$, where vertices arrive in a uniformly random order and each new vertex connects to its nearest earlier vertex on each side. We construct an infinite graph on $\mathbb{Z}$ from i.i.d. continuous insertion times and prove quenched Benjamini--Schramm convergence to it almost surely. The limit is almost surely one-ended and recurrent. We resolve an open problem of Ponomarenko by proving that the maximum degree is asymptotic in probability to $\log n/\log(3/2)$ as $n\to\infty$. We obtain the probability generating function and a CLT for the number of edges crossing the boundary of $[n]$ in the infinite limit. We also study the $K$-nearest-predecessor graph, in which each new vertex attaches to its $K$ nearest earlier vertices without regard to side. For every fixed $K\geq1$, we construct the infinite limit, prove almost sure quenched Benjamini--Schramm convergence, and show that it is almost surely connected, one-ended, and recurrent, as well as nonplanar when $K\geq2$.

papers.title: Pyroelectric Harvesting from Steady Heat Sources via Active Piezoelectric Thermal Switching
Blow-up phenomena and ill-posedness for the 2D Euler-Poincaré equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study finite-time blow-up and critical norm inflation for the Euler--Poincaré equations on $\mathbb R^2$. We consider a class of momentum fields admitting the div--curl decomposition with radial scalar potentials. The potentials satisfy a nonlocal transport system. By virtue of the conservation law and the finite propagation speed property, we obtain a growth estimate for the potential, which yields a sufficient condition for finite-time blow-up. Furthermore, combining a multiscale construction of the initial data with a blow-up criterion formulated in terms of the Besov norm of the deformation tensor, we establish norm inflation at the zero initial datum in $H^2(\mathbb R^2)$, thereby proving ill-posedness in this critical Sobolev space.

papers.title: Orthogonal lifting and amenability in ultrapowers
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor and let $\omega$ be a free ultrafilter on $\mathbb{N}$. We prove that any two orthogonal separable amenable von Neumann subalgebras in the ultrapower $\mathcal{M}^{\omega}$ admit orthogonal finite-dimensional lifts. In particular, two independent unitary operators in $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ admit independent finite-spectrum representatives. We also show that the orthogonal lifting can fail whenever one of the subalgebras is nonamenable and Connes-embeddable.

papers.title: Schur decomposition with logarithmic precision in cubic time up to logarithmic factors
papers.abstract: How much arithmetic precision is needed to compute a Schur decomposition to a prescribed tolerance? Let $A$ be a complex matrix of order $n$ with spectral norm at most one, let $0<\delta<1/2$ be the tolerance, and let $0<p<1/2$ be the requested failure probability. Our randomised floating-point algorithm uses $O(\log(n/(\delta p)))$ mantissa bits per real component and $O(n^3\log^2(n/(\delta p)))$ arithmetic operations on every execution, with universal constants. It returns $Q$ and an exactly upper triangular $T$. With probability at least $1-p$, both $\|A-QTQ^*\|_2$ and $\|Q^*Q-I\|_2$ are at most $\delta$. We sample a small perturbation using finitely many bits and use Gaussian estimates to bound the eigenvector conditioning and eigenvalue gap. A single contour estimate bounds the effect of a rounding error through any number of remaining Newton steps. At each subdivision level, the full matrix is unitarily similar to a small perturbation of the regularised input. This allows us to bound the conditioning of each diagonal block directly from that input and to use the same precision throughout.

papers.title: Beyond PINNs: Boundary-Enriched Holomorphic Networks for Laplace Problems
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) solve partial differential equations by penalizing their residual, but this formulation can be difficult to optimize for solutions with singular behaviour. We focus specifically on the two-dimensional Laplace equation, whose strong analytical structure allows the governing equation to be enforced directly in the neural representation. We compare a hybrid harmonic-neural model with a holomorphic neural network whose output is harmonic by construction and therefore requires only boundary training. We further enrich the holomorphic model with singular functions chosen according to the interior angle and boundary conditions at each junction of boundary segments. On six singular benchmarks, the enriched model is the most accurate of the neural models we compare. On the four with a closed-form solution, however, that solution lies in the span of the enrichment terms, and a least-squares fit of these terms alone is exact to rounding error. On Motz's problem and the cracked beam, the neural core reduces the relative error of the recovered leading singular coefficient from about $10^{-2}$, for a least-squares fit with the same four terms, to about $10^{-6}$, and on four variants whose solution has a smooth part outside the span, the network is $4\times10^{4}$ to $2\times10^{7}$ times more accurate than a fit of its singular terms alone; classical least-squares fits with more singular terms, or with harmonic polynomials and rational poles, are more accurate still. Our results demonstrate how exploiting problem-specific analytical structure can provide an alternative to base and residual PINNs for challenging scientific computing problems.

papers.title: XTCP: an open-source FPGA TCP endpoint for readout over 10 and 25 Gigabit Ethernet
papers.abstract: XTCP is an open-source implementation of the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) for high-rate detector readout. It targets sustained single-connection throughput near the TCP payload limit. In separate 10 Gigabit Ethernet transfers on the same Kintex UltraScale+ KU5P card and Linux host, XTCP and SiTCP-XG each delivered a median application-level throughput of 9.49 Gbit/s towards the host. Towards the FPGA, the medians were 9.49 Gbit/s for XTCP and 5.76 Gbit/s for the tested SiTCP-XG configuration. The XTCP prototype used more lookup tables and on-chip memory. In a 96 GiB echo test spanning repeated sequence-number wraps, recording when an acknowledgement first crossed the recovery boundary allowed four fast recoveries that the earlier signed comparison would have blocked. On one 25 Gigabit Ethernet bitstream, increasing the IP maximum transmission unit from 1500 to 9000 bytes raised median one-way throughput from 23.30 to 24.70 Gbit/s towards the host and from 22.09 to 24.08 Gbit/s towards the FPGA. At 9000 bytes these rates reached 99.7% and 97.1% of the TCP payload limit, respectively. In a separate echo test, the host verified all 8.77 TB returned by a jumbo-frame prototype over one connection in 3595 s, averaging 19.51 Gbit/s per direction.

papers.title: Generalizable Variable-Rate Adaptation for Image Coding for Machines
papers.abstract: Image Coding for Machines (ICM) aims to preserve task-relevant information for machine vision under limited bitrates. However, most ICM models are trained for a fixed operating point, and extending them to variable-rate compression is challenging because their training objectives differ across tasks and model designs. In this paper, we propose a loss-agnostic distillation framework for variable-rate ICM. A pretrained fixed-rate ICM model is used as a frozen teacher, while a student model learns variable-rate behavior through importance-adaptive quantization and distillation-based optimization. This enables continuous bitrate control with a single model while preserving task-relevant latent components, without requiring the original task-specific loss or downstream task labels. Experiments based on existing ICM models demonstrate that the proposed method provides continuous bitrate control and achieves competitive recognition performance compared with the fixed-rate models.

papers.title: Modelling of post-reconstruction galaxy clustering with a hybrid bias expansion
The XRISM view of the front and rear ejecta dynamics in Tycho's SNR
Identification multiplicity across study designs
papers.abstract: The answer to a causal question often admits several translations in terms of observed data. These may differ in adjustment sets, comparison groups, instruments, mediators, cutoffs, eligibility occasions, or data sources. We describe the resulting collection of analyses by three structures: the causal target that each analysis identifies under its assumptions, the assumptions that the analyses share, and the sampling dependence among their estimates. A single decomposition separates identification discrepancies from differences in causal targets, and we make both terms explicit in fourteen examples spanning adjustment, comparative panels, proxies, mediators, instruments, discontinuities, staggered adoption, sequential trials, and source combination. Comparisons within a collection can reveal differential violations of assumptions but not a bias common to all analyses; agreement is therefore evidence about the assumptions that differ, not about those that are shared. Averaging retains a causal interpretation in three ways: efficient combination of analyses that identify one target, a projection of a causal curve with a declared approximating family and weighting measure, and inference under weaker premises such as validity of at least one analysis or a known sign of its bias. Precision weights, regression-implied weights, and hierarchical models do not supply these interpretations by themselves. We relate this account to triangulation, overidentification, marginal treatment effects, transportability, and recent methods for inference under model uncertainty, and distinguish identification multiplicity from multiple testing.

papers.title: Voltage Ride-Through-Constrained Power Capping for Large-Scale Data Centers
papers.abstract: Large-scale data centers may satisfy steady-state network constraints while violating operational limits during voltage disturbances. This paper proposes a voltage ride-through (VRT)-aware power-capping framework that integrates AC optimal power flow scheduling with dynamic ride-through assessment. The proposed dynamic model captures converter limits, DC-link energy dynamics, battery support, and IT-bus voltage response. A simulation-based checker evaluates VRT constraints under prescribed faults, and the power caps are iteratively updated to obtain feasible schedules. Case studies on the IEEE 14-bus system with two data centers demonstrate that steady-state feasible operating points may violate transient voltage and power-import limits. Selective power capping achieves approximately 5\% demand reduction during capped periods while satisfying the prescribed VRT requirements. The results highlight the necessity of incorporating dynamic security assessment into data-center operational limit determination.

papers.title: Autonomous Multireference Quantum Chemistry with Artificial Intelligence Agents
papers.abstract: Accurately describing chemical reactions that involve strongly correlated electrons remains a major challenge in computational chemistry. Multireference electronic structure methods can address this challenge, but their application requires expert decisions that are di!cult to automate, particularly when the electronic structure changes as chemical bonds form and break. Here we introduce CASPER, an autonomously agentic workflow that performs multireference calculations along chemical reaction pathways. CASPER combines chemical knowledge, electronic structure calculations, and iterative assessment to identify chemically meaningful active spaces and maintain their consistency as bonds form and break. We demonstrate its capabilities on five transition-metal reactions, for which CASPER generates consistent multireference potential energy profiles with minimal human intervention. Importantly, in two reactions, CASPER identifies critical electronic-structure problems that an independent Claude session fails to recognize without the structured workflow. These include an electronic-state crossing and the exclusion of an orbital involved in bond breaking. Our results show the importance of combining language models with chemical knowledge and independent assessment of computational results. Beyond automating calculations, such agents have the potential to help researchers better understand the underlying physics and chemistry and open new opportunities for investigating complex chemical reactivity and generating high-quality quantum chemical data at scale.

papers.title: Frobenius $2$-algebras and $R$-matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, introducing Frobenius $2$-algebras, which are categorical generalizations of Frobenius algebras, we show that every Frobenius $2$-algebra determines an $R$-matrix satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation in the monoidal category of endomorphisms of its underlying object. Moreover, we illustrate this construction through three examples: a pair of objects in a braided monoidal category, a Hopf algebra with invertible antipode, and representations of the Heisenberg double of a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra. In particular, in the third example, we recover Kashaev's construction of the universal $R$-matrix. Thus, our construction provides a categorical generalization of Kashaev's construction.

papers.title: The Optimal D.C. Bound Is Dominated by the Reciprocal of the Lovász Theta Number
papers.abstract: We resolve a question left open by Anstreicher and Burer (J. Global Optim. 33, 299--312, 2005). For the standard quadratic formulation of the stability number, we prove that the optimal difference-of-convex (D.C.) bound is at most the reciprocal of the Lovász theta number. The dominance is strict whenever the Lovász theta number is not exact.

papers.title: Binning is Sinning: Absolution for the Unbinned Supernova Hubble Diagram
Global strong solvability of the two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes equations for large initial data
papers.abstract: In 1995, Kazhikhov and Vaigant introduced a two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes model with constant shear viscosity and bulk viscosity $\lambda(\rho)=\rho^\beta$. For $\beta>3$, they proved global existence of smooth solutions for arbitrarily large initial data with strictly positive density. More recently, Fan-Jiang-Li-Lü ( arXiv:2611.20264 , 2026) proved global strong solvability for every $\beta>1$ in bounded simply connected domains with Navier-slip boundary conditions. In this article, we prove global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to the Kazhikhov-Vaigant model on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ at the critical point $\beta=1$, for every $\gamma>1$ and arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum.

papers.title: On the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on a product with a torus
papers.abstract: We prove that if $N$ is a closed smooth manifold admitting a Riemannian metric of negative sectional curvature and $T^k$ is the $k$-dimensional torus, then there is a retraction from the moduli space of nonpositively curved Riemannian metrics on $T^k\times N$ onto the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$. As an application, we combine our retraction with Tuschmann and Wiemeler's work on the rational topology of the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$ to deduce that the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on $T^k\times N$ has nontrivial higher rational homotopy and cohomology groups when $k\geq5$.

papers.title: QuakeConsensus: Reducing false detections in automatic earthquake catalogs through consensus phase association
papers.abstract: Automatic earthquake catalogs rely on phase associators to group the picks of a phase picker into events. Associators also produce false events that inflate the catalog. We measure the false events of five associators, PyOcto, GaMMA, REAL, GENIE, and backprojection, on two benchmarks built from observed phase picks in Taiwan. The first benchmark isolates 28,129 cataloged earthquakes in 20-minute windows, adding noise by shifting unassociated picks independently. The second evaluates 11,917 earthquakes from the 2024 $M_w$ 7.4 Hualien aftershock sequence, shifting unassociated P and S pairs together. We also propose a consensus association strategy that keeps an event found by at least two associators. With noise picks, single associators produce 5.3% to 10.2% false positives on the regional benchmark and 11.8% to 46.8% on the Hualien benchmark, whereas the consensus catalog reduces these false positive percentages to 4.2% and 11.5%, respectively. The consensus has the highest F1 score and the smallest percentage of false positives on both benchmarks.

papers.title: Parking Functions inspired by board games
papers.abstract: We introduce two new parking schemes inspired by the classic board games Monopoly and backgammon. We consider a one-way street with $n$ parking spots and a queue of $n$ cars waiting to park. Each car has a preferred parking spot and enters in sequence to park. Under the Monopoly parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. Under the backgammon parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it bumps the already parked car out of that spot and takes its place. The bumped car then returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. A preference list is a parking function for a given parking scheme if all cars successfully park under that scheme. We prove that all preference lists are parking functions under both the Monopoly and backgammon parking schemes. However, the final parking order differs significantly between the two schemes. For a fixed permutation $\pi$, we provide a product formula for the number of Monopoly parking functions resulting in the outcome $\pi$. Analogously, we show that the number of backgammon parking functions with outcome $\pi$ is bounded below by $2^{n-1}$ and bounded above by the $n$-th Catalan number. We also obtain exact formulas involving Motzkin numbers for several families of outcomes. We define the displacement of a car as the absolute difference between the spot where a car ultimately parks and its preferred spot. Displacement multisets encode the displacements for cars with nonzero displacement. We provide formulas for the number of backgammon parking functions with a fixed displacement multiset of cardinality at most $2$, as well as for the number of Monopoly parking functions whose displacement multiset is a given singleton set. We conclude with some directions for further research.

papers.title: Unveiling the Complex high-pressure phases of Sodium at the Melting Curve Minimum via Data-Drive Crystal Structure Prediction
Second-Order Dynamics in Noisy RNNs Produce Exploration and Temporal Compression in Replay
papers.abstract: Biological neural networks (like the hippocampus) can internally generate "replay" resembling stimulus-driven activity. Recent computational models of replay use noisy recurrent neural networks (RNNs) trained to path-integrate. Replay in these networks is described as Langevin sampling, but this theory alone fails to capture the environmental exploration and temporal compression observed in real biological replay. To close this gap, we re-examine spontaneous noisy RNN activity ("replay") as Langevin sampling, one timestep at a time, from a time-series distribution resembling lived experiences (unlike previous works which defined sampling as Monte Carlo inference over a static distribution). We provide a normative second-order Langevin sampling framework wherein spike-frequency adaptation drives spatial exploration at the cost of speed, and momentum via dendritic input differentiation drives temporal compression. We numerically verify our framework via simulations of noisy RNNs trained on 2D triangular and T-maze navigation activity, and others trained on place cell activity of synthetic rats. Crucially, we observe that simultaneous adaptation and momentum increases both replay exploration and speed, and provide one of the first accounts for biologically plausible temporal compression in rate-based RNN replay. Our findings encourage experiments into whether dendritic input differentiation, or other mechanisms, may support temporal compression in memory circuits like the hippocampus.

papers.title: Logarithmic Potential and its Applications in Conformal Geometry
papers.abstract:
We establish an intrinsic characterization of the end invariants $
u_i$ in the Chern--Gauss--Bonnet formula for complete, simply connected, locally conformally flat 4-manifolds with non-negative scalar curvature and $Q$-curvature non-negative outside a compact set. For each end $M_i$, we show that $
u_i$ is the cube root of its normalized asymptotic geodesic-ball volume growth: \[ 
u_i=\left(\lim_{r	o\infty}  rac{V_g(B_r(p)\cap M_i)}{(\pi^2/2)r^4}ight)^{1/3}. \] This characterization uses only the Riemannian distance and volume of $g$; it is independent of the base point $p$, the choice of compact truncation of the end, and any conformal coordinates. The proof is based on asymptotic radial symmetry of the logarithmic potential outside a sparse $\mathscr{E}$-set, inspired by Hayman's work \cite{hayman1960slowly}, together with comparisons of radial lengths and geodesic distances.

papers.title: Active sensing as control over sensory acquisition
papers.abstract: The term "active sensing" is used across neuroscience and engineering to describe a wide range of sensing behaviors, but there is no consensus on what makes sensing "active." We propose that the behaviors grouped under this label are better understood as forms of control over sensory acquisition and develop a framework that distinguishes three interacting forms of control. Mechanistic control physically structures sensory input, strategic control modulates sensing in closed loop through adaptive and attentional processes, and agentic control concerns the sensing policies available to an agent and its authority to choose among them. These forms of control can occur separately or in combination, and have distinct consequences for sensory input, perception, behavior, and performance. The framework clarifies active-passive comparisons and provides a common basis for analyzing biological, engineered, and hybrid sensing systems by asking what is controlled, how, and by whom.

papers.title: G-Wave: Bit-to-Waveform Generation for Adaptive Wireless Communications
papers.abstract: Wireless waveforms are traditionally hand-designed for general propagation conditions, rather than adapted to each specific environment. Existing neural transceivers seek such adaptation, but often rely on relatively simple architectures with limited long-range modeling capability. More expressive Transformer-based generative architectures are difficult to apply directly because wireless communication demands extremely accurate bit recovery, often with BER below 0.1%, while providing no ground-truth waveform supervision. To address these limitations, we introduce G-Wave, a channel-conditioned generative transceiver that directly synthesizes environment-adaptive physical time-domain waveforms from bits. G-Wave consists of Transformer-based transmitter and receiver models equipped with a multiscale architecture that combines long-range sequence modeling with fine-grained signal synthesis to meet the stringent precision required for communication. The two models are jointly optimized end-to-end using only bit-reconstruction error, allowing the waveform itself to be discovered without waveform labels. Across diverse 3GPP wireless environments, G-Wave achieves lower BER than the SOTA neural transceiver (DeepOFDM) and a strong conventional baseline (OFDM) under estimated channel information, reducing mean BER by 42.4% and 72.6%, respectively.

papers.title: An eight-channel RFSoC waveform digitizer with AC- and DC-coupled front ends and transparent dual-DDR event memory
papers.abstract: We present Transparent Dual-DDR Event Memory (TDEM) for the triggered readout of an eight-channel radio-frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) digitizer. With either an AC- or a DC-coupled front end, each accepted trigger records 4096 samples per channel at 5 GSa/s. Two pulses 100 ns apart produced separate, overlapping records. On one DC-coupled input, interleaving calibration reduced an eight-sample periodic residual by a factor of 29 at +100 mV, but not at zero input. After a power cycle, the digitizer restored the coefficients for all eight DC-coupled inputs without a training tone. TDEM assigns complete events to 64- and 32-bit DDR4 memory interfaces in a 2:1 ratio. With this allocation alone, host page requests still determined which memory served each read. In two runs of approximately 6 s at 160 kHz, the peak receiver backlog fell from 20 140 events with the earlier readout to 1457 with event-level prefetch. Prefetch raised the sustained rate of the DC-coupled system from 150 to 170 kHz under repeated host readout pauses. With the same receiver design and a revised host buffer allocation, the AC-coupled system passed three 30 min tests at 175 kHz, each with 48 readout pauses and no rejected triggers. Without imposed pauses or background load, the host verified all 323 452 631 events in 30 min at 179.7 kHz. At 180 kHz, triggers were first rejected at the digitizer, consistent with a modelled transmitter capacity of 179.730 kHz for this event format.

papers.title: Infrared Relaxation Modes and the Emergence of Collective Order in Neural Dynamics
papers.abstract: We develop a microscopic field theory of collective order formation in interacting nonlinear neural systems. Integrating out microscopic neural degrees of freedom yields an effective action whose quadratic kernel determines the ordering threshold, while higher-order connected responses govern nonlinear stabilization. Spectral decomposition reveals that relaxation rates and collective-mode overlaps control collective instability and memory dynamics. Enhanced infrared spectral weight lowers the critical coupling and generates long-time memory, revealing a common spectral origin of collective ordering and persistent dynamics. Controlled numerical constructions verify the spectral dependence of collective instability and response, while nonlinear mean-field scaling follows from the microscopic Landau expansion. Transformer Jacobian spectra further reveal learning-induced infrared organization and transient memory enhancement consistent with critical-like response. Our results establish a microscopic framework linking neural interactions, collective order, and long-time memory.

papers.title: Topological Pharmacokinetics: A Model-Free Framework for Quantifying the Shape of Concentration-Time Curves
papers.abstract: Pharmacokinetic analysis compresses concentration-time curves into scalar summaries (non-compartmental analysis, NCA) or pre-specified compartmental models, approaches that are either model-free but shape-blind or shape-sensitive but structure-dependent. We introduce Topological Pharmacokinetics (TPK), a framework that reads curve shape directly from data without committing to any model. TPK delay-embeds each curve into a state-space trajectory and applies persistent homology to extract a nine-component topological invariant: multi-scale shape descriptors (peak hierarchy, secondary-peak isolation, loop structure) with established perturbation-stability properties. We evaluate the framework on four layers of increasing realism. Monophasic linear systems generate no spurious cyclic signals, whereas double-site absorption and enterohepatic recirculation produce distinct loop signatures; 12 nonlinear scenarios resolve as curvature-without-cycles; a weak endogenous rhythm survives superposition with a large exogenous drug signal (inter-peak interval recovered at exactly 24 h); and loop detection stays stable to 10 percent of Cmax additive noise and to sampling thinned to 7 points. As clinical proof of concept, we apply the same pipeline to 15 mycophenolic acid profiles digitized from a published kidney-transplant study. The secondary-persistence ratio associates with ex vivo gut-microbiome reactivation at Spearman rho = 0.815 (p = 0.0002, q = 0.002), whereas the tested exposure metrics show weak, nonsignificant associations (rho <= 0.38). Analyses are fully automated and reproducible; code and data are public. TPK is proposed as a complementary, model-free, shape-sensitive layer alongside NCA and model-based methods.

papers.title: Explicit Response Formulae and Request Problem for Smooth Expanding Endomorphisms
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the higher order differentiability of physical measures, in the category of smooth expanding endomorphisms of compact manifolds, and we establish the explicit response formulae of any order. The proof is based on the elegant Keller-Liverani-Gouëzel perturbation theory of transfer operators. Furthermore, we provide the solutions to the high order request problem, which is regarded as the inverse problem to response formulae, that is, we make perturbations to realize prescribed responses up to any finite order, and we establish the existence of minimizers for a relaxed optimization problem associated with suitable cost functionals.

papers.title: Sondheimer oscillations in Weyl semimetal films
Which Layer to Trust? Layer Selection in Frozen Speech Encoders for Singing-Voice Deepfake Detection under Signal Corruption
papers.abstract: Frozen self-supervised speech encoders have been frequently used for audio deepfake detection. However, the layers are usually chosen from a development set. We examine this choice for singing-voice deepfake detection on CtrSVDD. We train one detection head per layer, plus a learned layer mix, on frozen XEUS (3-4 seeds) and XLS-R (2 seeds). We test on clean audio and under noise, reverberation and lossy coding. On clean audio, the middle layers beat the last layer in both encoders and the learned mix does not beat the best single layer. The layer chosen on the development set is 2.3 (XEUS) and 4.1 (XLS-R) percentage points of EER worse than the best test layer. Under noise and coding, XEUS's best layers stay in the middle, while under reverberation its upper layers catch up, whereas XLS-R's best layer moves shallower. In an exploratory analysis, XEUS detects a commercial synthesis attack best with an earlier layer, especially under noise. The layer therefore cannot be chosen reliably on an in-domain development set and clean audio alone.

papers.title: FL-CsLoc-DH: A Federated Learning-Based Crowdsensing Localization under Dual Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Mobile Crowdsensing (MCS) provides a scalable way to collect indoor fingerprints and reduce professional calibration effort. To protect the location privacy of participating clients, Federated Learning (FL) is used so that raw fingerprints and measurement trajectories remain local. However, owing to the open and uncontrollable nature of MCS, participating clients collect fingerprints in different propagation environments and possess unequal labeling availability. These conditions jointly cause data and annotation heterogeneity, which degrades FL-based crowdsensing localization. In this work, we propose FL-CsLoc-DH, a federated semi-supervised learning framework for crowdsensing localization under dual heterogeneity. FL-CsLoc-DH coordinates Two-Stage Noisy Gradient Rejection (TS-NGR), Soft Fisher Confidence Alignment (S-FCA), and Trajectory-Smoothed Model Averaging (T-SMA) throughout localization model learning. TS-NGR suppresses unreliable client updates caused jointly by environment dependent data shifts and noisy pseudo labels. S-FCA limits parameter increments dominated by unlabeled data, thereby alleviating annotation heterogeneity during local training. T-SMA smooths the aggregated global localization model trajectory to reduce drift induced by data heterogeneity. Experiment results show that the three mechanisms provide complementary improvements in localization accuracy under the MCS environment while retaining raw client data locally.

papers.title: Sharp integral Ricci pinching on manifolds with positive total scalar curvature
papers.abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a closed connected Riemannian three-manifold with $\int_M R \mathrm{d}v>0$, and assume that $M$ is not diffeomorphic to a spherical space form. We prove the sharp integral Ricci pinching inequality $$\mathrm{vol}(g)\int_M |\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2 \mathrm{d}v \geq \frac{1}{6}\left(\int_M R \mathrm{d}v\right)^2.$$ Moreover, equality holds if and only if $(M,g)$ is locally isometric to $\mathbb{S}^2(a)\times\mathbb{R}$ for some $a>0$. By the same method, we prove $\mathrm{vol}(g)\int_M |\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2 \mathrm{d}v \geq \frac{1}{12}\left(\int_M R \mathrm{d}v\right)^2$ on closed four-manifolds with $\int_M R \mathrm{d}v>0$ that have a finite cover with positive first Betti number, and we provide a new proof of Gursky's inequality. We also show that the corresponding inequality fails in every dimension $n\geq 5$, and we give a metric on $\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^1$ that disproves a conjecture of Ge, Li and Lian.

papers.title: Characterizing Frozen SSL Encoders and Backends for Cross-Domain Speech Deepfake Detection
papers.abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) encoders are the dominant front end for speech deepfake detection, and the prevailing recipe fine-tunes the full encoder on a small spoofing corpus, maximizing in-domain accuracy at the cost of known degradation under domain shift. Taking a recent cross-attention fusion of SSL and constant-Q cepstral features as a fixed reference recipe, we freeze its encoder and ask which encoder and which backend behave best across domains. We cross two frozen encoders, the massively multilingual XEUS and Wav2Vec2 XLSR-53, with two backends, multi-head factorized attentive (MHFA) pooling and AASIST, and evaluate on ASVspoof 2019 LA, ASVspoof 2021 LA and DF, In-the-Wild (ITW), and ASVspoof 5, training every system in one pipeline over three seeds. We report three findings. First, encoder and backend interact: MHFA suits the stronger encoder, while AASIST recovers more from and stabilizes the weaker one. Second, within this recipe, the frozen encoder produces large, repeatable differences. With MHFA, frozen XEUS lowers error relative to frozen XLSR-53 by 58-77% on LA21, DF21, and ASV5, and more modestly on ITW. This ordering persists in a matched-aggregation ablation, and a capacity-matched WavLM Large diagnostic shows that parameter count alone does not explain XLSR-53's weaker performance. Third, against a three-seed fine-tuned baseline, frozen XEUS updates under 0.4M parameters versus 316M, wins on ASVspoof 5 (in EER and min-DCF) and modestly on LA21, trails on DF21 and ITW, and shows lower seed variation on three of the four out-of-domain sets.

papers.title: Grothendieck--Serre for quasi-split groups over two-dimensional regular local rings
papers.abstract: We prove the Grothendieck--Serre conjecture for quasi-split reductive group schemes over two-dimensional regular local rings, that is, every generically trivial torsor under a quasi-split group scheme $G$ over a regular local ring $R$ of dimension two is trivial.
