Our main result is new when $R$ is ramified and generalizes Nisnevich's result by removing the assumption that the residue field is infinite. By formal patching of torsors and valuative criteria, we are reduced to showing a product formula when $G$ is semisimple and simply connected. Then, we take advantage of relative simple reflections and relative Bruhat decomposition to prove a generation by rank-one subgroups. The analysis on Dynkin diagrams with Galois actions reduces us to $\operatorname{SL}_2$ and three-dimensional $\operatorname{SU}$ factors. For the special unitary case, we treat Hermitian forms by using stabilizations and cancellation to finish the proof.

papers.title: Sharp constant off-diagonal extrapolation for Muckenhoupt bases
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a sharp constant version of off-diagonal extrapolation for matrix weights, improving the result we proved in an earlier paper. In an appendix, we give a new and simpler proof of this result in the scalar case.

papers.title: Exceptional Rays of Invariant Processes on Trees
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be an ergodic, non-constant random process on the $d$-regular tree $T_d$, with marginal distribution $X$. We prove that there always exist "exceptional" rays, whose asymptotic means are at least $\mathbb{E}(X)+\delta$; furthermore, for edge processes, $\delta > 0$ can be taken to depend only on the law of $X$. We compare different definitions of "maximal asymptotic means", relating them to different notions of speed of tree-indexed random walks.

papers.title: Where does pancreatic lesion segmentation fail on public CT? An attenuation-stratified analysis of a duct-guided pipeline on PanTS
papers.abstract: Lesion segmentation is a building block of most CT pipelines for pancreatic cancer detection, yet lesion overlap scores stay low. Instead of proposing a new architecture, we report where an end-to-end pipeline fails on a large public dataset. On PanTS we built a three-stage pipeline: pancreas segmentation, maps of the main pancreatic duct (MPD) and common bile duct (CBD), and a lesion model that receives the CT with or without the predicted duct maps. Both lesion models were trained identically on 4007 scans and evaluated once on 737 held-out test scans (127 with a lesion) under a comparison rule fixed before the test run. Lesion Dice was 0.213 with duct maps and 0.209 with CT only (paired difference +0.004, 95% CI -0.011 to +0.019). The duct maps raised the share of lesions touched by a prediction (+0.079, 95% CI +0.024 to +0.134) but also enlarged predictions in lesion-free scans, and lesion-like regions were predicted in all lesion-free test scans. Out of fold, keeping only the predicted components that touched the lesion raised Dice only from 0.285 to 0.309; the loss came mainly from the extent of correctly located predictions. Clearly hypoattenuating lesions, which intensity alone separates from normal pancreas, had the lowest coverage (median 16.6%). From the predicted maps alone, the MPD diameter separated lesion from lesion-free test scans with AUC 0.794 (95% CI 0.747 to 0.839), while the CBD diameter was weak (AUC 0.603) and added nothing. Code for training, inference and evaluation is publicly available.

papers.title: Cylindrical dimers and monomial immanants
papers.abstract: For a bipartite graph on a cylinder, group its perfect matchings by homological height and sum their weights in each group. We prove that every minor of the resulting Toeplitz matrix has nonnegative coefficients in the edge weights, settling a question recorded by Lai. We first prove conjectures of Galashin and the author concerning directed cycles in cylindrical networks, and then deduce the dimer theorem from them. A related, stronger positivity property for superpositions of cylindrical matchings turns out to be equivalent to Stembridge's interval-product conjecture on monomial immanants. Using annular webs, we prove this conjecture for partitions with at most four columns. A stretching argument extends this to all partitions with parts in $\{n,2n,3n,4n\}$.

papers.title: Electric polarizabilities with phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo
Context-Aware Proactive Self-Adaptation: A Two-Layer Model Predictive Control Approach
papers.abstract: In self-adaptive software systems, the role of context is paramount, especially for proactive self-adaptation. Current research, however, does not fully explore context's impact, for example on priorities of the requirements. To address this gap, we introduce a novel contextual goal model to capture these factors and their influence on the system. Using this, we propose a two-layer control mechanism with a context-aware model predictive control to achieve proactive adaptation for the software system and adaptation for the controller itself. By contextual prediction and a more accurate system model, our approach utilizes model predictive control to facilitate timely and efficient system adaptations, improving both performance and adaptability. Meanwhile, we perform requirement adaptation to update the contextual goal model, which in turn updates the objective function and constraints of the controller. Our experimental evaluations across two scenarios demonstrate the significant benefits of our approach in enhancing system performance.

papers.title: World Models Are the Right Foundation for Simulating Mars Terraforming
Global classification and local asymptotics for a Monge-Ampère obstacle problem
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq2$ and $0<q<n$. We prove that every nontrivial convex entire solution of $$\det D^2v = v^q, \quad v \geq 0, \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^n$$ with bounded (possibly empty) coincidence set $\{v=0\}$ is affine equivalent to a radial solution. Together with the classification for unbounded coincidence sets by Jin-Tu-Xiong \cite{JTX2025}, this completes the classification of nontrivial nonnegative convex entire solutions. The proof uses an affine-invariant monotonicity formula extending the two-dimensional formula in Mooney-Sen \cite{MooneySen2026}. Combining this global classification with level-set parametrization and spectral analysis, we also obtain precise asymptotics of local solutions at isolated zeros, settling the remaining case, namely, a singleton free boundary, in the regularity theory for the Monge-Ampère obstacle problem studied in \cite{JTX2025}.

papers.title: A Positron Spectral Dip near 20 GV in Selected Orbital Projections of AMS-02 Data
Circle-Pattern Linear Systems for the Twenty Trivalent Delaunay Types of a Genus-Two Surface: Rank, Feasibility and Polytope Dimension
papers.abstract: The hyperelliptic quotient of a closed genus-two Riemann surface is a hyperbolic sphere with six cone points of angle pi. Its Delaunay triangulation T is dual to a trivalent Voronoi graph G of one of twenty combinatorial types. For each type we study the angle system Ax = 1, x >= 0, where A is the vertex-edge incidence matrix of T and pi x_e is the angle subtended at a cone point by the Voronoi edge dual to e, equivalently the intersection angle of the two circumcircles adjacent across e. We prove that rank A = 6 for all twenty types, including the six whose triangulation has a loop, so the affine solution space always has the dimension of Teichmuller space. The polytope P = {Ax = 1, x >= 0} behaves differently. It is six-dimensional for exactly ten types, the ten Delaunay-realizable ones. For nine types it has dimension one, two or three, because non-negativity forces some wedge angles to vanish, and for the type of signature (2,2,2,2,8,8) it is empty. We show that five of the nine and the empty type never occur as Delaunay triangulations, and that the other four occur only as triangulations of non-trivalent Delaunay decompositions. Every vertex of every P is half-integral, as for fractional perfect matching polytopes. For the ten full-dimensional types every facet x_e = 0 lies at an edge where the Whitehead move is admissible, though not conversely, and the move identifies the facets of the two polytopes; these identifications pair the facet orbits of the ten cells under their automorphism groups. The free unfolding of the gluing grows at rate about 7.093. All finite statements are checked by an independent program, and the rank, infeasibility, forced coordinates, dimensions, vertices and facets are verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: Second Moment Penny Packings via Rolling Spaces
papers.abstract: We solve the unrestricted minimum second moment problem for six unit disks in the plane by proving that the minimum is \(29/3\) attained uniquely up to isometry and relabelling by one disk together with five of its six neighbours in the triangular lattice. The realised contacts themselves define the space of admissible motions, while the directions preserving those contacts to first order define the rolling space consisting of motions whose relative velocities have zero normal component at every realised contact. Together, these spaces lead to an exact tangent cone formula and to a criterion by which a strictly positive centroidal contact balance, combined with rolling rigidity, implies strict local minimality modulo Euclidean motions. Our method recovers the classical five disk minimum \(34/5\) of Graham and Sloane, previously the largest unrestricted case known exactly. Geometric reductions and a graph census reduce the global search to finitely many contact graph classes. Exact analysis and validated interval arithmetic then exclude competing configurations, establishing the global bounds and uniqueness. Our method allows us to pass from putative lattice extremisers to unrestricted optimality.

papers.title: Is Classical Error Control Ready for IMT-2030? Information-Loss Interfaces in Channel Estimation, FEC, CRC, and ARQ for Machine-Type Services
papers.abstract: Fault tolerance and structured error control in mobile communication networks--historically implemented as a modular cascade of pilot-aided channel estimation (CE), forward error correction (FEC), cyclic redundancy check (CRC), and hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ)--remain foundational to 5G New Radio (NR). Although finite-blocklength coding, joint estimation-decoding, and grant-free access have been active academic topics for over a decade, commercial 3GPP specifications up to Release 18 still enforce rigid cross-layer boundaries between these blocks. In short-packet machine-type communications (MTC) for IMT-2030 (6G), inserting separate redundancy for channel training, error correction, and error detection shrinks the net payload entropy resolved per channel slot, while standardized UE processing timelines and HARQ round-trip delays collide with sub-millisecond reliability targets. Combining a multi-user MIMO short-packet simulation with real 3GPP TS 38.214 numerology latency budgets, this article diagnoses the structural bottlenecks of the legacy reliability pipeline and outlines an interoperable roadmap for 3GPP Release 20+--spanning soft-output universal decoding, sensing-assisted priors, grant-free joint detection, and task-oriented error control.

papers.title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with a Matern Kernel
papers.abstract: Gaussian processes (GPs) provide a flexible framework for modeling complex dependence structures through a covariance function, or kernel, whose parameters determine the variability, correlation, and smoothness of the underlying process. The Matérn kernel is among the most popular choices due to its flexibility in modeling different degrees of smoothness. Although the identifiability of Matérn kernel parameters under fixed-domain asymptotics is completely understood, identifiability alone does not establish the consistency or asymptotic behavior of the maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs) routinely used in practice. In this paper, we address this gap by developing a sharp asymptotic theory for the joint MLE of Matérn kernel parameters. Since parameter identifiability depends critically on the dimension of the observation domain, we characterize the estimable parameters and establish their convergence rates across different dimensions. We establish joint asymptotic normality and minimax optimality of the convergence rates. In addition, we establish asymptotically valid confidence regions for the estimable parameters. Our results accommodate irregular sampling designs and extend to sub-Gaussian measurement errors. Extensive simulation studies illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: The Coupled Scaled Dirichlet Distribution
papers.abstract: We introduce a coupled scaled Dirichlet distribution for paired compositions that may have different dimensions. Building on the matched Gamma-sharing construction of Trick, Rothkopf, and Jäkel (2023) for ordinary Dirichlet vectors, we allow scaled Dirichlet margins and extend the construction to include crossed sharing between non-corresponding latent components. We propose a signed coupling parameter whose sign selects matched or crossed sharing and whose magnitude controls the strength of sharing. We then develop a time-varying extension in which observed covariates determine this parameter. The model can therefore switch between matched and crossed sharing over time while preserving both scaled Dirichlet margins. We derive the joint mixed moments and use them to estimate dependence after fitting the margins separately. The moments can be evaluated by Monte Carlo simulation or by two-dimensional numerical quadrature, regardless of the dimensions of the compositions. Simulations show that the estimator generally recovers the sharing pattern, although weak crossed sharing is harder to detect. In an application to four U.S. equity-index futures, the time-varying model modestly improved the held-out energy and variogram scores for the trading-volume and intraday price-range compositions relative to the static-dependence model.

papers.title: Cumulants, Partitions, and Generalizations of Pólya's Characterization of the Normal Distribution
papers.abstract:
Let $X_1,X_2$ be independent, identically distributed random variables with finite variance. Pólya (1923) proved the celebrated result that if $\sqrt{2}X_1 =^L X_1+X_2$ then $X_1$ is normally distributed. Pólya's theorem has been extended in many ways, e.g., to the case of random coefficients $R_1,R_2$ such that, under certain regularity conditions, if $(R_1^2+R_2^2)^{1/2}X_1 =^L R_1X_1+R_2X_2$, then $X_1$ is normally distributed. In this article, Pólya's theorem is generalized {\it via} the combinatorics of $\Pi_n$, the set-partitions of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Let $X_j,R_j$, $j=1,\ldots,n$, be mutually independent random variables, where $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are identically distributed. For each $
u \in \Pi_n$, a random variable $W_
u$ is constructed from $\{X_j,R_j, j=1,\ldots,n\}$ and, subject to regularity conditions, the normality of $X_1$ is deduced from functional equations involving linear combinations of the characteristic functions of the $W_
u$. For $n = 3$, the $W_
u$ are $(R_1^2+R_2^2+R_3^2)^{1/2}X_1$, $(R_1^2+R_2^2)^{1/2}X_1+R_3X_3$, $(R_1^2+R_3^2)^{1/2}X_1+R_2X_2$, $R_1X_1+(R_2^2+R_3^2)^{1/2}X_2$, and $R_1X_1+R_2X_2+R_3X_3$, corresponding to the partitions $123$, $12|3$, $13|2$, $1|23$, and $1|2|3$, respectively. By modifying the regularity conditions, we also obtain characterizations of some contaminated normal distributions. A characterization of the exponential distribution through the minimum of a random sample leads us consider mutually independent random variables $X_j\ge0$, $R_j>0$, $j=1,\ldots,n$, where $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are identically distributed. For each $
u\in\Pi_n$ a random variable $	ilde{W}_
u$ is constructed from $\{X_j,R_j, j=1,\ldots,n\}$ and, subject to regularity conditions, the exponentiality of $X_1$ is derived from functional equations based on linear combinations of the survival functions of the $	ilde{W}_
u$, $
u\in\Pi_n$.

papers.title: Identifiability of infinite location-scale Gaussian mixtures
papers.abstract: The problem of identifiability of the mixing measure for a location-scale mixture of Gaussian distributions is considered. We give sufficient and necessary conditions on the compact support of the mixing measure on unknown location and scale parameters for which the mixing measure's uniqueness can be guaranteed. This is achieved by an analytic and probabilistic framework that characterizes the null space of the Gaussian mixing operator, a linear mapping that transforms a space of mixing measures with compact support into that of Gaussian mixture distributions. This framework exposes a fruitful connection between the infinite location-scale Gaussian mixtures and the exiting behavior of a space-time backward Brownian motion from a compact domain, as well as the nature of the support of the heat potential associated with such a stochastic process. As a consequence of this theory we obtain complete characterizations of identifiability for several natural classes of location-scale parameter sets in terms of their topological and geometric properties. Our theory also yields canonical and identifiable representations of infinite Gaussian mixtures with mixing support contained within enclosed boundaries.

papers.title: The replication-energy limit of PQG reduced-density-matrix theory from a single-fragment semidefinite program
papers.abstract: Variational two-electron reduced-density-matrix calculations are not size extensive: the energy per fragment can decrease when identical, strictly noninteracting fragments are replicated [M. Nakata and K. Yasuda, Phys. Rev. A 80, 042109 (2009)]. For the $P$, $Q$, and $G$ conditions (PQG) we prove the following. (i) The energy per fragment converges to the minimum of a semidefinite program (SDP) on one fragment. The limit is reached through negative interfragment covariances of order $1/(k-1)$ for $k$ replicas, which cancel the local electron number and spin fluctuations consistently with a global singlet. (ii) The energy per fragment is nonincreasing in the replica count. (iii) It reaches the limit exactly at a finite replica count. (iv) The defect is tied to the local electron-number variance: a sharp local electron number restores additivity without a spin constraint. (v) In chains of identical units the energy per unit has a limit that tends to the same minimum as the coupling vanishes. The key tool is that the $G$ condition [C. Garrod and J. K. Percus, J. Math. Phys. 5, 1756 (1964)] keeps the variances and covariances of one-body operators positive semidefinite without a representing state, so that the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality applies. PQG therefore admits explicitly constructed replicated points whose compensated local fluctuations lower the energy per fragment below the isolated value. Be, CH$_4$, N$_2$, and H$_2$O (STO-6G) and a four-site Hubbard fragment illustrate the results; in these examples the gap to the isolated value persists with three-index conditions $T_1$ and $T_2$.

papers.title: Computational Strategies for Mixed Logit Estimation Automatic Differentiation, GPU Computing, and Floating-Point Precision
authors: Hengzhe Zhao Jinhui Zhang Yuanyuan Gu
papers.abstract: Mixed logit estimation can become computationally demanding as sample size and the dimension of preference heterogeneity increase. This study examines how derivative computation, processor choice and floating-point precision affect estimation time and parameter recovery across problem sizes. This paper provides a controlled benchmark, comparing finite differences (FD) with automatic differentiation (AD), central processing unit (CPU) execution with graphics processing unit (GPU) execution, and double-precision (FP64) with single-precision (FP32) arithmetic using Monte Carlo experiments that hold the data-generating process, simulation draws, optimiser, starting values, and objective function fixed across strategies. The results show that AD is the dominant source of acceleration. Combining AD with FP32 arithmetic provides further gains, while combining AD, GPU execution, and FP32 arithmetic delivers the largest speed improvements, particularly as sample size and model complexity increase. Our findings indicate substantial computational gains with broadly comparable parameter-recovery performance in the simulated settings this http URL empirical application in health preferences illustrates what extra empirical evidence and statistical benefit on model fit could be achieved, when researchers are made possible to estimate a richer, correlated preference specification. We provide an open sourced prototype to for model estimation with AD-FP32 strategy workflow that automatically detect hardware and provide the fastest estimation. Faster estimation can make richer random-coefficient specifications, larger simulation draw counts, bootstrap inference, multi-start optimisation, and robustness checks more feasible in applied choice modelling research.

papers.title: Baker-Akhiezer realization and reconstruction for three-wave interactions in canonical multiwave Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We revisit the canonical multiwave Hamiltonians with three-wave interactions studied by Menyuk, Chen and Lee, and by Jiang, Rauch-Wojciechowski and Bullough. With compatible linear phase terms, we construct their general solution on the generic spectral locus from multipoint Baker-Akhiezer functions. Conversely, we give a finite interpolation criterion and completion procedure that realize prescribed Baker-Akhiezer evaluations on arbitrary smooth algebraic curves in the same Hamiltonian system. We identify the prescribed curve with the normalized spectral curve and show that commuting polynomial Hamiltonians span every Abel direction on each birational spectral level, including the accompanying mode phases. Together, these results establish a correspondence between Baker-Akhiezer data and canonical multiwave dynamics, supporting our view of this system as a fundamental canonical Hamiltonian setting for Baker-Akhiezer functions. We make explicit its connections with other established integrable systems and validate hyperelliptic, trigonal and multipuncture examples numerically.

papers.title: Modulation equations and coherence dynamics in a qubit chain coupled to a circulating fluxon
papers.abstract: We derive modulation equations for the joint quantum amplitudes of a circulating fluxon and an exchange-coupled qubit chain whose endpoint interacts with the field. A unitary passage operator combines the translational packet, vacuum dressing, and discrete oscillatory modes. A resonant normal form separates the slow amplitude evolution from nonresonant corrections. Ordered emission and return amplitudes generate a second-order correction that changes the population and coherence of an internal qubit. The next ground-band coefficient gives compensating diagonal and near-resonant off-diagonal contributions to the accumulated error. We bound the state error a posteriori. At a velocity-selected resonance, direct propagation over 81 passages gives a mode contribution of order $6\times10^{-8}$; the cubic ground-band approximation agrees with an expanded full calculation to $1.5\times10^{-9}$ in the tested observables. The equations describe how the source profile and field memory affect coherence inside the chain.

papers.title: Essentially Order-Preserving Fourth-Order Exponential Runge--Kutta Methods for Non-Commuting Operators
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the convergence of explicit exponential Runge--Kutta methods for the linear evolution equation \(u'(t)+Au(t)=Bu(t)\), where \(-A\) generates an analytic semigroup, \(B\) is unbounded and relatively bounded with respect to \(A\), and \(A\) and \(B\) do not commute. It is known from our previous work on order reduction of exponential Runge--Kutta methods for non-commuting operators that this non-commutativity can cause order reduction even for linear problems. In a further work on third-order methods, we showed that this reduction can be avoided by adding a stage and imposing higher regularity on the initial data. Here we treat the fourth-order case. We identify conditions on the coefficients of explicit fourth-order exponential Runge--Kutta methods under which the full order four is retained for this class of problems, and we state the convergence rate as a function of the regularity of \(u_0\). The analysis shows precisely which defect terms, caused by the non-commutativity of \(A\) and \(B\), are eliminated by these conditions. The classical methods of Krogstad and of Strehmel--Weiner do not satisfy them and converge only with order \(11/4\) under the corresponding regularity assumptions, whereas the six-stage method expRK4s6, constructed by Luan (2021), satisfies them and attains order four. Numerical experiments for an advection--diffusion problem involving non-commuting operators confirm the theoretical convergence rates.

papers.title: Twisted K-Theory and Reduced Norms over Global and Higher Local Fields
papers.abstract: We prove the Merkurjev--Suslin conjecture concerning reduced norms over both global and local fields. Furthermore, in both settings, we construct maps between truncated K-theory spectra that induce the reduced norms in degrees 1 and 2, and show that these maps are equivalences over local fields. Over global fields, we establish finiteness properties of their fibers and give a detailed description of their structure. We also extend the Merkurjev--Suslin conjecture to two-dimensional local fields and three-dimensional local fields with characteristic sequences (0, 0, 0) and (0, 0, p), and prove it in these settings. Finally, we apply these results to noncommutative class field theory over number fields and obtain a description of the Artin map associated with a central simple algebra.

papers.title: A linear bound in Waring's problem
papers.abstract: We show that $G(k) \asymp k$ in Waring's problem.

papers.title: Extreme Value Theory for Peak Power in Discrete-Time Complex Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: The peak power for a band-limited, radio frequency (RF) signal, often expressed using the dimensionless peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), is an important quantity for signal analysis and the design of RF transmitters and receivers. Modern digital instrumentation, like vector signal analyzers, collect and process discrete-time samples of the complex baseband signal. Also, computer-based simulations of continuous-time processes must be carried out with discrete-time sequences. Therefore, to design such measurements and simulations, accurate models for the distribution of the PAPR for discrete-time complex baseband processes are required. In particular, band-pass thermal noise and modern communication signals, like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), are often modeled as complex Gaussian processes. To address this problem, we present a new analytical model for the PAPR distribution of a stationary, discrete-time, complex Gaussian process. We demonstrate that the new discrete-time model subsumes prior models based on asymptotic extreme value theory as special cases while providing a larger domain of efficacy. Specifically, using Monte Carlo simulations of filtered complex white Gaussian noise, we show that the new model is more effective for practical sample sizes and dual-band spectra than previous approaches.

papers.title: General bounds for metric dimension of diameter-two graphs with applications
papers.abstract: We study the metric dimension of several classes of graphs with diameter two. First, we establish a general lower bound for the metric dimension of graphs with diameter two in terms of their order and maximum degree. We then apply our results to Grassmann graphs, Moore graphs, and bilinear forms graphs. For Kneser graphs, we obtain new upper bounds, while for $G_q(n,2)$ Grassmann graphs we establish new upper bounds provided by constructions of resolving sets. For Moore graphs of diameter two, we derive improved lower bounds, and for $H_q(n,2)$ bilinear forms graphs, we obtain new upper and lower bounds on their metric dimension.

papers.title: Mixed-State Magnetotransport Below $T_c$ in Type-II Superconducting NbN Thin Films
Predicting the Orbital Retention of Habitable-Zone Planets Following Stellar Flybys Using Machine Learning
Inferring Experimental Objectives in Microscopy Experiments from Decision Traces
Form of Words in Free Products with scl 1/12
papers.abstract: Let $G = *_\lambda G_\lambda$ be a free product of groups and let $g\in G$ be any element not conjugate into any free factor and not conjugate to its inverse. Then $\mathrm{scl}(g) \ge \frac{1}{12}$ and $\mathrm{scl}(g) = \frac{1}{12}$ if and only if $g$ is a product of an element of order $2$ and an element of order $3$. In particular, this classifies all elements in $G = \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ with $\mathrm{scl}_G(g) = \frac{1}{12}$.

papers.title: Notes on Generative AI for Mathematical Research
papers.abstract: These notes describe how generative AI is now used to solve and to check research-level mathematics, with a focus on agents and their harnesses. For the proving agents Rethlas, Danus, and Pharos and the verification agent OSVerify, we explain the design principles, compare each with its base model, present case studies, and show how to use and contribute to them. We also briefly review the history of AI for mathematics and the community's reactions to it.

papers.title: Simple closed geodesics on the Klein bottle: the sharp lower bound
papers.abstract: We revisit the Klein bottle case of Ballmann's theorem on simple closed geodesics. The final counting argument in Ballmann's proof relies on the existence of a nontrivial homological family in a primitive one-sided free homotopy class. We identify an obstruction to this assertion and establish instead the lower bound of four geometrically distinct simple closed geodesics: two in the horizontal two-sided class and one in each of the two primitive one-sided classes. We then show that this bound is sharp. The exclusion of any additional simple closed geodesics is obtained by combining the topology of the orientation double cover with a separation of the geodesic equations and a period estimate based on Wirtinger's inequality.

papers.title: On the Bourgain-Rudnick eigenfunction restriction conjecture in four dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform upper $L^2$ bound for eigenfunctions of the four-dimensional flat torus on the compact paraboloid $\mathbb{P}^3$. The main novelty is the use of Fourier restriction estimates. We interpret spherical lattice point statistics as non-concentration inequalities of the strength needed to apply the Du--Zhang fractal restriction theorem. We apply their result on two-dimensional slices of $\mathbb{P}^3$. Further possible extensions are also discussed.

papers.title: The dimensions of curly and dipolar Besicovitch-Kakeya sets
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp Hausdorff dimension and box-counting dimension bounds for sets containing meridian circles and for sets whose difference sets contain a sphere. Fix two antipodal points N, S on S^{n-1}, n\ge 3, and consider the family of great circles passing through them. Assuming the Besicovitch-Kakeya overlapping conjecture in R^{n-1}, we prove that every bounded set K\subset R^n containing a translated and dilated copy of each circle in this family satisfies \dim_H K\ge n-1. In particular, the same conclusion holds for bounded sets containing a circle in every orientation. This bound is sharp, as shown by the unit sphere. We also prove unconditionally that every bounded set K\subset R^n, n\ge2, satisfying S^{n-1}\subset K-K has lower box counting dimension greater than or equal to n(n-1)/(2n-1), and the bound is also sharp.

papers.title: On the Spectrum of the Iwatsuka Hamiltonian with Equal Magnetic Field Limits
papers.abstract: We consider the two-dimensional magnetic Laplacian associated with a magnetic field that depends on a single spatial variable, known as the Iwatsuka Hamiltonian. We focus on the equal-limit case, where the magnetic field is of the form $b(\cdot)=b_\infty+q(\cdot)$, with $b_\infty>0$ and $q\in C_0(\mathbb R)$. We prove that the Iwatsuka Hamiltonian admits an absolutely continuous spectrum whenever $q$ is compactly supported and has a constant sign near one edge of its support.

papers.title: Revisiting RadioGalaxyNET: modern detectors for radio galaxy detection and host identification
Shadow economy as a null set. Measure-theoretic approach to shadow economy
papers.abstract: In this paper we asked if the shadow economy can be defined as a system of null sets for institutional measures or sensors that measure economic transactions. As an answer a measure-theoretic testable framework to redefine and quantify the shadow economy was designed. Traditional economic definitions frequently conflate the actual shadow economy with the observational limitations of state institutions. To resolve this, we model the shadow economy as a null set relative to institutional measures and analyze three complementary economic regimes. We explore in this context how standard mathematical tools can be given economic meaning. First, in the low-resolution regime, we apply Banach Lattices and Lebesgue decomposition of a measure to address transaction underreporting by aggregating incomplete institutional registries using a supremum fusion operator. Second, for hidden economic dimensions, we utilize Copula theory and Kullback-Leibler divergence optimization to reconstruct unobserved financial flows from technological and physical indicators. Third, we address audit scalability by modeling the shadow economy as a sparse vector, applying Compressed Sensing to detect high-volume sparse evasion networks through random, incoherent, and privacy-preserving sampling.

papers.title: A Tributary of Tucana III? The Sutlej Stellar Stream in DELVE DR3
A phenomenological decomposition of SRC-inspired occupation effects in imbalanced Fermi superfluids
Interpolation of nonlocal Sobolev spaces for general gradients
papers.abstract: We study the interpolation structure of nonlocal Sobolev spaces associated with general radial gradients. For compactly supported kernels satisfying suitable regularity and two-sided growth assumptions of fractional order, we characterize the spaces $H^{\rho,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $1<p<\infty$, by the Gustavsson--Peetre interpolation method between $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $W^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The function parameter is determined, up to equivalence, by the behavior of the kernel near the origin. We also establish a complex interpolation formula between spaces associated with different kernels and integrability exponents, in which the interpolated kernel is their geometric mean. For the corresponding nonlocal Gagliardo spaces $W^{\rho,p}(\R^n)$, defined through an integral seminorm of first differences, we prove an identification with generalized Besov spaces and a real interpolation characterization involving the same function parameter. These results extend the classical relation between Bessel potential and Gagliardo spaces beyond power-type kernels, yielding continuous embeddings between the two families and their coincidence in the Hilbertian case. We further discuss logarithmic kernels and restriction spaces on Lipschitz domains, and obtain extension and compact embedding results for the Gagliardo spaces under weaker assumptions on the kernel.

papers.title: One machine, three drawings: a didactic analysis of a teaching progression for the function concept from Grade 4 to Grade 10
papers.abstract: The function concept can be entered through a correspondence between sets, a relation that is single-valued, or through a process that turns an input into an output. This paper presents the design rationale and a critical analysis of a source progression for functions (Grades 4-10, nominal ages 9-16, with two levels on relations between quantities), from which French-curriculum and International Baccalaureate chapters published at this https URL are assembled. One schema is presented first and kept throughout: a function is a machine that takes an input, applies a rule and gives exactly one output. Its drawing changes with age (a robot, then a box, then the arrow $f : x \mapsto f(x)$), and each change is shown once, the two drawings side by side; after 15 the box returns only in the lessons, to explain composition and the inverse. The properties that research identifies as difficult (the uniqueness of the output, the constant function, the function without a formula, two rules for one function, preimages) are posed on the machine from Grade 4; the word relation is kept for the link between two quantities, where covariation is taught; the set of ordered pairs comes back as the graph. The choices are related to the function machine as a cognitive root and to its authors' own warnings, to process-object accounts, to studies of concept images and of covariation, and to the French and IB curricula. A block-level audit of the dated source documents found the machine in only 2 of the 177 exercise blocks of Grades 7 to 10, no exercise asking pupils to draw a machine, and public chapters that opened on the relation; the revisions made after the audit are recorded with their counts before and after. No empirical evaluation is reported; hypotheses for one are stated.

papers.title: Parity-safe digraphs with countably many ends are kernel-perfect
papers.abstract: A kernel of a digraph is an independent set that every other vertex points into, and a digraph is kernel-perfect if every induced subgraph has a kernel. A digraph without odd cycles in which no ray contains infinitely many vertices that each send an infinite fan of disjoint paths to that ray is safe. The conjecture that every safe digraph is kernel-perfect was proved earlier for digraphs with finitely many ends. We prove a stronger statement for at most countably many ends. Number the vertices of a ray, and let the type of a path that ends on the ray be the parity of the sum of its length and the number of its last vertex. A fan is mixed if it has infinitely many paths of each type, and a digraph is parity-safe if it has no odd cycle and no ray containing infinitely many vertices with a mixed fan to it. Yablo's graph (omega,<) is not parity-safe. Its variant with edges only between vertices of different parity has a kernel - it is parity-safe but not safe. Our main result is that a parity-safe digraph with at most countably many ends is kernel-perfect, and the claim for safe digraphs follows since safety implies parity-safety. The digraph may have any cardinality, and nothing is assumed about the structure of the ends, but the case of uncountably many ends remains open.

papers.title: Low Vibration Closed-Cycle Flow Cryostat for Ion-Cavity Experiments
papers.abstract: Cryogenic operation below 10 K suppresses trap-electrode and dielectric heating of trapped ions while cryopumping residual gases to ultra-high vacuum (UHV) without requiring a bakeout. These advantages are particularly important for cavity-integrated ion traps, where nearby dielectric surfaces can increase motional heating and rapid design-build-test iterations benefit from eliminating bakeout cycles. We have developed a custom 4 K cryostat cooled by a ColdEdge Technologies (CET) Stinger closed-cycle $^{4}\text{He}$ flow cryogenic system to study various ion trap optical cavity structures designed to serve as a photonic interconnect between remote, compute-capable trapped $^{171}\text{Yb}^{+}$ ion quantum processors, enabling long baseline entanglement distribution $(>10\text{ km})$. We integrate an Alpine Quantum Technologies (AQT) Paul trap and Fabry-Pérot optical cavity at the 4 K stage. The cooling capacities of the cryostat 40 K and 4 K stages were measured to be 5 W at 45 K and 0.5 W at 6.1 K. Vibrations of the 4 K stage relative to the optical table are less than $12\text{ nm}_{\text{RMS}}$ in three dimensions, as measured using a Michelson interferometer. An ultra-high vacuum (UHV) is inferred by studying the rate of hydrogen-$\mathrm{Yb}^{+}$ ion collisions. Ion storage times exceeding 5 days without laser cooling have been reported and the position of the trapped ions are reproducible within $\sim10\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ following repeated thermal cycles to room temperature. The uptime of this system is 72 days and offers convenient access to the 4 K stage for in-vacuum maintenance and system modifications. Using this platform, we demonstrate spatial overlap and interaction between a trapped $^{174}\text{Yb}^{+}$ ion and the optical cavity mode on the 1345 nm transition, establishing preliminary experimental validation of the integrated cryogenic ion-cavity structure.

papers.title: A surprising bound for the $2\times2$ matrix weighted martingale multiplier
papers.abstract: For real $2\times2$ matrix weights, we prove that a scalar martingale multiplier on a dyadic root has $L^2(W)$ norm at most $CQ\sqrt{1+\log(Q)}$, where $Q$ is the dyadic matrix $A_2$ characteristic. A single multiplier, with signs alternating by generation, attains this order for every sufficiently large characteristic scale. We show that the restriction on the matrix size is essential: these estimates jump to the order $Q^{3/2}$ from the matrix size $3\times 3$ onward.

papers.title: Commutative bishuffle algebras and Pattern Avoidance
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the notion of a commutative bishuffle algebra, that linearizes classical pattern avoidance. The free commutative bishuffle algebra on one generator has a basis of permutations, divisibility of monomials is pattern containment, and the classes of permutations avoiding given patterns are the monomial bases of its quotients by monomial ideals. This free algebra is not Noetherian, but we show that its quotient by the antisymmetrizer $e_k$ is Noetherian for every $k$, and we conjecture that the same holds for its quotient by any nonzero ideal stable under the symmetric groups, in analogy with the Specht problem. We develop Gröbner bases for ideals of the free algebra and prove that the elements $e_k\oplus\tau$, with $\tau$ ranging over any set of permutations, form a Gröbner basis for the lexicographic ordering and for its opposite. This gives an algebraic form of the theorem of Backelin, West and Xin: the permutations avoiding all $k\cdots21\oplus\tau$ and those avoiding all $12\cdots k\oplus\tau$ are two monomial bases of one and the same quotient.

papers.title: Gorenstein homological algebra over comma categories
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be abelian categories with enough projective objects. In this paper, we characterize those functors $F:\mathcal{A}\to \mathcal{B}$ for which the Gorenstein projective objects in the comma category $(F\downarrow \mathcal{B})$ admit an explicit description in terms of the Gorenstein projective objects of $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$. As a main application, we obtain estimates for the global Gorenstein projective dimension of $(F\downarrow \mathcal{B})$ in terms of those of $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ and the functor $F$, and derive exact formulas in several important cases. Our categorical approach also yields dual results concerning Gorenstein injective objects and dimension. Special attention is devoted to the module category over a triangular matrix ring $ \begin{pmatrix} A & 0\\ U & B \end{pmatrix}$, the product category $\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{B}$, and the $n$-morphism category $Mor_n(\mathcal{C})$ associated with an abelian category $\mathcal{C}$ and an integer $n\geq 2$.

papers.title: Characterizing Ultrafast Processes via Work
$w_0$ Is All You Need: Field-Level Matching of General Dark Energy Models to $w_0$CDM Simulations
Principles of Material Memory
py4radiation: a framework for generating heating/cooling functions and ion fractions from custom radiation fields for astrophysical simulations
Classes de Steinitz d'extensions galoisiennes non ramifiées
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and $Cl_{K}$ its class group. Let $\Gamma$ be a finite group. We denote by $ R_{nr}(K,\Gamma)$ the subset of $Cl_{K}$ formed by the classes which are realizable as Steinitz classes of Galois extensions of $K$, unramified at the finite places of $K$ and having a Galois group isomorphic to $\Gamma$. If $\Gamma$ is abelian and the narrow class number of $K$ is prime to the order of $\Gamma$, then $R_{nr}(K,\Gamma)=\emptyset$. In the present article, for any $\Gamma$ we consider the set $R'_{nr}(K,\Gamma):=\lbrace 1 \rbrace \cup R_{nr}(K,\Gamma)$. We prove that $R'_{nr}(K, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$ is a subgroup of $Cl_{K,2}:=\lbrace c\in Cl_{K}\vert c^{2}=1\rbrace$ ; furthermore, it is equal to $Cl_{K,2}$ under a certain assumption on $K$. Using this result we show that $R'_{nr}(K,\Gamma)$ is a subgroup of $R'_{nr}(K, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$ if $\Gamma$ either has odd order, or has a noncyclic $2$-Sylow subgroup (for instance $\Gamma$ a nonabelian $2$-group, $\Gamma=S_n$ or $A_n$, with $n\geq 4$), or has a normal cyclic $2$-Sylow subgroup (for instance $\Gamma$ nilpotent having even order).

papers.title: When Simpler Beats Learned: Dual-Weighted Sampling vs. Machine Learning for the Pricing Subproblem in Graph Coloring
papers.abstract: The graph coloring problem can be solved to optimality by branch-and-price (B&P), but its performance hinges on the column generation (CG) step, where each iteration requires solving a maximum weight independent set (MWIS) pricing problem. The state-of-the-art machine-learning (ML) pricing heuristic follows a prediction-sampling paradigm: a learned model scores each vertex of a graph, and independent sets are sampled from the induced distribution. We observe, however, that the scoring procedure does not need to be learned, and critically assess the role of ML by replacing the learned scores with the dual solution of the restricted master problem, resulting in Dual-Weighted Sampling, a proposed lightweight alternative that requires no feature engineering or training. Within a unified CG and B&P framework that varies only the pricing oracle, Dual-Weighted Sampling outperforms MLPH, hand-crafted heuristics, and exact solvers on the established graph coloring benchmark in both runtime and solution quality. In particular, it remains competitive on the DIMACS random family, where MLPH was shown strongest in the original evaluation, while achieving more than a two-fold speedup in CG runtime on recursive-sparse and real-world graph families.

papers.title: From Distributional to Temporal Interactions in McKean--Vlasov Games and Control
papers.abstract: The paper examines the relation between time and population in stochastic games and control. The idea is to substitute the interaction described via the population law with the interaction described via the occupation measure of a single self-interacting trajectory. Thus we study how McKean--Vlasov fixed point games and Mean Field Control problems compare with their resulting self-interacting counterparts. Assuming appropriate dissipativity and regularity conditions, we find that the ergodic costs, value functions and optimal feedback sets are identical, and the fixed point equilibria are equivalent. In addition, we obtain uniform bounds on both trajectories and costs for finite horizon problems. These bounds allow proving asymptotic equivalence of the normalized value functions, and enable the transfer of equilibrium strategies and optimal feedbacks from one representation to another, with approximation errors that vanish as the horizon length increases.

papers.title: Selecting Stable Sampling Dynamics for Compositional Diffusion: A Feynman-Kac Weight Reduction
Hodge cycles of Klein hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We study the space of Hodge cycles on Klein varieties. Relating it to the Hodge characters in a covering Fermat variety, we decompose the space of Hodge characters into a part generated by classes of rational subvarieties, and a non-trivial part which we call exceptional. Using Dirichlet characters we show that the exceptional part is always finite. Furthermore, we give sufficient conditions under which there are no exceptional characters, providing infinitely many new cases of the Hodge conjecture for Klein varieties. Finally, we describe the set of exceptional characters of Klein varieties for small dimensions.

papers.title: The Kaplansky-Aupetit conjecture for C*-algebras
papers.abstract: We settle the Kaplansky--Aupetit conjecture when either algebra is a $C^*$-algebra. More precisely, if $A$ is a unital Banach algebra and $B$ is a unital $C^*$-algebra, or if $A$ is a unital $C^*$-algebra and $B$ is a unital semisimple Banach algebra, then every unital invertibility-preserving linear surjection $\phi: A\to B$ is a Jordan homomorphism. In fact, it suffices to assume that $\phi$ preserves the invertibility of products of two exponentials, or of individual exponentials when both algebras are $C^*$-algebras. Claude Opus 5.5 found the original proof when both $A$ and $B$ are $C^*$-algebras by adapting a resolvent estimate from a recent preprint of Colbrook and Stepaniants, while OpenAI's GPT-6.1 further generalized this to the case where only one algebra is a $C^*$-algebra.

papers.title: Blind Channel and Noise-Variance Estimation for MIMO Thermal Noise Modulation Systems via Generalized Expectation-Maximization
papers.abstract: Thermal Noise Modulation (TNM) is a communication paradigm in which information is conveyed through different thermal-noise variance levels rather than deterministic signal waveforms. Its stochastic nature makes conventional pilot-based channel estimation challenging, while pilot transmission introduces additional overhead and reduces spectral efficiency. This paper proposes a pilot-free blind receiver for M-ary TNM systems based on the Generalized Expectation-Maximization (GEM) framework. The proposed receiver jointly estimates the channel matrix, latent transmitted symbols, mixture probabilities, and unknown transmit-noise variance levels directly from received observations, without requiring pilot symbols or prior knowledge of the variance constellation. The modulation order M and receiver-noise variance are assumed to be known. Since the maximization step has no closed-form solution, a gradient-ascent procedure is incorporated into the GEM framework to iteratively update the unknown parameters. The proposed approach enables simultaneous channel estimation, symbol detection, and variance learning within a unified blind-receiver framework. Simulation results demonstrate accurate channel Gram matrix estimation and effective symbol detection without pilot overhead. Moreover, the proposed variance learning scheme achieves performance close to that obtained with perfectly known transmit variance levels, with only moderate BER degradation, demonstrating its potential for practical MIMO TNM systems.

papers.title: Monogenic signal analysis for wavefield characterisation in distributed acoustic sensing
papers.abstract: The spatio-temporal wavefield sampled by distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) contains intertwined information about signal strength, oscillatory structure and propagation. We introduce a methodology to disentangle these properties, with applications to the analysis of weak arrivals obscured by noise or stronger wave trains. The method is based on the monogenic signal, a two-dimensional extension of the analytic signal defined via the Riesz transform. In DAS, the monogenic signal decomposes locally dominant arrivals into their amplitude, phase and apparent slowness along the fibre. Moreover, the consistency of the wavefield orientation, quantified using the notion of directional coherency, allows coherent arrivals to be identified and enhanced. In this work, we apply the monogenic signal to analyse submarine T-wave recordings following the magnitude 3.5 earthquake of 5 October 2023 in the western Alboran Sea, acquired along approximately 60 km of the Estepona-Tetouan fibre-optic cable. Directional coherency allows us to enhance coherent wave trains, attenuating the incoherent background while preserving their oscillatory structure. Combining the monogenic attributes, we track individual oscillations across the fibre, obtaining spatially consistent apparent-slowness estimates. Together with varying cable geometry, these estimates allow us to infer the incoming directions of two wave trains, revealing distinct backazimuths. We extend the methodology to direction-selective enhancement, revealing a weaker third wave train with opposite moveout that is obscured by stronger arrivals. Beyond these examples, we show that monogenic analysis offers new possibilites for wavefield comparison, with promising applications to lossy data compression and inversion. Our results highlight the versatility of monogenic analysis and its potential to become a central tool for interpreting DAS recordings.

papers.title: Exact many-body scars of generic spin models from singlet covers
A compact nonformal manifold with holonomy Spin(7)
papers.abstract: We construct a compact simply connected eight-manifold with holonomy Spin(7) and a triple Massey product of degrees $(3,2,2)$ that does not contain zero. The manifold is a resolution of a flat orbifold. Joyce's gluing theorem gives it a torsion-free Spin(7) structure. The resolution map factors through a quotient of $Y\times S^1$, where $Y$ is Martín-Merchán's nonformal $G_2$ manifold. The map to this quotient has degree one, so pullback preserves a nonzero Massey pairing. On the resolution the detecting degree-two class annihilates the full indeterminacy. Simple connectivity and nonformality imply full Spin(7) holonomy. The manifold has $(b_2,b_3,b_4^+,b_4^-)=(22,10,91,27)$.

papers.title: Performance Evaluation of Nonlinear Model Predictive and Sliding Mode Controllers on a 4-Cable Spatial CSPR in Simscape
papers.abstract: This paper offers a comprehensive comparative study between Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) and Sliding Mode Control (SMC) applied to a spatial Cable-Suspended Parallel Robot (CSPR) actuated by four cables. The robot is modeled in two parallel ways: (i) via an analytical dynamic model with included cable elasticity and frictional losses, and (ii) in MATLAB Simscape Multibody, capturing realistic physical effects. Both controllers are implemented under identical reference trajectories, system constraints, and tuning strategies. Our results show that NMPC achieves superior tracking accuracy and stronger disturbance rejection compared to SMC, but at the cost of higher computational demand. Moreover, both controllers were tested on an analytical model of the robot and a Simscape model. The close agreement between the two, for both control schemes, confirms the accuracy of the analytical formulation and its consistency with the physics-based simulation. The study highlights the value of physics-based simulation as a complementary tool for validating advanced controllers under realistic conditions, and demonstrates that NMPC offers superior performance for the studied high-precision, constrained CSPR.

papers.title: Sharpe Ratio Inference after Machine Learning
papers.abstract: The economic value of return signals is often assessed using the Sharpe ratios of portfolios based on those signals. In modern asset pricing, return signals often depend on many features, including state variables and firm-specific characteristics, and machine-learning methods are increasingly used to estimate them. But how much confidence can we place in the estimated Sharpe ratios? We find that signal-estimation error can remain consequential for inference even in large asset panels. Moreover, pooling observations across assets does not necessarily make this uncertainty negligible when predictors contain common features or exhibit substantial cross-sectional dependence. As a remedy, we develop a debiased Sharpe-ratio estimator that accounts for signal-estimation error and provides valid confidence intervals and tests against benchmarks. Our target is the population Sharpe ratio of a specified portfolio rule evaluated at the true conditional expected returns given the features. The framework covers market-timing, long-short, and other signal-based portfolios, allowing the number of assets to grow with and greatly exceed the time-series sample size. The method combines orthogonal portfolio moments with time-series cross-fitting and remains valid under suitable estimation-error bounds for machine-learning forecasts. Empirically, we revisit the setting of Gu et al. (2020) using machine-learning estimators of the return signals. The strongest long-short Sharpe-ratio gains relative to market benchmarks remain significant after debiasing, providing statistical evidence of the economic value of their feature set. Conventional and debiased Sharpe-ratio estimates are generally similar, while the associated confidence intervals and tests can differ substantially. These differences vary across signal estimators and portfolio rules and do not uniformly weaken the evidence of portfolio performance.

papers.title: The probability that two random generalized derangements have the same number of cycles
papers.abstract: Using singularity analysis, we show that the probability that two independently and uniformly selected generalized derangements of size $n$ have the same number of cycles is asymptotically the same as the corresponding probability for unrestricted permutations, namely, $\sim \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\pi\log n}}\;.$

papers.title: On the linear stability of elliptic relative equilibrium in planar restricted $(n+1)$-body problem
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the restricted $(n+1)$-body problems, where the $n$ primaries forming an a homographic motion generated by the planar central configuration, and the massless particle is attracted by this $n$ primaries. We are interested in the linear stability of the elliptic relative equilibria of the massless particle under the pulsating coordinates. The main contribution of this paper first lies in the investigation of a general $(\alpha,\beta)$-system (1.7). We obtain large-range spectral instability and small-range stability results valid for arbitrary eccentricity. The restricted $(n+1)$-body problem arises as a special case of this system. Accordingly, we derive several criteria for spectral instability and linear stability for this problem. As a final application, we establish some stability results of elliptic relative equilibria for massless particle under some special central configurations.

papers.title: Giant magnetic anisotropy in layered polar metal Sr$_3$Co$_2$O$_7$ from Charge-disproportionation orbital unquenching
Two-term Rogers dilogarithm identities over cubic fields
papers.abstract: We study normalized two-term Rogers dilogarithm relations in cubic fields. For integral, nonunimodular rank-two monomial configurations whose base argument generates a totally real cubic field, finite-prime valuations force the arguments and their complements to be units. Normalization preserves the generated order and reduces the problem to two cubic families without a maximal-order assumption. In the simplest cubic family, an existing unit-equation classification yields exactly ten relations up to simultaneous reflection, with distinct coefficients 2, 3, 7, 13, 19, 31 and 97. Explicit five-term certificates prove all ten evaluations. In the second family, a sharpened lower bound for the height of a solution, together with the two-logarithm theorem of Laurent, Mignotte and Nesterenko, reduces the unit equation to a short certified computation, and the family contributes no relation in this class. A unit-index argument restricts, independently, wedge relations between arbitrary exceptional units of non-Galois totally real cubic fields: any such relation would have a coefficient with no prime factor below 23 and would contradict Ennola's conjecture on fundamental units. In cubic fields with one real embedding, the only five-term certified relation between exceptional units with coefficient greater than one is Lewin's identity. Together, these results give exactly eleven identities in the two classes considered, up to the stated reflections.

papers.title: Turing Completeness of Greedy UNO with an Ultimately Periodic Infinite Deck
authors: T. V. Kuptsov (Lomonosov Moscow State University)
G. A. Khaziev (Institute for Information Transmission Problems RAS
papers.abstract: We encode an arbitrary two-counter Minsky machine as a two-player UNO round with an ultimately periodic infinite draw pile $uw^\omega$. The construction uses a fixed $17$-card prefix and a period of length quadratic in the number of instructions. When both players follow the same fixed greedy policy, the round terminates exactly when the machine halts, and every available hand play has a unique card type. Consequently, greedy termination and victory by a designated player -- as well as winning-strategy existence under forced-play rules without tie-breaking -- are $\Sigma^0_1$-complete. Under official voluntary-draw rules with unrestricted legal choices, however, the existence of a finite play is decidable (and primitive recursive) via reachability in fixed-dimension vector addition systems with states (VASS). Finally, the maximal duration of a finite greedy play has no total computable upper bound in the input length.

papers.title: Superpotentials for F-manifolds and bi-flat F-structures on the orbit spaces of reflection groups
papers.abstract: We extend Dubrovin's construction of a superpotential from Frobenius manifolds to biflat F-manifolds. The key step in this extension is choosing a flat coordinate of one of the connections studied in [11] and invert this coordinate with respect to the spectral parameter and the construction does not require an invariant metric. Suppose that the manifold has dimension n and that the superpotential admits a holomorphic continuation to n simple critical points with distinct critical values. These values give canonical coordinates, and the residue formulas recover both the product and the flat connection from the superpotential alone. Conversely, under suitable nondegeneracy conditions, a solution of the superpotential equations for a given product defines a biflat F-manifold. For $B_n$ and $G(m,1,n)$ we obtain the whole family of biflat structures from a polynomial superpotential by varying a twisted primary differential. For $G(m,m,n)$ we obtain the natural biflat structure from a Laurent superpotential. Keeping the Laurent polynomial fixed and varying the primary differential gives a new family of flat F-manifolds depending on one parameter. We use the superpotential and the poles of the dual product along the reflecting hyperplanes to prove the conjecture we formulated in [8] for irreducible Coxeter groups and in [10] for well generated complex reflection groups. The conjecture concerns biflat F-structures whose dual connection has the form studied by Dunkl and Kohno. When the reflecting hyperplanes form a single orbit, we identify the biflat structure associated with the flat structure of [24,25,27]. We obtain the remaining families from the polynomial construction for $G(m,1,n)$ and an explicit computation for $F_4$. In every case the first flat structure extends polynomially to the whole quotient, and the biflat structure is defined on the complement of the reflection discriminant.

papers.title: Collision of a sphere and a prolate spheroid settling in a quiescent ambient
papers.abstract: The collision rate of a prolate spheroid and a sphere settling through a quiescent fluid at small Reynolds number is computed for randomly oriented spheroids and for spheroids turned broadside by weak fluid inertia. Without hydrodynamic interactions, the collision cross-section is the projection of the spheroid enlarged by the radius of the sphere. The ideal kernel then follows in closed form for aligned spheroids and from a one-dimensional quadrature for isotropic ones. Alignment raises the ideal kernel by at most a factor of 4/{\pi}, but extinguishes it on the extinction locus, where an isolated broadside spheroid settles as fast as the sphere. Hydrodynamic interactions are computed from pair trajectories in a first-reflection slender-body model, in which the interaction velocity is proportional to the difference of the buoyant weights and only the flow of the sphere rotates the spheroid. A strongly aligned spheroid weathervanes, whereas a freely rotating one feathers and glides. Weathervaning lowers the collision efficiency, as does feathering far from the extinction locus, but gliding raises it near the locus. There, the collision rate of spheroids aligned at a finite rate lies far above both the strong-alignment result and the ideal isotropic kernel. Just above the extinction locus, where strongly aligned spheroids are blocked, collisions persist at all the finite alignment rates computed. A boundary-element solution shows that the model overestimates the rate at which the gap closes near contact. A lubrication film largely corrects this and reduces the collision efficiencies from their interception values. Simple fits for the ideal kernels, the efficiencies and the near-contact correction are provided for use in collision models.

papers.title: Topological analysis of permeability tensor in anisotropic porous media
papers.abstract: The permeability of an anisotropic porous medium is a tensor whose off-diagonal components, which describe the deflection of the macroscopic flux away from the driving force, are small and change sign under reflections. We ask whether direction-aware topological data analysis can predict the full permeability tensor of three-dimensional porous media directly from their geometry. We introduce two direction-aware topological descriptors for flow problems: a cone-based filtration, adapted from our earlier work on the elastic stiffness tensor, and a throat-scale filtration built on the distance transform of the pore space. Using permeability tensors computed with the lattice Boltzmann method, we compare them with a comprehensive set of non-topological baselines, comprising statistical microstructure descriptors and physics-based permeability estimators. The topological descriptors are most informative for the off-diagonal components, which the baselines capture least well. There the throat-scale filtration alone outperforms every non-topological descriptor set, including the union of all statistical descriptors and physics-based estimators, and adding it to the baselines consistently improves the prediction. We also confirm the approach on real rock data.

papers.title: Rethinking Discovery Research with AI: The promise of transdisciplinarity and the danger of reductionism
papers.abstract: In theory, transdisciplinary research focuses on solving real-world problems without being constrained by disciplinary boundaries and methodologies. In practice, doing so is challenging, as recognized by the phrase "The world has problems; universities have departments." As a powerful integrative tool, AI may help overcome traditional reductionist approaches and enable genuine transdisciplinarity. In this essay, we discuss how this could happen and why, within the current system of incentives, it is not happening.

papers.title: Counting Eulerian Orientations in Regular Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a pseudograph, and let $\varepsilon(G)$ denote the number of Eulerian orientations of $G$. Lieb and Wu, and later Schrijver, showed that if $G$ has degree sequence $(d_1,d_2,\dots,d_n)$, where each $d_i$ is a positive even integer, then \[ \varepsilon(G) \geq \prod_{i = 1}^n 2^{-d_i/2} \binom{d_i}{d_i/2}.\] Schrijver conjectured that for simple $d$-regular graphs, $\varepsilon(G)\leq\varepsilon(K_{d+1})^{n/(d+1)}$, with equality attained by disjoint unions of cliques of order $d+1$. In this paper, we prove a multigraph bound that implies the known case $d=4$, and we also improve Schrijver's lower bound for $d$-regular graphs, using an inductive relation between $\varepsilon(G)$ and the number $\ell_i(G)$ of cycles of each possible length $i \geq 1$ in $G$. We define \[ \ell(G) = \sum_{i = 1}^n \frac{\ell_i(G)}{(d - 1)^i}\] and we prove with $\lambda = (d - 1)\log(1 + 1/(d - 1))$ that for all $d \geq 2$, \[ \varepsilon(G) \geq \exp(\lambda \ell(G)) \cdot S_d(n),\] where $S_d(n)$ denotes $2^{-dn/2}\binom{d}{d/2}^n$. The bound sharply improves the lower bound of Lieb, Wu and Schrijver, and gives good estimates for $\varepsilon(G)$ for various graphs, such as integer lattices. The bound is almost tight for random regular graphs, and we conjecture for each even $d \geq 4$ that there exists a constant $c_d > 0$ such that $\varepsilon(G) \leq \exp(c_d\lambda \ell(G)) \cdot S_d(n)$ for every $n$-vertex $d$-regular pseudograph.

papers.title: Continuous-Time LQR from a Single Discrete-Time Off-Policy Batch
papers.abstract: We study discounted continuous-time linear--quadratic regulation (LQR) with unknown drift parameters and additive noise, using a single batch of discrete-time off-policy transitions. Discrete-time methods target a policy tied to the training interval, while shortening this interval can make learning from finite data more sensitive to noise. Learning an accurate continuous-time controller therefore requires balancing discretization and finite-sample errors while preserving stability throughout policy improvement. We develop a drift-only policy iteration algorithm, termed PhiBE-PI, using one quadratic state--action critic for policy evaluation and explicit greedy improvement. Reusing the batch makes later policies depend on the data. Exploiting the quadratic structure of LQR, we show that the data enter every policy evaluation only through one policy-independent empirical matrix, so a single high-probability bound controls all iterates. For sufficiently large discount~$\beta$, small observation intervals, and a sufficiently large batch, we prove that all iterates are stabilizing for the discounted problem and converge quadratically to a data-dependent fixed point. The gain bound separates iteration, finite-sample, and discretization errors. In this regime, the finite-sample and discretization terms scale as $1/(\beta\sqrt{n\Delta t})$ and $\Delta t/\beta$, respectively. The bounds thus reveal a tradeoff: at a fixed batch size, finer observations reduce discretization error but increase finite-sample error. Because PhiBE-PI approximates the continuous-time optimal gain rather than a discrete-time one, its policy can remain near-optimal when deployed at faster control rates. Experiments confirm this advantage over discrete-time Bellman-equation baselines when the observation interval is small relative to the system's time scale.

papers.title: Interface currents of magnetized differential systems: quantization and bulk-interface correspondence
papers.abstract: This paper concerns transport along an interface between two insulators modeled by self-adjoint differential systems $H$ of arbitrary order, coupled to a magnetic field either by Peierls substitution or, for operators of the form $L^*L+W$, in the factor $L$. Each bulk carries a constant field, which may vanish. The principal symbol of $H$ is either elliptic or has a kernel of constant rank, in which case finitely many bands remain bounded at large momentum, as in rotating shallow water, cold plasmas, Maxwell's equations and pseudospin-one materials. Ellipticity is then replaced by a Douglis-Nirenberg structure and by a gap condition on an effective flat symbol. We show that, for every energy $\alpha$ away from the flat-band set and in a spectral gap of both bulks, the interface current $\sigma_I=\mathrm{Tr}\,i[H,P]\varphi'(H)$ is well defined, with $2\pi\sigma_I$ a Fredholm index, and that it is given, for all walls in the elliptic case and under a freezing condition otherwise, by a bulk-interface correspondence of the form $2\pi\sigma_I=J(a_+,B_+;\alpha)-J(a_-,B_-;\alpha)+\mathsf{C}$. For a nonzero bulk field, $J=2\pi\sigma_H$ is the Kubo-Chern Hall conductivity, which we compute by an extension-corrected count of generalized Landau levels. For a vanishing field, $J$ is the Chern integral of the field-free symbol, which is also, under a weak-field condition, the weak-field limit of the Hall conductivity. The term $\mathsf{C}$ is a Chern integral of the occupied projector at infinite momentum across the wall. The current is stable under large perturbations, and boundaries of the applied field inside a homogeneous material carry quantized currents that change at field-induced transitions. Near flat-band energies, where generalized Landau levels may accumulate, the current may diverge.

papers.title: Unary maps are restrictions of linear maps and $k$-ary maps are restrictions of homogeneous maps
papers.abstract: We study maps on a finite set $S$ under renaming elements of $S$ and extending $S$. We show that every unary map is linear and every $k$-ary map is homogeneous with respect to such renamings and embeddings.

papers.title: Lie Algebra Cohomology and Seiberg-Witten Theory
papers.abstract: We compute the algebra of perturbative holomorphic-topological local operators of pure $\mathcal N=2$ gauge theory with gauge group $SU(2)$, proving a conjecture of the author: it is the Poisson vertex algebra generated by a Virasoro element $X$ of central charge zero and an odd primary $Y$ of weight three, subject only to $X^2=0$. Equivalently, we compute the relative Lie algebra cohomology $H^*(\mathfrak{sl}_2[z,w]/(w^2),\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and the self-Ext groups of the unit in the coherent Satake category for $SL_2$ and $PGL_2$. The proof uses factorization on configuration spaces of points on the affine line, a depth argument, and two deformations of the coefficient algebra $\mathbb C[z,w]/(w^2)$.

papers.title: Accurate rank-controlled step-truncation methods for matrix differential equations
papers.abstract: A class of explicit time stepping schemes is introduced for the integration of matrix differential equations in low-rank format. These schemes combine explicit Runge-Kutta time stepping with rank-adaptive recompressions. For suitably chosen truncation thresholds, they converge at arbitrary order, while having close to optimal ranks, without any prior assumptions on the best approximation ranks. The ranks of the scheme also necessarily depend on the time step, as shown by counterexamples. A numerical experiment illustrates the advantages and performance of the proposed scheme.

papers.title: Leray's Problem for the Stationary Navier-Stokes Equations with Low-Regularity Data in Planar and Three-Dimensional Axisymmetric Lipschitz Domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the steady Navier-Stokes Dirichlet problem in bounded planar and three-dimensional axisymmetric domains with finitely many disjoint Lipschitz boundary components. For prescribed velocities in $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ and forces in the dual of the solenoidal energy space $V=H_0^1(\operatorname{div}0,\Omega)$, we establish finite-energy solvability under the sole compatibility condition of zero total boundary flux. Individual component fluxes are subject to no smallness or sign restrictions. In three dimensions the domain and data are axisymmetric, and swirl is allowed. The result addresses the regularity of the domain and data within these two geometric classes. The proof combines Leray-Schauder continuation with pressure compactness on Lipschitz boundary collars and a total-head level-set argument. Continuation of the limiting Euler fields through complementary components supplies separating cycles, while viscous identities are evaluated inside the physical domain. A nonlinear correction of smooth force approximations controls the volume and surface errors in the passage to energy-dual data. An isometric extension from $V'$ to $H^{-1}$ preserves the prescribed symmetries and fixes the force representative used in the compactness argument. For each selected $H^{-1}$ representative, the resulting velocity admits an associated mean-zero $L^2$ pressure; the velocity equation depends only on the force class modulo gradients.

papers.title: Multiphase Gas in the Ram-Pressure-Stripped Elliptical Galaxy NGC 1404
Around the base ideal and the base locus of a Keller map
papers.abstract: Let $\varphi_F:\Bbbk^n\to\Bbbk^n$ be a Keller map defined by $n$ polynomials $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ in $n$ indeterminates $X=X_1,\ldots,X_n$ over a field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic zero. Miranda-Neto defined the base ideal of $\varphi_F$ as the ideal $I_F$ generated by $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ and the base locus of $\varphi_F$ as the affine algebraic set $V_F=V(I_F)$ determined by the ideal $I_F$. He proved that $I_F$ is a radical ideal, which is a finite intersection of $v_F$ maximal ideals, where ${\rm card}(V_F)\leq v_F$, understanding that $v_F=0$, when $I_F$ is improper. In this paper, we first prove that $v_F\leq \dim_{\Bbbk}(\Bbbk[X]/I_F)\leq [\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$. Using invertible affine transformations on the recent counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture announced by Alpöge, we show that $I_F$ might indeed be improper and that the following cases, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F=[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ and $0={\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ might occur. We finish by giving a purely topological equivalent reformulation of the Jacobian Conjecture in terms of the irreducibility of $V_F$.

papers.title: A high-dimensional perspective of assortative mating: definition, dynamics, and limiting results
papers.abstract: Assortative mating, or the systematic (dis)similarity of traits between mate pairs, has wide-ranging consequences. Chiefly, it modulates genetic variance in offspring due to the coupling of inherited trait-associated loci in parents. Over many generations, this buildup becomes appreciable at the trait level and may confound statistical genetics techniques, such as association analyses and heritability estimation. Theoretical characterisations of this effect are well-developed in the univariate case, where mates assort on a single trait pair. However, empirical studies increasingly show that assortment is not only multivariate, but high-dimensional, in that the correlation structure exhibited between mates cannot be represented by a single or few linear combinations of the constituent traits. In spite of this, the mathematical theory of assortment has not scaled with awareness of this fact. In this paper such a generalisation is developed. We begin by deriving sufficient conditions under which an estimator is invariant to assortment, followed by studying existence conditions and limiting behaviour of equilibria under assortment. Finally, univariate results involving trait heritability and consanguineal genetic correlation are generalised to the multivariate regime.

papers.title: Unresolved binaries from Gaia XP to SPHEREx
Two-loop correction to the complex-bion amplitude in a quasi-exactly solvable sextic oscillator
papers.abstract: In this study, a quasi-exactly solvable sextic potential is analyzed by two diagrammatic calculations. At positive coupling, factorization fixes the ground-state energy $E_0$ exactly and forces every perturbative coefficient to vanish.
