Yet people routinely move across space, creating opportunities for encounters that extend beyond geographical proximity. How these opportunities relate to inter-firm transaction relationships remains poorly understood. Here, we combine large-scale mobile phone mobility data with a multi-year panel of transactions among 196,317 firms in Tokyo to quantify encounter opportunities between workers and examine their association with inter-firm transaction ties. We find that pairs of areas with greater opportunities for encounters one another are more likely to have transaction links and new link formation between previously unconnected firms. This association is particularly pronounced in information- and service-intensive industries, reflecting the importance of encounter opportunities for exchange involving intangible knowledge and service. Indirect connections through shared neighbors in the encounter network are also positively associated with subsequent transaction formation across industries, but not within industries. These findings suggest that urban policies shaping connectivity formed through human mobility could play a significant role in the development and resilience of economic networks.

papers.title: A Hyper-Reduced Reduced Order Model Built From Streaming Tensor Train Data
papers.abstract: Low-rank PDE solvers based on tensor-decompositions inside physical space leverages low-rank structures across different physical dimensions, while projection-based reduced order models (ROMs) for parametric PDEs exploit low-rank structures across parameter spaces. Recently, to use the complimentary strength of these two methods, a ROM framework is proposed by incrementally constructing compressed reduced bases directly from streaming tensor-train (TT) snapshots provided by low-rank solvers, but it omits hyper reduction and consequently incur substantial online costs for nonlinear or non-affine parametric PDEs. To address this issue, we develop a hyper-reduced TT ROM for streaming TT data by combining incremental low-rank TT compression and nested TT discrete empirical interpolation (TT-DEIM). Numerical experiments on nonlinear and non-affine parametric PDEs achieve mean relative errors, matching the accuracy of non-hyper-reduced TT-Galerkin ROMs while achieving mean online speedups of approximately 8 times to 1500 times compared to them.

papers.title: Ziv Meets Sumcheck: Zero-Knowledge Proofs of Floating-Point LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Zero-knowledge proofs can show that a neural network produced a given output without revealing the network, but current systems for language models prove integer approximations of the model rather than the floating-point arithmetic that is actually deployed. Proving floating-point matrix multiplication has been regarded as hard, because rounding after every addition makes the result depend on the order of the additions. We avoid this obstacle by proving the correctly rounded product, in which every dot product is computed exactly and rounded once. This result is independent of the hardware and at least as accurate as standard kernels. We give an interactive proof for this relation whose cost is close to that of integer matrix multiplication, with roughly a thousand times fewer committed values than per-operation floating-point circuits need constraints, extend it to every layer of a transformer, and give a privacy construction for the complete argument whose zero knowledge we prove under explicit hypotheses. We implement the system and prove the full forward pass of GPT-2 small, including all twelve blocks and the output over the whole vocabulary, in 19 minutes on two processor cores; verification takes 21 seconds. The verifier rejects all 236 attacks we tested, and the model's outputs agree with high-precision inference at least as closely as standard 16-bit inference does.

papers.title: CLFF: Automated Framework for Concurrent Learning Force Fields and Material Property Calculations
The broken-sample problem revisited II: Detecting hidden linear dependencies
papers.abstract: We study the detection problem for shuffled linear regression, in which the covariates and the responses are either independent or linearly related through a latent correspondence. Consider independent standard Gaussian covariates \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\mathbb R^d\) and scalar responses \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\). In a shuffled linear model, \(Y_i=\langle X_{\pi_*(i)},\beta_*\rangle+\sigma Z_i\), where both the permutation \(\pi_*\) and the regression coefficient $\beta_*$ are latent and $Z_i$'s are white Gaussian noise. The goal is to distinguish this model from one in which the covariates and responses are independent with the same marginal distribution. In the low-dimensional regime of $d \ll \frac{\log n}{\log\log n}$, we show that the detection threshold is given by $\sigma=o(1)$ for fixed $d$ and $\sigma^2 = \Theta(\frac{1}{d\log d})$ for growing $d$; both thresholds are achieved in nearly linear time using moment-based test statistics inspired by matched filters in signal processing. For higher dimensions, tests based on sliced Wasserstein distance succeed when $\sigma^2 = o(\frac{1}{(d\log d)^2})$, while the optimal threshold remains open. As a by-product, we show that the shuffled linear model exhibits an ``all-or-nothing'' phase transition for estimating $\beta_*$ at $\sigma^2\asymp \frac{1}{d\log d}$ in low dimensions. In particular, $\beta_*$ can be consistently estimated in nearly linear time, even when it is information-theoretically impossible to recover any positive fraction of the latent matching $\pi^*$.

papers.title: Area Stability for Largest Small Polygons
papers.abstract: We develop a second order calculus for area maximisation among small polygons of diameter at most one, culminating in rigorous computational proofs of stationarity, spectral stability and strict local maximality modulo orientation preserving Euclidean motions for the polygons $Q_n$, whose diameter graphs consist of a cycle on $n-1$ vertices and one pendant edge, for every even $n$ with $6\le n\le 64$. At a stationary configuration, positive multipliers force first order area decrease along feasible directions that shorten at least one active diameter. Along directions that preserve all active diameters to first order, the reduced Hessian governs second order area change modulo Euclidean motions. Positive multipliers, independent active constraint gradients, and a negative reduced spectrum imply strict local maximality. Outward rounded interval arithmetic establishes existence of strictly convex stationary configurations $Q_n$ with all $n-3$ reduced eigenvalues strictly negative. Together, these results yield explicit neighbourhood radii and rigorous quadratic area decrease bounds for all sufficiently nearby feasible polygons. The reduced spectrum also detects second order degeneracy and instability, as illustrated by an optimal quadrilateral and the regular hexagon.

papers.title: Sound of Keplerian binaries in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background
A logic of strong contingency
papers.abstract: In this paper, inspired by the notions of contingency and strong possibility, we propose a notion which may be called 'strong contingency'. This notion can be seen as a mixture of contingency and strong possibility. We investigate the logic with strong contingency as a sole primitive modality, including its bisimulation notion, expressivity, frame definability, and axiomatizations. It turns out that this logic is expressively incomparable with the standard modal logic and the logic of contingency even over the class of S5-models, and less expressive than the logic of strong possibility and weak necessity over the class of S5-models. Besides, as the introduction of the inequality into the semantics makes the completeness proof much harder, instead of showing the completeness via a canonical model construction, we reduce the soundness and strong completeness of the involved proof systems to those of the existing proof systems in the literature.

papers.title: Identifying Distant and Highly Reddened Star Clusters: 486 Open Clusters and Candidates in the Dusty Galactic Disk
Extensive-Rank Matrix Denoising Under i.i.d. Non-Gaussian Noise
Rateless Lattice Codes over Fading Wiretap Channels: Finite-Length Secrecy and the Secret-Key Capacity of Degraded Sessions
papers.abstract: In rateless transmission the transmitter keeps sending until the legitimate receiver (Bob) can decode. Over a wiretap channel this has a useful side effect: the eavesdropper (Eve) sees only as many symbols as Bob needs, although the transmitter knows neither channel. We study the secrecy of rateless lattice codes in this setting. First, using a public dither and privacy amplification, we prove a finite-length secrecy bound, in total variation distance, for every channel realization, even if Eve knows all codes and seeds and combines all packets. Second, stopping when Bob acknowledges successful decoding, as in hybrid ARQ, costs at most the logarithm of the number of possible feedback outcomes in secret bits. Third, for degraded sessions with state-based stopping and without a pre-shared key or other public discussion, the secret-key rate of a session cannot exceed its accumulated Gaussian secrecy capacity, and adaptive key generation with shaped rateless lattice codes comes within any $\epsilon>0$ of this limit when Eve's channel states are revealed after the session. If only their statistics are known, choosing the key length after the session guarantees a prescribed secrecy-outage probability. Finally, over block Rayleigh fading with a CRC-based acknowledgement and joint belief-propagation decoding, and with Eve $20$~dB weaker on average, the scheme reaches $59$--$69\%$ of the outage-weighted throughput of an ideal infinite-length secure hybrid-ARQ benchmark for Bob SNRs of $8$--$20$~dB.

papers.title: Cramer-Rao Bound Minimization for Discrete SIM-aided ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIM) have recently emerged as a promising wave-domain signal processing architecture for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), owing to the capability of efficient beamforming with reduced number of radio-frequency chains. However, most existing SIM-aided ISAC designs rely on maximizing beampattern gain under continuous phase shifts, which cannot explicitly characterize the fundamental estimation accuracy under practical deployment. In this paper, we investigate Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) minimization problem for a discrete SIM-aided ISAC system. To tackle the resulting non-convex problem, we develop a two-stage transmit design that decouples CRB optimization from cascaded multi-layer SIM realization. In the first stage, an ideal precoder is obtained. In the second stage, it is synthesized on the practical SIM by alternating power allocation and phase-shift updates, with a closed-form discrete projection and linearized QoS constraints. Numerical results demonstrate fast convergence, reveal the sensing-communication trade-off, and verify CRB improvements with higher phase resolution and larger SIM configurations.

papers.title: Is every knot a three-way deadlock? Counterexamples and a universality conjecture for the segment number
papers.abstract: The segment number $s(K)$ of a knot $K$ is the minimal number of arcs into which a diagram of $K$ can be cut so that, for every pair of arcs, one of them passes over the other at all of their common crossings. Every non-trivial knot satisfies $s(K)\ge 3$. In the paper introducing this invariant it was conjectured that the bridge number satisfies $b(K)\le s(K)$, and the torus knot $5_1$ was proposed as a candidate for a knot with $s(K)=4$. We show that both expectations fail: the torus knots $T(2,q)$ with $q=3,5,7,9$ have segment number three, and there is a knot $K$ with $s(K)=3$ and $b(K)\ge 4$, detected by its $3^4$ Fox $3$-colourings. We also give a knot with $s(K)=3$, signature $-6$ and $\tau=-3$, so four-dimensional invariants do not bound the segment number from below either; since $g_4(9_1)=4$, even the inequality $g_4(K)\le s(K)$ fails. Both connected sums of two trefoils, the square knot and the granny knot, also have segment number three, although a $3$-segment presentation can never be visibly composite. These results lead us to conjecture that every non-trivial knot has segment number three. We show that this is a statement about plane curves cut into three simple arcs, give a normal form in which one of the arcs is a straight segment, and report a computer census of $3$-segment presentations of prime knots, which covers all prime knots with at most eight crossings except $8_{15}$ and $8_{19}$. We also prove that every $3$-segment presentation of $K$ has at least $3u(K)$ crossings and that a minimal one has at most six bigons. All presentations are certified by exact arithmetic or combinatorial checks.

papers.title: An informational interpretation of the reverse nonequilibrium molecular dynamics
Simulation and Rejection of Radon Progeny Backgrounds in nEXO
papers.abstract: Radon-induced backgrounds from $^{214}$Bi decays remain a significant challenge for liquid xenon (LXe) detectors searching for neutrinoless double beta decay ($0\nu\beta\beta$). We present a simulation-based study of the $^{214}$Bi background in nEXO, incorporating a physically motivated model of the transport and implantation of radon progeny into the detector cathode. We show that the spatial distribution of scintillation light provides an additional method for background discrimination for events surviving standard energy, event topology, and fiducial volume selections. A simple discriminator based on the scintillation light detected below the cathode rejects 41% of the remaining $^{214}$Bi backgrounds while retaining 95% of $0\nu\beta\beta$ signal events, and a convolutional neural network classifier improves this rejection to 57% at the same signal efficiency. An updated optical model provides a more accurate estimate of the light collection efficiency below the cathode than used in previous work, increasing the expected $^{214}$Bi-$^{214}$Po (Bi-Po) coincidence-tagging efficiency for bottom-surface $^{214}$Bi decays from less than 1% to approximately 50%. Together, these results demonstrate improved rejection of cathode-implanted $^{214}$Bi backgrounds in nEXO through complementary prompt scintillation-based discrimination and delayed coincidence tagging.

papers.title: Product Enrichment of Spline Spaces for IGA: Polynomial Reproduction, Approximation, and Stable Computation
papers.abstract: We study product enrichment of spline spaces under a fixed isoparametric geometry map for isogeometric analysis (IGA). For each fixed integer $\ell\ge1$, a locally $L^\infty$-stable initial operator reproducing $\mathbb P_k$ yields an explicit linear map from $L^2(D)$ into $W_h^\ell$ that reproduces $\mathbb P_{\ell k}$ and is locally stable in $L^2$ and $L^\infty$, uniformly in the mesh scale. Under additional initial-space regularity and derivative stability, the construction gives integer-order Sobolev error estimates of order $h^{s-m}$ for $1\le s\le\ell k+1$ and admissible $m$. Independently, the geometry representation implies reproduction of physical polynomials of degree at most $\ell$ by the enriched space. Polynomial containment also yields algebraic and analytic best-approximation estimates as the product order increases. For every fixed product order, we give a compatible redundant Galerkin formulation and an explicit initial-space injection. A local spectral construction and an initial-space correction give a two-level energy condition-number bound without requiring independent product generators. These solver results concern exact arithmetic; coarse-space cost, quadrature consistency, boundary constraints, and numerical rank truncation require separate control.

papers.title: Rateless Lattices: Constructions, Coding Theorems, and Capacity
papers.abstract: A rateless code sends a fixed message as an unbounded stream of symbols such that every prefix is a codeword. We introduce rateless lattices, sequences of integral lattices of increasing dimension in which each lattice projects onto the first coordinates of the next while the induced finite codebooks retain constant size. Our first contribution is a family obtained from Construction D' with two nested Raptor codes. We derive generator matrices, volume, and an encoder. For every noise or fading sequence unknown to the transmitter and independent of the code randomness, we prove an ensemble random-coding bound for multistage decoding. These results quantify the loss created by a fixed split of information between two levels, and the bound remains valid for sparse LT stages of logarithmic degree. They concern recovery of the message, or finite-codeword residue; lattice-point recovery with a fixed alphabet incurs an additional coarse-lattice error term. We then show that the split loss is caused by stage-by-stage decoding. For a dense ensemble with ring coefficients, we characterize the rateless capacity region under joint decoding. With equal level sizes, the ensemble achieves the accumulated capacity of uniform pulse-amplitude modulation for two levels and for additional levels. Single-level $p$-ary rateless lattices achieve the same performance, satisfy a finite-parameter rateless Poltyrev inequality, and, with geometric shaping, approach within any $\epsilon>0$ of the Gaussian incremental-redundancy capacity for bounded SNR. Repetition of a fixed-dimension lattice codeword instead incurs a loss that grows unboundedly with retransmissions. We also analyze a joint belief-propagation decoder over $\mathbb Z_4$ using density evolution on a tree-like surrogate ensemble. Simulations on AWGN and block-fading channels show that joint decoding removes most of the multistage-decoding loss.

papers.title: Improved Lower Bound on the Hadwiger-Debrunner Numbers
papers.abstract: The celebrated $(p,q)$-theorem of Alon and Kleitman asserts that for any $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and any $p \geq q \geq d+1$, every family of convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ in which among any $p$ sets, some $q$ intersect, can be pierced by $c(p,q,d)$ points. The minimum numbers $c(p,q,d)$ are called the Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers and denoted $\mathrm{HD}_d(p,q)$ and determining them is a longstanding open problem. We prove that for any $d \geq 2$, $\mathrm{HD}_d(p,d+1) \geq p^{d-o(1)}$, and more generally, $\mathrm{HD}_d(p,q) \geq p^{\frac{q-1}{q-d}-o(1)}$. Our bound is obtained by a family of parallelotopes, and is tight up to polylogarithmic factors among all families that have a bounded VC dimension. The proof uses the hypergraph container method.

papers.title: Split Hamiltonian structure for Vlasov--Maxwell equations and cylindrical pinch equilibria
papers.abstract: We study the linearized Vlasov--Maxwell equations for cylindrical pinch equilibria, including the classical Bennett pinch, Gaussian equilibria from our earlier work, and a rigidly rotating $\theta$-pinch. Conservation of particle momentum along a symmetry brings the energy principle of Lin and Strauss into these geometries. We work on a graph space for the symmetry component of the vector potential. For the Bennett $z$-pinch the bare potential form has one negative direction, but the particle-number constraint removes it and the entire $z$-independent spectrum lies on the imaginary axis. For a $z$-pinch with variable axial drift, every $z$-independent growing mode is radial. We prove axisymmetric spectral stability for a Gaussian $\theta$-pinch in an explicit range of axis slopes and for a center-peaked, rigidly rotating $\theta$-pinch. In a screw-pinch the helical twist couples the magnetic flux to the particle and electric constraints. The radial equations still separate, and all sufficiently high helical harmonics have imaginary spectrum. For two Gaussian screw-pinch equilibria we verify spectral stability in the full helical symmetry class.

papers.title: Rough structure. I. Exclusion among series-parallel graphs
papers.abstract: This is the first in a series of papers about rough structure theorems: graph properties that are implied by the exclusion of some graph as a minor, and imply the exclusion of some larger graph of the same type. Here we look at the structure of the series-parallel graphs that do not contain a given series-parallel graph as a minor. We prove that for every series-parallel graph $H$, there exists $m$ such that every simple two-connected series-parallel graph that does not contain $H$ as a minor admits a tree-decomposition of height at most $m$, where each "torso" is either an outerplanar graph or a planar dual of one. We prove similar theorems about the series-parallel graphs that exclude an outerplanar graph, the series-parallel graphs that exclude a dual of an outerplanar graph, the graphs of tree-width three that exclude a series-parallel graph, and the general graphs that exclude a fan.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the $k$-harmonic conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct nonminimal $k$-harmonic hypersurfaces in $\R^{n+1}$ for every $k\geq3$ and $n\geq3$, giving counterexamples to the $k$-harmonic conjecture. Each example has exact order $k$ and is an incomplete circular cone or a Euclidean product of such a cone. We also classify the $k$-harmonic circular cones, determine the possible dimensions of nonminimal cones with closed links, and give constructions in higher codimension.

papers.title: Principal Eigenvalues for Transport-Nonlocal Operators on Compact Manifolds: Ergodic Averages and Quotient Reduction
papers.abstract: We study principal eigenvalues for transport--nonlocal operators on connected compact Riemannian manifolds. Transport changes the natural spectral threshold from the pointwise maximum of the potential to a maximal invariant average. We establish a necessary and sufficient criterion based on a resolvent spectral radius and derive sufficient existence conditions for uniquely ergodic flows and, through quotient reduction, for flows arising from compact abelian Lie group actions. Examples on the two-dimensional torus show that, for weak nonlocal coupling, transport can create or suppress principal eigenvalues, while sphere rotations illustrate how the quotient criterion accommodates singular orbits.

papers.title: Implementation and Software-in-the-Loop Evaluation of a Trans-Domain Digital Twin Architecture for Autonomous Guidance of the Phoenix VTOL UAV Without Online GNSS
papers.abstract: Autonomous UAV guidance in emergency response, infrastructure monitoring, and cargo transportation requires reliable navigation. However, satellite-based positioning may become unavailable or unreliable in enclosed spaces, blind spots caused by natural obstacles and structures, and environments affected by radio interference and signal spoofing during electronic warfare. This study designs, implements, and evaluates a system based on a Trans-Domain Digital Twin (TDDT) for autonomous guidance of the Phoenix VTOL UAV. Independent navigation, flight dynamics, and meteorological models are coordinated within a cycle of state estimation, prediction, decision-making, command execution, and feedback. Data from inertial, magnetic, pressure, and airspeed sensors, together with environmental information, form the basis for estimation and prediction. Furthermore, a shared state, temporal synchronization, preservation of information provenance, and command traceability establish continuity between models and decisions. The system was tested with a simulated physical twin in a software-in-the-loop environment. Vertical takeoff, movement toward the destination, landing, and autonomous stopping were recorded, and the dynamic model was adjusted to a limited extent based on sensor-derived feedback. Separating the evaluation reference from navigation inputs enabled independent assessment of positioning error and computational performance. The results confirm operational coordination, decision traceability, and closed-loop guidance under the tested conditions, providing a reproducible platform for the development and evaluation of navigation without satellite-based positioning.

papers.title: Infinitely many spectral gaps for Anderson--Bernoulli operators with sparse periodic backgrounds
papers.abstract: We consider discrete Anderson--Bernoulli operators with a periodic background. At a single coupling, every minimal period of at least three admits a background with at most four nonzero sites per period whose almost sure spectrum has infinitely many gaps. We give two constructions. The first uses at most seven nonzero sites per period and fixes the accumulation point at zero. For periods of at least five, the second uses exactly four nonzero sites per period and takes the lowest Dirichlet eigenvalue of the inserted chain as the accumulation point. In both constructions the gaps approach from the right. The widths of the selected gaps and their distances to the accumulation point are comparable to a common geometric factor divided by the period in the first family and by its cube in the second. Spectral intervals of comparable length separate successive gaps in each selected sequence.

papers.title: Local and Global Bifurcation for Axisymmetric Stationary Relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell Equilibria
papers.abstract: We study bifurcation of stationary two-species relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell equilibria on bounded axisymmetric domains. Velocity-moment and elliptic spectral bounds give computable tests for simple crossings, their number and separation, while the local theorem gives a branch-direction formula. Explicit two-species families exhibit electric-only, magnetic-only, and joint field-norm escape.

papers.title: Taming Fitch's and Humberstone's Paradoxes
papers.abstract: Fitch's Paradox says that if every true proposition is knowable, then every true proposition is known. Humberstone's Paradox states that if every true proposition is known by at least one of a set of finitely many agents, then some agent in that set knows every true proposition. Both paradoxes give rise to surprising and unacceptable consequences. In this paper, we diagnose a crucial tacit presupposition underlying these paradoxes, namely that the domain of propositions is closed under Boolean operations such as intersection and union, and offer a uniform resolution. We argue that the paradoxical inferences rely implicitly on this closure assumption. By adopting weak propositionally quantified modal logics that drop these closure conditions, we provide a semantically motivated account that blocks both paradoxes. The restriction on universal instantiation is not an ad hoc technical device, but reflects a conception of propositions as graspable objects of epistemic attitudes, on which the domain of propositions need not be closed under Boolean operations, since some Boolean combinations of graspable propositions may not themselves be graspable.

papers.title: OpenGLSA: A high-order matrix-free solver for global linear stability analysis of compressible flows on structured grids
papers.abstract: We present OpenGLSA, an open-source code for the global linear stability analysis of compressible flows. It is based on a high-order finite-difference method on structured curvilinear grids and parallelised via the Message Passing Interface (MPI). The code supports linear stability analysis around planar and axisymmetric two-dimensional base flows with three-dimensional perturbations represented by Fourier mode expansions (BiGlobal), and on fully three-dimensional base flows (TriGlobal). Curvilinear coordinate grids are employed to facilitate flow analysis around complex geometries. Base flow computations employ the Selective Frequency Damping (SFD) method combined with weighted essentially non-oscillatory (WENO) reconstruction for shock capturing. A linearise-then-discretise approach is adopted for the linearised equations, and eigenmodes are computed using matrix-free time stepping coupled with the implicitly restarted Arnoldi method. This strategy significantly reduces memory requirements, thereby enhancing both the efficiency and tractability of memory-intensive compressible flow analyses. The solvers are validated against published results for low-Mach-number flows past a circular cylinder and a sphere, hypersonic flow over a compression ramp, and square and cubic lid-driven cavity flows.

papers.title: Structure-Preserving Analysis of a Nonlinear Reaction--Diffusion Model for Homogeneous Redox Catalysis
papers.abstract: We study a reduced nonlinear reaction--diffusion model for homogeneous redox catalysis under a low-scan-rate, frozen-potential approximation motivated by cyclic voltammetry. The reduced system contains two concentration fields coupled through the same nonlinear reaction term and therefore satisfies, exactly within the reduced model, \[ (a-q)_\tau=(a-q)_{yy}. \] This identity yields an exact reconstruction of the substrate concentration from the electroactive concentration and provides the organizing principle for the structure-preserving approximations developed below. Formulation I applies the homotopy perturbation method (HPM) to the catalyst field using a constant-coefficient Green-function hierarchy and reconstructs the substrate field from the exact heat equation. Formulation II linearizes the nonlinear reaction about a space- and time-dependent reference profile while preserving the same difference structure and the physical far-field state. The methods are evaluated using fourth-order method-of-lines discretizations, direct Green/heat-kernel formulas for the electrode current, and an independently refined nonlinear PDE benchmark. For the baseline problem, the published substrate approximation has maximum error \(1.69\times10^{-1}\), whereas the \(N=3\) errors are reduced to \(2.09\times10^{-5}\) for Formulation I and \(3.61\times10^{-6}\) for Formulation II. At \(N=1\), Formulation II improves the errors in the catalyst, substrate, and current by factors of approximately \(18.2\), \(46.9\), and \(42.1\), respectively, relative to Formulation I. The results show that preserving the exact coupled structure substantially improves accuracy and yields an efficient low-order analytical framework for nonlinear electrochemical reaction--diffusion problems.

papers.title: Towards Edge Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Antimicrobial Resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) poses a major challenge to global tuberculosis control, as multidrug-resistant strains limit available treatment options. Rapid and accurate prediction of drug resistance from genomic data could support timely treatment decisions and public health interventions. However, many existing computational approaches for genomic AMR prediction rely on computationally intensive pipelines, limiting their suitability for deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. This limitation is particularly relevant in hospital settings in low- and middle-income countries, where computing infrastructure and access to high-performance computational resources may be limited. To address this challenge, we present a lightweight, novel machine learning (ML) approach suitable for running on edge devices that combines 4-mer frequency features derived from whole-genome sequences with a Random Forest classifier to predict antibiotic resistance in MTB. The proposed ML approach achieved an average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.82 across 20 antibiotics on an independent test set.

papers.title: Antinucleon--nucleon interaction at next-to-next-to-leading order in covariant chiral effective field theory
papers.abstract: We construct antinucleon--nucleon ($\bar NN$) interactions at next-to-leading order (NLO) and next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) in covariant chiral effective field theory. The short-range interaction is represented by complex covariant contact terms, while the long-range part is obtained from the corresponding nucleon--nucleon interaction through $G$-parity transformation. The low-energy constants are determined from the Nijmegen partial-wave analysis, and phase shifts and mixing angles are calculated for all partial waves with $J\leq2$. Compared with NLO, NNLO improves the overall description of the phase shifts and mixing angles, particularly in several $J=2$ channels, although the improvement is not uniform across all partial waves or at higher energies. We estimate Bayesian truncation uncertainties and compare the results with heavy-baryon chiral interactions. We also revisit the pole candidates identified in our leading-order study and calculate the corresponding threshold parameters. The isoscalar ${}^{13}P_0$ pole remains a few MeV below the $\bar NN$ threshold with a width of about 40 MeV at both NLO and NNLO, whereas the $S$-wave candidates show stronger sensitivity to chiral orders. The NNLO covariant $\bar NN$ interaction therefore provides a useful basis for studies of antinucleon--nucleon scattering and near-threshold phenomena.

papers.title: Blocks with one simple module and solvable groups
papers.abstract: Let $b$ be a block of a finite group with one isomorphism class of simple modules in characteristic $p$. We construct, over a sufficiently large complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero, a Morita equivalence between $b$ and a block of a finite solvable group. The proof uses equivariant Morita bimodules for the quasisimple blocks that occur in the component reduction. We also prove that a block over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ is nilpotent whenever it is Morita equivalent to the group algebra of a finite $p$-group. For the latter result, we establish a criterion for twisted group algebras using derivations of the basic algebra and group transfer.

papers.title: Semiclassical Weyl laws and noncommutative geometry on open manifolds with conformally cusp metrics
papers.abstract: We establish semiclassical Weyl laws on open Riemannian manifolds with conformally cusp metrics of finite volume. These metrics need not be complete, and even when complete they do not have bounded geometry. Moreover, the potentials are bounded, the discreteness of the spectrum being a consequence of the geometry rather than of a confining potential. Therefore, our results lie beyond the scope of recent semiclassical Weyl laws of Dai--Yan and Braverman. The semiclassical Weyl laws are established for fractional Schrödinger operators associated with Dirac operators, magnetic Laplacians, and Hodge Laplacians, under conditions of Moroianu and Golénia--Moroianu which ensure that these operators have discrete spectra. We also obtain extensions of Connes' integration formula for the same operators. In addition, we deal with a class of conformally cusp metrics of infinite volume, in which case the semiclassical Weyl laws and the integration formulas only involve the values at infinity. The results are obtained by applying the abstract semiclassical Weyl laws and integration formulas for spectral triples established in a previous paper.

papers.title: Sharp Convergence of Extended Douglas--Rachford Splitting with Variable Relaxation
papers.abstract: We establish a sharp convergence theory for extended Douglas--Rachford splitting when the first operator is maximally monotone and the second is a convex subdifferential on a real Hilbert space. The resolvent stepsizes may be chosen independently, and the relaxation parameter may depend on the current and past iterates. For fixed stepsizes $\alpha,\beta>0$, let $\vartheta=\min\{2,2\alpha/\beta\}$. Assuming the sum of the operators has a zero, we prove weak convergence under $0<\theta_k\le\vartheta$ and $\sum_k\theta_k(\vartheta-\theta_k)=\infty$. Within these pointwise bounds, the divergence condition is also necessary for a universal convergence guarantee when the relaxation sequence is prescribed in advance. Constant relaxation recovers the exact range $0<\theta<\vartheta$, resolving a conjecture of Nilsson, Åkerman, and Giselsson. We also establish a sharp bound on growth of the residual, defined as the difference between the two resolvent outputs. We combine this bound with a new Lyapunov function whose definition is independent of the relaxation parameter to obtain a last-iterate residual rate, including $o(N^{-1/2})$ when the relaxation parameters remain uniformly separated from both endpoints.

papers.title: On the General Position Number of Cacti
papers.abstract: Given a graph G=(V,E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges, a subset of vertices $S \subseteq V$ is called a General Position Set (GPS) if no shortest path on G between any two vertices in S contains another vertex from S. The General Position Number (GPN) of a graph G is the maximum size of a GPS in G. The decision version of this problem, determining whether the GPN of a graph G is at least a given integer i, is known as the General Position Problem (GPP). The GPP is known to be NP-complete, making the computation of the GPN for general graphs computationally challenging. Hence, much of the existing research has focused on determining the GPN for special classes of graphs. One such class is that of cactus graphs (i.e., cacti), in which any two simple cycles share at most one vertex and no edge. For cactus graphs, several upper and lower bounds on the GPN have been previously presented. In this paper, we determine the exact value of the GPN for cactus graphs. We propose a novel graph decomposition that partitions a cactus graph into two types of subgraphs, called bearded cycles and non-beard trees. For each subgraph, we compute a special GPS, named a subGPS. We prove that the union of all maximum subGPSs constitutes a maximum GPS for the original cactus graph. This result allows us to compute the exact GPN for any cactus graph.

papers.title: Counting fluctuations in the GOE-GUE crossover
papers.abstract: We study bulk eigenvalue counting fluctuations in a Gaussian ensemble interpolating between the Gaussian orthogonal and Gaussian unitary ensembles. Realizing this ensemble as the distribution at a fixed time of Hermitian matrix Ornstein-Uhlenbeck flow started from the GOE, we prove a central limit theorem for the one-sided counting function, centered by the semicircle prediction. Its variance grows logarithmically, with a leading coefficient that interpolates between the GOE and GUE values. Specifically, at times $T_N \asymp N^{-1 + \vartheta}$ with fixed $0 < \vartheta < 1$, we prove that the one-sided bulk count is asymptotically Gaussian with leading variance $(1 - \vartheta/2)\pi^{-2}\log N$. Although the microscopic bulk correlations have their GUE limit throughout this regime, the leading counting variance retains a contribution from the initial GOE matrix.

papers.title: Undecidable quantum storage: no algorithm can tell from the noise rate whether a fixed circuit remembers
papers.abstract: Below a threshold noise rate, error correction lets larger quantum memories store a qubit for longer, without limit. Can the noise rate alone tell us whether a given noisy circuit does this? We construct fixed local circuits for which no algorithm can, already in one dimension under single-qubit noise. Each circuit is translation-invariant and time-periodic, with depolarizing noise on every wire after every layer, including all classical control. A computable list of disjoint rate intervals is indexed by the inputs $n$ of a universal Turing machine; local noise statistics select the input that the circuit simulates, and halting triggers erasure. If the machine runs forever on $n$, a qubit is stored throughout the $n$-th interval at entanglement fidelity at least $15/16$ for a time that grows without bound with size: linearly on rings, exponentially in six dimensions. The encoding and decoding maps are noiseless and global; they depend on $n$, the system size and, for decoding, the time, but not on the rate. If it halts, the fidelity of every encoding falls below $1/2+\eta$, for any fixed $\eta>0$, after a time independent of size and rate. The labels of the intervals with unbounded storage form a $\Pi^0_1$-complete set, and intervals of both kinds accumulate at zero, so these circuits have no noise threshold. Without rate selection, the ring construction is a translation-invariant, time-periodic memory: from an initialized classical hierarchy it stores a qubit for a time linear in the ring length at every sufficiently small rate, addressing the memory part of a one-dimensional question raised by Dünnweber, Styliaris and Trivedi. These are existence results: registers and interaction ranges are very large and the rates astronomically small.

papers.title: DeepDOSReasoner: Physics-Grounded Reasoning for Density-of-States Prediction and Materials Discovery
Feedback Exact Controllability of the Nonlinear Diffusion Equation with Controller in Coefficients
papers.abstract: One designs a feedback controller for semilinear parabolic equations with controller in diffusion coefficients which steers the initial data y0 in a given state y1 in a finite time.

papers.title: Handover Cost Optimization in LEO Satellite Networks using an RL-based Multiple-Column Selection Strategy via Branch-and-Price
papers.abstract: Next-generation wireless networks increasingly rely on low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites for broad coverage and low latency, making efficient handover management essential. We formulate satellite handover as a combinatorial optimization problem, assigning each ground user to exactly one capacity-limited, visible satellite while minimizing network handover costs. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based branch-and-price (B&P) framework with learned multiple-column selection (MCS) to accelerate column generation while retaining exact dynamic programming pricing. We also develop two lightweight heuristic policies: handover-aware visibility duration (HAVD) for online decisions and congestion-aware predictive (CAP) for offline planning. Additionally, a local-search repair algorithm adapts precomputed B&P or MCS-B&P solutions to demand perturbations through single-flip and per-user trajectory re-optimization, avoiding complete re-optimization. Simulations using realistic large scale constellations, including Starlink Gen-1, demonstrate that MCS-B&P achieves solution quality comparable to exact B&P with fewer column-generation iterations, fewer branch-and-bound nodes, and reduced computation time. HAVD and CAP offer effective online and offline cost-latency trade-offs, while local-search repair recovers most performance losses due to demand perturbations at a fraction of the computational cost of full re-optimization.

papers.title: Contact rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants
papers.abstract: We study $C^0$-rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants on closed contact manifolds. We prove that Poisson commutation is closed under uniform convergence, establish weak rigidity for pairs without common zeros, and obtain lower semicontinuity under quantitative control of Reeb derivatives. A three-dimensional counterexample shows that unrestricted weak rigidity fails. For partitions of unity, the contact bracket itself controls the Reeb derivatives. Using monotone homogeneous quasi-morphisms and the Cant--Kilgore--Zhang spectral invariant, we derive positive lower bounds for invariants of open covers and configurations of compact subsets. Applications include a quantitative contact big fiber theorem, bounds on Hamiltonian chord durations and Reeb travel times, and deformations of contact one-forms.

papers.title: Killing Scales for Conformal Killing Tensors of Rank Two and Higher
papers.abstract: We study which metrics in a conformal class admit a Killing tensor with prescribed conformal Killing trace-free part. We call such metrics Killing scales. We also consider whether a given conformal Killing tensor is itself a Killing tensor for some metric in the conformal class, as well as the analogous problem for conformal Killing-Yano forms. Our approach to this problem uses conformal and projective tractors, and the prolongations provided by the BGG splitting operators of the projective and conformal Killing operators. For rank two conformal Killing tensors, we characterise local Killing scales for arbitrary scales on arbitrary conformal manifolds, extending recent results that were restricted to Einstein scales on conformally flat manifolds. The criterion is expressed in terms of the scale tractor and the BGG prolongation of the conformal Killing tensor. We also obtain Killing scale criteria for higher-rank conformal Killing tensors and conformal Killing-Yano forms, under additional hypotheses involving Einstein scales and normal solutions. We describe the tractor geometry of special Einstein products, including Ricci-flat products, and use these constructions to give examples beyond the conformally flat setting.

papers.title: Measuring the Neutrino Mass with $^{241}$Pu
2D MXene integrated optical polarizers based on TiO2 with high performance
papers.abstract: Polarization control is essential for modern optical systems. Recently, two dimensional (2D) materials featuring highly anisotropic absorption across broad wavelength regions have emerged as a promising solution for realizing optical polarizers with operation bandwidths far exceeding those achievable using bulk materials. Despite this, existing 2D material based optical polarizers face critical limitations in simultaneously delivering high polarizer figures of merit (FOMs), robust power endurance, and scalable fabrication, hindering their practical deployment beyond laboratory. Here, we overcome this bottleneck by demonstrating optical polarizers through integrating 2D MXene films onto silicon photonic devices and subsequently converting them in situ into 2D titanium dioxide (TiO2). The 2D TiO2 exhibits significantly improved anisotropic absorption and thermal / chemical stability compared with MXene, enabling the hybrid polarizers to achieve a record high polarizer FOM of 17.5 (among 2D material-coated devices) and excellent power tolerance (stable under > 2 W coupled average power), together with a broad operation bandwidth (> 140 nm) and a high fabrication yield ( 98%). We also demonstrate microring resonator polarizers achieving high polarization extinction ratios up to 12 dB. With outstanding overall performance and strong capability for large-scale manufacturing, these polarizers represent a solid step towards industry ready implementations of 2D material based optical polarizers.

papers.title: From Footprints to Service Regions: Modeling and Analysis of Dense LEO Satellite Networks Using an Orbit-Aware Cox Point Process
papers.abstract: In dense low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks, several accessible satellites cover the same location. A footprint therefore identifies where communication is feasible but does not determine which satellite serves each user. The service region of a satellite, namely the set of locations it serves, governs satellite load, resource sharing, and user throughput. Using an orbit-aware Cox point process on a common orbital shell, we model each service region as the intersection of a satellite's spherical-cap footprint and its spherical Voronoi cell under nearest-satellite association. We then use Palm calculus to derive exact expressions for the mean area and perimeter and a coverage--load identity. After coverage saturates, mean area and load decrease inversely with population. In contrast, adding satellites along existing orbits leaves a positive limiting mean perimeter. We connect this geometry to an approximate noise-limited user rate. Along the tested densification paths, the increase in user rate comes mainly from the decrease in mean satellite load rather than from the improvement of the serving link. We also compare the model with Walker constellations with Starlink-type parameters, using Cox parameters matched to the local orbit and satellite densities at each latitude. The model reproduces the mean area and perimeter of these constellations over broad latitude ranges, with larger differences near component maximum latitudes. These results show that service-region geometry, and hence satellite load and user rate, depend not only on the total satellite population but also on its allocation across orbital planes.

papers.title: Digital Models of Widely-Used Powder Characterisation Tools and their Application in DEM Calibration Part III: Packing and Flow Testers
papers.abstract: Accurate calibration remains a critical challenge in the field of discrete element method (DEM) simulations. To work towards more standardised and rigorous methods, this research contributes to a growing open-source library of digital models that faithfully replicate powder characterisation instruments. This paper expands that library by developing and validating digital models for two widely used instruments: the GranuFlow flow through an orifice tester and the GranuPack tapped density analyser. These models are designed to replicate the experimental instruments while incorporating computational optimisations to improve efficiency without compromising on accuracy. An example application of the digital models is shown through a calibration case study for two example materials: micro-crystalline cellulose (MCC) and ion exchange resin. The calibrated models show strong agreement with experimental data through cross-validation, yielding a relative percentage error of 0.57\% for the Hausner ratio (the ion exchange resin) and 4.17\% for a Beverloo fitting parameter (MCC). The addition of these validated, open-source models provides the DEM community with further models for more robust, multi-instrument calibration, and potential for more insight into bulk behaviours under different conditions.

papers.title: A Camera-Based Single-Volume, Monolithic Compton Camera
papers.abstract: A Compton camera measures two events in a detector from individual gamma-rays to reconstruct the radiation source. Conventional scintillator-based Compton cameras consist of two separate scintillator volumes or a single segmented scintillator, resulting in drawbacks regarding detector bulkiness and efficiency. Their scintillator readout techniques struggle to resolve two nearby events in one monolithic scintillator. Single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) cameras have recently been proposed for measuring scintillation events in various configurations. SPAD array sensors enable high-resolution photon-counting acquisition at high rates that is easily scalable to millions of pixels. Prior work has explored different optics and measurement arrangements as well as demonstrated measurement of single interaction locations. In this work, we extend these capabilities to demonstrate a practical radiation imaging device in the form of a Compton camera consisting of a SPAD camera and one compact, monolithic scintillator. Our Compton camera prototype successfully reconstructs a gamma-ray source over multiple locations that span a 4$\pi$ steradian field of view. Our approach is able to resolve two simultaneous events in one monolithic scintillator and enables Compton camera devices with compact, monolithic scintillator volumes for enhanced portability.

papers.title: Reconfigurable Microwave Photonic All-Pass Filters based on Optical Kerr Microcombs
papers.abstract: Microwave photonic (MWP) all pass filters (APFs), which enable phase manipulation without altering signal amplitudes, are essential for phase engineering in high bandwidth microwave signal processing. However, achieving a high degree of reconfigurability in the filter order and characteristic parameters of APFs remains challenging for conventional methods. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a new strategy for realizing MWP APFs based on a microcomb driven transversal filter system, enabling high reconfigurability, sharp phase transitions with high group delays, and low loss. We experimentally demonstrate both 1st and 2nd order APFs, achieving a maximum amplitude variation (MAV) of 1.95 dB and a maximum group delay (MGD) of 580 ps for the former, and a MAV of 2.01 dB and an MGD of 1740 ps for the latter. In addition, both independent and joint tuning of APF characteristic parameters are demonstrated by simply programming the tap coefficients without changing any hardware, enabling highly reconfigurable filter response for diverse phase engineering functionalities. These results highlight the potential of our approach for implementing MWP APFs with both high performance and reconfigurability for practical applications requiring dynamic and versatile phase control.

papers.title: A Fiber-Optic Platform for Cryogenic Laser-Pump Neutron-Probe Magneto-Optical Measurements
When do local bounds permit optimal edge-colorings?
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a multigraph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)$, maximum multiplicity $\mu(G)$, and chromatic index $\chi'(G)$. A proper edge-coloring is locally bounded if each edge $e$ in $G$ with endvertices $u$ and $v$ is assigned a color at most $\max\{d_G(u)+\mu_G(u),d_G(v)+\mu_G(v)\}$, where $d_G(w)$ and $\mu_G(w)$ respectively denote the degree of $w$ and the maximum multiplicity of an edge incident with $w$. The well-known Vizing's theorem guarantees a proper edge-coloring with at most $\Delta(G)+\mu(G)$ colors. Recently, the local version of this theorem was established for simple graphs by Christiansen, resolving a conjecture posed by Bonamy, Delcourt, Lang, and Postle, and extended to multigraphs by Conley, Grebík, and Pikhurko. In this paper, we define the local chromatic index of $G$, denoted by $\chi'_{loc}(G)$, as the least positive integer $k$ for which $G$ admits a locally bounded proper edge-coloring with colors in $\{1,2,...,k\}$. Thus $\Delta(G)\le\chi'(G)\le\chi'_{loc}(G)\le\Delta(G)+\mu(G)$. We give equivalent characterizations and sufficient conditions for the equality $\chi'_{loc}(G)=\chi'(G)$, identifying when the local bounds in Vizing's theorem can be satisfied using the minimum possible number of colors. In particular, we prove this equality for every regular multigraph, every multigraph $G$ with $\Delta(G)\le 4$, and every simple graph in which the vertices of degree at least five induce a subgraph of maximum degree at most two. Moreover, we construct a simple graph $G$ with $\chi'(G)=\Delta(G)=5$ and $\chi'_{loc}(G)=6$, showing that these local bounds can force the use of an additional color even in simple graphs. Consequently, five is the smallest possible maximum degree for which satisfying these local bounds can require more than $\chi'(G)$ colors.

papers.title: Random homomorphisms from affine to spherical reflection groups
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to understand the set $\mathrm{Hom}(\widetilde{W},W)$ of homomorphisms from an affine reflection group $\widetilde{W}$ to its associated spherical reflection group $W$. We do this in three ways: numerically, by deriving an explicit formula for $|\mathrm{Hom}(\widetilde{W},W)|$; probabilistically, by exploring the question what does a random homomorphism $\widetilde{W}\to W$ look like?; and algebraically, by explicitly writing down all possible homomorphisms on the standard generators. For example, we show that as $n\to\infty$ the probability that a random homomorphism $\widetilde{W}_n\to W_n$ is surjective tends to $\frac{3}{4}$ if $W_n$ is of type $C_{2n}$ or $D_n$, to $\frac{9}{16}$ if $W_n$ is of type $C_{2n+1}$, and to $1$ if $W_n$ is of type $A_n.$

papers.title: MRI Acquisition Parameters Influence Magnetic Resonance Hydrophone Measurements
papers.abstract: Purpose:} To characterize the accuracy and precision of magnetic resonance hydrophone (MRH) measurements in response to changes in MR acquisition parameters. \textbf{Methods:} A human compatible MRH coil was coupled to a 500 kHz ultrasound transducer in a gel phantom. MRH acquisitions were repeated in a 3T scanner while altering in-plane resolution, slice thickness, encoding time, and device orientation within the MRI bore. The average and standard deviation of acoustic pressure estimates within a ROI near the encoding coil were compared to that obtained from the same transducer using a calibrated hydrophone in a water tank. The accuracy and precision of MRH scans, as well as a maximum detection depth, were then estimated. \textbf{Results:} Under high signal-to-noise (SNR) conditions, the MRH average pressure corresponded closely to those obtained by the hydrophone with no consistent measurement bias. However, too large or too small of voxel dimensions produced measurement underestimation, as expected by theory. Rotations as small as 15$^\circ$ out of alignment with the MRI bore also produced larger measurement underestimation than predicted by a dipole model of the encoding gradient coil. Increasing encoding times improved measurement precision but to a degree less than expected by theory. \textbf{Conclusion:} MR acquisition parameters exert a strong influence on MRH measurement accuracy and precision.

papers.title: Effect of Transmission Line Switching on Damping of Interarea Modes
papers.abstract: This paper will explore the impact of switching transmission lines on the damping of interarea oscillation modes. This phenomenon played a central role in the 2025 Iberian blackout and in some North American oscillation events. The paper first assesses the effectiveness of line switching for enhancing mode damping by studying the problem in classical test power systems. The paper then tests these observations in realistic large-scale models of the Western Interconnection that represent recent real-time system conditions. It is shown that the switching of key transmission lines can have a significant impact on the damping of inter-area modes depending on system operating conditions.

papers.title: Neural Costate Guidance for Autonomous Cislunar Low-Thrust Trajectory Generation
papers.abstract: Future missions will benefit from onboard autonomous low-thrust trajectory generation to correct deviations from the nominal flight path caused by navigation errors and thruster outages. Onboard computing resources rarely allow the solution of a cold-started, long-duration nonconvex optimal control problem, especially in dynamically challenging regions such as the cislunar to translunar corridor of the Earth-Moon system. This paper develops data augmentation and training techniques that enable a neural network to predict accurate initial costates of the indirect method. A recovery trajectory is then built from repeated network queries in a computationally efficient guidance algorithm. Training data are produced by the backward generation of optimal examples method, extending prior approaches to the circular restricted three-body problem. A novel anchor trajectory approach is developed to cover the relevant state space, and costate rescaling and a Hamiltonian loss term are used to improve learning. The method is demonstrated on Earth-Moon transfers from a high Earth orbit to halo orbits about L1 and L2. Under navigation errors and thruster outages, a spacecraft reaches the target orbit more often with the proposed method than with nominal-trajectory tracking or fully numerical reoptimization. Onboard computation is reduced by more than an order of magnitude compared with reoptimization.

papers.title: A ring of symmetric Hermitian modular forms of degree $2$ with integral Fourier coefficients II
papers.abstract: We exhibit 24 homogeneous generators for the graded \(\Z\)-algebra of symmetric Hermitian modular forms of degree 2 over \(\Q(i)\) with integral Fourier coefficients, where the weight \(k\) is even and the character is \(\det^{k/2}\). We prove that 24 is the minimum number of algebra generators. For the subalgebra in weights divisible by 4, Kurihara reduced the generating set given in our earlier work to 11 forms. We show that 13 further forms generate the direct sum of the components in weights congruent to 2 modulo 4 as a module over this subalgebra. For \(p=2\) and \(p=3\), we show that the ring of Fourier expansions modulo \(p\) is a polynomial ring over \(\F_p\) generated by the reductions of 4 forms of weights \(8,12,12,16\). We also record the diagonal Sturm bound \(\lfloor k/8\rfloor\) modulo every prime \(p\) and verify its sharpness in every even weight \(k\ne2\).

papers.title: FAS-Assisted Self-Interference Mitigation for In-Band Full-Duplex Communications
papers.abstract: In-band full-duplex (IBFD) communication relies on effective self-interference cancellation (SIC) to overcome the strong loopback self-interference (SI). While fluid antenna system (FAS)-assisted SIC offers superior SI suppression by dynamically selecting the FAS port to minimize the residual SI power, it incurs high pilot overhead to acquire channel state information (CSI) for both forward and loopback channels. This raises the question of whether forward channel CSI is necessary for effective SI mitigation. To address this challenge, we propose a pilot-efficient FAS-assisted SI mitigation (FAS-SIM) approach that selects the FAS port solely based on the loopback SI channel. Theoretical performance analysis of the forward signal is provided. Numerical results then reveal that FAS-SIM achieves SI suppression and a forward-link rate comparable to the conventional method, while reducing port-selection training overhead by 50%, offering a low-overhead solution for IBFD communications.

papers.title: Interface invariants of rhombohedral graphene with layer-dependent potentials and couplings
Acoustic bound states in the continuum in a labyrinthine meta-atom
papers.abstract: In this Letter, we theoretically and experimentally study acoustic bound states in the continuum (BICs) emerging in labyrinth meta-atom embedded in an acoustic waveguide. A symmetry-protected BIC is supported in the lossless limit when the meta-atom is positioned on the waveguide axis. Breaking the symmetry by shifting the meta-atom away from the center of the waveguide transforms the BIC into a radiative quasi-BIC, manifested by the emergence of a narrow resonant feature in the transmittance spectrum. The proposed concept is experimentally tested using a 3D-printed labyrinthine meta-atom placed inside an impedance tube. The measured transmittance spectra are consistent with numerical simulations and support the BIC-to-quasi-BIC transition induced by symmetry breaking in the presence of thermoviscous losses. The resonance frequency, contrast, and linewidth can be controlled by varying the meta-atom position. The observed behavior is interpreted within a two-mode temporal coupled-mode theory (TCMT), providing an analytical description of the resonant response. The ability to tune radiative leakage in the presence of absorption makes the proposed acoustic BIC platform promising for the development of tunable absorbers, sensors, and modulators.

papers.title: Single-Shot Single-Stage Stellarators
papers.abstract: In stellarator design, the plasma and the coils are so geometrically complex that they are usually designed separately, so that a high-performance plasma may be impossible to reproduce with coils that can actually be manufactured and assembled. We present a new method to close this gap. In this framework, the plasma shape is optimized while, for every candidate shape, near-optimal coils that satisfy hard engineering limits are found. Without any manually-tuned weights, the method steers the plasma towards shapes that real coils can produce. Moreover, we demonstrate the first single-shot optimization runs starting from tokamak ``cold-starts''. From a single-shot cold-start, we design a finite-$\beta$ stellarator comparable to reactor-scaled NCSX, as well as a compact aspect-ratio 2.5 and $\langle\beta\rangle=2\%$ quasi-axisymmetric stellarator with one field period and self-consistent bootstrap current. Starting from a boundary derived from W7-X, we design a quasi-isodynamic stellarator with reactor-relevant stability properties. We then use this to warm-start an optimization for a single coil-set solution that produces a high-performance QI stellarator at every pressure value from vacuum to $\langle\beta\rangle=4\%$, addressing directly the ``start-up'' phase of a reactor. The self-consistent free-boundary solutions for these stellarators typically have better coils than a traditional separate-design approach, at comparable or better plasma performance, illustrating that robust single-stage methods are possible and providing a direct route to the design of reactor-scale stellarators.

papers.title: Construction of Universal Safe Stabilizing Formulas with Weighted Centroid Methodology
papers.abstract: Control Lyapunov and control barrier functions ensure stability and safety, respectively, by imposing state-dependent affine constraints on the control input. Controller design can therefore be viewed as the problem of selecting an admissible input from the set defined by these constraints. This paper adopts this perspective and develops a weighted-centroid methodology for constructing explicit feedback formulas that are provably smooth. The selection method relies on the fact that weighted centroids of a convex set lie within the set. We establish conditions on the weight functions that guarantee smoothness and continuity for several classes of constraints, including single constraints, mirrored constraints, linearly independent multiple constraints, and two-constraint Gaussian constructions. The framework recovers Sontag's universal formula and generates other new explicit formulas. When specialized to control-theoretic settings, the resulting formulas yield smooth safety filters, stabilizing controllers, and safe-stabilizing controllers. Simulation and hardware experiments on a small quadrotor illustrate the practical benefits of the proposed construction.

papers.title: On rescuing diverging algorithms: crossing infinity in continuous Newton methods via a self-similarity detection framework
papers.abstract: We address the solution of systems of nonlinear algebraic equations via continuous Newton methods; these methods reformulate the discrete Newton update as an initial value problem for a system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) whose stationary points correspond to the desired roots. A fundamental challenge arises when the Jacobian of these ODEs becomes singular along the solution trajectory, inducing blow-up in the vector field --or in the state itself-- and causing the numerical integration to break down before reaching the desired root. To overcome this difficulty, we propose a directional self-similar blow-up detection and crossing procedure, wrapped around an adaptive step-size ODE solver with event detection. The method assumes local self-similar behavior near the blow-up; the self-similarity exponent, blow-up time, and amplitude are estimated on the fly from a short sequence of threshold crossings via linear regression, requiring no prior knowledge of the singularity location, its order, or the blow-up regime---in contrast to approaches that rely on explicit analytical continuation or problem-specific coordinate transformations. The estimated exponent distinguishes two qualitatively different scenarios at finite time: one in which only the vector field diverges while the state remains finite, admitting an explicit integral correction, and one in which the state itself blows-up. In addition, infinite-time divergence of the state (the so-called "grow-up" regime) is handled through a suitable time reparameterization. In higher dimensions, we track the norm of the vector field along its instantaneous direction; near a simple singularity, the flow asymptotically aligns with a single dominant direction (see text), reducing detection and estimation to a scalar problem regardless of ambient space dimension.

papers.title: The Role of Mathematicians in Mathematics
papers.abstract: Some reflections on the role of mathematicians in an age of proofs found and verified by machines.

papers.title: Tipping cascades may lock the Earth system on a pathway towards a melthouse
papers.abstract: The potential for the Earth system to transition irreversibly into a hothouse Earth has attracted considerable scientific and media attention but remains insufficiently explored in modeling studies. Using a reduced-complexity Earth system model that includes a dynamic carbon cycle and interacting tipping elements, we find no planetary threshold beyond which the Earth system irreversibly shifts into a hothouse state. Instead, tipping cascades can drive the system towards an irreversible melthouse state with over 10 m of sea-level rise. Such cascades may occur even under low-emission scenarios, preventing long-term stabilization of sea level at intermediate values. Our results overall highlight the substantial risk of a melthouse rather than a hothouse Earth, and call for drastic emission reductions to avert dramatic impacts on coastal cities and communities.

papers.title: TrustFlow-ECG: Reliability-Aware ECG Restoration with Calibrated Risk Estimation
papers.abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) restoration models can reduce noise and motion artifacts, but they rarely estimate whether the restored waveform is reliable for downstream analysis. We propose TrustFlow-ECG, a reliability-aware restoration framework that combines a one-step conditional rectified-flow restorer with a lightweight window-level risk predictor. The predictor uses the noisy ECG, restored ECG, and correction residual, then applies validation-set isotonic calibration for selective ECG analysis. We evaluate on MIT-BIH ECG windows corrupted with NSTDB artifacts, powerline interference, and mixed noise across multiple SNRs, with an external 9,675-window PTB-XL stress check without retraining. TrustFlow achieves 0.862 Spearman correlation with true risk and 0.911 AUROC for failure detection, while calibration reduces ECE from 0.0385 to 0.0098. At 80% coverage, selective rejection reduces RMSE from 0.1848 to 0.1345, improves R-peak F1 from 0.8778 to 0.9175, and reduces HR MAE from 6.26 to 4.88 bpm.

papers.title: Weighted Carleson embedding on product of trees in general dimension
papers.abstract: We prove the equivalence of the Carleson embedding on $n$-trees (arbitrary Cartesian product of trees) and the box condition, for arbitrary nonnegative measures and generalized product weights. For product weights, we obtain the sharp coefficient $4^n$. This extends the bi-tree and tri-tree embedding theorems of \cite{AMPVZ} and \cite{MPVZ} to every dimension. We also give two applications of the Carleson embedding: we characterize Carleson measures for the classical Dirichlet space on the polydisc $\mathbb D^n$ and deduce criteria for bounded composition operators from this space into weighted Bergman spaces, generalizing the results from \cite{MPVZ} and \cite{Beslikas2025}. Finally, we define a generalized logarithmic Dirichlet space and characterize its Carleson measures.

papers.title: Deliverable Frequency Regulation Reserve for VPPs via Transmission-Distribution Co-Simulation
papers.abstract: Aggregations of distributed energy resources can provide frequency regulation services. However, device-level power headroom may not accurately represent the power deliverable at the transmission-distribution interface. This paper proposes a bidirectional, storage-aware power-sharing framework for a virtual power plant (VPP). Delivery factors obtained from the perturbations used to construct the voltage-sensitivity matrix account for feeder losses and voltage-dependent loads, while battery energy limits and state-of-charge weights are included in the allocation. The framework is evaluated using the IEEE 8500-node feeder and IEEE 14-bus system. The proposed method tracks the feeder-head request within 2% compared with 23-26% over-delivery under the injection-headroom framework. It also sustains the requested power response 22% longer before reaching the storage energy limit. Moreover, communicating the updated VPP reserve to the transmission system operator reduces the post-transient integrated area control error by 80% relative to fixed reserve registration.

papers.title: The dimension of optimal plans in multi-marginal optimal transport
papers.abstract: For general cost functions, we determine the maximal dimension on which solutions to the multi-marginal optimal transport problem with absolutely continuous marginals are concentrated. The dimension is obtained via a novel characteristic integer associated with the Hessian of the cost function. Applications are given to important examples of multi-marginal problems like Wasserstein barycenters, Wasserstein cubic splines and Brenier's generalized Euler equations.

papers.title: Uniguided and unicoupled resonances in an asymmetric acoustic metasurface
papers.abstract: We theoretically study an acoustic metasurface that exhibits ultimate asymmetry in absorption under oblique incidence. This behavior arises from a counter-propagating pair of uniguided (UGR) and unicoupled (UCR) resonances. The UGR radiates to only one side, while the UCR radiates to both sides but can be excited from only one. In the lossless regime, the transmission phase winds by $2\pi$ across both UCR and UGR while the transmittance remains flat at any prescribed nonzero level. Thermoviscous losses introduce resonant intensity modulation and enable critical coupling, yielding perfect sound absorption exclusively for incidence through the channel that excites the UCR. Therefore, asymmetric metasurfaces with UCR and UGR offer a route to full phase control and perfect sound absorption.

papers.title: Note on the extendability problem for invariant quasimorphisms for mapping class groups
papers.abstract: In this note, we study the extendability problem of invariant quasimorphisms for short exact sequences related to mapping class groups of surfaces, possibly with one boundary component or one marked point. Using a recent result of Blatz, we prove that if the genus is at least two, then every homogeneous quasimorphism on the Torelli group that is invariant by the conjugation action by the mapping class group is uniquely extendable to the whole mapping class group. Contrastingly, for the surface with one marked point whose genus is at least three, we show the existence of a homogeneous Torelli-group-invariant quasimorphism on the Johnson kernel that is not extendable.

papers.title: Stability of a Paraboloidal Steady Solution for the 2D Surface Growth Model
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the stability problem of 2D surface growth model. To be specific, we prove that the small perturbation of the paraboloidal steady solution decays to zero in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^2)$. The decay occurs both for the perturbation and its gradient, whose decay rates are $O(t^{-1/2})$ and $O(t^{-1}\log t)$, respectively. The proof is based on the linearization of the perturbation equation and the bootstrap argument to close the statement in nonlinear equation. Sufficient conditions for stability require the initial data and its gradient of the perturbation to be small in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and Wiener algebra $\mathcal{A}$. It is notable that the smallness in second derivative is not necessary, which is physically reasonable because large second derivative would lead to high surface energy and it is expected to be relaxed in short time. We also prove existence and uniqueness of mild solution for perturbation equation under those conditions.

papers.title: Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli with multilinear weights
papers.abstract: We study the average distribution of primes up to $x$ in arithmetic progressions to moduli $q$ larger than $\sqrt{x}$, where $q = q_1 \cdots q_n$ ($n \geqslant 2$) with conveniently sized divisors $q_1, \ldots, q_n$ and the average is weighted by an arbitrary divisor-bounded multilinear weight. Specifically, we show that the primes up to $x$ are equidistributed in the residue class $a \pmod{q_1 q_2}$ on average over moduli $q_1 q_2$ as large as $x^{8/15 - \varepsilon}$ when the average is weighted by a bilinear weight and the sizes of $q_1$ and $q_2$ lie in an explicit region, improving the exponent $9/17$ for bilinear weights obtained recently by Li. The new ingredient here is an estimate for the Type-II convolution sums with both factors have size about $x^{1/2}$. With this estimate, the level of distribution $8/15$ in the bilinear case is no longer limited by the Type-II sums but by the Type-I$_3$ sums, or the current range in the ternary divisor problem. We also get further improvements for $n \geqslant 3$ using a simple form of Harman's sieve together with various arithmetic information, including the Type-II estimate mentioned above. We group the divisors $q_1, \ldots, q_n$ in different ways in order to use arithmetic information more efficiently. Specifically, we reach $x^{145/266 - \varepsilon}$ for trilinear weights, $x^{457/814 - \varepsilon}$ for quadrilinear weights and $x^{3614/6353 - \varepsilon}$ for quintilinear weights. As the number of divisors increases, the exponent approaches $4/7$, the long-standing result with well-factorable weights proved by Bombieri, Friedlander and Iwaniec.

papers.title: Quadratic Forms of Multivariate $t$-Distributions
papers.abstract: This paper concerns quadratic forms of multivariate $t$-distributions. This paper derives the joint distribution and density of multiple quadratic forms, and establishes the possibility of a finite series approximation to the CDF. The paper also provides closed-form expressions for all the mixed moments that exist. Inverses of quadratic forms and ratios of quadratic forms are also considered.

papers.title: Moore spaces, polyhedral products, and positive scalar curvature
papers.abstract: Gromov conjectured that the macroscopic dimension of the universal cover of a closed $n$-manifold of positive scalar curvature is at most $n-2$. Gromov's conjecture holds for a closed spin manifold of dimension $n\geq 5$, provided that its fundamental group has property $(*)_m$, i.e., its classifying space is stably homotopy equivalent to a wedge of Moore spaces. We prove property $(*)_m$ for a large class of groups, including for instance the fundamental groups of closed hyperbolic $3$-manifolds, the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups with low-dimensional nerves, pure braid groups, and many graph products thereof. As an additional application of independent interest, we show that there are finite-index subgroups of right-angled Artin groups that do not have property $(*)_m$ and can have arbitrary torsion in their (co)homology in any degree.

papers.title: Finite-size reversal of a multiparticle correction to local spin spectra in a flux-disordered Kitaev honeycomb model
Plane Curves Whose Curvature Is a Function of the Distance to the Tangent Line: Relations Between Karpenkov's Areal and Angular Densities
papers.abstract: For a plane curve and a point $O$, O. Karpenkov introduced the areal density $A$ and the angular density $B$ as smooth counterparts of the alternating entries of an LLS sequence. Here $A$ is the signed distance from $O$ to the tangent line, and, with the order of the chords in the signed definition fixed here, $A^2B=\kappa$, where $\kappa$ is the signed curvature.
