A relation between the two densities therefore prescribes the curvature as a function of the distance to the tangent line. Karpenkov asked which curves have $AB$, or $B$ alone, constant. The equation $AB=C$ gives the shrinking, stationary and expanding profiles of planar curve shortening. For constant nonzero $B$, choose the orientation so that $B>0$. Curves with positive support have periodic support or are centred circles. The noncircular closed curves are classified by their turning fractions in $(1/2,1/\sqrt3)$; the centred circle is the only embedded closed solution. Negative support gives smooth open graphs whose two ends approach rays from the origin. On positive support the polar reciprocal is a constant-force orbit, and the original curve is a rotated and scaled velocity curve of that orbit. For $A^3B=C$ we determine which ends extend to infinity, reach a cusp, or spiral into the origin. We describe regularity and the range of turning fractions for the positive-support family $A^pB=C$. Finally, for a general relation $B=\Phi(A)$ the polar reciprocal is an orbit of the central force $L^2/\Phi(1/r)$; we describe the ends of all arcs with $AB<0$ and show that a closed curve with turning fraction $m/n$ has exactly $n(m-1)$ double points. We also describe the curves whose areal or angular density is a linear function of the arclength.

papers.title: Strong holonomicity of functions on curves
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth affine irreducible curve over $\mathbb C$, and let ${\mathcal D} = {\mathcal D} (X)$ be the ring of global differential operators on $X$. To every nonzero operator $L \in {\mathcal D} $ we attach a non-negative integer $n(L)$, the holonomicity index of $L$, which is defined in an elementary way, by counting solutions of $L$ in the truncated local rings at the singular points of $L$. Our main theorem shows that $n(L)$ coincides with the Calogero--Moser index of the Weyl closure ${\rm cl}(L) = {\mathcal D}(K) \cap {\mathcal D} $ of $L$, i.e. with the integer $n$ labelling the Calogero--Moser space $ {\mathcal C}_n(X,\mathcal{I})$ that contains the isomorphism class of the left ideal ${\rm cl}(L)$ under the classification of ideals of ${\mathcal D}$ given in [Berest--Chalykh, 2012]. The proof is based on a dual version of the Cannings--Holland correspondence, which describes left ideals of ${\mathcal D}$ in terms of finite-dimensional spaces of algebraic distributions on $X$, and an explicit formula for the Calogero--Moser index given in terms of these distributions. We apply these results to annihilators of locally holomorphic functions on $X$: we call a holonomic function $f$ strongly holonomic if the Calogero--Moser index of ${\rm Ann}_{\mathcal D}(f)$ is positive, and we compute this index in a number of interesting cases.

papers.title: Sub-Gaussian HDLSS Principal Component Analysis: High-Probability Theory and Numerical Evidence for NRM, CDM, and Block Noise Reduction
papers.abstract: We study principal component analysis when the dimension d is much larger than the sample size n under an independent-factor sub-Gaussian model. The dual sample covariance is decomposed into a finite-rank score matrix, an isotropic bulk shift, and a high-probability remainder governed by the bulk trace \tau_0, Frobenius scale q_0, and largest noise eigenvalue b_0 = ||\Lambda_0||_{op}. This decomposition separates fixed-score HDLSS limits from joint limits in which n also grows. It shows that sequential noise reduction generally targets a score oracle containing a later-spike subtraction, while an oracle block correction avoids that subtraction when the signal rank is known. A parallel cross-data-matrix bound explains the benefit and cost of sample splitting. Reproducible Gaussian-factor simulations with 1,000 replications per configuration confirm the score-oracle approximation, the multi-spike subtraction, the separation between eigenvalue and eigenvector scales, and the population transition when n grows.

papers.title: Note on OpenAI's proof of the base of Lagrangian fibrations
papers.abstract: OpenAI proved that every Lagrangian fibration of a compact hyper-Kähler manifold has a base $\mathbb P^n$. This expository note summarizes the last section of their paper.

papers.title: Fractal dimension of velocity-driven mixing: Reanalysis of Cao et al. (Phys. Rev. A 45, 3841 (1992)) and the universality of the Marstrand co-dimension rule
papers.abstract: Cao et al. [Phys. Rev. A 45, 3841 (1992)] compared box-counting fractal dimensions of interfaces from continuum (SOLA-VOF) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of zero-Atwood-number mixing driven by random velocity perturbations. They reported D ~ 1.1-1.4 across physical models. We revisit their results with grid-converged geometric VOF simulations and modern box-counting algorithms. The grid-converged continuum dimension depends on the initial-condition realization (D = 1.13-1.38). Independent LAMMPS simulations show that Cao's MD dimension measures thermal scatter of atomic positions, not interface geometry, because their box-counting window lies below the scale of the interface structure: a flat interface at t=0 gives the same D ~ 1.36. When the thermal scatter is filtered by reducing the midpoint cloud to a curve (median binning at 2 sigma), the MD trajectory converges to the same late-time D ~ 1.43 as the continuum, recovering cross-model universality. We prove that the linear-regime box-counting dimension is exactly D = 2 - beta (A > 0) and D = 5/2 - beta (A = 0), where beta is the spectral exponent of the initial perturbation. For white noise (beta = 0) neither formula applies; Cao's early-time D ~ 2 is a boundary artifact. A three-dimensional grid convergence study gives D_3D = 2.361 +/- 0.002 at 400x400x200. Marstrand's co-dimension rule D_3D = D_2D + 1 shows a 7% discrepancy reflecting IC-realization dependence at A = 0, unlike the buoyancy-driven case where the discrepancy falls with resolution.

papers.title: High-Resolution 3D Micro-CT Database of Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) Coils for More Accurate Modelling, Technology Benchmarking, and Progress in Coil Design
papers.abstract: Accurate modelling of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) coils requires coil-specific geometric and electrical parameters. Yet detailed manufacturer models are rarely available, and internals may be widely available to companies in the field but not to researchers. The development of new coils should ideally build on all existing prior art. This work presents a technology benchmark and modelling-ready dataset for seventeen widely used commercial TMS coils across multiple manufacturers and geometries. High-resolution micro-CT (0.0495 mm resolution, material and density contrast) serves to reconstruct winding and casing structures and to extract parameters directly usable in numerical models, including loop dimensions, conductor cross-section, turn count, winding height, and winding-to-surface (casing) thickness. Complementary electrical measurements provide spectral impedance (series resistance and inductance) scans from 20 Hz to 200 kHz, together with dc resistance. In addition to baseline geometry and impedance, the study documents practical construction features relevant to safety and usability with detailed insights into their internal construction (e.g., cooling architectures and embedded sensing). The resulting benchmark dataset supports coil-specific electric-field simulations, reduces modelling uncertainty associated with generic assumptions (e.g., fixed coil-scalp spacing), and provides a quantitative reference for designing and evaluating new coil technologies against established commercial solutions. As a simulation-readiness example, we generated a calibrated CT-derived MCB70 line-current model for SimNIBS and evaluated its effect on predicted electric-field metrics. Compared with the SimNIBS MCB70 model, the CT-derived model produced measurable differences under identical placement conditions. We provide the dataset online.

papers.title: A bound for Stieltjes constants of the Riemann zeta function
papers.abstract: The coefficients appearing in the Laurent expansion of the Riemann zeta function are known as the Stieltjes constants and are denoted by $\gamma_n$. Several authors, including Berndt, Matsuoka, Williams and Zhang, and Saad Eddin, have investigated upper bounds for $|\gamma_n|$, with the best known result due to Pauli and Saidak \cite{MR4671618}. In 2003, based on numerical evidence, Kreminski \cite{MR1972742} conjectured that Matsuoka's bound \cite{MR827790} could be considerably improved. Motivated by this conjecture, we employ the saddle-point method to derive an asymptotic formula for the Stieltjes constants, with the saddle point expressed explicitly in terms of the Lambert $W$-function. The resulting formula yields an asymptotic upper bound of the correct order of magnitude. Moreover, the resulting bound is consistent with the conjecture of Farr, Pauli, and Saidak \cite{MR4280128}.

papers.title: On the performance of the randomized Euler scheme for nonlinear ODEs under inexact information
papers.abstract: We analyze the randomized explicit Euler scheme for nonlinear ordinary differential equations under a local one-sided Lipschitz condition, local Hölder regularity in the space variable, and Hölder regularity in the time variable. We allow for noisy evaluations of the right-hand side. For the resulting approximation, we derive an error bound in which the contribution associated with the Hölder regularity in the time variable exhibits the characteristic 1/2-order gain of randomized methods. While existing results cover deterministic schemes under the one-sided Lipschitz condition and randomized schemes under the classical Lipschitz condition, our results combine randomized approximation and one-sided Lipschitz regularity.

papers.title: Linear and non-linear integro-differential equations with variable coefficients and Sonin kernels
papers.abstract: We study linear and non-linear integro-differential equations, with Sonin and absolutely continuous kernels, and with variable coefficients which are either integrable or continuous functions. In the linear case, for all cases, the unique solution is given explicitly by a convergent infinite series involving compositions of convolutions of the kernels and the variable coefficients. Many examples are provided. For the non-linear case, the existence and uniqueness are established under a suitable condition in the non-linear term. The analytic solution is given by the limit of the iterative sequence found from the method of successive approximations. The exact analytical expressions for several problems are found by computing the iterative sequences that approximate the solution.

papers.title: Path Integrals on Functional Lattices
papers.abstract: Path integrals in quantum field theory are commonly approached through finite-dimensional approximations, but existence and regulator independence of the infinite-dimensional limit require separate analysis. We introduce a scheme in which spacetime remains continuous and the field is expanded in a discrete complete family of localized functions, called a functional lattice. Truncation to finite-dimensional functional subspaces yields ordinary finite-dimensional integrals while leaving the continuum differential operator unchanged. For the massive free Euclidean scalar field, we prove convergence of the finite-dimensional covariance operators and normalized generating functionals by a Galerkin argument. The limit is independent of the compatible functional lattice: any sequence of finite-dimensional subspaces dense in the quadratic-form domain converges to the same continuum covariance and generating functional. A direct Minkowski construction is obtained at fixed Feynman regulator $i\epsilon$, followed by the distributional limit $\epsilon\downarrow0$. For interacting theories, each truncation gives an ordinary non-Gaussian integral. At fixed perturbative order, convergence follows when the finite-resolution graph integrands converge pointwise and admit an integrable majorant independent of the functional resolution. Numerical results for one-dimensional $\phi^4$ theory approach the known first- and second-order mass-gap coefficients, while four-dimensional calculations exhibit the expected mass divergence and logarithmic wave-function renormalization. Thus functional lattices provide a continuum-space approach to path integrals with mathematically controlled limits in the cases considered here.

papers.title: Mirror Descent at the Edge of Stability
papers.abstract: In many deep learning settings, gradient descent has been shown to operate at the edge of stability -- a regime where the largest eigenvalue of the loss Hessian hovers around $2/\eta$. We study this phenomenon in mirror descent, a generalization of gradient descent. As mirror descent is non-Euclidean, existing explanations of the edge of stability phase do not extend to this setting. We generalize the existing notion of sharpness to introduce mirror sharpness, which measures the curvature of the loss with respect to the mirror potential. Empirically, we observe that the mirror sharpness hovers slightly above the $2/\eta$ threshold. Furthermore, we derive a dual central flow ODE for mirror descent that models iterates in continuous time at the onset of edge of stability. Our ODE provides insights into the difficulties of extending existing arguments for why sharpness stabilizes at $2/\eta$ from gradient descent to mirror descent in full generality.

papers.title: An Exact Penalty Method for Large-Scale Equality-Constrained Nonlinear Optimization
papers.abstract: We present an exact penalty method for equality-constrained nonlinear optimization. Our approach transforms the smooth, constrained problem into a sequence of nonsmooth, unconstrained problems by penalizing the constraint violation by its Euclidean norm. An outer loop updates the penalty parameter and the subproblem tolerances, while an inner loop solves each penalized subproblem with a quadratic regularization method. The method also includes a local infeasibility detection mechanism, an extrapolation strategy for warm-starting subproblems, and nonmonotone acceptance rules. We establish global convergence to first-order stationary points under a bounded penalty parameter assumption, with a worst-case complexity of \(\mathcal{O}(|\log \epsilon|\,\epsilon^{-2})\) inner iterations. We implement the method in Penelopt, an open-source Julia solver for constrained nonlinear optimization. On \(224\) problems from the CUTEst collection, Penelopt is competitive with IPOPT and more robust than the recent solvers MadNLP and Uno. These results establish exact penalty methods as a practical alternative to conventional methods for solving equality-constrained nonlinear optimization problems. To the best of our knowledge, Penelopt is the first practical implementation of an exact penalty method for large-scale constrained nonlinear optimization.

papers.title: Speech Emotion Recognition Across Languages: Prosodic Patterns and Self-Supervised Learning
papers.abstract: This study investigates the prosodic patterns of emotional speech across Chinese (CN), German (DE), and English (EN), with a focus on acoustic characteristics. Using ANOVA and mixed-effects modeling, we reveal cross-linguistic and emotion-specific prosodic patterns. A comparative analysis of Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) performance demonstrates that humans outperform Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) models in cross-lingual tasks, while SSL models show significant improvement in cross-lingual SER through an efficient fine-tuning process, achieving performance competitive with native human speakers. The study also analyzes the performance of Speech Emotion Diarization (SED) between models and humans, highlighting the effectiveness of SSL models in transfer learning scenarios. These findings emphasize the interplay between universal prosodic features (e.g., intensity, pitch) and language-specific factors. Moreover, the SSL model's outstanding performance indicates the potential value of these acoustic features in emotion processing, implying possible advancements in cross-lingual emotion recognition through refined training techniques.

papers.title: Distributed Interactive Conformal Prediction for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems increasingly rely on learning-enabled components and distributed algorithms for perception, estimation, and control, introducing uncertainty that makes it challenging to satisfy mission requirements. Conformal prediction quantifies uncertainty with distribution-free guarantees, but existing methods do not address the challenging combination of dependence among robots, distributed calibration, and the distribution shift induced when calibrated uncertainty bounds modify the closed-loop system. We introduce Multi-Agent Interactive Conformal Prediction (MA-ICP), a distributed framework for computing robustness margins in heterogeneous systems to satisfy mission requirements with high probability. MA-ICP aggregates robot-level nonconformity scores, which measure errors in modeled or estimated quantities, into one mission-level score per robot class, allowing dependence among robots within each mission. Mission-level scores and quantiles are computed using neighbor-to-neighbor communication in a finite number of communication rounds. Updating the robustness margins changes robot trajectories and distributed algorithm outputs, so we use class-dependent score sensitivities to upper bound the shift in mission-level scores. We then establish calibration-conditional coverage guarantees per robot class for the updated margins. We demonstrate MA-ICP on cooperative payload control, formation control with obstacle avoidance, and distributed target tracking missions.

papers.title: Optical Motion Sensing for Piezoelectric-Resonator-Based Power Converters
papers.abstract: Piezoelectric components present a promising alternative to conventional magnetics for miniaturized, high-frequency power converters. While high-Q piezoelectric resonators have demonstrated high efficiencies and large power densities in prototype high-frequency dc-dc converters, their optimal operating conditions are sensitive to temperature fluctuations and load variations. Therefore, robust closed-loop control is essential for practical deployment. Electrical approaches for sensing motional current may compromise the electrical isolation and electromagnetic interference (EMI) immunity inherently provided by the mechanical nature of these resonators. Here, we present an optical motion sensing approach for piezoelectric power converters. The optical sensing system comprises a laser, fiber optics, and a photodetector. The proposed approach uses optical interference to monitor the mechanical displacement in real time. The resulting optical signal carries both the amplitude and phase of the mechanical motion, which are necessary for closed-loop control. We experimentally characterize and validate this optical motion sensing approach using a 45-kHz piezoelectric resonator driven by a GaN half bridge with input voltages up to 45 V. We further experimentally demonstrate closed-loop control using the proposed optical motion sensing for a 99-kHz isolated piezoelectric converter. These initial results establish a viable pathway toward optically closed-loop control of piezoelectric power converters.

papers.title: Automorphism groups of Severi--Brauer varieties of odd prime degree over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that the only non-trivial finite subgroup of automorphism group of non-trivial Severi--Brauer variety of odd prime degree $p$ over the field of rational numbers is $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}.$

papers.title: A Calculus Gradient: Child Poverty, Mathematics Preparation, and First-Year College Performance at a Hispanic-Serving University
papers.abstract: The San Antonio metropolitan area has one of the highest poverty rates among large U.S. metropolitan areas. Within Bexar County, where the city is located, child poverty varies widely across school districts. We link entrants of the city's public research university, a broad-access Hispanic-Serving Institution, to their sending schools and districts, and examine their preparation scores and first-year outcomes. Across the nation's school districts, enrollment in widely taken core courses (Algebra II, Geometry, Biology) shows little relation to child poverty, while enrollment in Calculus and Advanced Placement mathematics and science is far lower where child poverty is higher, nationally and within Bexar County. Among linked entrants, mathematics preparation differs with the school and district. Entrants with stronger mathematics preparation earn higher first-year grades in nearly every subject. Most entrants who do not return after the first year had unsuccessful courses, and mathematics is the largest single source of those outcomes. Among students who change major, mathematics is one of the subjects with grades furthest below their own averages. Within the same course and term, larger mathematics sections go with more unsuccessful outcomes for entrants with lower mathematics preparation, which identifies a hypothesis for testing smaller sections. Recorded between Fall 2014 and Fall 2019, these outcomes offer a reference point for change after the pandemic, test-optional admissions, and generative artificial intelligence. The analysis is reproducible; adapting it elsewhere requires local definitions and linkage validation. All results are associations among the students of one institution; establishing causes would require a designed study.

papers.title: Parallel batch scheduling for optimizing hospital sterilization operations: arc-flow formulations, column generation and Lagrangian heuristics for flowtime minimization
papers.abstract: In a recent work by Schlembach et al., the problem of optimally managing sterilization operations in hospitals has been modeled as a machine scheduling problem with parallel batch processing and minimum flowtime objective, and heuristically solved by column generation. We draw upon this approach, developing arc-flow formulations and related column-generation procedures, using an exact dynamic programming algorithm to solve the pricing problems. We further derive Lagrangian relaxations based on minimum cost flows and shortest paths, with subgradient optimization and the volume algorithm guiding batch generation. A makespan bound for schedules minimizing total flow time provides a finite horizon when no operational limit is known. Computational experiments on literature benchmarks and more challenging generated instances demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches. The arc-flow model solves all literature benchmark instances to proven optimality within seconds, while the Lagrangian heuristics deliver high-quality schedules with substantially reduced computational effort.

papers.title: 3D-EMCAD: Efficient Multi-scale Convolutional Attention Decoding for Volumetric Brain Tumor Segmentation
papers.abstract: Encoder-decoder networks are widely used for volumetric brain tumor segmentation, yet recent trends favor high-capacity decoders that incur steep computational costs in 3D at high spatial resolutions. The Efficient Multi-scale Convolutional Attention Decoder (EMCAD) is a lightweight decoder that achieves strong accuracy at very low cost, but it has been validated only in 2D. Here, we extend EMCAD to volumetric segmentation (3D-EMCAD) by converting all operations to 3D and replacing standard normalization layers with group normalization to suit the small batch sizes of volumetric training. To isolate the impact of decoder choice, we evaluate five decoders: the proposed 3D-EMCAD, a vanilla SegResNet decoder, an Attention U-Net decoder, UNet++, and a plain U-Net decoder using an identical 3D SegResNet encoder and training protocol on BraTS 2020 (369 cases, three-fold cross-validation). The five decoders yield statistically indistinguishable performance: their mean Dice scores span only 0.0071, less than the fold-to-fold variation of most models, and a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test shows no significant difference between 3D-EMCAD and three of the four baselines. Importantly, 3D-EMCAD achieves this shared accuracy with the fewest decoder parameters (1.15 M) and operations (8.6 G), requiring $7.3\times$ fewer operations than UNet++, which scores no higher. These findings demonstrate that decoder capacity beyond a modest budget offers no measurable benefit for volumetric brain tumor segmentation.

papers.title: Multi-Sensor Fusion for False-Alarm Reduction by Timed Electromechanical Corroboration
papers.abstract: A physician checks the clinical electrocardiogram against other observations. A wearable monitor has no physician. This paper shows that a mechanical sensor worn beside the electrocardiogram can take over that check, and that the right added sensors lower false alarms further. A beat is accepted only when a mechanical contraction follows at the delay learned for the wearer. Beat-shaped artifacts injected into resting and exercise recordings passed the electrocardiogram alone almost every time. A seismocardiogram or phonocardiogram as the second channel rejected most while keeping nearly all true beats, strongly at rest and partly during exercise. Shifting the mechanical signal in time removed the benefit. A detection criterion scores an added sensor by the part of its response that the sensors in place cannot predict. With four sensors, this score ranked the sets as their measured false-alarm rates did. With the two sensors it selected, 6.2 percent of the artifacts passed while 95 percent of true beats were kept, half the rate of the best single sensor. In integer arithmetic on a low-cost microcontroller, the detector made the same decisions as the software. These rates come from injected artifacts, not alarms in patients. Natural motion and clinical events remain untested.

papers.title: The marginal sine-Gordon field theory
papers.abstract: At $\beta_*^2=8\pi$ we construct the two-dimensional sine--Gordon vacuum from a noncompact real lattice field with nearest-neighbor kinetic energy, positive cosine activity and zero Dirichlet data. Its mass $M$ is the lower edge of the energy spectrum above the vacuum. In units of the length $a_{\rm exit}$ at which the flow leaves weak coupling it obeys $0<c_-\le M a_{\rm exit}\le c_+<\infty$ on compact positive endpoint intervals, with uniform constants. A prescribed response to a smooth background in a fixed square determines the nonlinear asymptotically free bare parameters at each sufficiently fine cutoff. In the local relativistic continuum theory the vacuum is unique, physical dilation realizes every positive mass, and literal derivatives generate the reflected Hilbert space even for finite composite and contact families. Variance and exponential moments of a derivative smear rule out a Gaussian law. A connected correlation of some finite even order above two is nonzero on separated supports. The construction gives universality for the specified finite nonnegative higher harmonics, the field equation, topological current and geometric stress tensor with their Ward, trace and contact identities, and a normalized source-transfer theorem with explicit finite-scale hypotheses.

papers.title: Convergence analysis of resonant frequency approximation in periodic Helmholtz problems
papers.abstract: We investigate resonant frequencies of the Helmholtz equation in periodic structures under quasi-periodic conditions, using approximations of the associated quasi-periodic Green function, which is represented by a lattice sum. By formulating the periodic Helmholtz problem using layer potential operators whose kernel is given by the quasi-periodic Green function, resonant frequencies correspond to characteristic values of an associated operator-valued function. Based on two approximation methods for the quasi-periodic Green function, the Ewald method and the shifted Green function method, we propose the corresponding approximation schemes for resonant frequencies. Furthermore, we establish convergence rates for the resulting approximations using Gohberg--Sigal theory, where the Ewald method yields exponential convergence, while the shifted Green function method yields algebraic convergence. Numerical computations are presented to validate and compare the proposed approximation schemes.

papers.title: Suppressing Chaos Without Silencing Excitable Oscillators
papers.abstract: A negative Lyapunov exponent is not a sufficient goal for controlling an excitable oscillator. A gain can remove chaos by removing the excitation that the model is meant to keep. This manuscript studies that failure mode in three models: the forced FitzHugh--Nagumo neuron, the forced Aliev--Panfilov cardiac cell, and the autonomous Hindmarsh--Rose neuron. Chaos is measured by the largest state Lyapunov exponent. Excitation is measured by threshold crossings, by the excursion of the fast variable, and by the firing rate. Recovery damping, tracking of an unstable periodic orbit, Pyragas delayed feedback, and a change of the fast time scale are compared on the same chaotic regimes. In the forced models, large damping and large rate changes reach regularity by silencing the cell, while tracking and delayed feedback keep firing. In the autonomous model, recovery damping raises the firing rate several-fold instead. A classical matrix-measure bound links these outcomes to the channel through which the gain acts. A constant-metric contraction certificate coexists with substantial firing only under tracking, which subtracts a gain from the fast direction.

papers.title: Wet-part doubling for log-concave probability measures
papers.abstract: Let $\mu$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geqslant 2$. We study the growth of $w_\mu(t)=\mu(\{x:q_{\mu}(x)\leqslant t\})$, where $q_{\mu}$ is the Tukey half-space depth function of $\mu$. We prove that $w_{\mu}$ satisfies the doubling bound $$w_\mu(\lambda t)\leqslant C^n\lambda\left(1+\frac{\log\lambda}{n-1}\right)^{n-1}w_\mu(t)$$ for every $\lambda>1$ and $0<t<1/\lambda$, where $C>0$ is an absolute constant. It follows that for every $\varepsilon>0$ we may write $w_\mu(\lambda t) \leqslant A_\varepsilon^n \lambda^{1+\varepsilon}w_\mu(t)$ for some constant $A_\varepsilon>0$. We construct a family of symmetric log-concave measures in every dimension $n\geqslant2$ showing that no linear doubling bound with a dimension-dependent constant holds uniformly over this class. The proof of the doubling bound uses a pointwise comparison of half-space depth with the Cramér transform, dual radial coordinates, and a relative entropy estimate for transverse covariance determinants.

papers.title: The Dunford-Pettis property and complemented Hilbert subspaces of Sobolev martingale spaces
papers.abstract: Let $L^1_W$ be the space of integrable terminal values of martingales on a homogeneous tree whose local differences belong to a fixed matrix space $W$. We show that $L^1_W$ has the Dunford-Pettis property if and only if $W$ is spanned by its rank-one matrices. Every complemented reflexive subspace of $L^1_W$ is isomorphic to a Hilbert space. Under the second structural condition of Ayoush, Stolyarov and Wojciechowski, the martingale fractional integral of order $\frac12$ is completely continuous and fails to be absolutely $2$-summing. This gives nonisomorphism with $L^1$ for $W\ne0$. On the $4$-ary tree we exhibit all three possible combinations of the Dunford-Pettis property and the existence of a complemented copy of $\ell^2$. In one example a bounded operator into $\ell^4$ fails to be completely continuous, although every bounded operator into a Hilbert space is completely continuous. We also prove that, for every $n\ge1$, each complemented reflexive subspace of $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{T}^n)$ is isomorphic to a Hilbert space.

papers.title: Efficient phase-only wavefront shaping at 250 kHz for multimode fiber endomicroscopy
papers.abstract: Wavefront shaping through multimode fibers (MMFs) enables diffraction-limited fluorescence imaging with hair-thin probes, at a speed and light budget bounded by the wavefront modulator. Existing modulators provide at most two of three key characteristics: high refresh rate, (high) modal dimensionality, and light efficiency. Here, we demonstrate wavefront control through an MMF using a tailored phase-only microelectromechanical modulator that combines all three, with 8,192 elements arranged in a 32 x 256 array, 7-bit phase control, and a 250 kHz full-frame refresh rate. Direct on-axis phase modulation delivers 70+/-5% of the incident light into the modulated field and eliminates both off-axis encoding optical losses and hologram computation. The generated foci at the distal end of the fiber remain isotropic with high fidelity. We use singular-value decomposition analysis of the measured transmission to identify the effective degrees of freedom of our system. By scanning the focus at multiple depths, we demonstrate volumetric fluorescence imaging. These results open a new operating regime for adaptive in vivo multimode-fiber endoscopy.

papers.title: Economic cap coverings for log-concave measures
papers.abstract: Let $\mu$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Write $q_\mu$ for its half-space depth, $W_t=\{q_\mu \leqslant t\}$ for its wet part, and $w_\mu(t)=\mu(W_t)$. For sufficiently small $t$, we construct a cover of $W_t$ by half-spaces of measure at most $A_nt$, with cardinality bounded by $$D_n\frac{w_\mu(t)-w_\mu(a_nt)}{t},$$ where the constants depend only on $n$. For each $0<\varepsilon\leqslant 1$ we also construct a cover by half-spaces of measure at most $(1+\varepsilon)t$, with cardinality bounded by $$B_n\varepsilon^{-(n-1)/2}\frac{w_\mu(t)-w_\mu(a_nt)}{t}.$$ The exponent $(n-1)/2$ is optimal for $n\geqslant 2$, as shown by the Gaussian example. We further establish containment coverings for half-spaces in every dimension: there is a family of $O_n(w_\mu(t)/t)$ Borel covering sets, each of $\mu$-measure $O_n(t)$, such that every half-space of measure at most $t$ is contained in one covering set. We also obtain a relative wet-part estimate with sharp exponent $2/(n+1)$ and a reverse doubling inequality.

papers.title: Parallel Two-Photon Lithography: From Optical Nonlinearities to Energy Limits, Dose Control and Throughput Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Two-photon lithography (TPL) prints three-dimensional polymer architectures with sub-diffraction features, but writing them voxel by voxel limits its throughput. This review examines how parallelization overcomes this limit with fixed multi-focus arrays, reconfigurable holography using spatial light modulators and digital micromirror devices, hybrid metalens arrays, shaped beams, temporally focused projection and two-step absorption. An energy-deposition framework built on measured nonlinear absorption coefficients shows how the absorption order and coefficients of a resist determine its voxel size, energy per voxel and attainable voxel rate. Applied to parallel writing, the framework quantifies the costs of non-uniform foci, coherent crosstalk between foci, side-lobe losses in shaped beams and weaker axial confinement in projection. Published systems reach peak rates above $10^{8}$ voxels s$^{-1}$ with scanned focus arrays and up to $1.7\times10^{9}$ voxels s$^{-1}$ with grayscale projection under a fine-voxel definition, and parallel features as small as 20-55 nm. As rates rise, however, dose uniformity, proximity effects, heat, stitching and data bandwidth increasingly limit fidelity. A minimum reporting standard that includes the energy per voxel and sustained part-level rates is therefore proposed, together with priorities for the field: shared benchmark parts, predictive dose control and resists designed for parallel writing.

papers.title: Scale-dependent Dark Matter in a Multi-component Cosmological Framework: Distinct Components Governing Galactic and Cosmological Dynamics
Spin-geodesic systems
papers.abstract: We introduce and study a class of geometric dynamical systems on Riemannian manifolds called spin-geodesic systems, in which the motion of a point is coupled to an internal classical spin through a symmetric endomorphism field $B$, the spin-coupling field. These systems may be viewed as $B$-dependent deformations of geodesic motion and have connections with frame flows, magnetic geodesic flows, and nonholonomic rolling systems. We show that every spin-geodesic system admits an equivalent interpretation as a no-slip rolling system in an abstract ambient geometry; when the associated metric connection, determined by $B$, is flat, this construction reduces, under the usual integrability hypotheses, to ordinary rolling on a Euclidean hypersurface. Our second main result is a Liouville theorem: for an arbitrary symmetric spin-coupling field B, the spin-geodesic flow preserves the canonical Liouville volume on its mechanical phase space. This holds even though the flow is not symplectic unless $B$ is identically zero.

papers.title: A Candidate twin-spine photon model in MacCullagh's medium
papers.abstract: We model the vacuum as a rotationally elastic continuum, a low-energy electromagnetic approximation to the deformable spacetime metric of General Relativity. MacCullagh's single-parameter action yields the source-free Maxwell equations from resistance to twist, without separately postulating electric and magnetic fields. We show that a transversely localized field propagating rigidly at $c$ requires line defects; the minimal finite configuration is a twin-spine photon with two opposing displacement-current cores. It propagates without loss or transverse stress and admits linear and circular geometries with angular momentum $0$ or $\pm\hbar$. In a birefringent crystal, differential wave speeds reshape the shared spine trajectory, producing a continuous macroscopic torque without invoking superposed phase-delayed plane waves. For emission, we model the electron as a bound topological defect with a $\pi$-twist phase condition. Transverse acceleration shears its co-moving bow wave; the vacuum wave equation directs the residual dipole strain into twin-spine geometry, while the phase condition supplies a quantizing boundary condition. An accompanying SymPy Executable Research Record distinguishes postulated topology from derived mechanics.

papers.title: Finite-Temperature Stabilization of a KKLT Modulus in Three-Dimensional Lattice Simulations
The coordinate dependence of numerical rank: charts adapted to level sets
papers.abstract: Sampling a smooth field on a grid can give an array of high numerical rank even when the field is simple. A Gaussian ridge rotated off the grid axes is the standard example: in coordinates which follow the ridge, the same field has rank one. The rank therefore depends on the chart, that is, on the coordinates in which the field is sampled. We ask which properties of a chart control this rank. For a field which depends on position only through a function $\phi$, a chart whose coordinate lines follow the level sets of $\phi$ gives rank one. Building on this, we show four things. First, mesh quality does not control rank: a chart whose cells have perfect size and shape can still give infinite rank. Second, when a chart follows the level sets of an estimate of $\phi$, the extra rank depends on a single quantity, the defect, which measures how much the true field varies along each coordinate line. Its size matters only logarithmically, its complexity through a count which cannot be improved in general, and when the defect is simple across the level sets the cost stays small. Third, whether the defect is simple can be checked by differentiating the true level function along the flow which builds the chart. Fourth, rank and invertibility fail differently. When the curve behind an offset chart is perturbed, the rank grows slowly, but the chart stops being invertible abruptly, once the offset exceeds the distance at which neighboring normals of the curve first cross. A chart built from the level sets of a field estimate stays invertible when the gradient of the estimate does not vanish on the band and the coordinate lines along each level set do not cross themselves. Pre-registered experiments in two dimensions show how far the bounds are from the observed ranks, and suggest when each kind of chart is preferable; two choices in the last comparison were made after the experiments.

papers.title: A Principled Framework for PDE-Based Shock Capturing in High-Order Discontinuous Galerkin Methods
papers.abstract: PDE-based artificial viscosity (AV) captures shocks in high-order discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods by solving an auxiliary PDE for a smooth viscosity field. The behavior of that field is set by how the terms of the AV PDE scale with the element size $h$ and polynomial degree $p$, and by how its coefficients are parametrized. This work derives both choices from analysis and studies the impact these choices have on the implicit steady-state solver. First, an $L^2$-projection analysis shows that the thinnest shock a polynomial space can represent monotonically scales with the resolution length $\bar h = h/p$, and a scaling analysis of the AV PDE gives concrete conditions on its diffusion and source terms for the solution to be self-similar in $\bar h$. Prior formulations satisfy them only under $h$-refinement at fixed $p$; the AV PDE is scaled so that they hold under $hp$-refinement, and the captured shock thins accordingly. Second, a Green's-function analysis of the steady AV PDE gives closed-form expressions for the width and magnitude of the AV. In the standard parametrization the two are coupled: raising the diffusion coefficient widens the AV but lowers its peak. An alternative parametrization of the decay coefficient removes the coupling in the Green's-function response and inverts it in the coupled state-AV problem, so that widening the AV raises its peak instead of lowering it. Third, a parameter study on a Mach 5 viscous flow over a half-cylinder characterizes how the choice of solution variables and the AV PDE's time, width, and magnitude coefficients affect the robustness and cost of the implicit solve. The choice of variables dominates robustness, with entropy variables converging over the largest region of the width-magnitude parameter space. Together, the three contributions make PDE-based AV more predictable to tune and its implicit solve more robust.

papers.title: Trigonal Elliptic Coordinates on the Sphere and Some Applications
papers.abstract: We construct a theta-function parametrization of the unit sphere adapted to the eight trigonal directions. The construction follows from a cubic theta identity discussed by Bobek and admits an equivalent representation in Jacobi elliptic functions. The angular parameter and theta nome give a nonorthogonal coordinate system whose squared Cartesian components are related to the three-component Volterra chain. An algebraic change of angle, retaining the nome, yields orthogonal coordinates with explicit metric coefficients and a diagonal Laplace--Beltrami operator. We apply both parametrizations to the geometry of O'Brien's reduced Jahn--Teller model and give compact expressions for real spherical harmonics of degrees two and three. The orthogonal angle is the polar angle of an $E_g$ quadrupolar doublet, while one octupolar harmonic depends only on the nome within each octant.

papers.title: Anti-de Sitter charges and maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We construct conserved charges of asymptotic symmetries for negative-cosmological-constant vacuum spacetimes from the Neumann data for the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints on maximal conformally-compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. This gives a general and canonical initial value treatment of charges for vacuum spacetimes with timelike conformal boundary.

papers.title: On derived Galois deformation rings in characteristic 0 and a conjecture of Venkatesh
papers.abstract: Let $\Pi$ be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of $\operatorname{GL}_n$ over a CM field $F$, and $\rho$ its associated Galois representation in characteristic 0. With mild assumptions, we use the Taylor--Wiles method to define a free action of the potentially semistable derived deformation ring of $\rho$ on the $\Pi$-part of the $p$-adic cohomology of $\operatorname{GL}_n/F$, confirming a prediction of Venkatesh. As a key step, we establish an equivalence between the derived deformation ring of $\rho$ with the completion at the point corresponding to $\rho$ of the derived deformation ring of the mod $p$ reduction $\bar{\rho}$, generalising well-known results by Kisin.

papers.title: Perfect state transfer on trees in the normalized Laplacian quantum walk
papers.abstract: We prove that, in the normalized-Laplacian model, perfect state transfer between two vertices of a tree can only happen if they are at distance at most $2$. We show that a conjecture of Coutinho and Baptista, stating that the only trees admitting perfect state transfer are $K_2$ and $P_3$, is true when the two vertices are at odd distance. We then construct infinite families of trees admitting perfect state transfer, disproving their conjecture in the general case.

papers.title: Probabilistic Inversion of Strong Gravitational Lenses with Flow Matching Priors
Achievable Rate and Reconstruction Fidelity of FeFET-Based Compute-in-Pixel Arrays
papers.abstract: Compute-in-pixel (CiP) image sensors such as MACPix weight each photodiode voltage by a conductance stored in a ferroelectric FET and sum the currents on a column bus, so that $N$ pixels are read as $M<N$ weighted sums before digitization. We model the column bus as a Gaussian multiple-access channel and derive its achievable rate under thermal and shot noise, device variation, and ADC distortion. Conductance variation acts as noise proportional to the scene energy, which limits the rate to $4.5$ bits per readout and makes a 6-bit ADC sufficient. End-to-end simulations recover natural images at $26.3$ dB from 2 bits per pixel and, for sparse scenes, reduce the edge-node energy by up to $6.4\times$ against raw 8-bit readout.

papers.title: Improved Omega results for Riesz sums of a class of $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We investigate a general class of $L$-functions satisfying functional equations with multiple gamma factors, and establish sharper lower bounds for the error terms associated with the Riesz sums of their coefficients. By integrating the resonance method with Riesz smoothing, we improve upon previously known omega results for the corresponding Riesz sums. We prove these estimates within a unified axiomatic framework under a precise set of hypotheses. Our general theorem can be applied to several classical arithmetic problems, including the $k$-fold Piltz divisor function $d_{\mathbb{K},k}(n)$ over a number field $\mathbb{K}$, as well as the lattice point counting functions for the circle, ellipse, and sphere problems. In particular, we sharpen the classical $\Omega$-bound for the error in counting lattice points in the ellipse $u^2+5v^2\le x$, strengthening a result of Nowak. Moreover, for the smoothed error terms corresponding to the divisor and circle problems, we improve upon previously known $\Omega$-bounds by increasing the exponent of the $\log\log x$ factor and sharpening the $\log\log\log x$ dependence by replacing exponential decay factors of the form $\exp(-c\sqrt{\log\log\log x})$ in previous results with an explicit polynomial power of $\log\log\log x$.

papers.title: Observation of nonadiabatic quantum tunneling in a driven correlated insulator
Elliptic curves with torsion Z/5: exact rank four over Q(k) and rank at least five infinitely often
papers.abstract: We give two elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}(k)$ with torsion group $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank exactly $4$, with four explicit independent points. The upper bounds come from reducing the relevant elliptic surfaces modulo suitable primes and are unconditional. They match the known lower bound for the generic rank with this torsion, due to Eroshkin, and are not isomorphic to Eroshkin's curve or to each other: their parametrising maps to $X_1(5)$ have degree $8$ instead of $12$, the constructions are dihedral rather than biquadratic, and their branch loci differ. In each case, two of the points come from a ``doubling'' step in the spirit of Jaswal. Adding one further condition to the second curve, coming from a quadratic twist over an intermediate conic, gives a fifth independent point over a genus-one curve of rank two. Hence there are infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank at least $5$, improving the known bound $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 4$ to $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 5$.

papers.title: Handed Ultrafast Dynamics in Chiral Cyanine Nanotubes
papers.abstract: We detect helicity-dependent excited state relaxation in a chiral exciton system. Using L-histidine as a chiral inducer, we prepared unbundled, double-walled J-aggregrate nanotubes of an amphiphilic cyanine dye with a net handedness, which gives a large circular dichroism dissymmetry factor ($g_{abs} = 3.6 \times 10^{-2}$). With two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy and circularly polarized pump pulses, we find that the relaxation rates of longitudinal excitons depend on pump helicity (4.5 $ps^{-1}$ for $\langle \textit{RRXX} \rangle$ vs 6 $ps^{-1}$ for $\langle \textit{LLXX} \rangle$, a difference of about 30%) and is the same in the inner and outer tubes. Transverse excitons show no significant dependence. Chirality and pump helicity therefore bias exciton relaxation on the femtosecond timescale for excitons delocalized along the helical structure.

papers.title: Validating Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations with Close Visual Binaries
Limit theorems for almost conditionally identically distributed random variables
papers.abstract: $\xi$-Almost Conditional Identically Distributed ($\xi$-a.c.i.d.) random variables are generalizations of conditional identically distributed (c.i.d.) and exchangeable ones. $\xi$-a.c.i.d. random variables arise naturally in applications in statistics, such as in recursive algorithms and heteroskedastic observations, and are parametrized by a sequence $\xi=(\xi_{n})_{n\geq 0}$ that quantifies departure from the c.i.d. property. In this work, we extend limit theorems for exchangeable and c.i.d. random variables to the more general setting of $\xi$-a.c.i.d. random variables. After proving a Strong Law of Large Numbers, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the asymptotic directing measure of the sequence to be absolutely continuous with respect to a given $\sigma$-finite measure. Then, under regularity assumptions on the parameter $\xi$, three different Central Limit Theorems for $\xi$-a.c.i.d. sequences are derived, involving the predictive, empirical and asymptotic directing distributions. These theorems have several statistical applications, including the construction of asymptotic credible intervals in Bayesian predictive inference.

papers.title: On locked states for damped driven Jaynes--Cummings equations
papers.abstract: We consider damped driven version of the Jaynes-Cummings equation which describes quantised one-mode Maxwell field coupled to a two-level molecule. The pumping and dissipation operator are polynomial in the creation and annihilation operators. The structure of the dissipation operator corresponds to the theory of completely positive trace preserving operators due to Lindblad, Kossakowski and others. We construct examples of {\it locked states} which are stationary states of the corresponding averaged dynamics in the interaction picture. The states are nonnegative Hermitian density operators with finite Hilbert-Schmidt norm. The calculations rely on the recurrence equation for diagonal entries.

papers.title: Estimating Extrapolation Factors in Time-Resolved Crystallography
papers.abstract: Time-resolved crystallography (TRX) captures macromolecules in action, but a triggered crystal contains a mixture of triggered proteins in an unknown state and untriggered proteins in the reference state. Separating these is necessary to isolate the dynamics of interest and is an underdetermined data-analysis task. For the simplest case, with one triggered state and one reference state, a range of methods exists, but their assumptions, accuracy, and domains of applicability have not been systematically investigated. Here, we deconstruct and review the methods in current use, employing a unified notation. We make their assumptions explicit and benchmark each on a simulated dataset. A key point is that many of these methods do not estimate the fraction of all triggered molecules in the crystal, but instead estimate a latent parameter we call the extrapolation factor, which is related to but distinct from the so-called "occupancy". As our simulations make apparent, current methods do not always yield accurate results, in particular with noisy data and when the fraction of triggered protein is low. Inspired by previous work, we introduce Vacuum Level Matching, a method that grounds the estimate in the physical constraint that electron density is a nonnegative quantity: it cannot fall below a vacuum level. Operating voxel by voxel, Vacuum Level Matching replaces the manual choices of previous methods with a data-driven procedure and reports quality-control metrics that flag data unable to support a confident prediction. On the same simulated data, it outperforms state-of-the-art methods, and on two experimental datasets, rsEGFP2 and a multi-time-point photolyase series, it recovers known structural changes while flagging issues where the data are weak. Finally, we report an implementation of Vacuum Level Matching in the form of a small, reusable Python package.

papers.title: Systematically improvable semiclassical clustering for accurate and efficient quantum dynamics in large spin ensembles
Exotic Universal Covers and Free Cyclic Actions from the Cartwright-Steger Surface
papers.abstract: For every $m\geq2$, we construct a closed minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $35$, and signature $1$. The construction is a genus-five symplectic sum of a blowup of the regular fourfold Cartwright-Steger cover and a cyclic Akhmedov-Park manifold. The gluing identifies the homomorphisms from the two surface groups to $\Z/m$. The universal cover is minimal symplectic and is homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $(18m-1)\CP\#(17m-1)\CPb$. It admits a free symplectic action of $\Z/m$. Intermediate quotients give examples with fundamental group $\Z/n$ and characteristic numbers $(e,\sigma)=(35k,k)$ for every $n\geq2$ and $k\geq1$. Using the same Cartwright-Steger summand, we also construct, for every $m\geq2$, a minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $31$, and signature $1$, whose minimal symplectic universal cover is an exotic copy of $(16m-1)\CP\#(15m-1)\CPb$ with a free symplectic $\Z/m$-action.

papers.title: The Z[tau]-foam: Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam as arithmetic in the icosahedral module
papers.abstract: Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam is a substitution that fills the regular dodecahedron with dodecahedral bubbles of sizes tau^{-k}, tau=(1+sqrt(5))/2, using the seven kinds of cells into which the twelve planes of its stellation cut it. We rewrite it as exact arithmetic in one Z[tau]-module of rank three, the span M of the six five-fold axes, on which the icosahedral group acts by 120 matrices in GL(3,Z[tau]). A placed inflated copy of a cell is a union of cells iff its facet levels lie in {+-1,+-tau^3} and it lies in the dodecahedron. Solving this finite linear system for all scales at once gives exactly the 22 rules known from a geometric search; no rule exists at any scale other than 1,tau,tau^2,tau^3. The substitution becomes integer arithmetic on six-tuples and reproduces the bubbles of the geometric foam exactly. Whether a point of M is the centre of a bubble of size tau^{-k} is decided by at most k+3 exact sign vectors (its address), without building the foam, and all bubbles of one size are obtained by sieving the points of M whose Galois conjugate satisfies |x^*|<=2 tau^k, a bound we prove with computer assistance. The number of bubbles of size tau^{-k} is A beta^k+O(|beta'|^k) with beta=(1+sqrt(29))/2. Hence the closure of the rescaled conjugates of the bubble centres has box dimension at most log_tau(beta)=2.4123<3, and the bubbles are not selected by any cut-and-project window with interior. The other foams of the 1999 article are sub-foams of this one. The 50400 substitutions allowed by the rule list give 18899 bubble sets, and the Dodecafoam is a product set of 13440 of them, to the depth tested. In four dimensions the same linear system, for the star cut of the 120-cell, reproduces the 718 clusters of a geometric search and adds the scale sqrt(5) tau^2.

papers.title: Nonparametric estimation of a common marginal hazard function under censoring and spatio-temporal dependence
papers.abstract: This article investigates the nonparametric estimation of a common pooled marginal hazard function from right-censored durations exhibiting spatio-temporal dependence. We propose two estimators based respectively on the Nadaraya-Watson method and the (k)-nearest neighbors (k)-NN) approach. Under assumptions of stationarity, regularity, non-informative censoring, and weak spatio-temporal dependence, we establish their pointwise and uniform convergence rates as well as their optimal asymptotic order. A simulation study compares their finite-sample performance. Two real-data applications with right censoring are considered: a multicenter clinical trial with 53.8 percent censoring and 1,746 geolocated and time-stamped requests submitted to New York City's 311 municipal service, of which 35.5 percent are censored. The empirical results illustrate the relevance of the proposed methods in the presence of spatial and temporal dependence.

papers.title: Nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in {-1,0,1}
papers.abstract: We determine all nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$. The problem reduces to describing the set $\cN_n$ of pairs $(d,b)\in\{-1,0,1\}^n\times\{-1,1\}^{n-1}$ for which the tridiagonal matrices with diagonal $d$ and with products $b_k$ of opposite off-diagonal entries have characteristic polynomial $\lambda^n$. We show that $\cN_n$ is obtained from $\cN_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ by one of two explicit ``folding'' operations, according to the parity of $n$. As a consequence, $\cN_n$ is non-empty precisely when $n=1$ or $3\cdot2^j-1\le n\le2^{j+2}-1$ for some $j\ge0$, in which case it has $2^{\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$ elements. This yields a formula for the number of nilpotent $n\times n$ tridiagonal matrices with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$, which begins $1,9,73,585,4809,39113$. The case $d=0$ is a conjecture of Corless, established in an earlier paper. The main new ingredient is a rigidity phenomenon: a pair as above, of size $n\ge2$, whose characteristic polynomial is congruent to $\lambda^n$ modulo $4$ is necessarily a fold of a smaller pair. It follows that such a pair is nilpotent as soon as its characteristic polynomial is congruent to $\lambda^n$ modulo $2^{1+\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$. Finally we show that the eigenvalue zero of an $m\times m$ matrix in Corless's skew-symmetric family has multiplicity at most $2^{v_2(m+1)}-1$, with equality attained. The classification, the rigidity statement, the cardinality of the sets $\cN_n$ and the criterion modulo $2^{1+\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$ have been formalised in Lean~4.

papers.title: AI-generated support, worked examples, and script-based learning in undergraduate physics: A comparative study
papers.abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used to support students during learning and problem solving, but its instructional value depends on how it is embedded in established learning approaches. Worked examples guide learners through the steps and reasoning of a solution; conversational AI may extend them by responding to individual questions. To isolate this added value, we compared a chatbot-delivered intelligent worked example with a matched static worked example and a lecture script. Nine recitation groups in an undergraduate electrodynamics course were cluster-randomized to the three conditions, and 86 students worked individually on a Gauss's law problem. Concept-test accuracy and self-efficacy increased significantly in all conditions, but changes did not differ significantly between groups (p=.07 for concept-test accuracy and p=.38 for self-efficacy). Four weeks later, in a reduced sample with selective participation and pre-existing group differences, students in the static worked-example condition scored higher than those in the script condition (p=.004, d=1.22), whereas the two worked-example conditions did not differ significantly. Usability, but not perceived educational value, was higher for the intelligent worked example than for the script (p=.011, d=0.88). In a subsequent homework assignment on Ampere's law with free choice of learning material (N=46), 62-71% of students in each condition reported using only the static worked example, at most 8% used exclusively the intelligent one, and 15-31% used neither. Thus, conversational delivery showed no clear additional learning benefit under the present conditions. More broadly, a learning format that is rated favorably need not be the one students voluntarily adopt.

papers.title: Fractional order Orlicz--Sobolev spaces revisited
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to revisit our work [J. Funct. Anal. 277 (2019), 333--367], where fractional order Orlicz--Sobolev spaces were introduced and their behavior as the fractional parameter $s\uparrow1$ was studied, and to redo it without assuming the $\Delta_2$ condition on the Young function $G$ or on its complementary function. Since that paper appeared, the theory of these spaces has been considerably developed, and the tools available today allow for a cleaner treatment in full generality. We prove a Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu type formula as $s\uparrow1$, a compactness and lower semicontinuity result for sequences with bounded energy, a Poincaré inequality uniform in $s$, and the $\Gamma$-convergence of the fractional modulars to a local modular on arbitrary open sets. As an application we study the asymptotic behavior of minimizers and of solutions of Dirichlet problems for the fractional $g$-Laplacian as $s\uparrow1$. This version also corrects some errors in the original paper, and it is intended to serve as a more complete and reliable reference for these results.

papers.title: Homological Properties of $L\otimes_{\Bbbk} N$
papers.abstract: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative Noetherian algebras over an arbitrary field $\Bbbk$ such that $A\otimes_\Bbbk B$ is Noetherian. Let $I$ and $J$ be ideals of $A$ and $B$, respectively, and let $L$ and $N$ be nonzero finitely generated modules over $A$ and $B$, respectively. In \cite{R4}, the author investigates the relationships between certain algebraic properties of $L\otimes_\Bbbk N$ and the corresponding properties of $L$ and $N$, and vice versa. In the present paper, we characterize the Gorensteinness, approximate Cohen--Macaulayness, and maximal depth property of $L\otimes_\Bbbk N$ with respect to $\mathcal{I}=I\otimes_\Bbbk B+A\otimes_\Bbbk J$ in terms of the corresponding properties of $L$ and $N$ with respect to $I$ and $J$, respectively. In particular, when $A$ and $B$ are local rings, we describe these properties of $L \otimes_{\Bbbk} N$ as a module over the local ring $A \otimes_\Bbbk B$.

papers.title: Independent and end-faithful spanning trees in infinite graphs
papers.abstract: Spanning trees rooted at the same vertex are independent if, for each vertex other than the root, the paths from the root to that vertex are pairwise distinct and internally vertex-disjoint. Zehavi and Itai conjectured that, for every positive integer $k$, every finite $k$-connected graph has $k$ independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex. We show that every $2$-connected graph, finite or infinite, has two independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex. For locally finite $2$-connected graphs, both trees can be chosen end-faithful. We also prove that every locally finite $3$-connected chordal graph has three independent end-faithful spanning trees. Counterexamples show that local finiteness is essential for the version with independent end-faithful spanning trees. We further show that every $3$-connected graph with a universal vertex or a finite vertex cover has three independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex.

papers.title: Multiscale wave-coupled neural networks for the inverse-design of broadband diffractive optics
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce an inverse-design model called multiscale wave-coupled neural networks (MSWNets) inspired by physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) that integrate the deep-learning capability of fully-connected neural networks with rigorous Rayleigh-Sommerfeld diffraction theory. MSWNets are trained using spatial input and output functions describing the height profiles of diffractive structures. Importantly, a MSWNet is composed of multiple sub-networks that provide learning across multiple frequency components of the optimal design solution. First, we validate and analyze the inverse design capabilities of the MSWNets' architecture through training on the complete complex field propagated from the analytical design of an axilens, demonstrating accurate reconstruction. Finally, we employ MSWNets, trained to maximize focusing efficiency, for the inverse design of novel diffractive devices. In particular, we design and display the performance of several achromatic lenses and doublets across the mid-wave infrared region ($3-5\rm{\;\mu} m$) with focal distance $f=500\rm{\;\mu m}$, demonstrating the potential of our inverse-design framework for the next-generation of broadband diffractive optical devices.

papers.title: Robust Pair--Restricted Lipschitz Regression with Global--Local Transfer
papers.abstract: We develop a robust pair-restricted Lipschitz regression framework for grouped longitudinal data represented as finite trajectories in a space equipped with a prescribed or learned pseudometric. For a fixed geometry, latent responses and a Lipschitz bound are estimated jointly through a convex optimisation problem with constraints imposed on selected trajectory pairs. We show that the choice of fidelity loss leads to different structural behaviour: Huber regularisation strictly reduces the pair-restricted Lipschitz seminorm whenever the exact interpolant has a finite positive seminorm, whereas $L^1$ fidelity can preserve exact interpolation below a data-dependent threshold. For grouped observations, global and local Lipschitz structures are combined while keeping group identity outside the trajectory geometry. The global component draws on observations from other groups, while the local component uses each group's history to account for group-specific behaviour. We also characterise when group-specific observations can be fitted exactly under a shared Lipschitz bound and establish a regularity bound for the combined predictor. We describe a computational implementation based on constraint generation and illustrate the framework through an application to longitudinal sow-production data.

papers.title: Neural Grey: Practical Vignetting Calibration from Casual Camera Rolls
papers.abstract: Neural Grey estimates a reusable camera-lens shading map from four approximate roll captures of a static, light-colored surface. Rolling the camera moves wall illumination across the sensor while lens shading stays fixed. We fit these two fields jointly, together with small pose and exposure errors, using a physical shading envelope and compact bounded neural residuals. Rotation alone, however, cannot distinguish radial lens attenuation from radial wall illumination. A focal-conditioned radial selector addresses this ambiguity: it uses focal length and sensor size to choose the broad radial profile while retaining the fitted spatial remainder. Component and sensitivity studies separate the roles of the field representation, radial selection, and numerical settings. Neural Grey reaches 25.43 dB on 100 synthetic cases, 24.49 dB on ray-traced lens architectures, and 25.38 dB on 21 real takes from seven optical configurations. On the real benchmark, it exceeds the strongest competing mean by 5.62 dB and wins five of seven configurations.

papers.title: Invariant subspace problem for trace-class perturbations of subnormal operators
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a subnormal operator on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, and let $K$ be a trace class operator. In the present paper, we prove that $S+K$ has a nontrivial invariant subspace. Furthermore, for a normal operator $S$, we prove that if the Hausdorff dimension of $\sigma(S)$ is greater than $1$, then $S+K$ has a hyperinvariant half-space.

papers.title: Weak-Weak Stability for Multi-Species Nonlocal Cross-Diffusion Systems with Endpoint Lorentz Kernels
papers.abstract: The quantitative weak-weak stability for multi-species nonlocal cross-diffusion systems on the torus is established. The interactions of the species are described by a symmetric, positive semidefinite matrix-valued kernel whose gradient belongs to the endpoint Lorentz space $L^{d,\infty}$, where $d\ge 2$ is the space dimension. The central estimate, formulated in terms of a modulated Hellinger distance-interaction energy, yields uniqueness of solutions with finite Boltzmann entropy and Fisher information. The proof relies on a two-level endpoint mechanism: The Boltzmann entropy controls the interaction energy, while the Fisher information controls the associated force field. Further results are the immediate $L^2$ regularization and the exponential decay to the homogeneous equilibrium. As a particular application, uniqueness and stability for the two-dimensional Poisson-Nernst-Planck system with periodic Coulomb kernels are obtained.

papers.title: Totally geodesic sets and Caratheodory geometry in the polydisk
papers.abstract: A subset $V$ of the polydisk ${\mathbb D}^N$ is called totally geodesic if every pair of points in $V$ lie on a Kobayashi geodesic of ${\mathbb D}^N$ that lies entirely in $V$. It is called a Caratheodory set if its intrinsic Caratheodory metric agrees with the Caratheodory metric inherited from ${\mathbb D}^N$. We prove that for algebraic subvarieties of the polydisk these two notions coincide, and we obtain a complete geometric classification of such sets. The invariant metric geometry of the polydisk is unexpectedly rigid: every such set is, up to automorphism, built from only two basic geometric objects: disks and a distinguished family of two-dimensional algebraic surfaces that we call Roman surfaces. Roman surfaces arise independently in the study of the three-point interpolation problem in the polydisk.

papers.title: Tuning of superconducting and physical properties of Mo$_{1-x}$Si$_x$ thin films for Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detector Applications
JAX-Nano: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Phonon Boltzmann Transport Solver for Nanoscale Heat Transfer
papers.abstract: As semiconductor device dimensions approach phonon mean free paths, heat transport enters ballistic and quasi-ballistic regimes where Fourier's law becomes inadequate. The phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) describes these nonequilibrium effects but presents significant computational challenges. This work introduces JAX-Nano, a GPU-accelerated, end-to-end differentiable phonon BTE solver for nanoscale heat transport. The solver integrates steady-state and transient BTE formulations within a unified finite-volume framework, supporting structured and unstructured meshes, mode-resolved transport, phonon scattering, volumetric heat generation, and multiple boundary conditions. Automatic differentiation enables gradient computation with respect to transport properties, boundary conditions, heat-generation rates, and geometric parameters without separately derived adjoint equations. Numerical predictions are validated against analytical solutions and established BTE solvers across diffusive-to-ballistic regimes. Applications to complex three-dimensional geometries are demonstrated using single-fin, double-fin, and arrayed fin field-effect transistor (FinFET) configurations. Gradient-based inverse learning enables single- and multi-parameter identification, including simultaneous recovery of mode-resolved phonon relaxation times and spatially distributed heat-generation rates in steady-state and transient problems. GPU performance and scalability are evaluated with respect to spatial resolution, angular discretization, and phonon bands, including comparisons with an MPI-based BTE solver. JAX-Nano provides a unified computational framework for three-dimensional phonon transport, automatic differentiation, and inverse parameter identification, enabling sensitivity analysis and optimization of nanoscale thermal systems.

papers.title: An Implicit Discrete Adjoint Unified Gas-Kinetic Scheme for Sensitivity Analysis and Shape Optimization in Multiscale Gas Flows
papers.abstract: Accurate and efficient gradient-based sensitivity evaluation remains challenging for performance optimization in multiscale flows with complex geometries. To address this challenge, this work develops a matrix-free discrete adjoint method for the steady implicit unified gas-kinetic scheme (UGKS) through the exact linearization and transposition of its converged fixed-point operator. The method employs a hybrid differentiation strategy that combines local automatic differentiation (AD) of complex nonlinear kinetic kernels with analytically derived tangent and transpose operators for the coupled macroscopic--microscopic implicit updates and mass-conservation projection. This formulation ensures exact discrete consistency across both flow and geometric dependencies while avoiding global Jacobian assembly and the memory overhead of end-to-end reverse-mode AD. Verification tests across continuum, transitional, and free-molecular regimes confirm machine-precision stepwise duality with the corresponding tangent-linear solver and close agreement with central finite differences. In a six-parameter shape-sensitivity analysis, a single adjoint solve achieves speedups of 7.54X and 3.88X over tangent-linear and central finite-difference evaluations, respectively. Finally, constrained shape optimizations of a periodic Knudsen pump and a Mach-2 NACA0012 airfoil converge within ten design updates, achieving up to 29.68% improvement in normalized mass flow and 7.46% reduction in aerodynamic drag across internal and external multiscale flows.

papers.title: Filters as a localization of nets
papers.abstract: Based on different notions of subnet in the literature, we define categories of nets and investigate their categorical relationships. We show that the category of proper filters with filter-preserving functions is, up to equivalence, a localization of four of these categories.

papers.title: Semantic Communication via Federated Learning with Knowledge-Enhanced Networks and Privacy
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel privacy-preserving semantic communication framework that combines Federated Learning (FL) with Knowledge-Enhanced Networks (KE-NET) for distributed wireless systems. Unlike centralized semantic communication approaches that require data aggregation, our method enables multiple clients to collaboratively train a knowledge-enhanced model while keeping their data and knowledge graphs private. We develop a multi-objective federated optimization strategy that balances semantic fidelity, knowledge integration, channel robustness, and reconstruction accuracy. Theoretical analysis reveals that federated aggregation improves effective SNR for $N$ clients through noise averaging. Numerical results with AWGN and Rayleigh fading channels demonstrate that multi-client federated learning consistently outperforms both single-client and centralized baselines across all SNR conditions, with particularly significant gains in low-SNR scenarios.

papers.title: DIPS-OjOS I: Project Design and Science Validation
Which Model Belongs in the Loop? Evaluating Fitness Functions for Network Topology Optimization with a Quality-Diversity Algorithm
papers.abstract: Network topology optimization (NTO) can reduce redispatch cost by rerouting power flows in transmission systems. To approach NTO, a complex combinatorial problem, gradient-free optimization algorithms that leverage diversity have shown promising results. These algorithms rely on frequent evaluations of candidate topologies by fitness functions. Recent work has shown that fast DC power flow-based fitness functions can serve this purpose. However, DC power flow fitness functions can misjudge the cost and feasibility of topologies, potentially leading to wrong operational decisions. Understanding the impact of fitness function accuracy on optimization performance is therefore crucial. This study compares the optimization performance of four fitness functions based on DC and AC power flow and on DC and AC optimal power flow. Furthermore, we propose a ranking-based metric to estimate the optimization performance of a fitness function on a curated dataset. Case studies cover the IEEE 118-bus case with 50 congested operating points and a 793-bus case for validation. Results show that optimal power flow-based fitness functions perform better in the optimization loop than power flow-based ones. Additionally, the results indicate that the metric can predict the optimization performance order of the fitness functions, but only if the distribution shift between the curated dataset and the search path of the optimization is small.

papers.title: MCP-based EUV ptychography with physics-simulation-trained residual learning
papers.abstract: Microchannel-plate (MCP) detectors offer high gain for extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) experiments, but spatial blur and nonlinear response hinder quantitative diffraction imaging. Here, we present an MCP-based EUV ptychography system that combines detector hardware with physics-simulation-trained computational restoration. A residual-learning neural network trained on simulated detector degradation restores diffraction patterns without experimentally acquired training pairs. This preprocessing substantially improves image quality compared with reconstructions from uncorrected data under identical reconstruction settings. Single-harmonic imaging at $57$~nm yields an effective edge-response width of $1.08~\mu$m, approaching the nominal diffraction-limited scale of the imaging geometry. The approach further enables wavelength-multiplexed imaging at $44.4$ and $57$~nm. By coupling high-gain detection with computational compensation, this system enables high-resolution, multi-harmonic EUV ptychography and offers a cost-effective alternative to scientific-grade EUV CCD detectors
