papers.title: Uniform dominance of Golod local rings
papers.abstract: We prove that every Golod local ring $R$ is uniformly dominant. More precisely, we show that its dominant index is at most the embedding dimension of $R$. The proof is based on a numerical criterion for formality of bounded complexes whose homology is annihilated by the maximal ideal.

papers.title: A Class of Monotone Quasi-Newtonian Flows Coupled to Nonlinear Equations: Analysis and Finite Element Approximation
papers.abstract: We analyze a monotone quasi-Newtonian flow coupled with nonlinear heat and concentration equations. In the model, the viscosity depends on the temperature, the concentration, and the velocity gradient, and the diffusivities depend on the temperature and the concentration. We show the existence of weak solutions without smallness assumptions on the data, and their uniqueness under suitable smallness and regularity assumptions. For the numerical approximation, we consider the Taylor--Hood and mini elements. We prove that the discrete solutions converge, up to a subsequence, to a weak solution, and we derive a quasi-best approximation result and convergence rates. We present numerical experiments in two and three dimensions that illustrate the theory.

papers.title: Long-time dynamics of open quantum systems: mathematical and physical aspects
papers.abstract: Quantum channels provide the mathematical framework for describing the evolution of open quantum systems, i.e., quantum systems interacting with an environment. This review focuses on the long-time or asymptotic dynamics of open quantum systems, a topic of growing interest due to its relevance for quantum information theory and noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. We present a comprehensive analysis of homogeneous evolutions in both discrete and continuous time, treating the dynamics in full generality within the Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures. By systematically studying the spectral properties of quantum channels, we present general structure theorems that characterize asymptotic behaviour, illustrated through several paradigmatic examples. We further discuss how the asymptotic dynamics can be exploited for dissipative state engineering, the identification of decoherence-free subspaces, the design of quantum error-correction schemes, and the evaluation of the asymptotic capacities of quantum channels.

papers.title: Beyond the section plane: Robust 3D reconstruction of multiplex immunofluorescence exposes limitations of 2D spatial cell statistics
authors: Nataša Sladoje (1 and 2) ((1) Department of Information Technology
(4) Vall d'Hebron Institute of Research & Institute of Oncology
papers.abstract: Spatial analysis of the tumour microenvironment with multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) typically relies on single thin tissue sections, which misrepresent the 3D tissue organisation and bias spatial cell statistics in ways that remain largely unquantified. We reconstruct 24 breast and lung tumour tissue microarray cores in 3D, each from 15-20 serial mIF sections, and compare spatial cell statistics in 3D with those from individual sections. Our pipeline combines affine pre-alignment with dense deformable refinement using RoMa v2, achieving a median target registration error of 1.79 $\mu$m, well below nuclear size, which allows nuclei to be linked across sections. While cell-type proportions are preserved in 2D (Pearson corr. $r \geq 0.99$), 3D analysis reveals up to 3.8 times shorter nearest-neighbour distances, 13-19% higher neighbourhood entropy, and 2-4 times more contacts per cell. Tissue composition can thus be reliably estimated from individual sections, whereas cell-cell interactions require volumetric analysis.

papers.title: Invariant subspaces and nest algebras in left-right operator splitting
papers.abstract: The left--right (L-R) splitting method for boundary integral equations in rough-surface scattering writes the integral operator as the sum of its lower- and strictly upper- triangular parts. This note examines the operator algebra formed by the lower-triangular ($L$-type) this http URL weak closure is a nest algebra; second-kind $L$-type operators with Hilbert--Schmidt kernels have $L$-type inverses; and Arveson's distance formula expresses the error of the best possible forward-only approximation in terms of the backward coupling across a single cut. Bounds and numerical results for the 2D double-layer kernel suggest that truncation is close to optimal, and that the worst-case input field is a predominantly left-going grazing wave rather than backscatter of a right-going incident field. For a hard surface the inverse $L$-operator is given, up to a second-order correction, by four times the $L$-operator of the mirror-image surface, and several open questions are posed.

papers.title: $\mathcal{PGF}=\mathcal{GP}$ over commutative Noetherian rings
papers.abstract: We prove $\mathcal{PGF}=\mathcal{GP}$ over every commutative Noetherian ring.

papers.title: Questions, Explanation and Synthesis in Service Mathematics: Course Design with Didactic Units and Hybrid Teaching
papers.abstract: Students may have access to a convincing mathematical explanation without being able to reconstruct or adapt it. A course must provide opportunities to develop that understanding while keeping the work sustainable for students and teachers. This article develops a methodology for service mathematics in which a question ledger guides both course authoring and classroom decisions. Course-relative didactic units organise explanatory purposes, prerequisites and connections, initially calibrated by a five-to-seven-minute expert account. Teaching combines preparation, student exposition and supported repair with substantial teacher exposition and synthesis. Their allocation changes with the topic, audience and conditions of teaching. Compression and recovery explain how developed constructions become reusable while their grounds remain accessible. Three analyses from mathematics for computing-full Sudoku encoding, grayscale projection and a software failure contract-show how contrasting cases guide explanation and revision. The practice-informed contribution connects coherent course design with adaptable teaching and manageable preparation, and identifies questions for evaluating learning, participation and sustained teacher effort.

papers.title: Formation of Multiple BGK-like Structures in the Time-asymptotic State of Collisionless Vlasov-Poisson Plasmas
papers.abstract: The time-asymptotic state of a finite-amplitude perturbation in a collisionless and Maxwellian plasma is typically represented as a steady state of two non-linearly superposed, counter-propagating Bernstein-Greene-Kruskal (BGK) modes. Using high-resolution Vlasov-Poisson simulations, we show that the plasma evolves self-consistently into a time-asymptotic state of multiple vortex-like structures that gradually fill the phase-space and reduce filamentation. This occurs without the need for external forcing or the presence of an energetic plasma population. This finding suggests that the time-asymptotic regime of the plasma is rather akin to a non-linear superposition of multiple BGK-like modes associated with nearly constant phase-speed waves. The electric field and the space-averaged particle distribution function exhibit a power-law broad spectrum, which is consistent with an energy cascade towards smaller scales in both position and velocity spaces.

papers.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Payoff-Gradient Learning in Möbius Pricing Games
papers.abstract: We prove global last-iterate convergence of payoff-gradient learning in every typewise Riemannian metric, which for scalar actions is the same as typewise mirror descent, with explicit rates, in a class of Bayesian bidding and pricing games that includes first-price auctions, unit-demand pay-as-bid auctions, rank-based generalized first-price auctions, and homogeneous-good price competition with inelastic demand. The result holds for symmetric self-play: all players use a common strategy and apply the same payoff-gradient update at each type. Convergence is from every continuous weakly increasing feasible initial strategy, including pooling, and does not rely on the monotonicity or Minty conditions that underlie existing guarantees in other games. Instead, the class is characterized by two structural properties: a direct payoff effect that is independent of the action, and a payoff difference at the allocation threshold that is affine in the action. These properties reduce the learning dynamics to a singular transport-damping equation for the common strategy, which, under the stated coefficient and metric assumptions, admits a unique viscosity solution. Comparison barriers make the uniform distance to the unique rest point a strict Lyapunov functional and yield convergence rates with optimal algebraic exponents. In allocation games, the rest point is the unique weakly increasing symmetric equilibrium under the stated tie-breaking conditions, and a positive lower slope bound converts strategy-error bounds into explicit approximate-equilibrium guarantees. A projected grid scheme with a slope floor makes the approximation constructive, with error bounds under deterministic perturbations and almost-sure convergence on a fixed grid under martingale gradient noise.

papers.title: An Efficient Long-Time Stable Second-Order Ensemble Method for the Parameterized Navier--Stokes Equations
papers.abstract:
Ensemble simulations for uncertainty quantification, ensemble forecasting, and long-time statistics require stability over arbitrarily long horizons without time-step restrictions. We develop a second-order ensemble method for parameterized incompressible Navier--Stokes equations that uses a common, time-independent Brinkman (shifted Stokes) operator for all members. The scheme combines BDF2, a mean-reverting scalar auxiliary variable (mr-SAV) treatment of convection, and viscosity splitting with a shared viscosity $ ar
u$ treated implicitly and memberwise deviations explicitly. For constant viscosities satisfying $0<
u_j<4 ar
u/3$, we establish unconditional, uniform-in-time dissipativity under uniformly bounded forcing, including an absorbing bound independent of initial data and time-step size. We show that the upper viscosity threshold is sharp for fixed $ ar
u$. For spatially varying random viscosities, unconditional long-time stability holds under a signed pointwise condition that confines $
u_j$ to $( ar
u/3,4 ar
u/3)$ uniformly away from the endpoints; for proportional spatial profiles, it holds over the full range $0<
u_j<4 ar
u/3$. Under the full-range constant-viscosity condition and sufficient regularity in two dimensions, we prove second-order temporal error bounds for velocity, the auxiliary variable, and the discrete time primitive of the pressure error. Numerical tests corroborate long-time stability at large time steps and the sharpness of the viscosity threshold, demonstrate accurate individual solutions and ensemble statistics, and show that mean reversion prevents long-time drift. Reusing the shared operator reduces computing time by about half relative to member-by-member solves.

papers.title: Multipliers and integration operators on Hardy--Bloch type tent spaces
papers.abstract: We investigate the boundedness of integration operators $J_g$ and $I_g$ and pointwise multipliers $M_g$ on Hardy--Bloch type tent spaces $\mathcal{BT}^p$. The main difficulty is that these spaces are defined through a non-tangential maximal function of the radial derivative, which places the problem at the interface of holomorphic function theory and harmonic analysis. We completely characterize the boundedness of $I_g:\mathcal{BT}^p\to\mathcal{BT}^q$ for all $0<p,q<\infty$, and obtain a complete characterization for $J_g$ and $M_g$ when $p<q$. For $p\geq q$, we establish separate necessary and sufficient conditions. The proofs in the case $p\leq q$ are mainly based on some fractional maximal function estimates, whereas those in the case $p>q$ are mainly based on a synthesis lemma. We also give examples showing that several converse implications in the range $p\geq q$ fail.

papers.title: Topological Neural Collapse
papers.abstract: Neural collapse (NC) predicts that, late in training, last-layer class features concentrate at their means and the means form a simplex equiangular tight frame (ETF). We ask whether NC also leaves a signature in the functional connectome of each layer: the graph of Pearson correlations between hidden-unit activations, built per class and summarized by persistent graph homology. Using deep MLPs, we observe two topological phenomena that co-occur with the well-studied geometric NC in the final layers during the terminal phase. Contrary to NC1, the split-half variability of a class connectome increases (TNC1). The mean pairwise $H_0$ distance $\bar{D}$ between class connectomes also rises (TNC2), but unevenly across class pairs, unlike the equidistance of NC2. We find that 24-56% of last-layer units become dead for some classes yet stay active for others, which inflates $\bar{D}$. After correcting for these units, both signatures remain elevated. These results from MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 provide preliminary evidence that a topological mechanism may accompany the geometric signatures of NC.

papers.title: Mean First Passage Times for Loop-Erased Random Walks and Erased-Loop Size Distributions on Graphs
papers.abstract: Loop-erased random walks provide a natural way to extract self-avoiding trajectories from ordinary random walks by chronologically removing loops. They are deeply connected with uniform spanning trees: the loop-erased path between two vertices has the same distribution law as the unique path connecting these vertices in a random spanning tree. In this work, we use this connection as a computational framework for finite graphs. First, using the classical transfer-current theorem, we obtain an explicit formula for the mean first passage time of loop-erased random walks. The resulting expression returns the expected length of the loop-erased path as a weighted sum over simple paths, where the weights are exact determinantal probabilities obtained from the spanning-tree kernel. Second, we express the distribution of erased loop sizes in the same framework. This distribution measures the scale of the redundant excursions removed during loop erasure and provides information that is complementary to effective path length. The approach is applied to arbitrary finite graphs and then specialized to complete graphs, cycle graphs, and motif-based networks, where explicit formulas and asymptotic behaviors are obtained. Numerical experiments show strong agreement between the theoretical predictions and Monte Carlo simulations. The results provide a unified method for quantifying both the effective paths kept by loop erasure and the loops removed during random exploration of networks.

papers.title: A feasible point method for derivative-free linearly constrained optimization
papers.abstract: This paper presents a framework for linearly constrained derivative-free optimization (DFO) in which the original objective function is evaluated only at feasible points. The method first analyzes the linear constraint system using certificates of infeasibility and implied activity to detect infeasibility or a singleton feasible set, or, when the feasible set has positive dimension, to identify the affine subspace spanned by the feasible set and obtain an equivalent reduced representation with a strictly feasible base point. It then transforms the resulting reduced problem into an unconstrained optimization problem by means of a pointed feasible retraction and an exact penalty function. The retraction maps arbitrary trial points to feasible points by an explicit scaling in the reduced coordinates, so that no constrained optimization or projection subproblem is required during objective evaluations. This construction permits a broad range of unconstrained DFO methods to be used as inner solvers while preserving feasibility of the original objective evaluations. Numerical experiments compare several such variants on linearly constrained test problems of different dimensions. The results show that the choice of inner solver affects robustness, the number of problems solved, function-evaluation efficiency, and computational time, and that relative performance changes with problem dimension.

papers.title: Separating physics from discrepancy: Orthogonalized kernels for physics-encoded system identification
papers.abstract: Physics-encoded identification combines a physical model with a data-driven correction, but the data alone do not determine how the input-output map is split between them: components representable by the physical model may be assigned to either part. In kernel-based model embedding, this allocation is governed by the kernel. As a consequence, the physical parameters lack a well-defined target. In this work, this ambiguity is resolved a priori by defining a canonical physical parameter as the parameter of the physical model that best approximates the noise-free map, in a weighted least-squares sense, over a user-defined operating domain, together with an orthogonal discrepancy. Specifically, an orthogonalized kernel is derived that restricts the correction to functions orthogonal to the physical model. The resulting estimator keeps the closed-form solution of model embedding, while the canonical parameter depends only on the prescribed geometry, not on the kernel or the data. As the inputs become dense and the noise vanishes, the set of parameters consistent with the data converges to the canonical parameter, a property that generally fails without orthogonalization. Under energy-bounded noise, suitable regularization attains optimal worst-case estimation accuracy. Numerical examples demonstrate consistent parameter estimates across different kernels and experiments.

papers.title: Three almost symmetric metatiles generate the Spectre tiling
papers.abstract: We present a system of three `metatiles' for the Spectre aperiodic monotiling, named `D23'. These are similar in concept to the {\HTPF} system for the hat tiling: the metatiles have their own substitution system which can be iterated as many times as desired, and then the lowest-order metatiles can be converted into Spectre tiles. One of the three metatiles has order-2 rotational symmetry, and the other two are `almost symmetric' with orders 2 and 3 respectively, in the sense that although the region covered by the tile's $n$-times deflation is not exactly identical to its rotation, within their intersection, the proportion of non-matching tiles tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$. This near-symmetry corresponds to cases of near-symmetry in the Spectre tiling itself. A curious property of this system is that one of the three metatiles disappears completely in the conversion to Spectres!

papers.title: Merits of Collocating Uptilted Antennas on Terrestrial Base Stations for Aerial Coverage
papers.abstract: The integration of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) into future wireless networks introduces challenges in ensuring reliable aerial coverage, particularly for UAV-based user equipment (UAV-UE). Traditional terrestrial base stations (BSs) with downtilted antennas, referred to as dt-BSs, are designed primarily for ground users. They provide inefficient connectivity to UAV-UE due to weak sidelobe gains, and susceptibility to ground reflection (GR) interference as well as sidelobe interference from non-serving dt-BSs. To address this, we propose a hybrid cellular architecture that collocates uptilted antennas on a portion of existing dt-BS towers, referred to as ut-BSs. These support UAV-UE exclusively, minimizing impact on ground users. We consider realistic antenna radiation patterns and probabilistic line-of-sight (LoS)/non-LoS (NLoS) links between ut-BSs and UAV-UE. Using stochastic geometry, we analyze the UAV-UE coverage probability, accounting for interference from both dt-BSs and non-serving ut-BSs, along with GR-induced interference. Results show significant improvements in UAV-UE coverage with only a small density of ut-BSs. GR interference is notable at lower altitudes but diminishes beyond 500 meters. This study highlights the potential of our hybrid architecture to enhance the reliability and scalability of UAV communications in large-scale deployments. It also offers actionable insights for telecom operators considering the collocation of uptilted antennas within existing infrastructure to better support aerial connectivity.

papers.title: On Partially Totally Real Riemannian Maps and Their Sharp Curvature Inequalities
papers.abstract: We introduce partially totally real Riemannian maps into Kähler manifolds and examine the geometry of their associated distributions. For complex space forms, we obtain a Chen-type curvature inequality retaining the contributions of the mixed second fundamental form and O'Neill's tensor, together with an arbitrary-codimension estimate involving partial mean curvatures. We characterize equality in the principal inequality and give an example attaining the bound when $\dim\mathcal D\geq4$, including a case with nonintegrable horizontal distribution.

papers.title: Finite abelian groups acting on rationally connected threefolds III: Classification
papers.abstract: We complete the classification of finite abelian groups that admit a faithful action on a rationally connected threefold. For a finite abelian group $G$ with invariant factors $1<d_1\mid\cdots\mid d_s$, put $c(G)=\sum_i(1-1/d_i)$. We prove that for $1\le n\le3$ such a group admits a faithful action on a rationally connected variety of dimension $n$ if and only if $c(G)\le n$. We also show that finite abelian subgroups of the Cremona group of rank three are, up to isomorphism, precisely the products of finite abelian subgroups of the Cremona groups of ranks one and two. Four further groups can act faithfully on rationally connected threefolds. For each of these groups, the faithful action is unique up to birational conjugacy and automorphism of the acting group.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of hard wall model of AdS/QCD at finite chemical potential with Gauss-Bonnet corrections
papers.abstract: We study the confinement/deconfinement transition of the hard wall model of AdS/QCD at finite quark density in five-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell--Gauss--Bonnet gravity, with the back-reaction of the quark matter on the geometry included. The deconfined phase is a charged Gauss--Bonnet black hole, and the confined phase is thermally charged AdS cut off in the infrared. The infrared value of the gauge field, which Lee, Park and Sin fixed by requiring a consistent quark number, becomes a function of the Gauss--Bonnet coupling. We obtain the transition line in closed form at fixed quark chemical potential and at fixed quark number density. At fixed density the transition passes through a region where the two phases coexist. A negative Gauss--Bonnet coupling raises the transition temperature and extends the confined phase to higher density. A value inside the causality bound gives a transition temperature at zero density close to the lattice value. In the dense confined phase we compute the masses and decay constants of the $\rho$ meson and its radial excitations. All masses increase with density. A WKB analysis relates the increase to a shorter effective size of the confining region, and at nuclear density the $\rho$ mass rises by about one percent.

papers.title: Refined, Reliable and Reproducible: Algorithmic Analysis and Reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder
Charge-fluctuation hot lines and superconductivity in Ba$_{1-x}$K$_x$BiO$_3$
Layered soft-output MLSE architecture for PAM4 short-reach optical interconnects
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of data traffic driven by artificial intelligence demands high-speed data-center optical interconnects, where soft-output maximum-likelihood sequence estimation (SMLSE) provides reliability information for soft-decision forward error correction. However, conventional SMLSE suffers from a latency bottleneck because sequential state-metric recursions cause latency to increase linearly with the number of symbols. Here, we propose a layered SMLSE architecture that reduces latency from linear to logarithmic order. Downward branch-metric accumulation combines adjacent interval metrics in parallel, while upward state-metric propagation reconstructs forward and backward state metrics at successive interval midpoints. Experiments with 112-Gbit/s PAM4 transmission over 2-km standard single-mode fiber demonstrate identical soft-output performance for layered and conventional SMLSE, while the total latency decreases from 26 to 10 processing cycles. The proposed layered SMLSE provides a low-latency architecture while preserving soft-output performance for high-speed optical interconnects.

papers.title: Time-Reversed Task Events and Thermodynamic Bounds for Stochastic Thermal Machines
Evaluating VLT SPHERE for Probing Diffuse Circumstellar Regions of Evolved Stars
Risk aversion with two risks for state-dependent utilities
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the concept of Arrow-Pratt risk aversion within a two-attribute, state-dependent utility framework, where a primary risk is accompanied by a background risk. Within this setting, we investigate the interrelationships among risk aversion toward one risk in the presence of another risk, the structure of state-dependent two-attribute utility functions, and the degree of correlation between the two risks. More specifically, we establish conditions on the state-dependent two-attribute utility function under which risk aversion toward primary risk is preserved when a background risk is involved, considering various correlation structures between the two types of risks. Additionally, a new concept, uniform risk aversion in the presence of a background risk, is introduced. We show that the above established conditions on the state-dependent two-attribute utility function are equivalent to uniform risk aversion toward primary risk in presence of a background risk. These findings offer new insights into state-dependent preferences for correlated risks. Two applications in the contexts of fair insurance contract and optimal prevention within a two-period model illustrate the practical usefulness of the proposed risk aversion with two risks under state-dependent utilities.

papers.title: Improved Singular Adams-type inequalities and the existence of extremals in dimension four
papers.abstract: Let $H_0^2(\Omega)$ denote the Sobolev space on $\Omega$, where $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ is a smooth bounded domain containing the origin, and let $\lambda(\Omega)$ denote the first eigenvalue of the bi-Laplacian $\Delta^2$ on $\Omega$ subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. We establish the following singular Adams inequality of Adimurthi-Druet type: for $0<\beta<4$ and $0\leq\alpha<\lambda(\Omega)$, \[ \sup\limits_{u\in H_0^2(\Omega),\|\Delta u\|_2^2=1}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{32\pi^2(1-\frac{\beta}{4}) u^2(1+\alpha\|u\|_2^2)}}{|x|^\beta}dx < +\infty. \] Moreover, this supremum is infinite for $\alpha>\lambda_1(\Omega)$. Furthermore, we show the existence of extremal functions, that is, for sufficiently small $\alpha>0$, there exists $u^*\in H_0^2(\Omega)\cap C_{\mathrm{loc}}^4(\Omega\setminus{0})$ with $\|\Delta u^*\|_2^2=1$ such that \[ \int_\Omega \frac{e^{32\pi^2(1-\frac{\beta}{4}) {|u^*|}^2(1+\alpha\|u^*\|_2^2)}}{|x|^\beta}dx=\sup\limits_{u\in H_0^2(\Omega),\|\Delta u\|_2^2=1}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{32\pi^2(1-\frac{\beta}{4}) u^2(1+\alpha\|u\|_2^2)}}{|x|^\beta}dx. \] These results can be regarded as a further development, in the singular setting, of the theory on the existence of extremals established by Lu and Yang [Adv. Math. (2009)]. Our proof relies on the blow-up analysis of the subcritical maximizers, combined with biharmonic truncation adapted to the singular weight, capacity-type estimates on annular regions and a test function argument. A key novelty of our approach lies in carrying out the blow-up analysis without relying on an explicit expression for the limiting profile near the blow-up point, which is unavailable in the present setting. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to perform such a blow-up analysis without the explicit form of the limiting profile.

papers.title: Learning the Boltzmann Collision Operator with Structural Constraints for Fast Kinetic Simulation
papers.abstract: The high-dimensional integration in the Boltzmann collision operator is a major computational bottleneck in deterministic kinetic simulations. We develop a structure-preserving neural operator that provides an efficient approximation of this nonlinear collision mapping. The operator maintains the gain-loss structure of the original Boltzmann collision operator, and, by construction, is proportional to the square of the gas density. Conservative moment projection and entropy correction enforce conservation of mass, momentum, and energy, as well as entropy dissipation. By construction, the collision term also vanishes at all Maxwellians. In the numerical scheme for simulations of gas dynamics, we establish nonnegativity of the distribution function with the learned collision operator and prove exponential relaxation to the moment-matched equilibrium when a positive spectral gap is imposed. Numerical experiments for a constant collision kernel demonstrate a favorable accuracy-cost tradeoff relative to Fourier spectral evaluations. Although trained on smooth distributions, the same operator handles discontinuous distribution functions and is embedded without retraining in steady Couette flow, normal-shock, and two-dimensional lid-driven cavity solvers. These results demonstrate a reusable approximation for repeated collision evaluations that retains kinetic structure and supports accurate deterministic simulation.

papers.title: Thickness-Dependent Morphology and Electrical Transport in Ultrathin Amorphous MoSi Films
Random Projection Neural Networks for Phase-Field Models: Model Reformulation, Scaling, and Network Architecture
papers.abstract: Phase-field models, particularly the Allen-Cahn(AC) and Cahn-Hilliard(CH) equations, are widely used to describe interfacial dynamics, but resolving their sharp transition layers and stiff dynamics presents substantial numerical challenges. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free approach, yet optimizing large numbers of network parameters can be computationally demanding and may still yield limited accuracy. We develop a random projection neural network (RPNN) framework that combines first-order PDE reformulations with independent random-feature representations of the unknowns. By fixing randomly initialized hidden-layer parameters and optimizing only the output coefficients, RPNNs reduce training to least-squares problems amenable to Newton-type solvers. Introducing auxiliary variables eliminates higher-order derivatives from the PDE residuals, while separate random feature bases in the unknowns provide flexibility in approximating fields with different scales and regularity. For the CH equation, we scale the chemical potential to address the disparity between its magnitude and that of the phase field. We compare the first-order and corresponding higher-order formulations and systematically examine the effects of initialization distributions, the random feature range $R_\xi$, seven activation functions, and dense versus separable space-time bases. We also evaluate gradient-based adaptive sampling, residual reweighting, and mild spatial derivative-penalty regularization. Across the reported benchmarks, the proposed framework reduces relative $L^2$ and absolute $L^\infty$ errors by nearly one to three orders of magnitude compared with the various PINN baselines. These results demonstrate the potential of first-order RPNNs for accurate approximation of phase-field dynamics with sharp transition layers.

papers.title: Torrelli's Question for Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
papers.abstract: Torrelli asked whether the class $[1/f]$ belongs to the intersection homology $\mathcal{D}$-module of a hypersurface if and only if $-1$ is a simple root of its local Bernstein-Sato polynomial. We prove this equivalence for isolated hypersurface germs with $2\le n\le 4$ variables, and we construct isolated counterexamples with $n$ variables for every $n\ge 5$. In fact a counterexample with $[1/f]\in\mathrm{IC}_D$ and $\mathrm{mult}_{s=-1}b_f(s)=r\ge 2$ always needs at least $r+3$ variables. The counterexamples modify a three-variable example of Saito and adjoin suitable pure powers in the new variables. We also show that a counterexample polynomial in $n$ variables needs at least $n+1$ monomials, and we record further cases in which the equivalence holds.

papers.title: Data handling, production, and simulation in the Muon g-2 Experiment at Fermilab
Twisted Block Particle Filters: A Local Particle-System Change of Measure for High-Dimensional State-Space Models
papers.abstract: Block particle filters mitigate weight degeneracy in high-dimensional state-space models, but their normalizer estimates can remain highly variable. We introduce a twisted block particle filter (TBPF) that incorporates predictive guidance through an exact change of measure at blockwise resampling. The method guide-tilts one uniformly selected offspring per block, leaves the state-transition kernel unchanged, and computes the resampling correction using finite empirical guide averages. We prove that this correction exactly preserves the finite-particle block particle filter normalizer expectation, separating the effect of guided sampling from the approximation introduced by spatial blocking. Our analysis provides exact conditional local moments and a one-step conditional central limit result. We further derive explicit bounds on the correction accumulated across blocks and time, establish fixed-horizon consistency of the block filter and corrected normalizer under suitable regularity and guide-range conditions, and identify conditional criteria for guide perturbations that reduce variance. Experiments on coupled linear Gaussian and stochastic-volatility models with up to 256 latent dimensions show lower measured log-normalizer variance. For stochastic volatility with a five-step guide, the median reduction is $38\%$. An application to a 100-dimensional financial portfolio panel extends the evaluation to real data.

papers.title: Increasing Quantum LDPC Code Distance through Explicit Extensions
papers.abstract: We give an explicit construction of quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes without searching for candidates at each size. A fixed pair partition (PP) and fixed integer parameters determine the parity-check matrices at a specified size. Using affine permutation matrices (APMs), we construct a $[[3072,772,32]]$ code with column weight 3 and check weight 8 in each of the X and Z parity-check matrices. A construction based on circulant permutation matrices (CPMs) gives $[[1270,260,\ge34]]$, with column weight 4 and check weight 10. We prove that the construction yields commuting checks and verify the resulting distances using exhaustive search and logical operators. For the main construction, we conjecture the existence of a finite structural distance upper bound and distance improvement toward that bound as the size increases.

papers.title: Degenerate symmetric formulation and principal subsystems for chemically reacting multi-temperature fluid mixtures
papers.abstract: We construct a degenerate symmetric first-order formulation and principal subsystems for chemically reacting multi-temperature fluid mixtures with independent constituent velocities and temperatures, viscosity, and heat conduction. Starting from the entropy-admissible Class-III theory of arXiv:2610.37637 , we characterize when its prescribed constituent Euler fluxes are generated by scalar potentials in the conservative entropy variables. Under the stated hypotheses the necessary and sufficient condition is that the separate Gibbs--Duhem one-forms $\omega_i$ vanish. This implies locally additive entropy, but it is not required by the general parent theory. In this subclass, the complete main field contains multipliers for both conservative balances and zero-storage constitutive equations. The spatial Hessians are symmetric, and the temporal Hessian is positive semidefinite and singular. For separated transport laws, eliminating auxiliary variables factorizes the positive-semidefinite dissipative principal symbol. We extend the algebraic Boillat--Ruggeri principal-subsystem construction to degenerate systems. Commuting restrictions yield a dissipative common-temperature system and a nested hierarchy of grouped-temperature Euler subsystems. Classical characteristic interlacing applies within the nested Euler hierarchy, whose temporal Hessians are positive definite. Separately, constrained entropy maximization defines an energy-equivalent common temperature and provides a thermodynamic Class-III-to-Class-II reduction for additive and nonadditive parent entropies. For a thermally reconstructed reference state, the full relative entropy splits exactly into the thermal projection deficit and the relative entropy of the retained variables. We derive the Class-II entropy-production identity and distinguish the thermodynamic projection from principal restrictions and dynamical relaxation limits.

papers.title: The Dynamical Manin-Mumford Conjecture for automorphisms of Hénon type
papers.abstract: We prove the dynamical Manin--Mumford conjecture for polynomial automorphisms of the complex affine plane of dynamical degree $>1$ proposed by Dujardin and Favre. More precisely, we prove that an irreducible algebraic curve contains infinitely many periodic points of such an automorphism if and only if it is the fixed locus of a polynomial involution conjugating some iterate of the automorphism to its inverse.

papers.title: Congruences modulo powers of $2$ and $3$ for Lin's function $\text{PDO}_t(n)$
papers.abstract: Let $\text{PDO}_t(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Confirming a conjecture of Singh and Barman (2025), Tang (2026) recently proved that $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{2m-1}n)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+1}}$ for all $m\geq1$ and $n\geq0$. Using elementary techniques, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{m+2}n)$, and we use them to determine $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{k}n)$ modulo one further power of $2$. More precisely, we show that the quotient of $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{k}n)$ by the relevant power of $2$ is odd exactly when $n$ is an odd square, or $2$, $3$ or $6$ times an odd square, depending on $k$. As a consequence, we obtain several new infinite families of congruences modulo arbitrary powers of $2$, such as \[ \text{PDO}_t\bigl(3\times4^{m}(3n+2)\bigr)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+4}}, \] and \[\text{PDO}_t\bigl(3\times4^{m}(6n+5)\bigr)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+5}}. \] We also obtain an analogous improvement of a result of Li and Tang (2026) modulo powers of $3$, and an infinite family of internal congruences modulo powers of $2$.

papers.title: Neutral and Charged Pion Modes in Magnetized Quark Matter with Chiral Imbalance
papers.abstract: We investigate neutral and charged pion correlations in a two-flavor Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model at finite temperature in the presence of a uniform magnetic field and a prescribed chiral chemical potential $\mu_5$, using the mean-field approximation and the single-channel random phase approximation (RPA). The pion masses are defined by the selected positive-energy zeros of the real parts of the corresponding inverse propagators. We demonstrate that, at zero external spatial momentum, the complete Dirac trace in the neutral channel eliminates mixed-branch contributions, thereby precluding a finite-energy Landau cut. In contrast, the charged channel allows non-diagonal Landau-level transitions and exhibits both pair-production and thermal-scattering contributions. With increasing $\mu_5$, the neutral-pion mass exhibits only a weak variation at low temperature, while the rapid decrease of the mass shifts toward higher temperatures. The charged-pion mass decreases with increasing $\mu_5$ over the selected solution segments. This behavior may help account for the lattice QCD results. At zero temperature and fixed $\mu_5$, increasing the magnetic field lowers the neutral-pion mass but raises the charged-pion mass.

papers.title: Censored Regression Models with Endogeneity: A Survey
papers.abstract: This survey article provides a comprehensive overview of methodologies developed to handle endogeneity in censored regression models. We emphasize their theoretical basis, and estimating methodologies. The paper summarizes the benefits and drawbacks of each technique and addresses expansions to nonlinear, panel, and high-dimensional settings, offering researchers practical assistance and identifying options for future methodological improvement in censored models with endogenous regressors.

papers.title: Lagrangian Construction of the Enveloping Superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$
papers.abstract: We give a Lagrangian construction of the enveloping superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$. More precisely, we realize the Schur superalgebra $S(m|n,r)$, the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$ on $(\mathbb Q^{m|n})^{\otimes r}$, via the top Borel--Moore homology of mixed Steinberg varieties. Their top-dimensional components are indexed by the admissible matrices of Du and Rui and meet a natural symplectic open subset in Lagrangian subvarieties. As applications, we realize the irreducible polynomial representations of $\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n}$ on the relevant homology of the fibers of these maps, establish a geometric $(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n},\mathfrak{gl}_{k|l})$-Howe duality and confirm new cases of a conjecture of Douglass and Röhrle on generalized Steinberg varieties.

papers.title: Perturbed QMC designs and reduced QMC strength
papers.abstract: Small errors in sampling locations can change the convergence rate of a cubature rule. We study this effect for equal-weight integration on spheres and determine how accurately the nodes must be realized to retain optimal Sobolev rates. Under an average energy condition on the reference nodes, we establish sharp perturbation bounds and characterize how the decay of node errors affects quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) strength, which measures the smoothness range over which optimal rates hold. We identify when this strength is preserved and when it can decrease, and show that sufficiently slow decay of node errors can destroy all optimal Sobolev rates. For a reference rule with optimal convergence, we further establish a necessary and sufficient condition on node accuracy for retaining the optimal rate uniformly over all permitted perturbations. Numerical experiments with spherical designs, Fekete points, and Coulomb-energy points illustrate the different stability regimes.

papers.title: Advanced Reactance Method - A Novel Approach for Distance Protection in Presence of Grid-Following Inverter-Based-Resources
papers.abstract: Renewable Energy Sources and consequently inverter-based resources (IBRs) are increasing worldwide. Grid-following (GFL) IBR control is the state-of-the-art. GFL IBRs exhibit different fault behavior compared to classical synchronous generators -- particularly in terms of Fault-Ride-Through (FRT) characteristics, which are critical for grid protection relaying. Grid protection must work securely, selectively and dependably, regardless of the feeding source. As common protection algorithms are designed for fault behavior determined by synchronous generators, their performance is expected to be compromised in the presence of GFL IBRs. Distance Protection is a widely used protection algorithm at all voltage levels. Literature shows that the FRT behavior of GFL IBRs impacts the Distance Protection relaying adversely. This paper proposes the Advanced Reactance Method, a further development of the Classical Reactance Method for Distance Protection in the presence of GFL IBRs. The key idea of the proposed method is to make the algorithm independent of the feeding source impedance. Therefore, the negative sequence voltage is taken into account along with the negative sequence current. This makes the algorithm independent of the FRT behavior of GFL IBRs, even in case of suppression of negative sequence current during unsymmetrical faults. Moreover, correct settings for the classical method in the presence of GFL IBRs are presented as a solution for relays without the advanced method. The novel algorithm is evaluated against the correctly parameterized Classical Reactance Method and the Distance Protection algorithm.

papers.title: Metastable states are precursors of Turing patterns in Adaptive Networks
Polynomial identities of the two-dimensional simple right-symmetric algebra
papers.abstract: We describe a basis for the polynomial identities satisfied by the unique two-dimensional simple right-symmetric algebra $B$ over a field of characteristic zero. Modulo the right-symmetric identity, this basis consists of two irreducible identities of degree three. We construct linear bases for the multilinear components of the relatively free algebra of the variety $\mathcal V=\operatorname{var}(B)$ and determine their decompositions into Specht modules. Using the resulting $S_n$-module decompositions, we prove that the commutator subspace is right nilpotent in every proper subvariety of $\mathcal V$. Moreover, in any proper subvariety satisfying a nontrivial identity of degree $n\ge2$, the index of right nilpotence of the commutator subspace is at most $2n$.

papers.title: Statistical mechanics of linear classification on hierarchical tree data
Finite-Time Singularities of the $L_β$-Gradient Flow in a Kähler Surface
papers.abstract: We study finite-time singularities of the $L_\beta$-gradient flow of closed symplectic surfaces in a compact Kähler surface, with $\beta > 0$ fixed. We derive the evolution equation for the second fundamental form and obtain a lower bound on the blow-up rate of its maximum squared norm. Combining this bound with a local curvature propagation estimate and the weighted monotonicity formula, we rule out Type I singularities.

papers.title: Reassessment of Planetary Parameters and Statistical Validation of 187 Kepler Habitable-Zone and Near Habitable Confirmed and Candidate Planets
Rate-Quality-Energy Convex Hull for High Dynamic Range Adaptive Video Streaming
papers.abstract: High Dynamic Range (HDR) video introduces substantially higher decoding complexity and energy consumption than Standard Dynamic Range (SDR), yet most adaptive streaming pipelines still rely on bitrate ladders optimized using SDR-oriented metrics such as VMAF. These ladders fail to capture HDR-specific perceptual behavior and ignore decoder-side energy, resulting in energetically inefficient operating points. This work proposes a rate-quality-energy convex-hull optimization framework that jointly considers bitrate, HDR-aware perceptual quality (HDRVMAF), and client-side processing energy, including decoding and upscaling. Experiments on twelve 4K HDR sequences from the LIVE HDR Video Quality Assessment Database evaluate 72 representations per clip and demonstrate that traditional VMAF-optimized ladders frequently select high-resolution encodes that become dominated once energy is accounted for. Compared to the Default HLS ladder, our HDR-aware method achieves substantial bitrate savings of up to 54.34% at equal HDRVMAF, while yielding relative client-side energy reductions of up to 43.10% under higher energy weighting. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework as a practical foundation for constructing HDR bitrate ladders that explicitly expose and control perceptual quality-energy trade-offs.

papers.title: A General Non-Stationary Channel Model for Autonomous Vehicle Communications in Underground Spaces
papers.abstract: Autonomous vehicles exhibit high mobility and environmental adaptability, making them well-suited for underground inspection and rescue missions. In this paper, a general three-dimensional (3D) non-stationary geometry-based stochastic model (GBSM) is proposed for autonomous vehicle communications in underground spaces. The proposed channel model accounts for the 3D mobility of autonomous vehicles and can be adapted to pillar, tunnel, and cave scenarios. To characterize the structural and physical features of underground spaces, the proposed model incorporates the generation and evolution of spatially dispersed and/or directionally confined clusters along with their constituent specular/dense multipath components (SMCs/DMCs). Additionally, the proposed channel model considers channel non-stationarity, waveguide effect, and near-field/far-field effects. Statistical properties, including space-time-frequency correlation functions (STF-CFs), delay/angular/Doppler power spectral densities (PSDs), root mean square (RMS) delay spread, and stationary interval, are derived and analyzed. The validity of the proposed channel model is substantiated through comparative analysis between measurement and simulation results.

papers.title: Inner derivations and automorphism groups of vertex operator algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type. We prove that the zero mode map $V_1\to\operatorname{Der}(V)$, $h\mapsto h_0$, is an isomorphism of Lie algebras. We prove surjectivity using traces on finite sums of weight spaces and Li's module construction, and injectivity using the vacuum character of Zhu's algebra. It follows that $\operatorname{Inn}(V)$ is the identity component of $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ and has finite index in $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$. Moreover, $\operatorname{dim}\operatorname{Aut}(V)=\dim V_1$, so $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ is finite if and only if $V_1=0$.

papers.title: Beyond Raw IQ: Compact Semantic Representations for Task Oriented Automatic Modulation Classification
papers.abstract: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is an important component of modern wireless communication systems, but conventional signal representations can be expensive to store, process, and communicate, particularly under noisy channel conditions. This work investigates whether learned semantic representations can provide a compact alternative to high-dimensional in-phase and quadrature (IQ) representations while retaining robustness to noise. Starting from a 2048-dimensional IQ representation, we evaluate learned semantic representations with dimensions of 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64. Across the evaluated configurations, a 16-dimensional representation provides the strongest overall trade-off between classification performance, robustness, and representation size. The resulting representation achieves a 128x compression ratio and a 99.22% reduction in dimensionality. We further evaluate representation stability across signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), compare semantic representations with a raw-IQ CNN, analyze per-class robustness, and perform five-seed validation. The five-seed evaluation produces an average accuracy of (49.22 +- 0.52)% and Macro-F1 of (49.27 +- 0.53)% across the evaluated SNR range. These results indicate that learned semantic compression can produce a substan- tially smaller representation while preserving useful classification information and improving geometric stability under noise.

papers.title: Large Deviations and Critical Scaling in the Finite-Population Granovetter Threshold Model
Learning free energy across a differentiable temperature range by deep generative modeling
Profinite groups with coprime automorphisms whose orbits generate nilpotent subgroups
papers.abstract: Suppose that a profinite group $G$ admits a finite group of coprime automorphisms $A$ such that for any $\varphi\in A$ every subgroup $\langle x^{\langle\varphi\rangle}\rangle$ generated by the $\langle\varphi\rangle$-orbit of an element $x\in G$ is nilpotent. It is proved that $[G,A]$ is pronilpotent, and if $A$ is soluble and the fixed-point subgroup $C_G(A)$ is locally nilpotent, then $G$ is locally nilpotent.

papers.title: Ion Backflow Suppression and Absorption Dynamics in Cascaded GEM Structures
Lagrangian particle simulations of an idealized deep convective squall line: Aggregation, fragmentation, and their polarimetric signatures
papers.abstract: We investigate secondary ice production (SIP) in an idealized deep convective squall line using the Lagrangian particle model McSnow coupled to ICON. The model represents ice particle properties, including habit, riming degree, and mass composition. We introduce a parameterization of collision-induced ice--ice fragmentation linked to apparent density as a measure of particle fragility. We compare rime splintering (RS), freezing fragmentation (FF), and collision-induced fragmentation (CF), including turbulence-enhanced collision rates. Collision-induced fragmentation is the dominant SIP mechanism, strongly increasing ice number concentrations in the dendritic growth zone. Freezing fragmentation contributes little because sufficiently large raindrops are scarce. Rime splintering produces secondary ice at lower altitudes and indirectly promotes large aggregates. Turbulence has little effect on fragmentation but enhances the aggregation of fragments. Fragmentation shifts the particle size distribution toward smaller sizes and reduces precipitation, while turbulence-enhanced aggregation partly restores large particles and precipitation. McRadar forward simulations show that SIP affects radar moments and Doppler spectra. Specific differential phase KDP provides the clearest conventional radar signature of fragmentation. Spectral differential reflectivity identifies secondary ice source regions through enhanced signals at the slow edge of the Doppler spectrum. Our results identify collision-induced fragmentation as a key source of secondary ice in deep convection and show that its impact depends on interactions with aggregation and turbulence. Spectral polarimetric radar observations may help constrain SIP in nature.

papers.title: History-bearing thalamocortical signals reconstruct and redirect later decisions in a circuit model
papers.abstract: Experience can guide an ambiguous choice or bias a choice despite strong current evidence. We asked how a thalamocortical circuit carries historical content forward and regulates its influence across successive decisions. In published data from adult male mice, suppressing posterior parietal cortex (PPC) or pulvinar (PUL) improved current judgments most when sensory history conflicted with the stimulus, reflecting reduced historical weighting. In trained thalamocortical circuit models, replaying recorded PUL input to PPC reconstructed a historical trace after equalizing complete recipient states across histories. Replaying the opposite history redirected the later choice, even after the circuit correctly judged an intervening strong stimulus. This historical message occupied a low-dimensional direction in thalamic output that remained broadly reachable under firing-rate bounds; redistributing the arriving current at matched energy showed that fine spatial organization, beyond total input strength, selectively shapes later history use without disrupting current choices. Strong sensory evidence suppressed historical output while preserving internal state differences, whereas ambiguity recruited neuronal rectification thresholds and readout alignment to express history. Small shifts in the cortical operating point modulated later historical influence, and partial attenuation of recurrent drive reduced it across all circuits while preserving current commitments; correspondingly, recurrent dynamics were essential for predicting post-stimulus trajectories in held-out histories. Together, these findings distinguish three operations in history-guided choice: returning thalamocortical input determines which past is reconstructed, recurrent dynamics carry its influence forward across intervening demands, and current sensory evidence gates how strongly it enters the decision.

papers.title: Floquet-Induced Valley Polarization and Topological Phases in Twisted Bilayer Graphene Heterostructures
AI Meets Turbulence Modeling: Balancing Causation, Correlation, and User Intent
papers.abstract: Turbulence states vary widely in modeling difficulty, requiring distinct paradigms; thus, no single AI or data-driven approach suits all flows. We propose an operational framework classifying data-driven turbulence modeling by balancing physical causation and statistical correlation via non-equilibrium flow memory and user intent. Using the Mori--Zwanzig projection formalism, we decompose unclosed turbulent stress into a local response ($\tau_{ij}^L$) and a spatio-temporally non-local memory integral ($\tau_{ij}^{NL}$). Near statistical equilibrium, rapid relaxation suppresses advective memory, letting local correlations capture physical causation via intrusive $\tau_{ij}^L$ constitutive relations in Reynolds-Averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) equations. Because the elliptic Poisson equation for fluctuating pressure couples stress evolution to eddy dimensionality beyond single-point velocity-gradient componentiality, local closures are not strictly valid even at equilibrium, yet remain acceptable engineering approximations. In non-equilibrium turbulence, modeling bifurcates by user intent. For predicting unseen geometries, large coherent structures sustain non-local memory ($\tau_{ij}^{NL}$), invalidating local total-stress closures and requiring first-principles causal scale resolution guided by Rules-Augmented AI (RAAI), with resolution set by a recent non-equilibrium theory. Conversely, for rapid design in a known, parameterized coherent flow class, a purely correlational strategy suffices: combining Non-Intrusive Reduced-Order Modeling (NIROM) with uncentered Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) across multi-realization ensembles yields zero-solver synthesis of stationary statistics and unsteady coherent evolution from governing dimensionless parameters. This framework aligns physical causation, statistical correlation, and user intent across flow regimes.

papers.title: Worst case tractability of weighted linear tensor product problems under the absolute error criterion
papers.abstract: This paper studies weighted linear tensor product problems in the worst case setting. We consider algorithms that use finitely many evaluations of arbitrary continuous linear functionals. We investigate algebraic and exponential tractability under the absolute error criterion in the case $\lambda_1>1$, where $\lambda_1$ is the square of the univariate maximal singular value. We obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for various notions of algebraic and exponential tractability on weights and univariate singular values. Our approach is to convert algebraic tractability of the problems for the absolute error criterion with $\lambda_1 > 1$ to exponential tractability of the normalized problems. Specifically, we solve Open Problem 27 as posed by Novak and Woźniakowski (2008).

papers.title: Simplified Plotkin-type Bounds for Function-Correcting Codes with b-Symbol and Sum-Rank Distances
papers.abstract: Function-correcting codes (FCCs) are a coding framework that enables reliable communication with minimal redundancy while ensuring the recovery of specific functions of transmitted messages. FCCs have been studied recently under the $b$-symbol distance and the sum-rank distance. Existing general Plotkin-type bounds on the optimal redundancy of FCCs under these distances require computing the pairwise distances between vectors that map to different function values. As a result, these bounds are often computationally difficult to determine. In this paper, we derive simplified Plotkin-type bounds on the optimal redundancy of FCCs under the $b$-symbol and sum-rank distances. These bounds depend only on the number of message vectors corresponding to each function value and the sum of pairwise distances among vectors mapped to the same function value. The proposed bounds apply to arbitrary functions and are considerably easier to evaluate than existing Plotkin-type bounds. The known simplified bounds for linear functions under the $b$-symbol and sum-rank distances are subsumed as special cases of the proposed bounds. Furthermore, we obtain a tighter bound for linear functions under the sum-rank distance than the existing bound.

papers.title: Local Pressure Induced Quantum Dot to Ring Transition and Aharonov Bohm Effect in Reconfigurable MoTe2 Bilayers
The Seifert--van Kampen Theorem
papers.abstract: The Seifert--van Kampen theorem computes the fundamental group of a space from an open cover by two path-connected subspaces, provided their intersection is path-connected. This article gives a self-contained account of the theorem, explains its universal-property formulation as a pushout in the category of groups, and derives several standard computations. Particular attention is paid to base points, the role of path-connectedness, and the passage from a topological decomposition to a group presentation. The purpose is expository: the results are classical, and no claim of a new theorem is made.

papers.title: Transient coupling of Marangoni spreading and interfacial waves
papers.abstract: How does an initially non-uniform distribution of surfactant generate waves on a de- formable interface, and how do those waves then govern the redistribution of the surfactant? We answer this question for the linear Cauchy-Poisson problem of an axisymmetric interface between two viscous fluids, released from rest with independently prescribed distributions of surfactant and of interface displacement, by Hankel and Laplace transforms. In Stokes flow the pressure and the viscous normal stress of the Marangoni flow cancel in the nor- mal traction on the interface, for any viscosity ratio, so that the surfactant relaxes without displacing the interface: the coupling between surfactant redistribution and interface de- formation is inertial. With inertia, the Marangoni flow initiates a capillary-gravity wave whose polarity, at leading order for thin boundary layers, is set by the sign of $\rho_l \mu_l - \rho_u \mu_u $, and the surfactant is then carried by the wave, so that its concentration performs weakly damped oscillations at the wave frequency after the Marangoni relaxation of a flat surface has ended. The amplitude of these oscillations is given in closed form at small viscosity; its maximum does not coincide with that of the familiar resonant damping, and the surfactant and the interface shape decouple exactly only when the two fluids have equal densities and viscosities. A localized displacement radiates a wave packet that the surfactant damps, and a localized surfactant redistribution initiates a wave on an initially flat interface. Direct numerical simulations with sharp geometric surfactant transport verify these predictions.

papers.title: Massive Particles in Carrollian Holography
papers.abstract: Understanding how massive particles are encoded in boundary operators is a central problem in Carrollian holography. We construct a three-dimensional Carrollian description of a massive scalar in four-dimensional flat spacetime, together with an explicit bulk-to-boundary integral transform. In this construction, nonzero mass requires infinitely many linearly independent primary states, while the absence of bulk spin imposes relations among their descendants. We show that these relations are equivalent to null-state decoupling and give a local constraint on the boundary fields. The integral transform preserves the full Poincaré symmetry and maps bulk scalar data to fields satisfying this constraint. We also obtain two- and three-point functions and the associated formal operator product expansion coefficients. The integral transform evaluates bulk data at complex momenta, making analytic continuation essential in Lorentzian signature. This construction provides a concrete starting point for relating massive scattering amplitudes to Carrollian correlators and for reconstructing bulk fields from boundary data.

papers.title: A Proof of Blackburn's Conjecture on Non-Overlapping Codes
papers.abstract: A code is non-overlapping if no nonempty proper prefix of a codeword is a suffix of a codeword. Let $S_n(q)$ be the largest size of a non-overlapping code of length $n$ over an alphabet of size $q$. Levenshtein proved that $S_n(q)\le c_nq^n$, where $c_n=(1/n)\bigl((n-1)/n\bigr)^{n-1}$. The codes $I^{n-1}J$, where $I$ and $J$ partition the alphabet, attain this bound when $n$ divides $q$, and Blackburn conjectured that for every $n$ and all sufficiently large $q$, the best such code is a maximum non-overlapping code. We prove this conjecture. The proof uses generating functions for the nested partitions that describe maximal non-overlapping codes. We also show that only the codes $I^{n-1}J$ with $|I|=(n-1)q/n$ and their reversals meet Levenshtein's bound.

papers.title: AdapToC: A Unified Framework for Multi-Task Visual Token Communication
papers.abstract: Pretrained discrete visual tokenizers supply compact latents for synthesis, recognition, and embodied perception, yet wireless token streaming remains fragile. Under fading and noisy pilots, hard cyclic redundancy check (CRC) erasures turn corrupted blocks into missing tokens while frozen decoders amplify edge errors, which can collapse unequal error protection (UEP) into a binary choice between strong coding and omission under severe fading. Soft bit posteriors break this collapse. We present AdapToC, a single-pass transceiver that restores multi-tier rate-distortion tradeoffs without altering tokenizer weights or differentiating through pixel decoders. We align codebook geometry to the channel via offline frequency-weighted Pseudo-Gray relabeling and Halton dispersion to contract bit and burst errors with zero overhead. Because soft recovery pulls intermediate rates onto the three-tier convex hull, our unit-gated AdaLN sender schedules protection tiers across channel budgets, while our pilot-calibrated receiver feeds factorized codebook posteriors into a ConvNeXt-attention restorer with CRC bypass. We co-train AdapToC solely in latent space via counterfactual utility estimation and codebook cross-entropy regularization. On identical VQGAN-f16 tokens, AdapToC outperforms TONIC and adaptive TokenCom+AMC, cuts multi-SNR Rayleigh LPIPS from 0.6551 to 0.3312 within the frozen-tokenizer PSNR ceiling, and saves 43.8% Rician-K6 symbols at matched quality. Our single-pass restorer runs 8.3x faster than iterative resampling, raises accuracy while accelerating decoder-free recognition 20.6x, and improves fidelity plug-and-play across TiTok, VAR, and zero-shot NuPlan.

papers.title: R2WM: Recursive Reasoning Wireless Model for Long-Horizon mmWave Beam Prediction
papers.abstract: Long-horizon beam prediction aims to extend beam-training intervals while supporting beam alignment in mobile millimeter-wave systems. Although pretrained large models can improve prediction over compact recurrent baselines, their large backbones impose substantial storage and computing requirements. To address this limitation, we propose a recursive reasoning wireless model (R2WM). Given a fixed history of beam indices and angles of departure (AoDs), R2WM repeatedly updates coupled latent and prediction states using a shared causal-attention backbone before jointly decoding the future beam indices. Backbone reuse increases computational depth at fixed parameter count. In the standard 10-step DeepMIMO setting, R2WM achieves an average normalized beamforming gain of 0.9597, compared with 0.8629 for the prompt-as-prefix large language model, with 99.1% fewer parameters and 59.1% fewer counted floating-point operations. Transfer experiments show that R2WM retains normalized gain under the tested carrier-frequency and antenna-count changes, while its beam-index-only variant retains gain under the tested base-station change. Component ablations show higher gains with historical AoD conditioning and causal attention. Recursion analysis reveals a gain-computation trade-off across separately trained configurations with the same parameter count. An additional comparison with a nonrecursive Transformer of similar parameter count shows higher gain for R2WM at greater computational cost. These results support accurate long-horizon beam prediction without a large pretrained backbone.

papers.title: Pauli-consistent ensemble Monte Carlo method for bipolar charge transport in graphene
papers.abstract: We develop a Pauli-consistent ensemble Monte Carlo method for bipolar charge transport in graphene, with an explicit treatment of phonon-assisted interband scattering, including electron-hole generation and recombination. The method employs a valence-vacancy representation to describe coupled electron and hole populations without explicitly simulating the highly populated valence band. It preserves the discrete occupation bounds during both free flight and scattering while conserving net charge. The numerical properties of the method are assessed through sensitivity and refinement studies and comparison with an independent deterministic discontinuous Galerkin solution of the same kinetic model. The two approaches show very good agreement for the time evolution, carrier distributions, and steady-state transport observables across the investigated transport regimes. The results also demonstrate the computational practicality of the method for microscopic simulations of bipolar graphene transport.

papers.title: Normal Homogeneous Counterexamples to Wolf's Homogeneity Conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct free Clifford--Wolf subgroups of order two whose quotients of compact, connected, simply connected normal homogeneous manifolds are not homogeneous. The universal covers are the oriented real flag manifolds $M_{d}=SO(N)/\prod_{i=1}^{q}SO(d_{i})$, equipped with the metric induced by the negative Killing form, where $N\geq4$ and $q\geq3$ is odd. We determine its full connected centralizer, the effective connected isometry group of the quotient, and the corresponding orbit space. These calculations prove nonhomogeneity and give explicit formulas for the cohomogeneity, fundamental group, and Euler characteristic. These examples are found by ChatGPT 6 Astra.

papers.title: Exact-Order Mellin Transfer and Prime-Support Filtrations
papers.abstract: We establish a unified exact-order Mellin transfer principle that converts the multiplicity of a critical Mellin pole into arithmetic prime-support depth. For an exact-order Möbius transform in lattice dimension $\ell$, a base pole of order $r$ at $s=\ell/2$ satisfies \[ \ord_{s=\ell/2}\widehat{\mathscr P_{N,\ell}H}=\omega(N)-r. \] The complete Jordan--Mellin jet is explicit, and its first surviving coefficient selects the canonical weight $W(N)=\prod_{p\mid N}\log p$. After the corresponding jet normalization, this weight governs a kernel-independent moving-support law and a mod-Poisson regime. With simultaneous splitting marks in finite Galois extensions, the same weight yields a multivariate polynomial whose mixed coefficients are reciprocal compositum degrees; it recovers pairwise intersection degrees and, under a full-rank hypothesis, also governs the coupled saddle and large-deviation geometry. In spectral geometry, a two-variable family attached to any positive self-adjoint elliptic operator has a transverse normal crossing whose parameter jets generate every higher critical pole order; exact-order dilation therefore realizes every positive prime-support depth. An explicit Bernoulli--Barnes/Barnes--Epstein model shows how a pole collision shifts the finite critical layer from one-prime to two-prime support. Thus arithmetic support, Galois compositum data, and spectral pole geometry arise from one exact-order Mellin mechanism.

papers.title: A high-speed and high-resolution 3D velocity map imaging system with a neuromorphic camera
Orthosymplectic $K$-matrices in small dimensions
papers.abstract: Using elementary methods, we describe coideal subalgebras of quantum orthosymplectic algebras of small dimensions, classify the corresponding $K$-matrices and find explicitly the centralizers of these subalgebras in the vector representation. The main attention is paid to generators with a Cartan term. For them, at generic values of the parameters, we find the centralizers and all $K$-matrices and describe the decomposition of the vector representation over the coideal subalgebra. We find all special values of the parameters of two types and, at a generic point of each set of special values, describe the decomposition of the vector representation and all $K$-matrices. At special values of the first type the dimension of the centralizer grows. One hypersurface of such values is related to Cartan terms, and on it one of the generators is given by the same formula as in the quantum electrical algebra. At special values of the second type the dimension of the centralizer is the same, but nonzero nilpotent elements appear in it. The $K$-matrices on the sets of special values of the second type are obtained from those already found by substituting the condition, and there are no others. We describe the classical limit, including the limit of special values. We formulate an observation relating the admissibility of a Cartan term to the first homology of the classical subalgebra.

papers.title: An Algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay
papers.abstract: A 4-dimensional algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay over an arbitrary field is constructed. Furthermore, it is shown that every three-dimensional graded ASL domain is Cohen--Macaulay.

papers.title: Operating-Condition Normalization in C-MAPSS: Matched Historical Baselines, Multi-Seed Robustness, and Prognostic-Score Trade-offs
papers.abstract: Operating-state changes can obscure turbofan degradation signals, but a reduction in remaining-useful-life (RUL) error after condition-wise standardization may reflect weaknesses of the comparison features instead of a unique benefit of normalization. A controlled retrospective audit examines NASA C-MAPSS FD002 and FD004 with engine-disjoint folds, raw condition identifiers, two constructions of causal history, early-life baselines, and continuous operating-setting correction. Ridge regression, random forests and XGBoost are compared under explicit training-engine-only fitting rules. The previously reported XGBoost FD004 terminal RMSE decreased from 30.38 to 29.08 cycles following six-condition standardization; however, raw sensor values accompanied by condition-matched histories and condition identifiers achieved 28.09 cycles, reversing the naive point estimate ranking, although the paired-engine interval spans zero. For FD002, normalized XGBoost reduced terminal RMSE yet increased the asymmetric NASA score (12,616 to 13,289). Additional model-seed, condition count, RUL-cap, grouped-validation and explanation checks test sensitivity rather than postulating a universally optimal representation. The six clusters reproduce known simulator operating regimes; no new condition discovery algorithm, causal diagnostic method, or field ready prognostic system is claimed. Since the official test endpoints were also used in earlier exploratory comparisons, all newly examined alternatives are reported as retrospective benchmark evidence, not as results from a pristine confirmatory holdout.

papers.title: Exactly solvable Brill waves: explicit gravitational-wave initial data with trapped surfaces
The Complexity of Oracle-Efficient Realizable Transductive Learning
papers.abstract: In realizable transductive online learning, the learner knows the entire sequence of $T$ instances in advance, and the labels are consistent with one of $N$ hypotheses. With explicit access to the hypothesis class, the halving algorithm makes at most $\log_2 N$ mistakes. Can a comparable guarantee be achieved using only polynomially many empirical risk minimization (ERM) queries? We answer this question negatively, even for a weighted-ERM oracle that optimizes arbitrary real-valued linear objectives and returns a complete maximizing hypothesis. For every fixed $\beta\in(0,1)$ and every randomized learner making polynomially many oracle queries, there exists a fixed realizable instance with exactly $N=2^{\lfloor T^\beta\rfloor}$ hypotheses on which the learner makes $\Omega_\beta(\sqrt{T\log N})$ mistakes in expectation. This matches the agnostic-rate upper bound achieved by random playout using $O(T)$ oracle calls. The separation persists for much smaller classes as well: along a sequence with $\log N=\Theta((\log T)^2)$, we establish a mistake lower bound of $\exp(\Omega(\log T/\log\log T))$. Our main technical contribution is a composition lemma that combines two realizable prediction problems such that their mistake lower bounds add, up to a small loss, while their hypothesis class sizes grow only additively. Iterating this lemma yields a family of hard instances spanning the desired parameter regimes, establishing a sharp separation between information-theoretic and oracle-efficient mistake guarantees.

papers.title: Synthesis Method-dependent Resist-like Behavior of Liquid Crystalline Graphene Oxide Films Under Electron Beam Irradiation
Quantum Hall Effect in a 3D Cross-Dimensional Quantum Anomalous Hall System
Nonlinear Stability of Two-Dimensional Poiseuille Flow via a Dilation Multiplier
papers.abstract: We investigate nonlinear stability of the Poiseuille flow for 2D incompressible Navier Stokes this http URL key observation is that, after Fourier transformation, the Poiseuille flow and its curvature give rise to a kinetic operator and a potential whose commutators with the same bounded dilation multiplier are both this http URL close the nonlinear estimates, we incorporate the zero mode of the initial velocity into the background shear flow, thereby further improving the threshold.

papers.title: Minimal Three-Band Model and $d$-Wave Superconductivity in La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_8$
Feshbach resonances of the second order in a Friedrichs model
papers.abstract: We consider an extended version of the matrix Friedrichs model that may produce Feshbach resonances of the second order. In this model, under enlarging of the coupling constant, a pair of eigenvalues of the unperturbed Hamiltonian embedded into the continuous spectrum first transforms in resonances of the first order. At some moment later on, these two resonances merge into a single resonance but of the second order, and we fix conditions for this event. Being based on the operator interpretation of resonances, we found that, in the case under consideration, the operator roots of the transfer function have a very particular structure.

papers.title: Evolution and Prospects of Higgs Boson Searches Beyond the Standard Model
