papers.abstract: The search for Higgs bosons Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) began intensively at the Large Electron-Positron (LEP) collider (1989-2000), continued at the Tevatron (2001-2011), and entered a new era with the start of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) in 2010. While the discovery of a Higgs boson in 2012 established the Standard Model mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking, it also opened a wide landscape of open questions that motivate ongoing BSM Higgs searches. This review traces the evolution of these searches across experiments, highlighting both experimental techniques and underlying theoretical ideas in an accessible manner. Emphasis is placed on how different collider environments shaped search strategies and how seemingly subtle experimental effects, such as small excesses, non-standard decay topologies, or suppressed couplings, can provide insight into the possible structure of extended Higgs sectors. By connecting historical developments with current analyses and future prospects, this article aims not only to summarise results but also to provide students and newcomers with intuitive insight into how Higgs searches are designed, interpreted, and continuously refined. It illustrates how experimental challenges translate into physics opportunities, thereby inviting the next generation of researchers to contribute to one of the central questions in particle physics: whether the Higgs sector is minimal or part of a more complex structure.

papers.title: VEGA: A Scalable Software-Hardware Co-design for Genome Alignment using RVV Extension
papers.abstract: Dynamic programming (DP)-based genome sequence analysis is fundamental to computational genomics, but it remains computationally intensive as genomic data volumes continue to outpace Moore's Law. Existing hardware accelerators often sacrifice programmability and scalability across diverse alignment algorithms. In this work, we present VEGA, a scalable software-hardware co-design that accelerates genome alignment using RISC-V Vector extensions. VEGA introduces specialized vector instructions and three key innovations: a Forefront Stationary dataflow that minimizes off-chip memory access, intersequence parallelism that maximizes SIMD lane utilization, and custom ISA extensions that accelerate core alignment operations. Evaluations show that VEGA achieves up to 15.1x and 9.7x speedups for Edit Distance and Smith-Waterman algorithms over the Ara2-RVV vector baseline, sustaining 10.2x and 6.7x gains for 10kbp sequences. Post-synthesis results indicate only 1.0% area overhead compared to a standard RISC-V core, with performance-per-area efficiency rivaling specialized ASICs. VEGA thus achieves a balanced advancement in efficiency, programmability, and scalability for genome sequence alignment.

papers.title: US-Seg: One Reference for Universal Ultrasound Segmentation
papers.abstract: Recent ultrasound foundation models have demonstrated strong feature extraction capabilities across organs, tasks, and imaging conditions. However, converting these representations into segmentation still requires finetuning on annotated target data. To reduce reliance on task-specific finetuning, existing universal ultrasound segmentation methods typically adopt prompt-based target specification, mainly through spatial prompts in SAM-style models or task prompts exemplified by MOFO. Yet, directly segmenting targets unseen during training still requires repeated per-image interaction or target-specific adaptation. We propose US-Seg, a universal ultrasound segmentation framework that uses only a single annotated reference to specify the target and directly predicts its mask in query images without finetuning. The fundamental insight of US-Seg is to reformulate segmentation from direct image-to-label mapping for predefined targets into a shared structural recovery process learned from heterogeneous reference-query pairs through masked label reconstruction, thereby making a single reference sufficient for target specification. Boundary-centric label masking emphasizes ambiguous boundaries, encouraging transferable structural cues rather than target-specific appearance patterns. Using these structure-enriched representations, multi-level bidirectional reference-query interaction aligns the reference-defined target with the query. Finally, a prediction-aware iterative decoder uses intermediate predictions to progressively correct residual structural errors under reference guidance. Without repeated interaction or laborious annotation, US-Seg achieves an average Dice of 81.85% across six evaluations covering cross-site and cross-task generalization, outperforming the strongest label-reference method by 24.30%, while also delivering the best in-domain performance.

papers.title: On a simple family of Ricci-flows of O(3)-hypersurfaces: Counterexamples to the theorem on the preservation of positive definite Ricci curvature everywhere
papers.abstract: This note provides a concise derivation of the equation of Ricci áows on O(n)-rotational hypersurfaces in En+1 which consists of a pair of parabolic equations (cf. Lemma 2 of ß4) via simple applications of classical theorems of rotational surfaces in E3, governing the Ricci-evolution of their generating plane curves. Furthermore, the second equation can be transformed to that of the evolution equation of their "curvature proÖles" (cf. Lemmas 3 and 3íof ß4). In ß5, we consider a speciÖc family of initial generating curves of "curvature proÖles" that are only tiny modiÖcations of the constant function K= 1 R ;R 1, in a very small vicinity of the symmetric middle point as indicated in Fig. 2. Note that the short-time unique existence of analytic solutions of such a simple system of parabolic equations follows simply via Nash-Moser Theory. The simple estimate of ß5 shows the curvature k1( t(0)) is already becoming negative at a very short time (cf. ß5.3).

papers.title: Integral abelianizations of higher spin Torelli subgroups
papers.abstract: We determine the integral abelianizations of the Torelli subgroups preserving an $r$-spin structure for $r\geqslant2$ and genus $g\geqslant5$. Set $n=r/\gcd(r,2)$. For a surface with one boundary component, the free rank agrees with that of the Torelli group, and the torsion subgroup is the direct sum of the usual Birman--Craggs--Johnson $2$-torsion and $\mathbb{Z}/n^2\mathbb{Z}$. For a closed surface, an $r$-spin structure exists precisely when $n\mid g-1$, and the same description holds with the additional cyclic factor replaced by $\mathbb{Z}/\gcd(n^2,g-1)\mathbb{Z}$. The additional cyclic torsion is determined by the Casson--Morita homomorphism.

papers.title: Relativistic Hydrodynamics as an Intersection Problem
The inverse Erdős--Fuchs problem for $k$-fold sums
papers.abstract: For every fixed integer $k\ge 3$, we construct an infinite set $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ such that $\sum_{h\le n}r_{kA}(h)=\Gamma(1+1/k)^k n+O_k(n^{(1-1/k)^2})$, where $r_{kA}(h)$ counts ordered representations of $h$ as a sum of $k$ elements of $A$, with repetitions allowed. This improves Dai and Pan's bound for a linear main term. In the paired random model used here, fluctuations of the stated order occur infinitely often almost surely.

papers.title: Gravitomagnetic Frame Memory
Differentiability of the solution to an SPDE with respect to the model for the associated regularity structure
papers.abstract: Given a stochastic partial differential equation that falls within the scope of the theory of regularity structures, we show that its solution is, in a suitable sense, a smooth function of the underlying model. This allows one to infer the regularity of the solution with respect to any perturbation of the noise from that of the model. As an application of our results, we provide an elementary proof of the Malliavin differentiability of solutions to a wide class of equations driven by Gaussian noises.

papers.title: Neural-Network Approximators for Low-Thrust Multi-Asteroid Rendezvous Optimization
Coordinate Ordering and Non-collinear Central Configurations
papers.abstract: We establish a mass-independent criterion for N-body central configurations based on a special coordinate ordering of the bodies. Moreover, we identify a region in the plane that contains no non-collinear central configurations. This provides a way to exclude non-collinear central configurations that are nearly collinear.

papers.title: Tannakian Brill-Noether theory of nodal curves
papers.abstract: Using the Tannakian categories arising from convolutions of perverse sheaves on semi-abelian varieties, we can associate to any subvariety of a semi-abelian variety a reductive group together with a representation. We compute these groups and representations for Brill-Noether varieties of all curves whose generalized Jacobian is semi-abelian, in particular for nodal curves. We also obtain new results on the dimension and non-degeneracy of these Brill-Noether varieties.

papers.title: Arithmetic jet stacks
papers.abstract: We construct a stack, which generalizes the notion of the arithmetic jet space functor constructed by Borger using the generalized Witt vector constructions. A priori we con- struct the jet space functor for prestacks, consequently showing that this functor preserves stacks. We then proceed to show the representability of the jet space functor applied to a representable morphism of stacks thereby showing that the jet space functor preserves algebraic and Deligne-Mumford Stacks. We also discuss the properties of morphisms preserved under the jet functor

papers.title: Vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and boundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type
papers.abstract: In present paper, for functional-differential equations of retarded type, the method of vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and the method of higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals are developed. On the basis of this methods, sufficient conditions for various types of uniform boundedness of solutions and sufficient conditions for various types of ultimate-uniform boundedness of solutions are obtained.

papers.title: Anomalous corrections to the inverse participation ratio in the localized phase on the Bethe lattice: insights from a solvable "toy" non-linear $σ$-model
Tuning the false discovery rate in the closed eBH procedure
papers.abstract: The closed eBH procedure controls the false discovery rate under arbitrary dependence between the input e-values. It takes the target false discovery rate $\alpha$ as its input and outputs a rejection set $R$, the usual goal being to maximize its size $\left|R\right|$. This note discusses a modification of the closed eBH procedure that allows choosing the target false discovery rate post hoc: the rejection set and its level $\alpha$ can be chosen after seeing the data, and the expected ratio of the false discovery proportion to $\alpha$ is at most 1. We adapt Vovk and Wang's (2023) algorithm for computing discovery e-matrices to computing, in quadratic time, the frontier of achievable combinations $(\left|R\right|,\alpha)$ of the size of a rejection set $R$ and its level $\alpha$. The frontier allows us to compute an optimal rejection set in view of a given utility function $F$, $F(\left|R\right|,\alpha)\to\max$, striking a balance between the goals of reducing $\alpha$ and increasing $\left|R\right|$.

papers.title: Corrections to the IPR in the localized phase of the Anderson model on the Bethe lattice
On non-canonical maximum cliques in the block graphs of orthogonal arrays
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove an Erdős-Ko-Rado characterisation of maximum intersecting families of columns of certain orthogonal arrays. This solves a problem of Chris Godsil and Karen Meagher and implies that, in all orthogonal arrays OA$(m,(m-1)^2)$, every non-canonical maximum intersecting family of columns necessarily has the structure of an affine plane.

papers.title: Phase-dependent atomicity and PPT edge states for cyclic-sign covariant qutrit maps
papers.abstract: Decomposable positive maps cannot detect entangled states with positive partial transpose (PPT). We obtain a necessary and sufficient criterion for decomposability in the entire seven-real-parameter class of Hermiticity-preserving cyclic-sign covariant maps on $M_3$. The criterion reduces to a one-variable inequality and, for positive maps in this class, characterizes indecomposability exactly. We apply it to a phase-dependent family obtained by adding a completely positive map to the Choi map. Every map in this family is positive, and we find the exact phase-dependent threshold for indecomposability and atomicity. At three phase values, the maps remain indecomposable for every finite deformation strength. Each indecomposable map gives an indecomposable entanglement witness through its Choi matrix. We construct PPT edge states of birank $(5,5)$ detected by these witnesses throughout the indecomposable region.

papers.title: How Brine Pockets Evolve and Release in Ice
papers.abstract: Liquid inclusions migrate through solids by melting at one end and freezing at the other, but how a macroscopic phase boundary regulates their deformation and release remains poorly understood. Here, we track individual brine pockets in saline ice through bulk migration, elongation, and release at the ice-water interface, resolving the motion of both ends. In the bulk, temperature-dependent thermomigration gradually elongates the pockets. Near the ice-water interface, the front slows, whereas liquid connection is followed by accelerated rear freezing and rapid shortening. These opposing responses arise from distinct changes in thermal-solutal transport: proximity to the boundary suppresses the local thermal-gradient enhancement and slows front-end melting, while liquid connection enables salt exchange with the surrounding liquid and accelerates rear-end freezing. A quasi-steady diffusion-resistance model captures the dependence of the half-length release time on the pocket length at connection and identifies an effective external exchange length consistent with a salt-balance estimate. Our results identify thermal proximity and liquid connectivity as distinct controls on inclusion evolution and release, providing a framework for understanding liquid redistribution in multicomponent solids.

papers.title: Weak-type bow shocks
papers.abstract: An existence proof is given for bow shocks ahead of blunt convex wedges that are transonic and of weak type at infinity, including cases for arbitrarily small shock strength. It is also proven that any such flow is necessarily univalent, meaning the position-to-velocity map is injective.

papers.title: Pre-d-algebras, pre-f-algebras and their completions
papers.abstract: We define pre-d- and pre-f-algebras on Archimedean pre-Riesz spaces by conditions on the order and the multiplication only, and show that a pre-Riesz algebra is a pre-f-algebra if and only if its multiplication extends to an f-algebra multiplication on its Riesz completion. On order dense subspaces of C(K), K a compact Hausdorff space, in which disjoint positive elements separate the points of K, a pre-Riesz algebra is a pre-f-algebra if and only if multiplication by every positive element is band preserving

papers.title: Wavelet-CFM for the extragalactic millimeter-wave sky
Numerical Integration of Geodesic Motion in Non-Schwarzschild Spacetimes
An extension of Janowski functions with applications
papers.abstract: Janowski functions are regular functions of the form $p(z)=1+p_1z+\cdots$, which are subordinate to $L_0(a,b:z)=(1+az)/(1+bz)$ for real numbers $a,b$ such that $-1\leq b<a\leq 1$. In this paper, we expand the space of the constants, $a$ and $b$, of the superordinate function, $L_0(a,b:z)$, to a larger set of complex numbers and provide some applications.

papers.title: Study of the $N^*(1535)$ and $N^*(1650)$ resonances from $πN$ $S_{11}$ scattering data and lattice QCD spectra
papers.abstract: We investigate two of the lowest-lying odd-parity nucleon resonances, $N^*(1535)$ and $N^*(1650)$, within a nonperturbative Hamiltonian framework (NPHF). The coupled-channel model contains two three-quark bare states with total quark spins $1/2$ and $3/2$, together with four meson-baryon channels: $\pi N$, $\eta N$, $K\Lambda$, and $K\Sigma$. Constraints from SU(3) flavor symmetry and the bare-state spin wave functions are imposed on the bare-state-channel vertices and the channel-channel Weinberg-Tomozawa interactions. This substantially reduces the number of free parameters. We combine fits to infinite-volume $\pi N$ $S_{11}$ scattering data with finite-volume lattice QCD spectra. We use Hamiltonian eigenvectors to analyze the model-basis compositions. A contamination function then compares the resulting operator-mixing pattern with lattice correlation-matrix eigenvectors. Within the scenarios considered, both bare states and coupled-channel interactions play important roles in describing the two resonances. From our combined infinite and finite volume analysis, in contrast to conventional quark-model expectations, the spin-$1/2$ bare state is heavier than the spin-$3/2$ bare state. The contamination analysis is consistent with the associated operator assignment and with a recent analysis of the relativistic wavefunctions associated with these states. The symmetry-constrained NPHF provides a unified description of the two $S_{11}$ resonances. The combined analysis also constrains their model interpretation.

papers.title: Exact almost sure scale for non-negative stochastic recursions
papers.abstract: We study exact almost sure scale for non-negative stochastic recursions whose conditional mean consists of a linear term and a signed adapted perturbation. The linear term determines a product normalization, but convergence after normalization does not ensure a strictly positive limit. Multiplying the state by the inverse of each deterministic contraction factor gives a contraction-adjusted state. On paths where this state tends to infinity, we prove that the logarithm of the normalized state differs from the cumulative relative perturbation by an almost surely convergent quantity. The assumptions control the effective step sizes, the quadratic positive relative perturbation, and the conditional quadratic variation of the relative martingale noise. If the positive perturbation is summable at the normalized scale, the normalized process converges to a finite non-negative limit; strict positivity is then equivalent to absolute summability of the relative perturbation. We also give criteria for divergence of the contraction-adjusted state, first-order comparisons, and counterexamples illustrating the role of the hypotheses. Harmonic step sizes yield exact power laws with strictly positive random coefficients. Applications include learning automata, urns with signed sampling bias, response-adaptive reinforcement, generalized Simon models with signed updates, branching processes in varying environments, and linear stochastic approximation with multiplicative noise.

papers.title: Spherical HgTe nanocrystal: a multi-band effective mass study
Emerging Topics for Hard Probes
papers.abstract: These proceedings present a personal selection of emerging topics in jet and heavy-flavor physics in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, based on a plenary talk delivered at Hard Probes 2026 in Nashville (USA).

papers.title: Structure-preserving active flux method for the compressible Euler equations with gravity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a structure-preserving active flux method for the compressible Euler equations under gravitational fields, ensuring exactness for the generalized hydrostatic equilibrium state and the preservation of positivity for both density and pressure. This approach entails the update of the cell average and the point values simultaneously. To obtain the equilibrium preservation of the scheme for the cell average, the strategy pursued is to reformulate the gravitational term using the steady state solution, followed by the application of a decomposition algorithm. For the point values, we introduce minor adjustments to the Lax-Friedrichs flux vector splitting, coupled with the same finite difference operator performed on the flux and source term to restore the well-balancedness. Furthermore, a posteriori Multi-dimensional Optimal Order Detection (MOOD) paradigm is adopted for achieving positivity preservation and oscillation control near strong discontinuities. A series of numerical experiments are performed to verify the high-order accuracy of our proposed method, along with its exact equilibrium and positivity preservation, and its ability to capture small perturbations at or close to steady flow without spurious oscillations.

papers.title: Stably irrational algebraically elliptic Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: We establish algebraic ellipticity in the sense of Gromov of a general hypersurface of bidegree $(2,2)$ in $\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$. According to a theorem of Böhning and Graf von Bothmer, a very general such hypersurface is a stably irrational Fano threefold.

papers.title: The Space of $k$-Positive Potentials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study weak geodesics in the space of $k$-positive potentials on a compact Kähler manifold. We prove that any two smooth strictly $k$-positive potentials can be joined by a weak geodesic of class $C^{1,1}$. As an application, we prove that the pair $(\mathcal H_k,d_2)$ is a metric space.

papers.title: Well-balanced nodal finite volume WENO scheme with flux localization for hyperbolic balance laws
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a general framework for constructing arbitrarily high-order well-balanced ``nodal" finite volume weighted essentially non-oscillatory (WENO) schemes, specifically tailored for hyperbolic balance laws. To handle complex systems involving nonconservative products and steady-state solutions with global integral quantities, we introduce a flux localization technique. This technique defines the numerical fluxes, incorporating the entire source term and nonconservative products, locally within each computational cell. By exactly preserving the nodal equilibrium state and conservatively updating the cell averages within a finite volume framework, the method avoids both reference-state reconstruction and the use of ODE solvers. The well-balanced property is achieved by performing high-order WENO reconstruction and employing a linear segment path in terms of equilibrium variables, rather than conservative ones. A rigorous theoretical analysis confirms that the scheme exactly preserves all the targeted stationary solutions. The effectiveness and versatility of the proposed method are demonstrated through a series of numerical experiments on various systems of hyperbolic balance laws.

papers.title: PAC Infinite-Time Safety Guarantees for Stochastic Systems with Unknown Probabilistic Distributions
papers.abstract: This paper studies infinite-time safety certification for discrete-time stochastic systems with continuous dynamics and unknown disturbance distributions that have full support on a known compact disturbance set. We develop a probably approximately correct (PAC) data-driven framework that uses only finitely many i.i.d. disturbance samples: with confidence at least $1-\delta$, if the certification procedure accepts a candidate certificate defining a nonempty subset of a prescribed compact safe set, then the system, starting from any state in this subset, remains within the safe set for all future times with probability at least $1-\epsilon$. Our approach builds on a fundamental characterization of infinite-time safety. We first prove that a robust invariant set exists within a compact safe set if and only if there exists an initial state from which the system remains in the safe set indefinitely with positive probability. This reduces infinite-time safety certification to two tractable subproblems: robust invariant-set computation and finite-horizon reach-avoid certification. We first compute a robust invariant set within the safe set, then use i.i.d. disturbance samples to certify, with PAC guarantees, a subset of initial states for which the probability of reaching this set within a finite horizon while remaining safe is at least a prescribed threshold. To our knowledge, this is the first PAC framework for infinite-time safety under unknown disturbance distributions. Finally, illustrative examples demonstrate the method using semi-definite programming.

papers.title: Quadratic unitary Cayley graphs over finite commutative rings
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring with identity, and let $T_R=Q_R\cup(-Q_R)$, where $Q_R=\{u^2:u\in R^\times\}$. In this paper, we investigate the spectral properties of quadratic unitary Cayley graphs $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$, over finite commutative rings with identity. We determine all the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ when $R$ has odd characteristic. Our results extend the previously known spectral formulas for this family of graphs. We also obtain all the eigenvalues when the characteristic of $R$ is $2$. Furthermore, for rings of odd characteristic, we give a complete characterization of when $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ is a strongly regular Cayley graph.

papers.title: Interface-aware dynamic mode decomposition with control for partitioned multiphysics systems
papers.abstract: We develop an interface-aware dynamic mode decomposition with control (DMDc) formulation for multiphysics systems, within an optimization-based partitioned coupling framework. The finite-element interface-input operator is projected onto the reduced space and kept fixed during identification, while the unknown state-dependent local dynamics are learned from trajectory data. The common interface control is recomputed online by minimizing the mismatch between the reconstructed physical interface quantities. The formulation accommodates local subproblems governed by ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and differential--algebraic equations (DAEs). For a DAE subproblem, tangent projection identifies the state dynamics, whereas a residualized normal regression identifies the pressure balance and provides an algebraic pressure reconstruction. We further propose regularized quadratic correction DMDc to enrich the tangent dynamics and, for DAEs, the normal pressure balance through jointly fitted linear and compact quadratic operators. Feature normalization and block-dependent regularization control the enlarged regression while retaining the prescribed interface operators and identified DAE geometry. The proposed framework is evaluated on problems involving both ODE--ODE and DAE--ODE couplings. The numerical results demonstrate accurate predictions and stable long-time behavior.

papers.title: Note on polychromatic coloring of hereditary hypergraph families III
papers.abstract: For every integer $h\ge4$ we construct a hereditary family of hypergraphs with $m_2=h$ and \[ m_3\ge 2(h-1)+2\left\lfloor\frac{h-1}{3}\right\rfloor+1 \approx \frac{8}{3}m_2. \] This improves the lower bound $m_3\ge 2m_2$ from the preceding notes for every $m_2\ge4$. We also show that the worst-case integrality gap of the weighted transversal problem over hereditary families with $m_2\le h$ is between $h-1$ and $5000h$. As a consequence, every such family admits strong $\varepsilon$-nets of size at most $5000h/\varepsilon$.

papers.title: Quantitative Convergence of the Spherical Brownian Motion collisional particle system for the Maxwellian Landau Equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the quantitative convergence of the spherical Brownian motion (SBM) collisional particle system for the Maxwellian Landau equation via Wasserstein distances. When used as numerical method, it enjoys linear complexity $O(N)$ in particle number $N$, and conserves the momentum and energy almost surely. Moreover, only random grouping and sampling are needed for simulations without further numerical discretization. In the first part, we identify the large particle mean field limit of the system, and the Wasserstein convergence to the limit is justified through a coupling similar to the recent work for the Nanbu type Monte Carlo method \cite{BorghiPareschi2025}. The key difference is that the particles in our coupled shadow system are not i.i.d. due to the perfect matching. In the second part, the convergence of the mean field dynamics to the Landau solution is justified by the relative entropy with a bound $O(\tau^2)$, being $\tau$ the stepsize. This results in an $O(\tau)$ bound for the Wasserstein distance error. A crucial technical tool in the convergence in relative entropy is to provide suitable bounds on the derivatives of the logarithmic density or score function in the mean field dynamics. The combination of these estimates leads to the full convergence of the squared Wasserstein distance with order $O(N^{-1/2}+\tau^2)$ for the numerical scheme in $d=3$.

papers.title: A $C_2$-cofinite non-rational principal $W$-algebra of type $D_4$
papers.abstract: We show that a simple principal $W$-algebra can be $C_2$-cofinite and non-rational. For $\mathcal W=\mathcal W_{-38/7}(D_4,f_{\mathrm{reg}})$ of central charge $-50$, D. Xie predicted seventeen irreducible modules and a logarithmic module of lowest conformal weight $-2$. We determine the Zhu algebra $A(\mathcal W)$ and the Poisson algebra $R_{\mathcal W}=\mathcal W/C_2(\mathcal W)$. Both have dimension $18$, and $A(\mathcal W)\cong\mathbb{C}^{16}\times\mathbb{C}[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$. We construct all seventeen irreducible $\mathcal W$-modules using the realization of $\mathcal W$ as a diagonal coset in $L_{-14/3}(D_4)\otimes L_1(D_4)$ and our previous classification of irreducible $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-modules in the category $\mathcal O$. We also construct an indecomposable $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-module and use the coset realization to obtain an indecomposable logarithmic $\mathcal W$-module. Its lowest generalized $L(0)$-eigenspace is two-dimensional, and $L(0)$ acts on this space by a nontrivial Jordan block with eigenvalue $-2$.

papers.title: Cayley Regression for Finite Groups with a Cyclic Subgroup of Index Two
papers.abstract: A finite group $G$ is a Cayley regression if every generalized Cayley graph of $G$ is isomorphic to a Cayley graph of $G$, and a $k$-Cayley regression if this holds for all such graphs of valency at most $k$. We show that the dihedral group $D_{2n}$, $n\geq2$, is a $2$-Cayley regression if and only if it is a $3$-Cayley regression, which holds exactly when $n$ is a prime power, and that for $k\geq4$ it is a $k$-Cayley regression if and only if $n$ is an odd prime power or $n\in\{2,4\}$. Groups with a cyclic subgroup of index two that are neither cyclic nor dihedral are not even $2$-Cayley regressions; consequently, a group with a cyclic subgroup of index two is a Cayley regression if and only if it is isomorphic to $C_2$, $C_4$, $C_6$, $C_{10}$, or $D_{2n}$ with $n$ as above. Finally, every split metacyclic group $C_m\rtimes C_q$ with $m>2$ and odd $q\geq3$ is not a $2$-Cayley regression.

papers.title: Conceptual Design of a 5 MV High-Voltage System for a Compact Orbitron Fusion Device
papers.abstract: The high-voltage system is a key part of the puzzle toward achieving net-positive fusion power in a compact Orbitron device. This paper presents a conceptual engineering design for a 5 MV, 20 mA, 100 kW HV system for a next-generation Orbitron, serving as an upper-bound design point for the HV system. The MC-TRANS++ 0-D code is used to set the load requirements: a 1 m long, 0.45 m first-wall-radius central cell, 2.5 T on-axis and 10 T mirror-throat fields, and a 5 MV radial potential drop sustaining supersonic rotation ($M = 4.8$). This delivers a triple product of $5.8 \times 10^{21}$ keV s /m3 and $Q_{sci}$ = 8.5. The HV power supply integrates an AC-DC converter, a SiC full-bridge inverter, a CLLC resonant network with an air-core step-up transformer, and feeds a 120-stage parallel-fed series-cascaded rectifier operating at 250 kHz. At full load, this architecture yields an end-to-end efficiency of 85%, much higher than the 60% typical of triode-driven MV-class power supplies. The 5 MV voltage is delivered to a radially nested 50-gap bushing system that interfaces pressurized insulating gas to high vacuum, using brazed alumina spacers with a corrugated profile. The design draws directly on the measured behavior of a previously demonstrated 300 kV prototype, from which six quantitative lessons are extracted and mapped onto the 5 MV design. Electrostatic simulations of the complete assembly at rated voltage show maximum surface fields of 30.3 MV/m on the corona rings, 7.7 MV/m at the cathode triple junction, and average vacuum-gap fields ranging from 5.5 to 40 MV/m. These field strengths remain below breakdown thresholds due to the implementation of triple-junction shielding, insulation corrugation, and axial magnetic insulation at 2.5-10 T. The conceptual system has a form factor of 2.7 meters in diameter and 6.5 meters in length, projected to deliver a net power output of 86-171 kWe.

papers.title: Global existence and decay estimates for classical solutions to 2D compressible micropolar fluid equations with vacuum
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional compressible micropolar fluid equations with far field vacuum. Under the assumption that the initial energy is sufficiently small, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong and classical solutions, allowing for large oscillations in the initial data. The key to the proof is to derive {\it a priori} decay estimates for the pressure, the velocity gradient, and the microrotational velocity, which enable us to close the bootstrap argument. We also handle the difficulties arising from the coupling between the velocity field and the microrotational velocity.

papers.title: Inverse problems for ZS operators and their isomorphisms, II
papers.abstract: We study isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators on the unit interval with generic boundary conditions. A unitary gauge transformation reduces these problems to the corresponding problems with basic boundary conditions, with an explicit shift of the spectral parameter. Using previous results for canonical boundary conditions and four-spectra data mapping we describe isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators. Moreover, study other inverse problems including replacing mappings and canonical relations.

papers.title: LayerCake v1.0: a framework for low- to intermediate-order automated models development
papers.abstract: A new model development framework called LayerCake is presented. It is written in the Python language and relies on the Sympy symbolic computation package to compute the Galerkin projection of two-dimensional spatially extended geophysical models. These projections provide their time evolution operator in the spectral space on a restricted set of modes. The resulting tendencies of the models can be evaluated either numerically (for time integration) or symbolically (for parameters sensitivity analysis and bifurcation analysis). We provide several simple examples of geophysical models to showcase the capabilities of the framework, and we hint at how more complex systems can be designed.

papers.title: Numerical approximation of the Hilfer fractional derivative using orthogonal Quasi-Polynomials
papers.abstract: A numerical approach based on a composite Gaussian quadrature for the Hilfer fractional derivative is presented. This approach employs quasi-polynomials that are orthogonal with respect to the weight function on the interval $(0,1)$. As special cases, the Riemann--Liouville and Caputo fractional derivatives are obtained. Error bounds for the approximation are derived. To confirm the convergence rates as well as the high efficiency of the new approach, numerical examples are provided.

papers.title: Finite-difference neural policy iteration for high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi equations
papers.abstract: We develop a finite-difference neural policy iteration method for high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and Isaacs equations. Artificial viscosity yields a monotone finite-difference operator, and neural networks approximate the linear equations of semi-discrete policy iteration using local stencil values. This avoids global tensor-grid storage. For measurable feedbacks, we bound the propagation of evaluation, terminal, gradient, and control optimization errors by a geometrically weighted sum. Discrete comparison, consistency, and vanishing viscosity relate the approximation to the original degenerate equation. On coupled manufactured problems with rank-deficient diffusion, the method achieves lower mean errors than direct physics-informed neural networks at every tested dimension from five to fifty under equal training time. At fifty dimensions and $900$ seconds, the mean relative $L^2$ error over three paired seeds is about $40\%$ lower. Two-dimensional refinement attains $0.297\%$ error against the original degenerate solution, with independent grid references separating approximation error from viscosity bias. In a twenty-dimensional game with finite control sets, reusing policies reduces the measured time to a relative error of $5\%$ by $24.3\%$ compared with direct minimization of the same discrete residual with fresh samples at every update.

papers.title: A two-sided continued-fraction criterion for the Erdős-Moser equation and Erdős's 1949 problem
papers.abstract: We give a two-sided continued-fraction criterion for the Erdős--Moser equation $1^k+2^k+\dots+(m-1)^k=m^k$. Writing $m=k/\log 2+3/2+\gamma_m/m$, Gallot, Moree and Zudilin showed that a solution yields a convergent of $\log 2/(2N)$, for a known divisor $N$ of $k$, followed by a large partial quotient. We show that an explicit two-sided estimate for $\gamma_m$, from our earlier centre-of-mass work, restricts this partial quotient, for each value of $\gcd(k/N,2m-3)$, to two consecutive values, or to three in the exceptional case that an integer lies in an explicit interval of relative length $O(1/m)$. This excludes the first index left open by their computation and, without extending their continued-fraction computation, raises the lower bound for a nontrivial solution from $m>2.71\cdot 10^{1667658416}$ to $m>6.26\cdot 10^{1667658425}$. The same criterion gives an effective form of the asymptotic results of Best and te Riele on Erdős's 1949 problem on the largest term of $1^n+\dots+(m-1)^n$. We determine all 50 pairs $(m,n)$ with $m<10^{399}$ for which $(m-2)^n<(m-1)^n/2$ and $1^n+\dots+(m-1)^n>m^n$; in particular, the smallest example found by Best and te Riele in 1976 is the smallest such pair, a question they had left open. For $n<0.69\cdot 10^{399}$ we also determine the 51 elements of O'Bryant's exceptional set $A_2$ and all 101 terms of OEIS A129935 below this bound, one of them not previously listed, and settle several conjectures recorded in the OEIS. Finally, using only the upper bound in our estimate for $\gamma_m$ and its positivity, we show that the second part of Erdős's problem, the existence of infinitely many such pairs, is equivalent to the infinitude of $A_2$ and to the existence of infinitely many even-index convergents $p_j/q_j$ of $\log 2$ with $p_j$ even, $q_j$ odd and $q_j(q_j\log 2-p_j)<\Theta(q_j)$, where $\Theta(q)=(\log 2)/3+O(q^{-2})$ is explicit.

papers.title: SemGuard: Semantics-Decoupled Watermarking for Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Gaussian Splatting provides an efficient representation for high-fidelity rendering of static and dynamic 3D scenes, motivating the copyright protection of Gaussian assets. In CLIP-guided Gaussian watermarking, a universal message decoder pretrained on textual watermark representations is subsequently applied to visual features containing both watermark information and scene-dependent semantics. However, text-only pretraining does not explicitly account for the semantic interference encountered during watermark extraction. To address this challenge, we propose SemGuard, a simple yet effective semantics-decoupled watermarking framework that learns to suppress scene-dependent semantic interference during universal message decoder pretraining. Specifically, SemGuard combines message-related CLIP text features with message-independent visual features extracted from unwatermarked scene images, constructing training representations with controllable semantic interference relevant to the target Gaussian assets. A progressive semantic interference curriculum gradually increases the contribution of visual features, allowing the decoder to first learn reliable message representations and then adapt to increasingly strong scene-dependent semantic interference. After pretraining for a given message length and semantic image pool, the decoder is frozen and reused across multiple Gaussian assets whose visual semantics are covered by the pretraining data. Experiments on static and dynamic Gaussian Splatting assets demonstrate improved rendering fidelity alongside reliable watermark extraction, while evaluations on static assets further show enhanced robustness against image-space distortions.

papers.title: The shortest figure-eight geodesics on random hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: We consider primitive unoriented figure-eight geodesics on a closed hyperbolic surface of genus $g$ sampled from Weil--Petersson measure. The shortest of these geodesics realizes the non-simple systole. He, Shen, Wu and Xue proved that its length is tight after centering at $a_g=\log g-\log\log g$. We prove that, as $g\to\infty$, the point process of centered lengths converges to a Poisson process on $\mathbb R$ with intensity $e^s\,ds/(8\pi^2)$. Its first arrival gives a reflected Gumbel limit for the centered systole $M_g$. We also prove convergence of the marked process in which each figure-eight carries the three cuff lengths of its supporting pair of pants, normalized by their sum. In the limiting process, the third cuff accounts for half the perimeter. The two winding cuffs, ordered at random, divide the other half uniformly. These splits are independent across points and independent of the limiting lengths. Uniform exponential bounds on both tails of $M_g$ give convergence of all fixed polynomial moments. At the critical exponent $-1$, we obtain $\mathbb E_g e^{-M_g}\sim(\log g)/(16\pi^2)$.

papers.title: Strictness of the containment of Kirk's asymptotic contractions in a class defined by two quasi-metrics
papers.abstract: Kirk's asymptotic contractions are defined by moduli $\psi_n$ which converge uniformly on $[0,\infty)$ to a Boyd--Wong function and are evaluated at the distance $d(x,y)$ only. A relaxed class, in which the estimate involves a lower and an upper quasi-metric built from the four distances $d(x,y)$, $d(x,Ty)$, $d(Tx,y)$ and $d(Tx,Ty)$, was recently shown to contain Kirk's class and to admit the same fixed point conclusion. It was left open whether the containment is strict. We prove that it is. The separating maps form a family of radial damping maps $T(x)=\lambda(\norm{x})x$ on a normed space, where $\lambda\colon[0,\infty)\to[0,\rho]$ is continuous, $0\le\rho<1$, nonconstant and periodic: every such map is a relaxed asymptotic contraction with explicit linear moduli, whereas its one-step dispersion at a fixed distance is unbounded, so that no finite Kirk modulus exists. A slowly modulated nonperiodic damping law is treated as well. We further show that strictness can occur only when the image $T(X)$ is not relatively compact: in a complete space, if $T(X)$ is relatively compact, the two classes coincide, hence on a compact (in particular finite) space no separating example exists. Applications to semi-active vibration isolation with amplitude-dependent damping and to digital maturity gaps in the digital transformation of small and medium-sized enterprises are discussed, and numerical illustrations are provided.

papers.title: Strong First-Order Phase Transition in a Pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone Boson Model
papers.abstract: We propose a novel, calculable model for realizing strong first-order phase transitions in the early Universe, in which the phase transition occurs along a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson (pNGB) direction. The model involves two scalar fields whose interactions exhibit collective symmetry breaking, protecting the pNGB potential from quadratically divergent radiative corrections induced by these interactions. This structure allows strong first-order phase transitions to be realized without severe parameter tuning while maintaining perturbative control. We investigate the finite-temperature effective potential and bubble nucleation dynamics, identifying parameter regions where strong first-order phase transitions can successfully complete. The strength and characteristic time scale of the transitions are evaluated, and the resulting gravitational-wave (GW) spectra are computed. The predicted GW signals can fall within the sensitivity ranges of planned GW experiments.

papers.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Sample Complexity of Natural Policy Gradient with a Matching Information-Theoretic Lower Bound
papers.abstract: A fundamental question in reinforcement learning is how many sampled transitions are needed to learn a near-optimal policy, and whether direct policy optimization can attain this statistical limit. To answer this question, we consider natural policy gradient (NPG), a widely used policy optimization method. We study tabular finite-horizon Markov decision processes (MDPs) with known rewards and unknown horizon-dependent transition kernels, accessed through a generative model. Our sample-based NPG algorithms update the policy by backward sweeps and do not estimate transition probabilities. Under three different batch-size and step size schedules, we establish last-iterate guarantees with sample complexity $\widetilde O(SAH^4/\varepsilon^2)$, where $S$, $A$, and $H$ denote the number of states, the number of actions, and the horizon length, respectively. In this setting, horizon-dependent transition kernels contribute a factor of $H$ to our transition-query bound. Our information-theoretic lower bound of $\Omega(SAH^4/\varepsilon^2)$ shows that the resulting $H^4$ dependence is unavoidable in the worst case, even for agents that select their queries adaptively. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first last-iterate guarantees for NPG whose sample complexity matches an information-theoretic lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Consequently, our results demonstrate that direct policy-space optimization through NPG can achieve the fundamental statistical limits of reinforcement learning while guaranteeing the performance of the final policy. Furthermore, for known kernels, we prove that exact NPG with a constant step size $\eta=1/H$ requires $\Omega(H^2/\varepsilon)$ iterations in the worst case, matching the known upper bound for that step size.

papers.title: A High-Frequency Flux-Driven DC-SQUID Threshold Detector at the Single-Microwave-Photon Energy Scale: A Numerical Feasibility Study
Probing tensor-polarized gluon TMDs through \texorpdfstring{$J/ψ$}{J/psi} electroproduction off the deuteron
papers.abstract: We investigate tensor-polarized gluon transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (TMDs) in semi-inclusive $J/\psi$ electroproduction off the deuteron. At leading order in the color-octet channels of nonrelativistic QCD, we derive the cross-section contributions associated with longitudinal-longitudinal ($LL$), longitudinal-transverse ($LT$), and transverse-transverse ($TT$) tensor polarization and define ten normalized observables for unpolarized and longitudinally polarized electron beams. Using gluon TMDs obtained in a spin-1 spectator model, we study their $q_T$, $y$, $Q^2$, and collision-energy dependences. The observables involving $f_{1LL}^g$, $f_{1LT}^g+h_{1LT}^g$, and $f_{1TT}^g-h_{1TT}^{\perp g}$ depend directly on ratios of gluon TMDs. The moments involving linearly polarized gluons exhibit a common zero at $Q^2=M_\psi^2$ for the adopted long-distance matrix elements, whereas the beam-helicity-dependent sine moments probe the T-odd distributions $g_{1LT}^g$ and $g_{1TT}^g$. We present fixed-scale model estimates that neglect transverse recoil from soft radiation and quarkonium formation.

papers.title: Finsler--Sobolev inequalities: optimality & rigidity
papers.abstract: We establish optimal Sobolev and logarithmic-Sobolev inequalities on non-compact, possibly non-reversible Finsler manifolds with non-negative weighted Ricci curvature. The optimal constants exhibit no dependence on reversibility -- confirming Ohta's conjectural principle -- being governed solely by the forward and backward asymptotic volume ratios. We then apply the logarithmic-Sobolev inequality to establish the optimal hypercontractivity estimate for the heat flow in the same geometric setting. The equality cases of the above optimal inequalities imply strong rigidity in the underlying manifold, characterized by fine properties of the flag and $S$-curvatures as well as the precise profiles of the corresponding extremizers. We illustrate our results by examples including Randers metrics obtained by Zermelo navigation with Killing vector fields, and weighted convex cones in $\mathbb{R}^n$ endowed with arbitrary Minkowski norms, the latter showing that the forward and backward asymptotic volume ratios may differ.

papers.title: Neural Schrödinger Bridge via Yasue Action with Applications to Generative Modeling
papers.abstract: We propose a novel neural solver for inferring the continuous state evolution of the Schrödinger bridge problem. The proposed solver builds on a saddle point formulation involving the Yasue action functional. This allows us to realize the continuous state evolution by learning the optimal velocity for an ordinary differential equation, as opposed to learning the optimal drift for a stochastic differential equation. The proposed solver only uses the source and the target samples, and not the source and target distributions per se, which makes it particularly suitable for high dimensional applications arising in generative modeling. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solver using several numerical experiments in low and high dimensions, using both real and synthetic datasets.

papers.title: Control of Underactuated Surface Vessels---Part II: Underway Docking
papers.abstract: In underway directional docking, a second-order nonholonomic problem, six pairs of states of two vehicles have to be made to match by two inputs. The key challenge is to design time-invariant feedback of the relative states and the leader's measured motion only, which makes the follower's convergence in range outpaced, with no sway actuation whatsoever, by the bearing and heading convergence of the follower relative to the leader's path. We begin with nonmodular backstepping, choosing speed and commanded heading jointly to control range and bearing. Curvature compensation and normalization of angular errors by different powers of range remove the range singularity from the model. Our construction passes from unicycle kinematics to the ships' zero-sideslip points and through the sway dynamics to the physical hulls. The design extends to a leader with a different hull and to a docking point astern or abeam of the leader, where we show that, while the leader turns, a follower without sway actuation holds the point only with a heading that differs from the leader's. With strict control Lyapunov construction, we achieve global $\kappa$-exponential convergence, with a rate independent of the initial error.

papers.title: Control of Underactuated Surface Vessels---Part I: Stabilization in Polar Coordinates
papers.abstract: A surface vessel with surge force and yaw moment as inputs and no sway actuation cannot be stabilized at a fixed pose by continuous time-invariant feedback. We introduce a zero-sideslip point, a point whose position relative to the hull depends on the surge and sway speeds and whose velocity points along the vessel's heading at every instant, and show that it moves as a unicycle. This reduction allows the time-invariant, polar-coordinate steering laws of Todorovski et al. (2025) to be applied to the underactuated vessel without modification. With two steering laws, GloBa and BoLSA, we construct strict control Lyapunov functions and prove global asymptotic stability, first for a four-state model with surge speed and yaw rate as virtual inputs, and then, by one step of backstepping, for the full six-state model with surge force and yaw moment. The analysis extends to hulls with fore-aft asymmetric sway-yaw damping, excluded in prior work by the assumption of diagonal damping. Unlike prior time-varying designs, the time-invariant controller yields smooth, non-oscillatory trajectories, an important practical advantage for docking. The designs are validated in simulation on the Cybership I hull model.

papers.title: Rank-unimodality of one-descent composition ideals
papers.abstract: The principal ideal of a composition consists of its distinct generalized subwords, ranked by the sum of their parts. We prove rank-unimodality for every composition with at most one descent and for every bitonic composition. Both the part sizes and the number of parts are unrestricted. The main ingredient is a coupling for a monotone host. If a subword is chosen uniformly among those of weight at most n, its length and its unused weight can be made to increase weakly when n increases by one. A decreasing threshold on the next available part then compares the positive difference of two ordinary rank coefficients with an earlier cumulative ratio. This supplies the coefficient inequality in the hereditary reduction at a strict peak.

papers.title: Deterministic regularisation of the nonsymmetric eigenproblem
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for pseudospectral shattering in exact arithmetic. This resolves an important open problem in the complexity of the nonsymmetric eigenproblem. Given a complex contraction $A$ of order $n\ge2$ and $0<\delta<1/2$, we compute a perturbation $E$ with $\|E\|<\delta$ such that $A+E$ has simple spectrum. The ratio of its eigenbasis condition number to its minimum eigenvalue gap is at most $C(n/\delta)^{20/3}$. The algorithm also computes an exact eigensystem of $A+E$. It uses $O(n^3\log^d(n/\delta))$ real-field operations and comparisons, where $C$ and $d$ are absolute constants. We choose the rank-one perturbations using a lower bound on the circle mean of the logarithm of the discriminant modulus. A quadratic penalty controls how far the accumulated updates move the matrix. By using the same reference eigenbasis for several updates, we can estimate all the current projector norms while recovering only the directions needed for the next perturbation.

papers.title: A Viscosity-Decoupled Uzawa Lattice Boltzmann Method for Incompressible Flows Across Reynolds Numbers
papers.abstract: Conventional lattice Boltzmann methods (LBMs) tie viscosity to collision relaxation, which induces diffusive stiffness at low Reynolds numbers, non-hydrodynamic instabilities at high Reynolds numbers, and passband breakdown in variable-relaxation dual-time schemes, whereas continuum incompressible solvers require global pressure-Poisson solves every step. We propose a Viscosity-Decoupled Uzawa Lattice Boltzmann Method (VDU-LBM) in D2Q9 and D3Q19 that permanently fixes collision at unit relaxation under smooth harmonic scaling and clears pre-collision non-conserved kinetic memory in one sweep. Constant, heterogeneous, and Smagorinsky eddy viscosities enter through a parameter-free post-streaming bond-symmetric momentum-flux lift that conserves discrete momentum pairwise without perturbing continuity. Variable-step BDF1/BDF2 marching is accelerated by a matrix-free local polynomial Uzawa smoother on the $(d+1)$ conserved moments, paired with link-wise Bouzidi curved walls and shifted ghost open boundaries. Across $\mathrm{Re}\in[10^{-4},10^6]$, VDU-LBM achieves smooth low-Mach second-order space--time accuracy, accelerates unsteady DFG 2D-2 shedding per cycle by $14.27\times\text{--}15.85\times$ over matched 20-core OpenFOAM-v2412, and lowers $256^3$ $\mathrm{Re}=1600$ resolved enstrophy error by $2.25\times$ versus hybrid recursive regularized LBM. On an NVIDIA A100 GPU, the fused D3Q19 solver attains $80.9\%\text{--}85.5\%$ of measured copy bandwidth in multi-pass port traffic and cuts bounded-relaxation diffusive step cost at high viscosity contrasts.

papers.title: From local competition to bump attractors:how excitation width sets capacity, interference and updating in recurrent models of visual working memory
papers.abstract: On-centre off-surround (OCOS) networks and bump attractors, the two main recurrent models of visual working memory, differ chiefly in how far recurrent excitation spreads. We place them in one family parameterised by excitation width at fixed total excitation, and ask how stable each stored item is and what it costs the circuit to hold and change it. The answer is that excitation width sets the price of continuity. In the OCOS limit, which we solve exactly by completing the energy-function formalism of \citet{Sengupta2024}, an item occupies a single unit, relaxes quickly and never drifts, and capacity follows in closed form, exact over all stable states. As excitation widens towards a bump-like regime, items become continuous but costly: per item, the circuit uses 15--29 units instead of one and 6.5--11 times the activity, relaxes 35--60 times more slowly after a perturbation, needs a 35--230 times stronger cue to accept a second item, and holds 7--10 items instead of at least 40. Under noise, with background false alarms approximately matched, about a third of wide items drift, whereas narrow items never move. Yet even as an item's translation mode softens towards zero, items remain locked to the lattice. Locking is poorly predicted by energy differences between item positions, but strongly predicted by how far the unit just beyond an item's edge sits below threshold (rank correlation 0.91 across 40 parameter settings). Where that margin vanishes, a new input captures the stored item instead of being added to memory.

papers.title: FastCREST: GPU-Accelerated CREST Conformer Searches with Consistent Energies and Gradients
papers.abstract: CREST conformer searches with GFN2-xTB take days for large, flexible molecules: one search of a 274-atom gallium(III)--peptide complex with CREST 3.0.2 took 321.5~h on 32 CPU threads. FastCREST keeps CREST's algorithm and changes how a search uses the hardware. Its metadynamics (MTD) and molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories run with tuned OpenMP settings and one GPU, which solves the self-consistent-charge (SCC) eigenproblem and evaluates the three-body dispersion term. About 15,000 geometry optimizations per iteration run as Slurm array jobs on other CPU nodes, and checkpoints let a search continue on preemptible GPUs. On A100 nodes, the OpenMP settings and loop changes made an MTD step 2.4 times faster and the GPU another 2.3 times; array jobs made a batch of optimizations 39 times faster. For six more molecules of 24 to 339 atoms, a FastCREST step was 2.2 to 7.1 times faster than a conventional CREST step. A complete FastCREST search, which also lifts CREST~3's cap of 200 optimization cycles, took 54.3~h, evaluating energies and gradients 8.1 times as fast as the CREST 3.0.2 search (on different hardware) with fewer CPU-hours per evaluation. Two opt-in settings (a warm-started Jacobi eigensolver and GPU-resident SCC iterations), LLVM's OpenMP library and one CPU socket per trajectory made an MTD step 8.3 times faster than conventional CREST. Energies agree with CREST 3.0.2 within $1.01\times10^{-10}$ Eh and gradients within $8.2\times10^{-11}$Eh bohr$^{-1}$, and controlled MD runs passed a prespecified equivalence test. Most replicate FastCREST and conventional CREST searches ended in similar compact conformers, with no detectable difference in energy.

papers.title: The Curved Exponential Family of Cylindrical Distributions: m-Projection, Curvature and a Test of the von Mises-Fisher Component
papers.abstract: Cylindrical data pair a vector in R^d with a direction in S^(m-1). We study a family in which the direction is von Mises-Fisher and, given the direction, the vector is Gaussian with mean affine in it; this generalizes the Mardia-Sutton model. The family is a curved exponential family inside a regular family with Fisher-Bingham directions. We state necessary and sufficient conditions for the maximum-likelihood estimator to exist and be unique. The estimator is explicit except for one scalar root and is the m-projection (Kullback-Leibler projection) of the moment-matching member. Every moment it does not match is a function of one residual, the gap between the sample and fitted second moments of the direction. The squared length of this gap in the Fisher metric is the classical score test of von Mises-Fisher against Fisher-Bingham directions, due to Cox on the circle and extended by Mardia, Holmes and Kent. Specific here are this reading and the exact invariance of its law to the regression part. The exponential curvature lies only in the directions of the regression matrix. In closed form, the information lost on this matrix against the expected information is m-1 observations for uniform directions and (m+1)^2/(m-1) in the limit of high concentration; conditioning on the directions recovers it. Finite mixtures are identifiable. On buoy records the test rejects von Mises-Fisher directions, and generalized von Mises directions raise the held-out log-density by 0.45 nats per observation with one component.

papers.title: Hartree--Fock analysis of the bilayer Hubbard model
Multi-location Newsvendor: An Interpretable Inventory Policy
papers.abstract: We study a multilocation newsvendor problem in which inventory is chosen before demand is observed and surplus stock can subsequently be transshipped to locations with shortages. The objective is to minimize expected holding, backlog, and transportation costs over a metric network. Under uniform transportation costs, the optimality conditions balance local and aggregate demand coverage and reduce to a scalar search under mild regularity conditions. We use this structure to develop an interpretable iterative heuristic for general metrics. The heuristic calibrates effective transportation costs from lateral shipments under independent stocking and uses them to construct location-dependent pooling weights. These weights have a direct operational interpretation through the cost of serving demand at other locations. Under the stated assumptions, the heuristic recovers the exact uniform-metric solution. Numerical experiments on structured and random networks show costs close to the sampled optimum on average and substantial savings relative to independent stocking.

papers.title: The chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory: partition functions beyond large-$N$ and quantum holography
papers.abstract: We identify families of Bethe vacua in the chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory whose individual free energies grow as $N^{3/2}$. High-precision data support closed forms for their all-order perturbative $1/N$ expansions. At a distinguished mixed Chern--Simons coupling, the baryonic magnetic flux distinguishes members of this family of vacua. We also study the three-sphere partition function numerically in the 't Hooft limit and Cardy limit, and propose an all-order Airy formula. The four-derivative and one-loop corrections are precision tests of holography.

papers.title: Competing magnetic correlations in the square-lattice Hubbard model with spin-dependent nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor hopping
Fermionic 2+1D SU(2) quantum link models: an ED/DMRG reliability study
papers.abstract: Non-Abelian lattice gauge theory with dynamical fermions is a central target for tensor-network and quantum-simulation methods, but controlled reliability studies on small systems are scarce. We benchmark two complementary Hilbert-space approaches for a 2+1D SU(2) quantum link model with one staggered fermion flavour on small two-dimensional lattices: sparse exact diagonalization (ED) and matrix-product-state density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG). The link variables use the five-state $\{5\}$ truncation, and fermions are represented by two-colour four-state sites. We implement ED with explicit cross-site Jordan--Wigner strings and DMRG with total-fermion-number conservation and a matrix product operator (MPO) built from local terms. We validate the link algebra, Gauss-law commutation, Hermiticity, the pure-gauge limit, and the MPO against ED component by component. The $2\times2$ methods agree to $10^{-13}$ and the $2\times3$--$2\times5$ ladders are controlled at or below the $10^{-5}$ level. The $3\times3$ geometry illustrates the role of colour neutrality: at half filling the odd fermion number makes $G^2=3/4$ the exact lower bound, while one hole or one doublon restores neutrality and lowers the residual to $\sim2\times10^{-5}$ at $\chi=2048$. An independent exact-Gauss fPEPS provides a reference for the even-filling $3\times2$ sector. The results define a reproducible reliability envelope for non-Abelian gauge-fermion benchmarks and show where larger-scale simulations require larger bond dimensions or different tensor-network geometries.

papers.title: Spectral radii of connected graphs with prescribed maximum degree
papers.abstract: For a real number $\alpha>0$ and a positive integer $r$, we give recursive characterizations of the existence of finite simple connected graphs $G$ with adjacency spectral radius $\rho(G)=\alpha$ and maximum degree $\Delta(G)\le r$ (or $=r$). Adding one vertex to a graph $F$ at a time to update the Schur-complement $q=\alpha-{\mathbf b}^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}{\mathbf b}$, where $B=\alpha I-A(F)$ is positive definite and ${\mathbf b}$ is a nonzero $0$--$1$ that specifies the neighbours of $z$ in $F$. Realizability is characterized by admissible constructions with positive intermediate outputs $q$ and a final zero output. We also establish a reduction for a graph $G$ obtained by attaching pairwise disjoint rooted trees, each by a single edge, to a nonempty connected graph $H$. Assume that $\alpha I-A(T)\succ0$ for every attached tree $T$. For each $z\in V(H)$, let $q_{z,1},\ldots,q_{z,s_z}$ be the positive root pivots obtained by the scalar tree recursion for the trees attached to $z$, and set \[ a_z=\alpha-\sum_{j=1}^{s_z}q_{z,j}^{-1}, \qquad M_H(\mathbf a)=\operatorname{diag}(a_z:z\in V(H))-A(H), \] where an empty sum is zero. Then $\rho(G)=\alpha$ if and only if $M_H(\mathbf a)\succeq0$ and $\det M_H(\mathbf a)=0$. Taking $H=K_1$ recovers the tree criteria, while $\delta(H)\geq2$ gives criteria for graphs with prescribed 2-core $H$. In particular, for unicyclic graphs of prescribed cycle length, path continuants reduce the spectral condition to positivity inequalities and one scalar equation.

papers.title: KAM theory for contact Hamiltonian systems
papers.abstract: In both finite and infinite dimensions, we establish the first frequency-preserving KAM theorems for full-dimensional Legendrian tori in contact Hamiltonian families with general analytic coupling between the momenta and the contact variable. After adjustment of external parameters, the flow on each torus is analytically conjugate in the original time to the prescribed translation, with estimates uniform as the damping parameter crosses zero. This coupling can generate nonzero mean damping at first order even when the damping parameter vanishes. In finite dimensions, nonzero mean damping yields a time-preserving analytic contact linearization near the torus. In both settings the invariant graphs give global analytic solutions of stationary Hamilton--Jacobi equations whose characteristic flows are conjugate to the prescribed translation. A novel consequence in finite dimensions is that, under global Tonelli assumptions and strict increase in the contact variable, this analytic solution is both the unique forward and the unique backward weak KAM solution, and its associated Legendrian graph is an invariant torus carrying quasi-periodic dynamics.

papers.title: AsyncMixVLA: Runtime Asynchronous Robot Policy Switching for Adaptation to Dynamic Environments
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models translate visual observations and language instructions into robot actions, enabling general-purpose robotic control. However, environmental perturbations, such as objects moving during execution, can undermine their reliability. Different policies exhibit complementary failures under mid-rollout perturbations, motivating selective switching between policies for recovery. Such switching can stall the robot during inference of the newly invoked policy or, if performed asynchronously, act on stale observations. We present AsyncMixVLA, an adaptive inference framework for proactive, asynchronous switching across heterogeneous VLA policies. A learned trigger balances recovery potential against intervention harm to selectively escalate to a higher-compute policy. AsyncMixVLA overlaps its inference with committed outgoing actions and aligns its context to the anticipated takeover state. On LIBERO-Long with mid-rollout perturbations, AsyncMixVLA improves perturbed task success from 69.5% to 77.1% over the lightweight policy. It achieves 84.9% overall success, comparable to 84.5% for synchronous switching, while reducing median exposed handoff latency from 226.5 ms to 0.1 ms. Without retraining or recalibration, it achieves 75.1% success across three unseen perturbation families, compared with 71.3% for the stronger constituent policy in aggregate.

papers.title: Some attractive bases for the Onsager Lie algebra
papers.abstract: The Onsager Lie algebra $\mathcal{O}$ is defined by generators $A$, $B$ subject to the Dolan-Grady relations $[A,[A,[A,B]]] = 4[A,B]$ and $[B,[B,[B,A]]] = 4[B,A]$. It is known that $\mathcal{O}$ is infinite-dimensional. In this paper, we consider three bases for $\mathcal{O}$. The first basis was recently introduced by the author, and the second basis is a variation of the first. The third basis was introduced by Baseilhac and Crampé in 2019. By construction, the elements in each basis are recursively obtained from $A$, $B$. Using the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ loop algebra, we express every basis element in closed form. We then describe how these three bases are related to each other. Next, we consider a finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathcal{O}$-module $V$. Associated with $V$ are six well-known decompositions: the eigenspace decomposition of $A$ and the eigenspace decomposition of $B$, together with four other decompositions of $V$ said to be split. We show that on each decomposition, every element of the first two bases acts in a block diagonal, block upper bidiagonal, block lower bidiagonal, or block tridiagonal fashion. We illustrate these actions using a tetrahedron diagram. We also determine how the elements of the third basis act on the six decompositions. To obtain our results about finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathcal{O}$-modules, we use the theory of tridiagonal pairs.

papers.title: The Gerards-Schrijver conjecture on the Edmonds-Johnson property is false
papers.abstract: An integral matrix $A$ has the Edmonds-Johnson property if, for all integral vectors $b,c,l,u$, the first Chvátal closure of $\{x: b\le Ax\le c,\ l\le x\le u\}$ equals its integer hull. Gerards and Schrijver conjectured that a totally half-modular matrix has the Edmonds-Johnson property if and only if it has no minor equal to one of two specific matrices, of size $3\times3$ and $3\times4$. We disprove this conjecture. We give a totally half-modular $5\times6$ matrix that does not have the Edmonds-Johnson property and has no minor equal to either matrix. It is a minimal obstruction: every proper minor has the Edmonds-Johnson property. The proofs work on a graph whose edges are the rows and bounds of the matrix, and on which the minor operations act by deleting, contracting and halving edges. For minimality, we reduce every proper minor to two classes of matrices known to have the Edmonds-Johnson property.

papers.title: An ADMM-Based Approach to the Large-Scale Geomagnetically Induced Current Blocker Placement Problem
papers.abstract: We propose an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)-based approach for addressing the challenge of determining placements for geomagnetically induced current (GIC) blocking devices on large-scale transmission networks. Traditional formulations of this placement problem lead to mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) that are difficult for state-of-the-art MINLP solvers, which often struggle to exploit problem structure and fail to produce high-quality solutions on large systems. To overcome these challenges, the proposed method employs a three-block ADMM decomposition enhanced with (i) partial linearization of the GIC-related nonlinearities, supported by conditions guaranteeing exactness, and (ii) heterogeneous penalty parameters that significantly accelerate convergence to high-quality local solutions. Numerical experiments on newly constructed large-scale benchmark systems (up to 10,000 buses) demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods by several orders of magnitude in runtime while producing solutions whose objective values closely approach the ideal all-blocker lower bound. These results highlight the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed approach for mitigation planning efforts in large transmission networks.

papers.title: Tritium speciation and transport in molten FLiBe: parameters, uncertainties and validation priorities
Geometrising discrete representations in \(\textnormal{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})\)
papers.abstract: We prove the Deroin--Tholozan conjecture for discrete representations into \(\textnormal{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})\). More precisely, we give a complete characterisation of those representations of a closed surface group with discrete image that arise as holonomies of branched hyperbolic structures. The proof combines a factorisation theorem of Rong for maps between Seifert fibred spaces with a local surgery that allows one to reinsert pinched handles while preserving the prescribed holonomy. As a consequence, we also obtain symmetric realisations on finite covers associated with normal torsion-free subgroups of the image.

papers.title: Jointly Recovering Destination Attractiveness and Spatial Preference Segments from Observed Tours via Inverse Optimization
papers.abstract: Quantifying destination attractiveness by counting visitors, the most direct approach, can favor accessible sites and understate destinations that travelers reach at considerable cost. Preferences may also cut across a priori socio-demographic groupings. This study develops an inverse optimization framework that recovers destination attractiveness and preference segments jointly from observed multi-stop trip tours and generalized travel costs, without prespecifying tour-level segment assignments or imposing a parametric distribution on the unexplained part of utility. Representing each destination visit as a link in an extended network turns utility-maximizing tour choice into an inverse shortest paths problem. We apply the framework to 2,931 holiday vehicle trip tours over 51 target municipalities in Hokkaido, Japan. Constraint generation and alternating optimization make estimation tractable in this multi-destination setting, and the segments recovered under a three-segment specification show contrasting spatial preferences across the established coastal centers, the corridor around Sapporo, and the inland lake districts. The recovered values are expressed on a common monetary scale across destinations and segments without segment-specific scale normalization. They are uncorrelated with visit counts in the input data (r = -0.01) yet moderately correlated with tourist arrivals from an independent prefectural survey (r = 0.40), and are positively associated with the cost of reaching a destination (r = 0.60); destinations above this cost-value relationship include niche places that visit counts alone do not distinguish. The results provide a spatially explicit account of destination value and preference heterogeneity that can inform urban and regional planning and segment-targeted marketing.

papers.title: Superintegrable Systems and the Tractor Connection
papers.abstract: Quadratic constants of motion for natural pseudo-Riemannian Hamiltonians with potential correspond to conformal Killing tensors admitting multiple Killing scales. Taking this correspondence further, we develop a dimension-independent ($n\ge 3$) framework for studying second-order superintegrable systems using conformal tractor calculus, and invariant BGG prolongation of the rank two conformal Killing equation. We apply this framework to classify second-order maximally superintegrable systems within certain natural families of Hamiltonians generated by pairs of conformally related Einstein metrics in arbitrary dimensions. We recover the second-order analogue of Bertrand's theorem as a special case.

papers.title: The Schürmann-Vallentin lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering in dimension six
papers.abstract: We prove that the lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ discovered by Schürmann and Vallentin in 2006 is the unique (up to similarity) six-dimensional lattice that gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering.

papers.title: Regularization for the inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger equation in one dimension
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the initial data problem for the following inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger (INLS) equation $$ i \partial_t u + \partial_x^2 u = \pm |x|^{-b} |u|^{2k} u, \quad u(0, x)= u_0(x),$$ where $b>0$ and $k\in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$. The singular potential $|x|^{-b}$ impairs the Sobolev regularity that can be propagated by the flow. We establish the regularization mechanism of this model and prove local well-posedness in $H_x^{\alpha}$ for $\alpha=5/2-b-$. Moreover, at the endpoint space $H_x^{5/2-b}$, we show that there is no $C^{2k+1}$ flow map at the origin. The proof combines the one-dimensional local smoothing effect with a normal-form reduction for the high-low interaction generated by the singular part of the coefficient. The argument applies to both the focusing and defocusing cases.

papers.title: From atomic events to material degradation across metre and year scales
A hybrid high-order discretization of a volume integral formulation for eddy currents on unstructured polyhedral meshes
papers.abstract: Volume integral formulations are attractive for eddy-current simulation because they require a mesh only of the conducting region. However, their dense interaction matrices make it important to control the number of unknowns needed for a prescribed accuracy. We propose an arbitrary-order Hybrid High-Order discretization of a current-based volume integral formulation on general unstructured polyhedral meshes.
