papers.title: Revisiting Index Performance under High Cache-Miss Penalties
papers.abstract: Modern data-intensive applications often query very large datasets, making index performance critical. Recent index structures exploit the fine-grained access capabilities of emerging storage devices such as DCPMM and CXL. However, existing benchmarks typically evaluate indexes in isolation using saturated, closed-loop workloads that emphasize maximum throughput. Such workloads favor highly concurrent designs while overlooking the application work that follows an index lookup and competes for cache, memory bandwidth, and CPU resources. We present AuxBench - a microbenchmark that evaluates indexes as auxiliary access paths within larger application workloads. Using AuxBench, we evaluate four byte-addressable indexes under controlled post-lookup memory activity, concurrency, and request arrival patterns. Our experiments show that post-lookup memory activity can change the relative performance of competing indexes, that concurrency-oriented designs may lose their advantages when substantial application work is introduced, and that time-varying request arrivals can produce severe tail latency near saturation. These findings demonstrate why index-only benchmarks may not adequately predict performance in larger application workloads

papers.title: Different Stories: European Astronomy as a Tool of Colonization in the Americas and Hawai'i
Mass-conservative voxelisation of smoothed particles using cumulative kernels
Jordan-Frame Dynamics of Curvature Inflation: A Derivative Expansion of the Friedmann Constraint
papers.abstract: We derive a slow-roll approximation for the Jordan-frame Hubble rate $H_J$ in metric $f(R)$ gravity. A derivative expansion of the vacuum Friedmann constraint to third order gives $\dot H_J$ as a function of $H_J$. In the Starobinsky model we also show that the difference in $\dot H_J$ between two expanding solutions decreases as they pass through successively lower values of $H_J$, and that a signed square root of $H_J$ evolves smoothly through the zeros that follow inflation. We test the approximation in a regularized inverse-logarithmic $R^2$ model and in $R+\alpha^{p-1}R^p$, taking the pivot from the exact background 60 Einstein-frame e-folds before the end of inflation. For the inverse-logarithmic coupling $\delta=3$, the third-order approximation reproduces $\dot H_J$ at the pivot with a relative error of $3\times10^{-8}$. Integrating the approximate branch between the pivot and exit values of $H_J$ taken from the exact background gives 59.98 e-folds, compared with 60 on the exact trajectory. At the six couplings $\delta=0,1,\ldots,5$, the absolute difference from the numerical mode result is below $1.1\times10^{-5}$ in the scalar tilt $n_s$, and the relative difference is below $0.0052\%$ in the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. Here the second-order spectral formulas account for nearly all of this difference. For $p=1.8$ the approximation itself adds to the error, which becomes $3.9\times10^{-5}$ in $n_s$ and $0.047\%$ in $r$. For $\delta=3$, perturbative scalaron decay into a minimally coupled Higgs doublet places the pivot 51.59 e-folds before the end of inflation and gives $n_s=0.9690$ and $r=0.0067$. At fixed $\alpha\mu_0^2=0.006065$ and with the same decay rate prescription, $\delta\simeq8.7$ gives the central $n_s$ value inferred from ACT DR6, Planck, CMB lensing and DESI baryon acoustic oscillations. This comparison uses the published one-dimensional constraint.

papers.title: A proof of the Reinhardt conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Reinhardt conjecture: among centrally symmetric convex disks in the plane, the smoothed regular octagon has the least optimal lattice packing density, and equality holds precisely for its nonsingular affine images. Local cost inequalities reduce arbitrarily long switching cycles of a minimizer to six types. We exclude those types by geometric comparisons and rigorous finite verification, and identify the remaining short minimizer.

papers.title: Sharp $L_p$-Regularity for Quantum Markov Semigroups
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp universal constants in positive-input $L_p$-regularity for finite-dimensional quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful invariant state. For $1<p<\infty$, they are $p\sin(\pi/p)/(2(p-1))$ under KMS symmetry and $\frac{p}{2(p-1)}\tan(\frac{\pi}{2}\min\{1/p,1-1/p\})$ without a symmetry assumption, with the endpoint values at $p=1$ given by $\pi/2$ and $\pi/4$, respectively.

papers.title: Exactly Proper Forcing
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of exact properness, a strong form of properness for uncountable models, and prove iteration theorems and the consistency of forcing axioms for this class. We discuss examples of posets in the class and give some applications of the forcing axioms.

papers.title: Neural Marked Point Processes for Health Insurance Claims
papers.abstract: Health insurance claims exhibit temporal dependence, as previous claims may provide information about the timing, type and amount of subsequent claims. Such dependencies are difficult to capture with traditional actuarial models based on aggregated claim counts. We investigate a neural marked point process in which a causal Transformer represents individual claim histories and determines type-specific conditional intensities, allowing for self-excitation and interactions between claim types. The framework also incorporates conditional severity distributions, reporting delays and stochastic medical-cost inflation. We develop a likelihood-based calibration procedure that accounts for incomplete claim reporting and evaluate the model using both simulated and empirical data. A simulation study with 10,000 insurance contracts examines the recovery of known claim dynamics, while an application to MEPS-derived medical-event data assesses predictive performance. The fitted model reproduces the main patterns in claim frequencies and severities, although some discrepancies remain in the tails of the distributions. On the MEPS data, the neural model achieves better predictive performance than two generalized linear model benchmarks in terms of claim-count deviance and expenditure discrimination.

papers.title: Liquidity Commitments and Strategic Settlement in Financial Networks
papers.abstract: Credible liquidity commitments can prevent self-fulfilling settlement freezes without being drawn. But how should they be designed to minimise reserved capacity while preserving banks' ordinary self-insurance? Missing incoming payments increase precautionary retention, allowing a freeze to coexist with feasible full repayment. We characterise a canonical contingent entitlement that uniquely implements full payment whenever any admissible continuous schedule can, even when alternatives induce nonmonotone repayment responses. Functional contract design therefore reduces exactly to capacity allocation. Contract shape matters even after commitments are optimally allocated within the affine benchmark. At zero usage prices, flexible commitments can require strictly less capacity than globally optimised affine reserve attenuation. An exact critical-mode criterion provides a sufficient condition for these global savings. For fixed positive reservation weights, strict savings are generic in a specified dense-network regime and arise in open families of sparse directed cycles. For heterogeneous directed cycles with one potentially amplifying bank, a compact linear programme characterises the reserve-preserving capacity infimum. Under stated reserve conditions, a sharp comparison identifies when eligibility restrictions increase costs and change the allocation of support. Verifiable incremental-risk eligibility provides a foundation for preserving ordinary reserves at zero usage prices. General-network bounds and exact exponential two-bank results establish that contractual flexibility retains value at positive usage prices.

papers.title: Condensation-related expansion work of water vapor as a major pathway for kinetic energy generation in the lower atmosphere
papers.abstract: Earth's atmosphere operates a steam cycle: water evaporates from the surface, expands as vapor, condenses in colder air, and returns as precipitation. Yet its power and relationship to atmospheric mechanical power remain poorly quantified. Applying the Clausius--Clapeyron relation between saturated vapor expansion work and latent heat converted at Carnot efficiency to vertically distributed condensation, we derive the steam-engine power as a sum of the gravitational and condensation-related contributions, $W_v=W_g+W_c$; it is not the net power of a complete moist-air cycle. Using twelve years of GPM/DPR spectral latent-heating profiles and MERRA-2 fields, we estimate $W_v\simeq4.1$ W m$^{-2}$, with $W_c\simeq2.8$ W m$^{-2}$. Separately, we diagnose total atmospheric mechanical power $W=W_P+W_K\simeq4.3$ W m$^{-2}$, comprising gravitational power of precipitation $W_P\simeq1.1$ W m$^{-2}$ and kinetic energy generation $W_K\simeq3.2$ W m$^{-2}$, including $2.4$ W m$^{-2}$ below 500 hPa. Both correspondences $W_v\simeq W$ and $W_c\simeq W_K$ lie within 20--30% uncertainty estimates. To explain these correspondences, we propose that $W_c$ generates the potential energy associated with surface pressure gradients. Cross-isobaric flow in the frictional lower atmosphere converts this energy into kinetic energy. In a horizontally isothermal atmosphere, this positive pressure work would be nearly cancelled by compression aloft. An idealized circulation illustrates how differential heating can offset compression, allowing nearly isobaric upper return flow. In the proposed mechanism, condensation-driven circulation unlocks this thermal compensation thus providing a major pathway for lower-atmospheric kinetic energy generation. We discuss how changes in the coupling between condensation and differential heating could test this proposed causal relationship.

papers.title: Adsorbate-Free Screening of Dissociative Water Adsorption on Nickel Nanoparticles via Graph Neural Networks
Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation with boundary in higher dimensions I
papers.abstract: We study isolated boundary singularities of positive solutions of the scalar-flat boundary Yamabe equation. We prove the critical upper bound for general smooth metrics in dimensions $3\le n\le17$ and for Euclidean domains with smooth boundary in dimensions $3\le n\le22$. For general metrics, this range extends to $n=18$ when the conformal metric is complete near the singularity. In every dimension, the critical upper bound implies removability or a matching lower bound and convergence to a unique flat Fowler solution with a positive power rate. Sharpness of these dimension ranges will be established in a subsequent paper.

papers.title: Degenerate Preconditioned Proximal Point Algorithms as Forward Methods for Nonmonotone Inclusions
papers.abstract: We study degenerate preconditioned proximal point algorithms (PPPA) for finding zeros of nonmonotone set-valued operators in Hilbert spaces under solution-relative $(U,V)$-semimonotonicity, with possibly indefinite $U$ and $V$. With a closed-range preconditioner $P$, the reduced PPPA dynamics admit a forward representation through the complementary resolvent of a parallel composition, without requiring monotonicity or admissibility. Relative semimonotonicity of the range-restricted operator transfers to the reduced forward map, allowing our forward theory for possibly set-valued mappings to yield Fejér estimates and residual rates. Under suitable conditions, including demiclosedness of the reduced map at zero, the projected PPPA iterates and shadows converge weakly to a common projected zero. Without demiclosedness, a counterexample shows that the projected sequences may converge to a point outside the projected zero set, even when the original operator is continuous. Bounded recovery condition yields weak convergence of the full (non-projected) shadows. The monotonicity modulus $U$ yields additional results: under suitable conditions, $U\succeq\tau P$ with $\tau>0$ gives strong and linear convergence of the projected PPPA sequences, while $U\succeq-\sigma P$ with $0\le\sigma<1/2$ still permits local linear rates under metric subregularity. These strong convergence and linear rate guarantees extend to the full shadows when a Lipschitz recovery estimate holds, such as when $U$ is strongly monotone on $\ker P$. For Chambolle--Pock and Douglas--Rachford splitting, we establish Lipschitz recovery even when $U=0$ by exploiting the primal--dual structure. Under suitable parameter conditions, full-shadow convergence guarantees, including $R$-linear rates, extend to the original PPPA iterates.

papers.title: What Can Postselection on Halting Decide?
papers.abstract: A probabilistic program can produce an answer on some runs and continue forever on others. Suppose it halts with positive probability on every input and we count only the runs that halt. Aaronson et al. showed that if the correct answer must be more than twice as likely as the wrong one, such programs decide exactly the problems solvable with a finite list of halting questions chosen in advance. They asked what happens when the correct answer need only be more likely than the wrong one. We prove that the resulting class is exactly $\boldsymbol{\Delta^0_2}$: the halting questions can now be asked one at a time, with each answer helping to determine the next question. This remains true if the program must halt with probability at least 99%, or with any other prescribed rational lower bound below one. Our main technical result is the exact query bound when the program gives two guarantees. Suppose it halts with probability at least $\rho$ and, among the runs that halt, the correct answer has probability at least $a$. For rational $0 < \rho < 1$ and $1/2 < a < 1$, these programs decide exactly the problems solvable with at most $n$ halting questions chosen in advance, where $n$ is the largest integer satisfying $\rho(a/(1-a))^n \le 1$. Every value of $n$ occurs, and different values give different classes. The proof measures how much additional halting probability a change of answer requires, and counts these changes as in Ershov's hierarchy. The results extend to quantum machines with computable gates.

papers.title: Winning Solution to UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge 2026 (V2X-Real Track): Site-Calibrated Synthetic Data and Multi-Detector Fusion
papers.abstract: This work summarizes a winning solution for the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge (V2X-Real track) at the IEEE BigData Cup 2026. The primary objective is to train 3D detectors for vehicles, pedestrians, and trucks using only synthetic roadside LiDAR data, and to generate synthetic scans that are sufficiently realistic to be indistinguishable from real ones. A CARLA-based pipeline was developed and calibrated to the fixed sensor site, accurately modeling the range image, including no-return beams, based on unlabeled real development scans. A combined inference detector, utilizing multiple 3D detectors (VoxelNeXt, PV-RCNN, and SECOND) trained exclusively on synthetic data, was also proposed. Each scan was aligned to the synthetic ground plane and processed through the detectors at multiple ground heights. The resulting bounding boxes were fused using bird's-eye view (BEV) clustering, followed by class-specific post-processing to refine heading and box size and to filter low-confidence detections. The final submission tied for first place with a combined score of 0.8947. The ablation study demonstrated that per-scan ground leveling more than doubled the real-scan mAP, while fusing boxes across different heights and models further improved performance. The proposed work narrows the gap between synthetic and real LiDAR data for 3D object detection in urban V2X scenarios. Reproducible code is available at this https URL

papers.title: Pair Correlation Conjecture for the Zeros of Artin $L$-functions I: Simple and Critical Zeros
papers.abstract: In 1973, Montgomery posed the pair correlation conjecture (PCC) for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Motivated by PCC, Montgomery conjectured that the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function are almost surely simple, and proved that at least $2/3$ are simple assuming the Riemann hypothesis (RH). In 1978, Mueller and Gallagher were able to prove asymptotically $100\%$ are simple assuming PCC and RH. Recently, Goldston et al. noticed that the assumption of RH can be removed in Mueller and Gallagher's method. In fact, assuming PCC by itself without RH is sufficient to prove that asymptotically $100\%$ of the nontrivial zeros are both simple and on the critical line. We adapt the notion of horizontal multiplicity from Goldston et al. to show that the nontrivial zeros of Artin $L$-functions attached to irreducible linear representation of the Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ are almost surely simple and lie on the critical line without assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH). We will assume the appropriate version of PCC along with some other widely believed conjectures.

papers.title: Faster $χ^2$ periodogram: Accelerating linear algebra with fast Toeplitz solvers
Inferring accretion bursts in intermediate-mass protostars from asteroseismic imprints
Linearization and local controllability of nonautonomous differential inclusions
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the linearization of nonautonomous differential inclusions, whose right-hand side is integrably Lipschitz in the state variable and measurable in time. We establish measurability results for time-dependent graphs and identify the Clarke tangent cone to the set of their measurable selections in $L^\infty\times L^1$. Combining this characterization with a subtransversality argument, we obtain a lower estimate for the Clarke tangent cone to the set of all admissible trajectories starting from a fixed set. As an application, we give sufficient conditions for local controllability around a closed terminal set.

papers.title: Basic introduction to Freidlin-Wentzell theory
Enumerating Solutions to Type (2,3) Composition Identities of Finite Endofunctions
papers.abstract: We enumerate ordered pairs $(f,g)$ of endofunctions on a finite labeled set $X$ satisfying a composition identity of type $(2,3)$, with two factors on one side and three on the other. For all sixteen forms up to exchanging $f$ and $g$, we give exact counting formulas as functions of $|X|$ in terms of finite sums and generating functions. Such pairs correspond bijectively to actions on $X$ of the semigroup presented by two generators and the prescribed relation. The proofs use images, fibers, and the decomposition of functional digraphs into directed cycles with rooted trees attached. Several constructions apply beyond these sixteen identities: they give recurrences for homomorphisms between arbitrary prescribed functional digraphs and formulas for pairs satisfying $f^a=g^b$, where $a,b$ are fixed positive integers. We also derive an explicit inclusion-exclusion formula over subsets of $X$ for the number of endofunctions $g$ on $X$ satisfying $B=gAg$ for arbitrary prescribed endofunctions $A,B$ on $X$. This generalizes the enumeration of compositional square roots, recovered when $A$ is the identity map.

papers.title: Quantum sine imaginary-time evolution: sequential and QSVT implementations of a probabilistic ground-state filter
papers.abstract: We propose quantum sine imaginary-time evolution (QSITE), a quantum algorithm for preparing ground states of a Hamiltonian. QSITE approximates imaginary-time evolution through an exact sine filter. We give two circuit implementations of this operator: a sequential one that applies it as a concatenation of linear combinations of unitaries (LCU), reusing two ancilla qubits across steps via mid-circuit measurement, and a coherent one based on the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). A telescoping identity shows the two prepare the same state and succeed with identical probability, differing only in how that probability can be boosted. QSITE belongs to the family of ancilla-based probabilistic imaginary-time filters and we state rigorous convergence guarantees: we prove that the QSITE operator converges uniformly to the exact ITE operator, that the prepared state converges to the ideal ITE state, and that the filter probability increases monotonically with each concatenation step. Although the construction applies to an arbitrary Hamiltonian, we specialize it to optimization Hamiltonians, and this specialization is what exposes its structure more easily. Since MaxCut eigenvalues are integers, the probability of failure is periodic in the evolution time, yielding safe zones, the first located analytically and the second numerically. For MaxCut we further show that, when the tolerated energy error is a fixed fraction of the ground-state energy, the probability of failure can be bounded below 1/2 with concatenation steps growing linearly with the number of qubits in the first safe zone. We present numerical results for random Erdös-Rényi instances with up to 24 qubits and benchmark QSITE against QAOA.

papers.title: On the Cauchy problem for $σ$-evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients via upper decay indicators
papers.abstract: In this paper, the first main goal is to investigate the Cauchy problem for the linear $\sigma$-evolution equation $$ u_{tt}+a^2(t)(-\Delta)^\sigma u+b(t)u_t+m^2(t)u=0, $$ where propagation speed, damping term and mass are time-dependent functions. Under suitable assumptions on the interaction among these coefficients, we not only derive decay estimates for the solution and its derivatives in terms of the effective parabolic time scale $\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(s,t):=\int_s^t a^2(\tau)/b(\tau) d\tau$, but also conclude the additional decay induced by the mass term and the upper decay indicators of the initial data. Especially, one can recognize that the time-derivative estimate for solutions exhibits a competition between $m^2(t)$ and $a^2(t)\left(1+\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(0,t)\right)^{-1}$. For the corresponding semi-linear problem with the nonlinear term $|u|^p$, we also establish global (in time) existence of small data solutions fulfilling decay estimates, coming from the mass factor $\exp\left(-\int_0^t m^2(\tau)/b(\tau)d\tau\right)$, under the same assumptions on these coefficients.

papers.title: Fixed-space indices and symmetry breaking in variational problems
papers.abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for variational bifurcation with prescribed exact stabilizers under finite group actions. Combining ordinary spectral flow on fixed-point spaces with minimal-overgroup nullities, we obtain a lower bound on the number of exact-stabilizer bifurcation parameters when the restricted singular set is finite. The theorem allows strongly indefinite Fredholm Hessians and requires endpoint invertibility only on the chosen fixed space, without parameter differentiability or regular crossings. When the restricted Hessians have finite Morse index, the criterion involves only indices and nullities. We also treat varying form domains under explicit transport assumptions and regular matrix Sturm--Liouville systems. As our principal application, we consider a Newtonian nine-body family consisting of two interlaced squares with fixed satellite masses and a varying central mass. We prove analytically that central configurations with two nonconjugate exact reflection stabilizers bifurcate at a common mass in $(142,150)$, displacing the central body from the centre of mass. The family contains a reported counterexample to Moeckel's linear-stability conjecture; our bifurcation proof is independent of that stability assertion.

papers.title: An all-steps-at-once algorithm for time-domain wave propagation in heterogeneous and unbounded media
papers.abstract: We propose, analyze, and implement a convolution quadrature (CQ) algorithm for transient acoustic waves in an unbounded medium consisting of a heterogeneous domain embedded in free space, where the wave speed may be spatially variable and discontinuous. Multistep CQ, applied to the time-domain solution operator, reduces the evolution problem to a family of Helmholtz problems with damped complex frequencies, which can be solved independently in parallel, all time steps at once. The frequency problems are discretized by an overlapping coupling of finite elements (FEM) on a polygonal/polyhedral domain containing the inhomogeneity, and boundary elements (BEM) on a smooth curve enclosed by that domain, in the region where the medium is homogeneous, which accounts exactly for the unbounded exterior. Neither discretization needs to conform to the geometry of the heterogeneous domain, nor to each other. For the resulting FEM--BEM coupling we prove bounds for the solution operators of the transformed problems that are explicit in the Laplace parameter and the wave speed. These bounds yield convergence of the time discretization for A-stable multistep schemes. We also prove explicit estimates on the exponential decay of the transformed solutions away from the heterogeneity, which show that the correction provided by the BEM part is small but relevant, and cheap to compute: a few GMRES iterations suffice, and the correction is needed only over a fixed range of weakly damped frequencies, beyond which it becomes negligible and can be dropped. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates in time and space and explore iterative (multigrid) methods for the interior FEM problems.

papers.title: PoRef-MIL: Plug-and-Play Posterior Refinement for Multiple Instance Learning in QSM-Based Brain Disease Classification
papers.abstract: Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) is a novel quantitative MRI contrast for studying tissue susceptibility changes in brain disorders, including Parkinson's disease (PD) and multiple sclerosis (MS). However, small cohorts and the lack of local annotations make developing deep learning models for QSM-based diagnosis challenging. In this work, we propose PoRef-MIL, a weakly supervised multiple instance learning (MIL) framework combining iterative slice relabeling and network retraining with a plug-and-play posterior refinement module (PRM). During training, a 2D dual-branch diagnosis network and a subject-level classifier were alternately trained for five rounds. The classifier was used to update slice pseudo-labels for retraining the diagnosis network. The PRM was applied during inference to refine slice probabilities through bidirectional posterior inference and calculate entropy-derived confidence from the refined probabilities, which was then used in sliding-window scoring to obtain subject-level predictions. PoRef-MIL was evaluated on an in-house PD cohort of 287 participants and a public MS cohort of 150 participants. Compared with eight classification methods, PoRef-MIL achieved the highest mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.942 and 0.872, and accuracies of 0.926 and 0.833, for PD and MS classification, respectively. Ablation experiments were conducted to validate the effectiveness of iterative relabeling and PRM, and the plug-and-play feature of the proposed PRM was also evaluated using four state-of-the-art MIL models. Overall, PoRef-MIL offers a promising approach to QSM-based disease classification in small cohorts without manual slice annotations.

papers.title: Classification of critical points of heat kernels on flat tori and Riemann theta functions
papers.abstract: For any two-dimensional flat torus $E_\tau:=\mathbb{C}/(\mathbb Z+\mathbb Z\tau)$ and any $t>0$, we prove that the heat kernel $p_{\tau}(z,t)$ has either four or six critical points on $z\in E_{\tau}$ (i.e., including four trivial critical points and at most one pair of nontrivial critical points). This is interestingly consistent with Lin-Wang's remarkable result (Ann. Math. 2010) for the Green function. The key idea is to show that any nontrivial critical point (if it exists) is a nondegenerate global minimum point. Furthermore, we classify the types of all critical points, as well as the splitting phenomena that occur when the number of critical points changes. Applications to Riemann theta functions are also given. In particular, we resolve a conjecture of Luo and Wei (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 2022).

papers.title: Discrete Hyperbolic Cosecant Distributions
papers.abstract: We introduce three families of discrete hyperbolic cosecant probability distributions, supported either bilaterally on $\mathbb{Z}$ or unilaterally on $\mathbb{N}_0$, inspired by series evaluations of Srinivasa Ramanujan. We determine their exact normalization constants in terms of singular values of complete elliptic integrals and the Gaussian constant $G=\varpi/\pi$ with the lemniscate constant $\Gamma^2(1/4)/(2\sqrt{2\pi})$ by explicitly calculating some series, e.\,g. $$ \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} 2k \operatorname{cosech}(k \pi) = G^2 + \frac{1}{\pi}. $$ Furthermore, by connecting these distributions to Fourier transforms of powers of the hyperbolic secant and applying the Poisson summation formula, we obtain closed-form evaluations for even moments and hyperbolic secant lattice sums, e.\,g. $$ \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathrm{sech}^4(k \pi) = \frac{2}{3} \left(G^4 + G^2 + \frac{1}{\pi}\right) $$ as polynomials of the Gaussian constant.

papers.title: Learn Locally, Extend Globally: Koopman Eigenfunctions and the Basin of Attraction
papers.abstract: Koopman eigenfunctions associated with the Jacobian eigenvalues of a stable equilibrium are Lyapunov functions defined exactly on its basin of attraction. We turn this into a computational procedure for power systems. Eigenfunctions estimated by extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) are written as functions of the state, made to vanish at the equilibrium by centering the lifted variable $\cos\delta$, and verified on a grid with the model: two Lyapunov candidates from the EDMD spectrum certify up to 66\% of the basin of a single-machine infinite-bus system from data in the linear region. The Koopman semigroup property then extends the EDMD-Lie eigenfunction to the whole basin, recovered at the grid resolution with its isostables and isochrons.

papers.title: A toric construction of the spectral Tate curve
papers.abstract: We develop toric geometry spectral algebraic geometry. In particular, we lift toric varieties to flat schemes over the sphere spectrum. Furthermore, we prove several rigidity and strictness results allowing us to define and produce strict group actions of flat algebraic tori. As an application, we give a construction of the Tate curve in spectral algebraic geometry. This approach lets us produce a lift of the Tate curve to $\mathbb{S}[[q]]$. We furthermore describe how to lift (arithmetic) toric stacks.

papers.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
Field algebras associated with non-symmetric lattices
papers.abstract: Field algebras, introduced by Bakalov and Kac, generalize vertex algebras by replacing locality with a weaker associativity-type axiom. We develop the structure theory of field algebras with a view toward geometric examples in which a natural bilinear form fails to be symmetric. We prove a reconstruction theorem for field algebras, producing a field algebra structure from a generating family of fields. We associate to every finite-rank lattice $L$ equipped with an arbitrary bilinear form a canonical field algebra $V_L$, generalizing the Heisenberg and lattice vertex algebras. We then study potential definitions of commutants in this setting and analyze when they are realized as subfield algebras. Finally, we realize these constructions geometrically by looking at the homology of the moduli stack of complexes of quiver representations, extending previous results from Dominic Joyce.

papers.title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions
papers.abstract: Barron et al. (2026) recently identified numerical issues in the softmax and soft cross-entropy loss. We show that similar issues are present in standard divergence operations between categorical distributions. This includes the forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), as well as Monte Carlo KL estimates and entropy. When the distributions are nearly equal, rounding and cancellation issues affect the forward and gradient computations. These issues can affect settings using divergences in optimization objectives, such as knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal methods. We propose numerically stable reformulations and provide example implementations for each setting, validated by property-based tests.

papers.title: Learning observable propagation with sparse local moments
papers.abstract: We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories. Thanks to the locality of the dynamics, we construct the transition moment matrices by projecting the Markov operator onto low-order connected-cluster basis functions supported near the target observable. Exploiting the spatial decay of time-lagged correlations, {these matrices} can be approximated in sparse-plus-low-rank form using trajectory samples, with computational cost scaling linearly in the system dimension and the number of trajectories. The learning error can be further reduced by correcting the memory effect induced by the Galerkin projection. We numerically demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in extrapolating the dynamics of various many-body systems, including Langevin and Glauber dynamics for classical systems as well as Lindblad dynamics for open quantum systems. For reversible local binary-spin dynamics, we establish volume-uniform $O(\varepsilon)$-$L^2(\pi)$ approximation bounds for local observable dynamics using connected-cluster spaces with neighborhood radius $O(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ and cluster order $O(\log^2(1/\varepsilon))$. We further establish error bounds for repeated one-step propagation using exact moment matrices and their sparse-plus-rank-one compressions, uniformly in the time step and number of iterations.

papers.title: Anomalous Sound Detection Using Separation Features and Paired-Mixture Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Acoustic monitoring often relies on normal machine recordings with limited information about operating conditions. We first train a separator to estimate a normal target recording from a mixture of machine sounds. With the separator frozen, we train regional attention on pairs of mixtures that share the target recording and contain different interfering sounds. Differences between the paired embeddings provide the covariance estimate for correction before cosine nearest-neighbor scoring. We evaluate the method on the development-test recordings of seven machine types in the 2022 Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events challenge. We summarize detection performance by the harmonic mean of source-domain, target-domain, and partial areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve. On the original recordings, a separator trained without external pre-training achieved a three-run mean of 64.56%, close to the 64.87% obtained by distillation from a pre-trained audio transformer. Using the same transformer as a frozen encoder gave a mean of 64.88%. With competing machine sounds added to the test recordings, both implementations outperformed distillation at all seven tested interference levels.

papers.title: Ergodicity without monotonicity: patch-positive spin systems
papers.abstract: Monotonicity is the standard tool for proving that an interacting particle system is ergodic. What can replace it when the system is not monotone and its invariant measure is unknown? The simplest such systems are kinetically constrained models such as FA-1f and East exposed to noise. In these models vacancies enable updates, so adding vacancies should help the system forget its initial state. We prove this for a broad class of spin systems, which we call patch-positive. If vacancies are created spontaneously at a uniformly positive rate, the system converges to the same equilibrium from a large class of initial states, and from every initial state if the threshold density is at most $\tfrac12$ or the interactions are oriented. In particular, the East model with noise is ergodic at every density, and we obtain new cases of the positive-rates conjecture. The key idea is to compare the dual processes of the system with and without the added deaths.

papers.title: Trainable sparse dendritic networks reveal regime-dependent roles for shunting inhibition and morphology
papers.abstract: Neural circuits must compute reliably despite noise and changes in context. We introduce DendriNet, a framework for training scalable rate-based networks with sparse excitatory and inhibitory contacts, controllable dendritic architecture and different synaptic integration rules. In image classification, shunting networks transmit and rely on distal dendritic signals more strongly than additive networks. Distributing limited contacts across compartments improves classification in small populations, whereas greater serial dendritic depth offers no clean-image benefit in resource-matched trees. Robustness depends on the perturbation. Deeper shunting trees better tolerate independent pixel noise, whereas additive trees better tolerate strong input scaling. On a contextual task with gain variation and noise, the primary shunting tree is more accurate than the separately tuned additive tree under the noise and gain conditions used during training, yet depends less on cue-specific inhibition. Learning dendritic leak conductances partly restores shunting accuracy on dim, noise-free inputs outside the training distribution. At AlexNet width, shunting integration and learned sparse connectivity support smaller deployed networks with accuracy comparable to the retrained dense layers they replace. These results relate dendritic organization and synaptic integration to noise tolerance and contextual computation, and suggest tests of dendritic function and design principles for brain-inspired networks.

papers.title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
papers.abstract: Neural surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD) are trained and ranked on single-family, fixed-domain datasets that cannot test the minimum bar for an aerodynamic foundation model: predicting CFD-quality incompressible flow in seconds for new shapes in new enclosures. On DrivAerML, larger models and longer training barely lower Transolver's error; doubling training cases cuts it by about 12% up to 400 cases, exhausting the dataset. We introduce AeroZoo, a benchmark and training corpus of 3,815 time-mean unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (URANS) solutions with a transition model across seven geometry families, eight enclosures, and Reynolds numbers from $10^3$ to $10^8$. Each sample poses a well-posed PDE problem as a solver receives it: boundary meshes grouped by condition type, prescribed values, and fluid properties. The 2,816 time-mean-stable samples form the canonical benchmark: two tasks, mean engineering metrics with an overall flow score $S_{\mathrm{flow}}$ (1.000 for uniform inlet flow), and 22 frozen geometry-disjoint splits holding out shapes, enclosures, boundary-condition layouts, and Reynolds ranges. On the random split, boundary-condition tokens cut GeoTransolver's mean velocity error from 89.8% to 15.2% of inlet speed (uniform flow: 44.0%; $S_{\mathrm{flow}} = 0.290$). ISLA, a boundary-driven transformer, reaches 8.2% ($S_{\mathrm{flow}} = 0.153$; 0.123 with boundary targets), about 6 times mesh-refinement sensitivity. On shared test samples, holding out a geometry family barely changes ISLA's mean velocity error, whereas holding out enclosures or boundary-condition layouts raises it 3.8 to 8.4 times. The dataset is public; the scoring code will be released.

papers.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
papers.abstract: Symmetry is a foundational principle of physics: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the coordinate frame, unit system, or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet today's leading neural surrogates lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation), rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs. Because the boundary determines the interior solution, ISLA encodes the posed boundary once into learned slices and evaluates arbitrary interior points independently through a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel. Inputs are nondimensionalized in scales computed from the boundary, sums over boundary cells are area-weighted quadratures that converge under mesh refinement, and geometry enters only as distances and relative angles to equivariant slice anchors, making the model equivariant to rigid motions and reflections up to optional token subsampling and tree clustering. On AeroZoo, 2,816 3D flows spanning diverse geometries, poses, physical scales, and boundary conditions, ISLA's mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are 1.9 and 2.2 times lower than the best baseline's. On full AirfRANS, ISLA is second only to an explicit boundary-integral network (GLOBE), with errors 1.6 to 2.6 times lower than the better of Transolver's and GeoTransolver's in every field.

papers.title: Mixed Inner Variation and Global Hessian Integrability for Degenerate Monge-Ampère Equations
papers.abstract: We study the global Hessian integrability for nonzero convex solutions of the degenerate Monge-Ampère equations $\det D^2u=M(-u)^p$ with zero boundary values on arbitrary bounded convex domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$ in the global Lipschitz regime $p>n-2$. We establish global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimates for every $0<\varepsilon<\min\{(p-n+2)/n,1\}$ and determine the optimal range of $\varepsilon$ in dimension two and on rectangular boxes. The flat faces of rectangular boxes and their intersections impose upper bounds on the admissible exponents of global Hessian integrability. A new input in the proof for general dimensions is a Caccioppoli-type estimate for the boundary Hessian mass using vector fields arising from a mixed second inner variation. For the sharp higher integrability result in the plane, we use the combined hodograph-Legendre transform to control the curvature of level sets.

papers.title: Control Variates to reduce the variance of the empirical Moment Generating Function: an extreme value perspective
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of Moment Generating Functions is fundamental in many applications, but empirical estimators have high variances. Within a control variate setup, Extreme Value Theory is leveraged to identify how extreme values affect the variance reduction method's optimality.

papers.title: Margin-Inducing Optimal Guidance and Control for Atmospheric Entry
papers.abstract: A method is presented for margin-inducing optimal guidance and control with application to atmospheric entry. The method induces margin in state inequality path constraints during entry while simultaneously retaining a large portion of the non-margin-inducing performance. The margin in the guidance trajectory is based on a differentiable approximation of the maximum of a continuous function. This differentiable approximation is derived from the Kreisselmeier-Steinhauser (KS) function, where the KS function is defined for a function over sampled data. The KS function is first modified into a weighted form where the data points and weights are associated with a multiple-interval Legendre-Gauss-Radau quadrature. This weighted form is then shown to be an approximation of a logarithmic integral. This smooth approximation of the maximum function is then used to formulate a margin-inducing optimal control problem, and this margin-inducing optimal control problem is re-solved at specified guidance update times. The method is applied to a reusable launch vehicle atmospheric entry problem subject to heating rate and dynamic pressure constraints. It is found that the method of this paper produces a guidance trajectory that remains a significant distance from the path constraint limits while maintaining a large portion of the performance of the constrained optimal control problem.

papers.title: Concentration of Quasimodes at Spherical Interface between 3D-Topological Insulators
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the edge states localized at a spherical interface between two $3\mathrm{D}$-topological insulators from a continuous model of the semiclassical Dirac equation. Using the dynamical and spectral properties of the semiclassical Dirac operator tangent to the interface and the Landau level stratification of the energy in the transverse variable, we describe several concentration and invariance properties of the semiclassical measures associated with quasimodes of the system localized at the interface. Moreover, we construct explicit quasimodes which fulfill some of these properties and concentrate on some particular single periodic geodesics of the sphere.

papers.title: Averaging Principle and Uniform Large Deviations for Time-Dependent Slow-Fast Systems via Young-Rough Integration
papers.abstract: The main aim of this work is to investigate the limiting behavior and asymptotic properties of time-dependent slow-fast stochastic dynamical systems. The slow component is driven by a stochastic process with Hölder-continuous paths of regularity greater than 1/2, while the fast component is driven by a Brownian rough path. We introduce a novel Young-rough integration framework tailored to such systems and establish well-posedness results, providing the analytical foundation for further asymptotic analysis. Building on this framework, we employ Khasminskii's time-discretization method to establish the strong convergence of the slow component to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation in the L^p-sense. Furthermore, when the driving noise in the slow equation is specified as a fractional Brownian motion, we apply the weak convergence approach to establish a uniform large deviation principle for the slow component, uniformly over compact sets of initial conditions, in the Hölder topology.

papers.title: Optimal Additive Integer Masks for One-Guess Vulnerability under an Absolute-Moment Budget
papers.abstract: A defender releases an integer-valued secret $X$ (a count, a discretised measurement, a clock value) as $Y = X + N$, where $N$ is an independent integer-valued mask whose expected absolute value, the expected distortion of the released value, is at most $c$. An adversary who knows the prior of $X$ and the law of $N$ observes $Y$ once and makes a single guess. We determine exactly how small the adversary's success probability, the posterior Bayes vulnerability, can be made, and which masks achieve it. For a secret supported on an interval of $m$ integers we give the optimum and an explicit optimiser for the uniform prior; by the maximal-leakage formula, the same mask minimises the worst-case-prior one-guess leakage for every prior with that support. For a biased bit, the simplest prior a defender can exploit, we characterise the masks that leak nothing on average, give the critical budget at which this becomes possible, and determine the entire cost-vulnerability frontier. It is the piecewise-linear interpolation of an explicit sequence of points generated by cost-optimally shifted truncated geometric masks, with infinitely many affine pieces accumulating at the critical budget, where the frontier meets the prior vulnerability with zero slope. The proof rests on a layer-cake decomposition of an arbitrary mask into truncated geometrics, along which both vulnerability and cost are exactly additive. The results give exact, prior-aware design guidance for additive integer noise against one-guess adversaries.

papers.title: On the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures: disjointness of the cohomology groups
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to start proving the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures concerning the cohomology of Deligne--Lusztig varieties attached to roots of the full twist. The main result establishes that the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebras of the cohomology complexes attached to roots of the full twist are concentrated in degree $0$. The main idea is to reduce the problem to a calculation in the Hecke category. The resulting argument is essentially topological and applies to all realizations of the Hecke category.

papers.title: Strong and weak mean value sets for elliptic operators: uniqueness and counterexamples
papers.abstract: Classical theorems of Epstein--Schiffer and Kuran characterize balls by the mean value identity for integrable harmonic functions. In the Fermi Lectures, Caffarelli described an obstacle problem construction of analogous averaging sets for symmetric uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators. For such an operator with bounded measurable coefficients in dimension $n \ge 2,$ fix a center $x_0$ and a volume $V > 0,$ and let $E$ be the corresponding canonical set. We prove that a bounded open set $D$ of volume $V$ containing $x_0$ satisfies the mean value inequality at $x_0$ for every integrable subsolution on $D$ if and only if $E \subset D \subset \operatorname{int}\overline{E}.$ In particular, every such strong mean value set agrees with $E$ almost everywhere. The proof uses weak modified Schwarz potentials and an energy comparison. Additionally, we construct smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic operators for which the unit ball satisfies the mean value identity for all integrable solutions but fails the subsolution inequality, showing that there can be two distinct notions for what one can consider to be a ''mean value set.'' The canonical mean value set with the same center and volume contains the entire unit sphere and has a hole of positive measure inside the unit ball.

papers.title: BPS invariants from resurgent topological string
papers.abstract: We review recent progress on the conjectural relation between the resurgent structure of topological string free energies and BPS invariants of type II string theory compactified on the same Calabi-Yau threefold. In this picture, Borel singularities are located at integral periods associated with central charges of stable D-brane bound states, while Stokes constants encode their BPS indices, or generalized DT invariants. After introducing resurgence and perturbative topological strings, we explain how trans-series solutions of the holomorphic anomaly equations determine non-perturbative amplitudes and illustrate the proposed correspondence in local and compact geometries. We discuss the behavior under changes of polarization and moduli, and review supporting arguments based on exact WKB analysis, blowup equations, the Stokes automorphisms of flat coordinates and dual partition functions, and Kontsevich-Soibelman wall-crossing. We conclude with open questions concerning a general proof, the interpretation of non-perturbative amplitudes, and the construction of non-perturbative completions.

papers.title: Canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction
papers.abstract: We study canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction. For any number of species and any rank of the fast subnetwork, the derivatives that enter the Krupa-Szmolyan conditions and coefficient are rational functions of the fluxes and the reciprocal concentrations. For a fast subnetwork of rank one, the dynamics is planar on stoichiometric classes and these forms are linear in the fluxes, extending our planar flux criterion; the criticality is an explicit cubic. When one species is fast, these forms decompose over the slow species, weighted by their reciprocal concentrations. The elementary-mode criterion then carries over, and the criticality depends on the composition of the slow pool, so one network can explode in either way. The obstruction that the slow flux cannot vanish on the fold is characterized by a Farkas certificate and a yield diagram decided on configurations of at most three reactions. Under four conditions on the critical curve, a canard point with $A\neq0$ unfolded by a rate constant gives the full canard explosion; with one fast species and a fast equation affine in the slow variable, these follow from sign conditions on the reactions and injectivity on the class. For fast subnetworks of higher rank, a centre-manifold reduction adds corrections through the group inverse of the fast Jacobian; in the Oregonator they make both canard points change criticality between its planar reduction and the full model. All results are proved; exact computations and simulations serve as independent checks.

papers.title: Splitting and Alternating Minimization Methods for Training Orthogonal Deep Feedforward Networks
papers.abstract: Training deep feedforward networks with weight matrices constrained to layer-wise Stiefel manifolds serves as an effective regularization technique to improve generalization. However, the simultaneous presence of orthogonality constraints and nonsmooth activation functions poses severe theoretical and computational challenges for standard stochastic gradient and Riemannian optimization methods. In this paper, we propose two splitting and alternating-based algorithms to train orthogonal deep feedforward networks (OrthDFNs). By introducing auxiliary variables, we decouple the nested nonsmooth compositions and manifold constraints into a structured equality-constrained optimization problem. To solve this model, we develop OrthALM, an inexact augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) that employs a proximal alternating minimization scheme to solve its subproblems. Crucially, every block coordinate subproblem admits an exact, closed-form solution. We establish a rigorous convergence theory for OrthALM, proving that every accumulation point of the generated sequence is a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) point of the regularized, reformulated problem. Furthermore, we introduce OrthADMM as a practical, proximal-free variant that executes a single inner alternating sweep per multiplier update to accelerate computation. Extensive numerical experiments show that OrthALM attains lower training error and constraint residuals than OrthADMM in most configurations. OrthADMM achieves competitive test accuracy and the lowest reported runtime in most comparisons with the selected baselines.

papers.title: Beyond weak convergence of signed spectral measures: Eigenvector overlaps and high-dimensional prediction risk
papers.abstract: Many results in random matrix theory and high-dimensional statistics depend on weak convergence of spectral measures, which is usually established via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms. This approach has recently been applied to signed measures. However, for signed measures, pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms alone no longer characterizes weak convergence. While this is unproblematic in many cases, in the high-dimensional regression setting, recently considered by Green and Romanov, the underlying signed eigenvector-overlap measures can fail to converge weakly, despite pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms. Using a novel approach to risk analysis, we show that weak convergence can be replaced by a simple convergence result for bilinear forms. This allows us to establish convergence of the prediction risk for estimators based on arbitrary continuous spectral filters, including (regularized) gradient descent and ridge regression, even when the underlying signed measures fail to converge weakly. Under additional regularity conditions, we construct an explicit finite signed measure yielding an integral representation of the asymptotic prediction risk. This representation provides necessary and sufficient conditions for minimum-norm interpolation and optimally tuned ridge regression to attain the smallest asymptotic prediction risk among estimators with continuous spectral filters. Moreover, we provide characterizations of weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures in terms of pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms.

papers.title: Singlet-triplet superconductivity from repulsive interactions in a $p$-wave magnet
The bias interval of the elephant random walk
Katz Kernel Based Stratification of Breast Cancer Patients
papers.abstract: The integration of mechanistic signaling networks into clinical research has become a cornerstone of precision oncology. By capturing the complex biochemical interactions within a cell, these networks provide a functional map of disease progression that goes beyond simple genomic mutations. Consequently, the development of specific signaling models of patients has significant relevance, allowing for a more granular representation of individual disease profiles. In this setting, there is a growing need for robust methodologies capable of comparing graph based pathway structures to identify similarities and differences across patient cohorts. Such comparisons are essential for the identification of clinically meaningful subgroups, and the discovery of novel biomarkers. Standard graph kernels, while mathematically rigorous, often remain too generic for this purpose. They frequently fail to capture features specific to gene signaling networks, resulting in suboptimal clustering performance. In this paper, we present a domain specific graph kernel designed for mechanistic signaling networks. Unlike generic approaches, our method explicitly incorporates biological constraints and gene interaction patterns into the kernel formulation, enabling a more accurate characterization of both topological structure and functional behavior. We assess its performance on breast cancer datasets, focusing on its ability to support disease subtyping. Our results suggest that our approach can effectively contribute to patient stratification.

papers.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the local rigidity of Bergman logarithmic flatness near the standard metrics associated with fixed invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Every sufficiently small smooth deformation preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness is induced by a holomorphic automorphism and a constant rescaling. In the Szegő setting, local rigidity was established by Lu--Tian (2004) on $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and, more recently, by Loi--Palmieri--Zuddas (2026) on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces.

papers.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
papers.abstract: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.

papers.title: Stagewise and interpretable emergence of inside-outside computation in Transformer-based language models
Thermodynamic Properties of the S=1/2 Zigzag Spin Ladder
The Grothendieck property of noncommutative Marcinkiewicz spaces
papers.abstract: We study sufficient and necessary conditions of a noncommutative Marcinkiewicz space to have the Grothendieck property. In particular, we show that every noncommutative weak $L_p$-space, $1<p<\infty$, is Grothendieck. We also prove that the intersection of two Grothendieck noncommutative $\cM$-bimodules is also Grothendieck. These answer several open problems in the literature.

papers.title: Stochastic homogenization of $p$-resistance forms on nested fractals
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic homogenization of $p$-energies on infinite nested fractals. We assign i.i.d. random $p$-resistance forms $D_{0,\alpha}$ to level-$0$ cells of an infinite pre-nested fractal, and study the scaling limit of the resulting random $p$-resistance form $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}$. Under a moment condition on the reciprocal of $D_{0,\alpha}$, we prove that the sequence of rescaled and renormalized random energies is almost surely Mosco convergent to an equally weighted self-similar $p$-resistance form. As an application, when $p=2$, we prove the almost sure weak convergence of the associated rescaled continuous-time random walk. In particular, we allow arbitrarily small random conductances and impose no condition on the upper bound of random conductances.

papers.title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
papers.abstract: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-\delta_k+o(1)})$ where $\delta_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large primes found by our attack when $k=2, 3$.

papers.title: Species sampling priors through exact augmentation
papers.abstract: Discrete random probability measures are central to Bayesian nonparametric modeling. In practice, their use often favors a few tractable priors with full weak support. Full support alone, however, does not specify how prior mass reflects beliefs about clustering, recurrence, discovery and other sample features. We develop a novel and general construction of species sampling process (SSP) priors from an index distribution and finite allocation probabilities, linked to these sample characteristics. Every proper SSP admits an exact two-stage representation through an almost surely finite index and a finite conditional measure. Averaging over the index recovers each realized SSP on every measurable set. Reversing this identity constructs priors whose tie probabilities, expected occupancy and discovery rates can be assessed without evaluating the infinite weights. We characterize compatibility among index laws, schedules and weights, and construct light-tailed, heavy-tailed and multimodal families with full weak support under suitable hyperpriors. A prior with paired weights combines full weak support with invariance under size-biased permutation in its defining order, an explicit finite index law and partition prediction. Exact simulation, recursive reweighting and finite posterior augmentation follow. Examples distinguish prior elicitation, exact averaging and fixed-level approximation.

papers.title: General non-extremal rotating charged AdS black hole solutions with four independent charge parameters in $D=4$, STU gauged supergravity
Ricci pseudo symmetric Anisotropic Fluid Spacetime admitting Hyperbolic solitons with Ricci vector field
papers.abstract: This work focuses on an anisotropic fluid spacetime with these unique forms of the stress-energy tensor associated with radial pressure and a transverse pressure p. In an anisotropic fluid spacetime , we mani- fest curvatures symmetry such as Ricci pseudo-symmetric and prove that Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime is generalized quasi- Einstein spacetime. We deduce the Einstein gravitational field equation of Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime. In the framework of pseudo-Riemannian geometry, specifically, we study the quasi-conformal Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime, which exhibit the dark matter era. Moreover, we discuss the hyperbolic Ricci soliton and Hyperbolic Yamabe soliton on Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime with a time-like Ricci vector field. Finally, we turn up the char- acteristics of hyperbolic Ricci soliton and hyperbolic Yamabe soliton on Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime with a time-like Ricci vector field.

papers.title: A virtual element exterior calculus framework
papers.abstract: We develop a unified virtual element framework for compatible polytopal discretizations of differential forms in arbitrary dimension and at arbitrary order. On general polytopal meshes, a central challenge is to construct de Rham subcomplexes and establish stability estimates with mesh-independent constants. We construct a trimmed complex of conforming virtual differential forms recursively from local Hodge--Laplace boundary value problems and obtain a complete subcomplex by imposing additional moment constraints. The local spaces of these two complexes contain the trimmed and complete polynomial differential forms, respectively, and admit unisolvent degrees of freedom from which polynomial projections can be computed. The canonical interpolants commute with the exterior derivative, and each virtual complex has cohomology isomorphic to that of the continuous de Rham complex. For both virtual complexes and in every form degree, we establish negative-norm inverse estimates and thereby prove a mesh-uniform equivalence between the $L^2$ norm and the scaled degree-of-freedom norm. Through the cochain isomorphisms induced by the degrees of freedom, these norm equivalences yield uniformly bounded liftings of fully discrete data into the corresponding continuous spaces, in particular for the Discrete de Rham method. We also derive canonical interpolation error estimates and discrete Poincaré inequalities. As an application, we obtain an inf-sup stable mixed Hodge--Laplace method with harmonic variables and optimal-order convergence under sufficient regularity.

papers.title: Theory of Optical and Magneto-Optical Properties of [111]-Oriented Site-Controlled Quantum Dots
Geometric folding and maximal asymptotic variance
papers.abstract: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $\Sigma_{\max}^2<1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions. We also show that the asymptotic variance for the Schwarzian derivative is at least $5.68\ldots$, which defeats the hypothesis that the Nehari criterion would be almost sharp.

papers.title: An Elementary Proof of the Binary Goldbach Conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish the binary Goldbach conjecture which asserts that every even positive integer greater than four can be expressed as a sum of two odd primes. This goal is achieved by proving that the number of ordered Goldbach pairs that add up to $2n$ is an $\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{n}{\ln^{2} n}\right)$ function. As an application, we provide a simpler verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture that was first established in [6,7].

papers.title: Native vacancies and antisites in rock-salt and wurtzite MnSe: formation energies across the growth window and spin splitting in the A-type order
Fourier inequalities and sign uncertainty II
papers.abstract: Building on our earlier work, we present an $L^2$-$L^1$ inequality for radial Fourier eigenfunctions, relating this to the sign uncertainty principle of Bourgain, Clozel and Kahane. We also propose a generalisation of the aforementioned uncertainty principle, and draw a connection with entropic uncertainty.

papers.title: Heat Transport Mechanisms in MOF-5
A true $Π^0_1$ sentence independence of PA
papers.abstract: We give a true $\Pi^0_1$ sentence $\varphi$ which is independent of Peano Arithmetic. Moreover, if $\widehat{\phi}$ denotes its interpretation on $\omega$ as a sentence of set theory, then $\widehat{\phi}$ is a $\Pi^0_1$ sentence independent of ZFC.

papers.title: A High Precision Transformer model for precessing binary black-hole merger waveforms calibrated to numerical relativity
An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
papers.abstract: We construct an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum in ranks at most 48. The construction begins with the Cayley table of $\mathbb{Z}/13\mathbb{Z}$, assigning a vector of norm four to each cell. We prove that the resulting incidence lattice has exactly 26 unimodular completions of minimum four, all isometric. The resulting Cayley lattice $\Lambda$ has automorphism group $\mathrm{AGL}(1,13)\times C_6$ and is $s$-extremal, with shadow minimum $13/4$ and kissing number $35\,594$. An explicit $4$-frame in $\Lambda$ yields a Type I self-dual $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$-code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16, resolving the corresponding open case in coding theory.

papers.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
The Cost of Minimal Completeness: Gamma-to-Delta Aliasing in Discrete Markets
papers.abstract: In one dimension, the symmetric binomial tree replicates quadratic payoffs using the Delta of its own price function. For every $d\geq 2$ and every centered, isotropic, minimally complete $(d+1)$-state model with $d$ risky assets, by contrast, some quadratic payoff requires a replicating hedge different from that Delta. In this nonredundant finite-state setting, centered one-step payoffs are spanned by the $d$ asset innovations; centered second-order (Gamma) contributions are therefore represented as first-order trading gains, potentially inducing additional asset holdings. We call this effect Gamma-to-Delta aliasing and measure it by the linear operator $\mathcal{A}_\xi(H)=\mathbb{E}[(\xi^\top H\xi-\operatorname{tr}H)\xi]$, where $\xi$ is the normalized one-step innovation and $H$ the Gamma matrix. For quadratic claims the replicating holding exceeds the price Delta by exactly $\sqrt{h}\,\mathcal{A}_\xi(H)/2$, where $h$ is the time step. Trading this holding in a Brownian market adds the tracking-error variance $hT|\mathcal{A}_\xi(H)|^2/4$, a fixed multiple of the ordinary discrete-Delta error that does not vanish in relative terms as $h\downarrow0$. We prove that the smallest worst-case aliasing over all minimally complete models is $\sqrt{d-1}$, so the worst-case relative excess variance is $(d-1)/2$; both are attained uniquely by the equal-probability regular simplex. For unit-Frobenius positive-semidefinite Gammas and for unit rank-one Gammas, the sharp minimax value is $(d-1)/\sqrt{d}$, with the same unique optimizer. We also show how aliasing trades off against unhedgeable quadratic risk when more states are allowed, and derive the leading implementation cost for smooth claims.

papers.title: First-principles study of the formation of Group-IV--vacancy color centers in diamond
On the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties of the differential system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$
papers.abstract: A prolongation variety of a polynomial differential system $S$ is an algebraic variety defined by the equations of $S$ and their derivatives up to a given order. We compute the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties associated with the system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$ in terms of the prolongation order, thereby proving a conjecture stated by Gleb Pogudin in Section 2, Question 6 of "Some Open Problems in Differential Algebra". Our approach is motivated from the beginning by doing computational experiments in OSCAR in order to find the number of solutions of a zero-dimensional system using algebraic Thomas decomposition. The result will follow from a coprimality condition on a family of polynomials with integer coefficients, which is verified by showing that their roots satisfy a strong interlacing property. Finally, we propose an extension of the conjecture for the systems $x_1'=x_2^n$, $x_2'=x_1^n$ with $n>2$.

papers.title: Fluctuating resource availability stabilizes coexistence beyond the oscillatory tragedy of the commons
papers.abstract: Fluctuations in ambient conditions such as temperature and humidity can alter the effective availability of a shared resource at a given abundance. Standard evolutionary games with environmental feedback treat the payoff matrix as a deterministic function of resource abundance, leaving open how fluctuations in availability affect the oscillatory tragedy of the commons. Using noise-corrected replicator dynamics and individual-based birth-death simulations, we show that zero-mean fluctuations in resource availability can stabilize an interior equilibrium and suppress coupled strategy-resource oscillations. We derive an analytical criterion, in terms of the payoff structure and feedback dynamics, for when increasing noise favors local stability. These findings identify environmental variability as a mechanism that can promote strategy coexistence and help maintain shared resources in systems prone to recurrent depletion.

papers.title: Finite refutations in countably additive quantum probability
papers.abstract: We axiomatize countably additive quantum probability and prove a completeness theorem for finite refutation beyond compactness: inconsistency is witnessed by refutations each of whose branches ends in finitely many jointly unsatisfiable commitments. Adjoining the hypothesis that every event has a predetermined, context-independent outcome makes the theory inconsistent, although every finite subset of the resulting axioms has a model. For a countable theory of closed bounds on sentence values in our real-valued infinitary logic, inconsistency is equivalent to a winning strategy for a challenger in a game against a model builder. The challenger chooses each test in response to the builder's commitments, and the plays that follow a winning strategy form such a refutation. For the quantum theory with predetermined outcomes, every winning strategy must branch infinitely at some node. In the strategy we construct, countable additivity locates the four-dimensional subspace in which a finite Kochen-Specker parity argument applies. In their standard models, our axioms describe the closed subspaces and the density-operator probabilities of a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. We prove in ZFC that the sets of probability values definable uniformly across standard models are exactly the $\sigma$-projective subsets of the unit interval.

papers.title: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta\ge750$ satisfies the Borodin--Kostochka inequality $\chi(G)\le\max\{\omega(G),\Delta-1\}$, conjectured for all $\Delta\ge9$. Reed (1999) established the inequality for $\Delta\ge10^{14}$, and Liu, Sun, Wang and Zeng (2026) lowered the threshold to $5.3\times10^6$. To extend a random partial colouring over large cliques, we find repeated colours using adaptively chosen vertex-disjoint stars and apply Hall's theorem to the available colour lists. We verify the required probability bounds by rational and interval arithmetic with directed rounding.

papers.title: Separately continuous maps into regular spaces and continuity of operations in separable semitopological groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every regular separable feebly compact semitopological group is a topological group. This answers a question of M. Tkachenko (2014) and extends the separable case of the author's 1994 theorem on Tychonoff pseudocompact groups to regular spaces. The proof rests on a new result: if $X$ is a separable Baire space, $Y$ is feebly compact and $Z$ is regular, then every separately continuous map $X\times Y\to Z$ is strongly quasicontinuous. Previously this was known only when $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ are Tychonoff. Using topological games of Banach-Mazur type, we extend the group theorem to regular separable Baire groups from a wider class of spaces, which contains all $p$-spaces, all feebly compact spaces and all products of a $p$-space with a feebly compact space. We also obtain local versions: the theorem holds for locally separable, locally feebly compact groups.

papers.title: Inverse powers and 2-adic properties of binary 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci sequence
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study binary 3 x 3 matrices with determinant one that generate the Tribonacci recurrence. Starting from a specific generating matrix, we obtain explicit expressions for its powers and inverse powers in terms of the Tribonacci sequence T_n and two associated sequences B_n and R_n. This matrix framework yields identities involving traces, determinants, and products, including addition formulas and Cassini-type relations linking T_n, B_n, and Rn. Moreover, we derive new identities from the matrix representation of inverse powers and establish structural relations between these sequences. As an application, we investigate arithmetic properties of Tribonacci numbers and determine the exact 2-adic valuation of T_2^k for sufficiently large k. Finally, we provide a classification of 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci recurrence via similarity over Q.

papers.title: Separating the Polar of Sets of Uniqueness from the Polars of All $H^{(d)}$-Sets
papers.abstract: We construct a perfect set of uniqueness on the circle carrying a continuous probability measure which annihilates every $H^{(d)}$-set, simultaneously for all finite dimensions d. This gives a strict inclusion between the polar of the compact sets of uniqueness and the polar of the union of the classes $H^{(d)}$, answering a question raised in earlier work on these polars. The construction uses random binary increments of size comparable to the reciprocal of a product of square roots. A Gaussian sampling estimate gives a uniform Fourier-tail bound for all pseudomeasures supported by the resulting set, and also bounded atomic approximation and spectral synthesis. A separate energy estimate, stable under deletion of a small number of increments, yields full support for every limiting quasi-independent image of every positive measure absolutely continuous with respect to the constructed measure.
