However, for stochastic nonconvex-strongly convex bilevel problems, existing first-order methods typically rely on nested loops and/or large batch sizes for attaining $O(\epsilon^{-6})$ or $O(\epsilon^{-4})$ sample complexity under standard bounded-variance assumption or mean-square smoothness assumption. Achieving these rates with a single-loop penalty method and a constant batch size remains challenging due to a large penalty value needed for an accurate approximation. To address this challenge, we develop a stochastic SIngle-loop COnstant-Batch first-order penalty method (SICO) that combines two complementary ingredients. First, it performs one stochastic-gradient update per-iteration for both the original lower-level and penalized problems, with a projection that controls the separation between their iterates. Second, it applies an exponential moving average to stabilize the upper-level gradient estimator. We show that this combination achieves $ O(\epsilon^{-6}) $ sample complexity using only $O(1)$ stochastic-gradient samples per iteration under unbiased, bounded-variance stochastic gradients. Under the additional mean-square smoothness assumption on the lower-level stochastic gradients, the same algorithm improves the complexity to $O(\epsilon^{-4})$ also with $O(1)$ batch size. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to match the best-known convergence rate for fully first-order SBO methods using a single loop and a constant batch size. This result addresses an open problem posed in the literature.

papers.title: Generalized Commutator on Octonion Algebra
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be an octonion algebra over a field $F$ of characteristic different from $2$, and let $A,B\in\mathcal O$, not both zero. We study the image of the generalized commutator $\Phi(x,y)=A(xy)-B(yx)$ on $\mathcal O$. We prove that $\Phi$ is surjective if and only if either one of $A$ and $B$ is invertible and $A\neq B$, or $A$ and $B$ are nonzero zero divisors and $A-B$ is invertible. In the remaining cases, the image of $\Phi$ is a hyperplane or a four-dimensional maximal totally isotropic subspace of $\mathcal O$, except when $A$ and $B$ are linearly independent zero divisors and $A-B$ is not invertible, in which case the image spans a six-dimensional subspace. Along the way, we show that every octonion of trace zero is a commutator. We also prove that the image of $Axy-Byx$ on any quaternion algebra over $F$ is a vector subspace, extending a result of Panja S., Saini P. and Singh A. (Images of polynomial maps with constants, Mathematika 71 (2025), no. 3, Paper No. e70031) for $2\times 2$ matrices over algebraically closed fields, and we give examples of other generalized polynomials whose images are not vector subspaces.

papers.title: Generalized eigenstate thermalization beyond leading order in 2D large $c$ CFTs
papers.abstract: We develop a Fock-space formulation that reduces expectation values of vacuum-family quasi-primaries in quantum Korteweg--de Vries (qKdV) eigenstates to a free-bosonic problem, and employ it to test the generalized eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (GETH) in 2D conformal field theories with a large central charge. We prove that the first two qKdV charges $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ lift all degeneracies except along at most countably many curves in the $(c,\,\Delta)$ plane, where $c$ is the central charge and $\Delta$ denotes the highest weight of the conformal family, so that the full-qKdV simultaneous eigenstates are unambiguously determined by $Q_1$ and $Q_3$. Based on this, a comprehensive toolkit for testing GETH within the scope of vacuum-family observables, i.e. equating qKdV eigenstates and thermal states of the generalized Gibbs ensemble in the sense of expectation values of vacuum-family local observables, is provided in this paper. We argue that GETH is satisfied when the infinite tower of qKdV charges is considered. A more restrictive form of the GETH, namely that all expectations of local observables of a definite level should be expressible in terms of the first few qKdV charges, is directly falsified at subleading order in the large-$c$ expansion. Specifically, at levels 6 and 8 in the vacuum family, expectation values of quasi-primaries in simultaneous eigenstates of the qKdV charges are not determined by any finite number of the lowest-index qKdV charges. The question of whether additional microscopic information about the eigenstate is required is left for future work.

papers.title: Optimal convergence rates in homogenization of Monge-Ampère equations with periodic measures
papers.abstract: We establish optimal convergence rates in periodic homogenization of Monge--Ampère equations, allowing the microscopic measure to be singular or degenerate. Let $\mu$ be a nonnegative $\mathbb Z^n$-periodic Borel measure with $\mu(\mathbb T^n)=1$, and set $\mu_\varepsilon(E)=\varepsilon^n\mu(E/\varepsilon)$. On a bounded convex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, let $u^\varepsilon$ and $u$ be the convex solutions of \[ \det D^2u^\varepsilon=F(x,x/\varepsilon)\,\mu_\varepsilon,\qquad\det D^2u=\overline{F}(x) \] with the same Dirichlet data, where the coefficient $F$ is bounded, uniformly positive, and periodic in its second variable, and $\overline F(x)=\int_{\mathbb T^n}F(x,y)\,d\mu(y)$. For $m=0,1$ and $0<\alpha\leq1$, we prove \[ \|u^\varepsilon-u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\leq C\varepsilon^{m+\alpha},\qquad \forall\,0<\varepsilon\leq1, \] provided that $u\in C^{m+2,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ and $F(\cdot,y)\in C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uniformly in $y$. These exponents are optimal in their respective regularity scales, and the constant $C$ is independent of the distribution of the microscopic measure. In particular, the estimates include the optimal quadratic rate for general periodic measures. Our proof of the lower-order estimate ($m=0$) relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for periodic correctors. For the higher-order estimate ($m=1$), we introduce a constrained Monge--Ampère problem that produces convex approximations with prescribed cell averages. This construction captures the cancellation in the third-order corrector expansion without uniform Hessian bounds for the correctors.

papers.title: Quillen's finiteness conjecture for the cotangent complex in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Building on work of Turner, we propose a proof in positive characteristic of Quillen's conjecture on finiteness properties of the cotangent complex for homomorphisms between noetherian rings of possibly infinite flat dimension.

papers.title: NeuroLens: Learning Latent Embeddings of Neural Semantics from Chronic Recordings
papers.abstract: Understanding how neural activity represents higher-order cognition and how these representations evolve during learning is a central pursuit in neuroscience. However, tracking meaningful representational changes remains challenging because recorded neural populations change across days. Here, we introduce NeuroLens (Latent Embeddings of Neural Semantics), a self-supervised model based on the Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (LeJEPA). An adaptive encoder maps changing neural populations into a common latent space, where a temporal predictor forecasts future latent states. Across mouse and human intracortical recordings, NeuroLens learns representations that improve decoding of abstract variables, including decisions and sentence meaning. In chronic mouse neural recordings during visual decision-making, these representations capture gradual transitions between learning stages and the progressive orthogonalization of neural states associated with different choices. They also reveal distinct timescales of cortical reorganization across tasks during learning. With multi-day pretraining, these representations also support stable decoding across days, including leading performance on the FALCON benchmark. Together, these findings support NeuroLens as a framework for tracking learning-related representational changes while maintaining stable decoding over long timescales.

papers.title: Lithium Niobate Surface-Acoustic-Wave Resonator for Very-High-Frequency Isolated Power Conversion
papers.abstract: Piezoelectric devices offer a promising magnetic-free alternative for high-frequency power conversion. Here, we demonstrate a lithium niobate surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator that is optimized for isolated power transfer and show advantages in operating frequency, power density, power handling, and electrical isolation. Our application-optimized 40-MHz SAW resonator, with two electrically isolated interdigital transducers (IDTs) and acoustic Bragg mirrors, achieves a 25.7 W output power at a temperature rise of about 15 °C with only passive cooling through the back mounting side. With a chip size of 0.095 cm$^3$ and an acoustic mode volume of 0.00255 cm$^3$, our device features a peak chip power density of 270.5 W/cm$^3$ and a mode-volume power density of 10,078 W/cm$^3$. Our device shows an isolation voltage of 2.17 kV. Driven by a GaN full-bridge inverter, our device can drive different load resistors with a calculated peak power transfer efficiency of 87.5%. Our results show the potential of SAW devices as a core component for next-generation power systems.

papers.title: From Redundancy to Minimality: Fixed-Point-Guided Hierarchical Reduction of Learned Piecewise-Linear Dynamics
papers.abstract: Understanding a nonlinear dynamical system from time series requires not only reproducing its trajectories, but also identifying a simple representation that preserves its essential dynamical structure. Almost-linear recurrent neural networks (AL-RNNs) are piecewise-linear RNNs in which only a subset of units use ReLU nonlinearities, so that nonlinear capacity is explicitly controlled by the number of ReLU units. Their activation patterns define linear regions, represented as symbols, whose observed transitions form a symbolic transition graph. However, directly training AL-RNNs with few ReLU units to realize minimal dynamical representations can be unreliable. We ask whether an AL-RNN with more ReLU units can instead be trained first and systematically reduced to a minimal dynamical representation. We introduce a fixed-point-guided hierarchical reduction procedure that progressively linearizes selected ReLU units, merging neighboring linear regions and graph nodes while preserving distinct symbols containing fixed points (FPs). The resulting reduction tree defines a hierarchy of progressively simpler candidates. Each reduced candidate is initialized from the parent parameters and retrained through gradual linearization with guidance from the parent dynamics. We also prove that, under certain assumptions, reproducing $Q$ distinct fixed points requires at least $Q$ FP-containing symbols, providing a certificate of symbol-level minimality when this bound is attained. Across six tasks spanning attractor reconstruction and flip-flop memory, our learn-reduce-retrain strategy substantially improves the recovery of minimal models, including settings where direct training rarely succeeds. These results show that redundant nonlinear capacity can serve as a scaffold for discovering and realizing minimal dynamical representations.

papers.title: A homotopical enhancement of Neisendorfer's algebraic models
papers.abstract: We give an $\infty$-categorical enhancement of Neisendorfer's equivalences between the homotopy categories of rational simplicial sets, commutative dg algebras (cdgas), cocommutative dg coalgebras (cdgcs) and dg Lie algebras (dgls), where these objects have respective hypotheses of connectedness, nilpotency and finite type. We do so by proving that linear duality is a partial Quillen equivalence between weak finite type connected cdgcs and cdgas, and that Quillen's Chevalley--Eilenberg adjunction is a partial crossed derivable equivalence between cdgcs and dgls, a concept we introduce in this paper to axiomatize precisely the behavior of this adjunction.

papers.title: Impact of Gain Layer Doping Concentration on the Performance of 4H-SiC LGADs
Montesinos Knots with Delta-Unknotting Number One
papers.abstract: The $\Delta$-unknotting number for a knot is defined as the minimum number of $\Delta$-moves needed to deform the knot into the trivial knot. In this paper, we discuss Montesinos knots whose $\Delta$-unknotting number is equal to one. We propose a conjectural characterization of Montesinos knots with $\Delta$-unknotting number one and provide examples admitting distinct $\Delta$-moves, each of which deforms the knot into the trivial knot. Furthermore, we present examples illustrating the relationship between the locations of $\Delta$-moves and $X$-moves for knots with $u^{\Delta}(K) = 1$, considering separately the cases $u(K) = 1$ and $u(K) = 2$.

papers.title: Asymptotic Throat as a Minimal Geometric Alternative to the Singularity in Schwarzschild Black Hole
Surveying for Close Binaries among Lithium-rich Giants
Finite-momentum trimers and Cooper quartets in a one-dimensional Fermi gas with coexistent $s$- and $p$-wave interactions
Transverse momentum as the counter-diabatic generator in bent waveguide couplers
papers.abstract: Axis bending of a mode-evolution coupler realizes the counter-diabatic (CD) protocol [Opt. Express 34, 1214 (2026)]. We identify the operator responsible. Rigid lateral displacement is generated by the transverse momentum $\hat p_x$, which in a real two-mode supermode basis is purely $\sigma_y$: exactly the form of the CD term, and the one form that detuning and coupling cannot supply. Equating the two gives the axis slope in closed form, as a ratio of two matrix elements at a single cross section, or $\dot{x}_0=\dot\theta/(\gamma\Delta\beta^{2})$ in coupled-mode variables. It agrees with a numerical offset search to 0.3% and is shown to be the earlier curvature condition viewed from the Kramers-Henneberger frame. Beam propagation simulations compare the bent coupler directly with the unitary-transformation realization built from the same reference structure: the two reach supermode fidelities of 0.994 and 1.000 against 0.886 for the untreated coupler, show comparable bandwidth and fabrication tolerance, and differ inside the device by the frame transformation that relates them.

papers.title: Faster Estimates from Binned Test Scores---With Discussion of Normality, Bias, and Reliability
papers.abstract: Education agencies often summarize test score distributions by counting how many students scored in 3 to 5 bins. Means and standard deviations (SDs) can be estimated from bin counts using a HETOP model, which assumes that scores are normally distributed within each school or district. However, most HETOP software takes minutes to hours if the number of schools or districts is large. We present a fast HETOP algorithm that produces HETOP estimates in less than a millisecond per district. The algorithm is implemented in the fast_hetop function of the binest package for RL: this https URL HETOP estimates of the mean are highly reliable; estimates of the SD are not as good. Maximum likelihood estimates are generally excellent but can be biased and unreliable if scores are not normal or scores are concentrated in the top or bottom bin. Empirical Bayes shrinkage improves unreliable estimates. Standard errors are smaller if the data represents the whole population of students rather than a sample. HETOP estimates are usable for many purposes, but it would be better if education agencies reported means and SDs directly.

papers.title: t-J model at 50
The overlooked price feedback: Why simulations overstate distribution grid peaks from home batteries under real-time pricing
papers.abstract: Simulation studies of home batteries under real-time pricing commonly find that synchronized charging creates new peaks in distribution grids. Yet all home-battery simulation studies reviewed here treat wholesale prices as exogenous, ignoring the effect of battery dispatch on prices. Charging in low-price hours raises the wholesale price, which dampens the incentive to charge. In equilibrium, charging is spread out across hours. This paper examines how accounting for this feedback changes peaks in local grids. A simulation of household battery dispatch under real-time pricing, calibrated to German data, finds that, if half of households own a battery, exogenous prices raise the coincident import peak by 83 % relative to the no-battery benchmark. With endogenous prices, the same fleet reduces the peak by 6 %. This finding is robust across alternative price functions, price paths, peak measures, and scenario assumptions. While new local peaks remain possible where batteries are geographically concentrated, these results suggest that published studies overstate the local peak-load effects of price-responsive batteries.

papers.title: Asymptotically Hölder gradient regularity for degenerate or singular parabolic normalized $ p$-Laplace equations
papers.abstract: We study bounded viscosity solutions of the degenerate or singular parabolic equation \[ u_t-|Du|^{\gamma}\Delta_p^{\mathrm{N}}u=f \qquad \text{in } Q_1, \] where \[ \Delta_p^{\mathrm{N}}u := \Delta u+(p-2) \left\langle D^2u\frac{Du}{|Du|}, \frac{Du}{|Du|} \right\rangle, \qquad -1<\gamma<\infty,\quad 1<p<\infty, \] and $f\in C^0(Q_1)\cap L^\infty(Q_1)$. Given any prescribed $\alpha\in(0,1)$, we prove that there exists $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(n,\alpha)>0$ such that \[ |p-2|+|\gamma|\leq\varepsilon \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1+\alpha,\frac{1+\alpha}{2}}(Q_1). \] In particular, the spatial gradient Hölder exponent can be chosen arbitrarily close to $ 1 $ as $(p,\gamma)\to(2,0)$. This extends the result of Andrade and Santos (Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations \textbf{61}, Paper No. 196, 2022) for $\gamma=0$ to the joint regime $(p,\gamma)\to(2,0)$ and answers affirmatively the question raised in Remark~1.1 therein.

papers.title: Contraction-Based Model Predictive Control using Bilinear Koopman Realizations with Proportional Error Bounds
papers.abstract: Data-driven model predictive control based on Koopman operator theory is a promising approach for constrained control of nonlinear systems with unknown dynamics. This paper proposes a robust model predictive control framework for such systems using bilinear Koopman realizations with state- and input-dependent proportional approximation-error bounds that vanish at the target equilibrium. Since prediction in lifted coordinates with a finite-dimensional Koopman realization need not remain on the manifold of valid lifted states, multi-step prediction may leave the region where one-step error certificates apply. We avoid this difficulty by reprojecting each predicted lifted state onto the original state coordinates and lifting it again, yielding an error-aware discrete-time control-affine predictor in the original state space without assuming invariance of the Koopman dictionary. For this predictor, we develop a homothetic tube construction based on a discrete-time robust control contraction metric whose radius explicitly accounts for the proportional approximation error bounds. The tube tightening handles arbitrary continuously differentiable nonlinear constraints, and the resulting model predictive control problem includes terminal ingredients and a tube-radius penalty that exploits the vanishing uncertainty near the target. We prove robust satisfaction of the original nonlinear constraints, recursive feasibility, and exponential stability of the sampled true closed-loop system with high probability over the training data without requiring a globally optimal solution to the model predictive control problem. Numerical examples, including nonlinear obstacle-avoidance constraints, demonstrate robust stabilization and higher performance of the proposed approach compared to existing Koopman-based model predictive control methods in terms of smaller closed-loop cost and flexibility.

papers.title: Breit interaction in elastic scattering of vortex electron on Hydrogen atomic target
papers.abstract: The interaction of electron vortex beams with atoms is fundamental to their applications, yet existing studies of elastic scattering have considered only the Coulomb interaction. The role of the Breit interaction, which represents the leading relativistic correction to the Coulomb potential between two electrons, has not been systematically examined. In this paper, we study the elastic scattering of a vortex electron by a hydrogen atomic target, with emphasis on the role of the Breit interaction. Comparisons are made between two situations: the pure Coulomb contribution and the pure Breit contribution. Our results show that the Breit interaction dominates the scattering process when the total angular momentum of the vortex electron is larger than a certain threshold, which challenges the conventional notion that the Breit interaction makes little contribution to electron scattering for low-$Z$ atoms. This phenomenon arises primarily because a vortex electron with large angular momentum possesses a substantial magnetic moment, and the Breit interaction precisely describes the interaction between magnetic moments. The threshold can be adjusted by changing the parameters of the initial vortex electron. Moreover, we further compare the single-atom, mesoscopic, and macroscopic target cases, and show that the target size significantly influences the observability of the Breit-induced effects, with a smaller target size being favorable for observing this phenomenon. Vortex electrons add a new tool to the well-established electron-atom scattering tool box. Our results are important for applications of vortex electrons: they show that, when large total angular momentum is involved, the Breit interaction must be taken into account in calculations.

papers.title: Scaling Density Functional Theory with Gaussian Splatting
Differential Recursions, Projective Discriminants, and Algebraic Generating Functions
papers.abstract: Two hierarchies of bivariate generating functions arise from differential recursions with rational initial data: a self-dual hierarchy and a reduced-symmetry hierarchy. At order $p=3$, their rational coefficients yield the triangles OEIS A140136 and A336110, together with a positive palindromic numerator triangle for the odd sector. In general, the reduced hierarchy decomposes into $p-1$ Horn companions, and an explicit differential intertwiner of order $p-3$ relates the last companion to the normalized self-dual series. The Narayana quadratic ($p=2$) and the $S_4$-symmetric Gross--Witten--Wadia quartic ($p=3$, with two tetrahedral edge resolvents) serve as explicit low-order benchmarks. For every $p \ge 3$, we prove that the distinguished reduced generating function has exact algebraic degree $2(p-1)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(x,h^{p-1})$ and that every Horn companion is algebraic. Over $h$, the rational uniformization lifts to the Fermat curve $s^{p-1}+w^{p-1}=1$ of genus $(p-2)(p-3)/2$ with generic monodromy and Galois group $S_{2(p-1)}$. This uniform cover establishes the universal boundary factorization at $H=h^{p-1}=0$ and explains the cubic characteristic factor $\mathcal{A}_p^3$ (carrying a projective $S_3$ action) in the discriminant via $(2,3)$-cusp geometry, illustrated by exact sextic and octic equations and higher-order slices. Conversely, a nonexact differential on the Fermat curve combined with full $S_{2(p-1)}$ monodromy proves that the distinguished self-dual function is transcendental for all $p \ge 4$. The complete factorization of the generic reduced discriminant remains open.

papers.title: The maximum number of edges in minimal matching covered graphs
papers.abstract: A connected graph $G$ with at least two vertices is {\em matching covered} if each of its edges lies in a perfect matching. A matching covered graph is {\em minimal} if the removal of any edge results in a graph that is no longer matching covered. Lovász and Plummer [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B 23 (1977) 127--138] proved by ear decompositions that every minimal matching covered bipartite graph $G$ with at least 6 vertices has at most $(3|V(G)|-6)/2$ edges, and this bound is sharp for all even $|V(G)|\ge6$. Very recently, Mallik, Diwan and Kothari [J. Combin. 17 (4) (2026) 559--606] determined the extremal graphs achieving this upper bound. In this paper, we prove that every minimal matching covered nonbipartite graph $G$ with at least 6 vertices has at most $(5|V(G)|-10)/2$ edges. Moreover, we show that if $G$ is not bicritical, then $G$ has at most $(5|V(G)|-14)/2$ edges and if $G$ is 3-connected and has at least 14 vertices, then $G$ has at most $(5|V(G)|-26)/2$ edges. All three bounds are sharp, and all the corresponding extremal graphs are characterized.

papers.title: Critical escape dynamics of an active particle moving on curved surfaces
Tails, Trails, and Transients: Comets, NEOs, and Supernovae in Rubin Early Data Preview 2
The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex
papers.abstract: A polyhex is a connected set of n cells of the regular hexagonal tiling, joined edge to edge, where each cell has area one. Kurz conjectured an upper bound for the area of the convex hull of a polyhex, after the corresponding problem for squares was solved. We prove that the convex hull of a polyhex with n cells has area at most one sixth of the ceiling of $n^2+14n/3$, and that for every n this value is attained by a path made of three straight runs of nearly equal length. This proves the conjecture of Kurz and improves his bound by 1/6 when n is divisible by 3. The proof bounds the hull of the cell centres and three of its widths with a spanning tree of the polyhex. The upper bound is formalised in the Lean 4 proof assistant with the Mathlib library. We also show that for every n the extremal polyhex is unique up to rotation, reflection and translation, which an exhaustive search had confirmed for at most 12 cells. The proof of uniqueness was generated by Claude at the request of Sascha Kurz, and it is also formalised in Lean.

papers.title: Boolean threshold functions, neuron capacity, and memory retrieval
papers.abstract: How much information can a single neuron remember? How many memories can neural networks retrieve without creating false memories? These questions are related to a basic question: how many Boolean threshold functions $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(a_0+\langle a,x\rangle)$, $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, are there? In this paper, we show that the number $T_n$ of distinct Boolean threshold functions is \[ T_n=2\binom{2^n-1}{n}\bigl(1+O(n^{-99})\bigr). \] Equivalently, the capacity of a single threshold neuron is $n^2-\log_2(n!)+1+O(n^{-99})$ bits, improving the $O(n)$ error term in the result of Kahn--Komlós--Szemerédi to $O(n^{-99})$. To prove this, we show that, for $1\le r\le n-1$, and $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ are chosen at random from $\{-1,1\}^n$, \[ \mathbb P\!\left\{ \langle v_1,\ldots,v_r\rangle\cap\{-1,1\}^n =\{\pm v_1,\ldots,\pm v_r\} \right\} =1-O(n^{-99}). \] In the context of the Kanter--Sompolinsky Hamiltonian for memory retrieval, this identifies $r=n-1$ as a sharp threshold, at which, for almost every collection of $r$ memories, the only ground states are these memories and their negatives, confirming a weaker form of the Kalai--Linial--Odlyzko conjecture. It also settles a recent open problem posed by M. Anthony on the specification number of Boolean threshold functions. In addition, we show that, for every $1\le r\le n-1$, \[ \mathbb P\{v_1,\ldots,v_r\text{ are linearly dependent}\} =2\binom r2\,2^{-n}+O\!\left(2^{-n}e^{-cn}\right), \] confirming a conjecture of Kahn--Komlós--Szemerédi.

papers.title: Pauli Spectra as a Boundary Spectroscope in Quantum Spin Chains
Magnetic Lifting of BIC Symmetry Protection Enables Nonreciprocal Beam Steering and Angular Information Encoding
papers.abstract: Symmetry-protected bound states in the continuum (SP-BICs) offer exceptional optical confinement but remain nonradiative. Here, we demonstrate that magnetically lifting their protecting symmetry enables nonreciprocal beam steering with intrinsic angular information encoding. In a magneto-optical photonic crystal slab, an in-plane magnetic field converts an SP-BIC into a radiative quasi-BIC and, together with vertical dielectric asymmetry, continuously displaces the associated band extremum away from the Gamma point. The steered beam exhibits two independent locking relations: its wavelength is locked to the elevation angle, while its polarization orientation is locked to the azimuthal angle. These relations embed complementary spectral and polarization information into the scanning beam, providing additional sensing channels for multidimensional LiDAR. Moreover, the nonreciprocal dispersion gives different resonance frequencies at opposite wave vectors, supporting resonant emission at +k while back-reflected light at the same frequency is off resonance at -k, opening a route to intrinsic self-isolation and reduced optical feedback. These findings establish a unified framework connecting magnetic beam steering, angular information encoding, and nonreciprocal feedback suppression, with prospects for compact reconfigurable light sources and integrated optical engines.

papers.title: The Uniqueness of Exponential Second-Order Expected Utility
papers.abstract: A decision-maker entertains several probability models of the state of the world, distrusts each of them, and is unsure which of them holds. She therefore carries two relative-entropy penalties: one on departures from a given model and one on departures from the reference she places on models. The literature that introduced this structure treats the equality of the two penalty parameters as a tractable special case. We show that it is in fact a necessary and sufficient condition: her criterion carries a single relative-entropy penalty if and only if the two parameters agree, that is, when she charges the same price for doubting a model as for doubting her weights on models. Under that one condition the two layers collapse: the criterion is an exponential second-order expected utility based at the Bayesian predictive distribution, for every compact model set and every prior, with no large-sample limit anywhere. When the condition fails, the caution she displays blends her two parameters, with a weight equal to the share of an act's predictive variance that comes from disagreement among the models; since that share varies across acts, no single parameter and baseline represent her, and the same variation identifies the two parameters separately. The exponential aggregator and relative entropy are each forced: no other continuous and strictly increasing aggregator delivers the collapse, and within the power-divergence family only relative entropy does.

papers.title: Evidence for the emergence of stellar magnetic fields during rapid mass transfer
When to Move: Online Repositioning of Movable Antenna Arrays Under a Long-Term Actuation Energy Budget
papers.abstract: Movable antenna (MA) arrays improve multiuser throughput by repositioning their elements, but mechanical movement reduces transmission time and consumes actuation energy. Changes in user configurations create nonuniform demand for repositioning over time, while each movement determines which positions are reachable in subsequent slots. Thus, online control must decide when to spend a limited actuation-energy budget, not only where to position the antennas. We formulate causal effective-throughput maximization under displacement-dependent movement delay, inter-slot reachability, and a long-term average actuation-energy constraint. We propose Lyapunov-based online movable-antenna repositioning (LOMA), which adjusts the price of movement through a virtual queue and solves the resulting nonconvex position problem via proximal minorization--maximization, accounting for nonsmooth movement delay and promoting sparse antenna updates. We establish monotone ascent of the smoothed per-slot objective, a finite-horizon sample-path energy bound, almost-sure long-term budget feasibility under a Gaussian fading model with bounded large-scale gains, and a state-matched throughput comparison separating temporal energy allocation from per-slot optimization error. Simulations show that LOMA concentrates actuation after intermittent user changes and improves effective throughput over optimized fixed arrays and a per-slot-budget counterpart, while continuous channel drift favors more frequent incremental repositioning. Additional simulations with pilot-based channel estimates in sparse millimeter-wave channels show that LOMA retains most of the throughput benefits of online repositioning while operating near its prescribed long-term actuation-energy budget.

papers.title: An irreducible decomposition of the Weil representation restricted to open compact subgroups
papers.abstract: For a $p$-adic field of any residual characteristic, we determine irreducible decompositions of the Weil representation restricted to the maximal open compact subgroups and the Iwahori subgroup by using the Schrödinger model. In particular, these decompositions show that the restrictions are multiplicity free.

papers.title: Towards Accurate Prediction of Mutation-Induced Changes in Protein Structure
papers.abstract: Proteins can possess numerous mutations relative to their wild-type amino acid sequences with minimal impact to their structure and function. However, in other cases, even a single amino acid mutation relative to the wild-type sequence can lead to a large change in structure or even a disease phenotype. While the accuracy of wild-type protein structure prediction has improved significantly in recent years, it remains difficult to accurately predict the structure of mutant proteins. Here, we characterize the local mutation-induced structural changes in proteins for a dataset of wildtype and the corresponding single-amino acid mutant x-ray crystal structures from the Protein Data Bank (PDB). We find that mutation-induced structural changes in these proteins are localized at the site of the mutation, decaying rapidly with increasing spatial distance from the mutation site. In addition, we evaluate how well AlphaFold3 can recapitulate the observed mutation-induced structural deformations in the x-ray crystal structures. We find that the accuracy of the AlphaFold3 predictions decreases strongly with increasing mutation-induced deformation. In contrast to the results for AlphaFold3, the Pearson correlation between a single physical feature, i.e. the change in solvent accessibility, and the mutation-induced deformation does not depend on the magnitude of the deformation. Our results and analyses provide a framework for further studies aimed at predicting the structural changes in proteins caused by single amino acid mutations.

papers.title: Optimal Allocation of Grid-Forming Frequency Shaping Control
papers.abstract: Various inverter-based control strategies have been proposed to improve frequency security for power systems with high renewable penetration. Among them, the grid-forming frequency shaping control is particularly promising due to its ability to shape the post-contingency aggregate system frequency dynamics into first-order with prescribed rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) and steady-state frequency deviation. Moreover, the shaped aggregate dynamics depends on the harmonic sum of all inverter transfer functions rather than on their distribution. In light of this, here we explore how to allocate shaping control resources to minimize the transient control effort needed to achieve ideal coherent dynamics. We formulate it as a constrained optimization problem by tackling two main difficulties. First, we make the squared $\mathcal{H}_2$ norm legitimate quantification of transient control cost under step power imbalances through a system transformation. Second, we simplify the $s$-domain constraint for Nadir elimination into a standard constraint that is easy to implement in optimization. The resulting non-convex optimization problem can be solved by existing successive convexification method. The effectiveness of the allocation has been verified on the modified Icelandic Power Network test case.

papers.title: Advanced 400G-SerDes Modulations and Equalizers for GPU Cluster in AI Era
papers.abstract: High-speed GPU cluster interconnects are evolving from 200 to 400 Gbps to meet the growing computing demands of artificial intelligence. We investigate high-order modulation and advanced equalization for 400 Gbps interconnects. Theoretical bit error rate (BER) expressions for 4/8-ary pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) and approximate expressions for six PAM6 formats generated from 32-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (32QAM) are derived. In additive white Gaussian noise, PAM6 generated by framed-cross 32QAM achieves the best BER performance among the PAM6 formats. PAM6 and PAM8 incur peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) penalties of approximately 4.2 and 7.2 dB, respectively, relative to PAM4 at the KP4 forward error correction (KP4-FEC) limit. Simulations compare PAM4, PAM6, and PAM8 at a line rate of 440 Gbps (net rate of 400G) under different bandwidth limitations. As bandwidth becomes more constrained, bandwidth requirements increasingly dominate performance over noise tolerance. PAM4 requires the lowest PSNR to reach the KP4-FEC limit in mildly bandwidth-limited channels, whereas PAM6 performs best under moderate limitations. PAM8 offers a significant advantage under severe limitations because of its lower bandwidth requirement and reduced susceptibility to high-frequency attenuation. With maximum likelihood sequence estimation, PAM6 and PAM8 reach the KP4-FEC limit under all evaluated channel conditions, while PAM6 requires a lower PSNR in most channels, highlighting its potential for 400G-SerDes systems.

papers.title: Stochastic optimisation method for estimating large deviations
Bulk-edge sticking beyond the Perron mode in Gaussian softmax attention
papers.abstract: We study row-softmax self-attention with independent Gaussian query and key weights in the proportional regime, at fixed inverse temperature. Hayase, Collins, and Karakida proved Gaussian equivalence for the empirical squared singular-value distribution after removal of the Perron direction. A global law alone does not exclude finitely many nonleading outliers. We prove that no such outliers persist: the rescaled squared singular value $\ell s_k(A)^2$ converges in probability to the upper edge of their bulk law for every fixed $k\ge 2$. In fact, this convergence is uniform over any deterministic sublinear number of leading non-Perron indices. The proof uses an exact decomposition of the softmax normalization, conditions on the key matrix, identifies the conditional covariance exactly with a diagonally conjugated inner-product kernel, linearizes that kernel in operator norm, and applies the outside-support local law of Fan, Ma, Paquette, and Wang. A separate stability argument identifies the finite conditional deformed Marchenko-Pastur edge with the limiting bulk edge. We also derive a scalar formula for that edge throughout the proportional regime and recover the explicit square-model formula of Hayase, Collins, and Karakida, including its physical branch.

papers.title: Uniform Inference for Parameters Identified by Conditional Quantile Restrictions
papers.abstract: Many structural and dynamic economic models imply that key parameters are identified by conditional quantile restrictions. Building on the exponential weighting approach of Bierens (1990) and the penalized maximum statistics of Chen et al. (2025), we develop a uniform inference method for such parameters. We construct an adaptive $\ell_1$-penalized statistic from a process indexed by quantiles and weighting directions. The statistic aggregates evidence across quantiles and regularizes maximization over directions. A shifted bootstrap is used to estimate local power for penalty selection. Under the stated conditions, adaptive selection asymptotically preserves or improves worst case local power relative to the unpenalized test over a prespecified set of alternatives. The improvement is strict when a positive candidate penalty raises the population level criterion above its value at zero. We also extend the process and bootstrap theory to the setting with pre-estimated nuisance parameters. We characterize their contribution to the limiting process, correct the variance estimator, and establish Gaussian multiplier bootstrap validity for null inference. Monte Carlo experiments favor the CvM-KS method for size control under pre-estimation and show that adaptive penalization can improve empirical power relative to the unpenalized test.

papers.title: First measurement of the forward rapidity dependence of $W$ boson transverse helicity fractions
A Geodesic Route toward Holography beyond AdS: Tessellating the Schwarzschild Black Hole
Fixed point properties for random groups in the density model with $d > \frac{1}{4}$
papers.abstract: We prove that random groups in Gromov's density model have Kazhdan's property~\((T)\) asymptotically almost surely (a.a.s.) at every density \(d>\frac14\). Together with Ashcroft's theorem for \(d<\frac14\), this establishes \(\frac14\) as the sharp threshold and settles the long-standing problem of determining the threshold for property $(T)$ in the density model. More generally, for every fixed number of generators \(n\ge2\) and density \(d\in(\frac14,1)\), there exists \(C_{n,d}>0\) such that, a.a.s., every affine isometric action on a real \(L^p\)-space has a fixed point simultaneously for all \[ 1\le p\le C_{n,d}\sqrt{\frac{l}{\log l}}, \] where \(l\) is the relator length. In particular, \(\frac14\) is also the threshold for each fixed \(L^p\) fixed point property, \(1\le p<\infty\). We also establish a simultaneous fixed point theorem for a large class of uniformly smooth real Banach spaces with a common power-type convexity bound and a suitable common bound on their uniform curvature moduli. We further prove that, for each fixed real Banach space in a class that, to the best of our knowledge, contains all currently known examples of super-reflexive Banach spaces, random groups at density $d>1/4$ a.a.s.\ have the fixed point property for affine isometric actions. The proof combines a fixed point criterion based on harmonic cocycles with spectral estimates for random bipartite multigraphs arising from decompositions of relators into four consecutive subwords. All asymptotic conclusions hold as \(\RelLen\to\infty\) through all positive integers.

papers.title: Functional Renormalization for Random Matrix Theory: The relational background field method
Positive normalized solutions for a singular regularized $p(x)$-Laplacian Dirichlet problem
papers.abstract: We study a singular Dirichlet problem driven by a regularized $p(x)$-Laplacian under a prescribed modular constraint. We construct nonnegative constrained minimizers for nonsingular approximating problems and, under the stated variational and boundary-control hypotheses, obtain a positive normalized weak solution as the reaction regularization vanishes. The approximation preserves the prescribed modular and yields subsequential strong Sobolev convergence of the states together with convergence of their constraint multipliers, while the gradient regularization remains fixed. Finally, we present a normalized singular problem on the unit disk as an illustrative example.

papers.title: Higher-Order Interactions in Complex Systems: Mechanisms, Behaviour, Representation and Reducibility
Affine dual Minkowski problem for general measures
papers.abstract: In 2025, the affine dual curvature measures $\widetilde{C}_m^a(K,\cdot)$ of convex body $K$ were introduced by Cai, Leng, Wu, and Xi, and the even Minkowski problem for the affine dual curvature measures was solved. In this paper, the necessary and sufficient condition of affine dual Minkowski problem for general measures with $m>1$ are proposed.

papers.title: Proposing, never assigning: fair allocation of shifts in experimental particle physics collaborations from ranked wishes under institutional quotas
The smallest square tileable by pairwise incomparable integer rectangles
papers.abstract: Croft, Falconer and Guy (Unsolved Problems in Geometry, Problem C5) exhibit a tiling of the 27 x 27 square by eight pairwise incomparable integer rectangles and remark that it is not known whether 27 is the smallest side length of a square that can be tiled by pairwise incomparable integer rectangles, no restriction being placed on the number of tiles. Knuth has since stated, in a 2019 draft of a section of The Art of Computer Programming, that 27 is indeed the smallest. We give a complete, independently reproducible proof: for every integer n <= 26 and every k >= 2, the n x n square admits no tiling by k pairwise incomparable integer rectangles. The proof combines two structural reductions with an exhaustive search over the 167538 surviving candidate tile sets, carried out by two independently written programs. The same search shows that at least eight tiles are needed at n = 27 and that the tile set of Croft, Falconer and Guy is the only one that tiles this square; it does so in exactly two arrangements up to symmetry. We also give explicit eight-tile tilings of the n x n square for every n >= 27, and seven-tile tilings for every n >= 34. With the classical lower bounds (every tiling of a rectangle by two or more pairwise incomparable rectangles uses at least seven, and no square of integer side less than 34 can be tiled by seven pairwise incomparable integer rectangles), this determines the least number of tiles for every square: there is no tiling for n <= 26, eight tiles are needed for 27 <= n <= 33, and seven for n >= 34. The complete software, build instructions and output logs are included as ancillary files.

papers.title: Radial Limits and Euler Exponents of a False Theta Series with Character Modulo 8
papers.abstract: Let $T_k=k(k+1)/2$ and let $N_n(q)$ be the series with terms $(-1)^{T_k}(2k+1)^{2n+1}q^{T_k}$ for $k\ge 0$. We study the false theta function $D=N_0$ and the moment quotients $N_n/D$. We prove an exact transformation formula for twists of even order. It expresses each moment as a convergent series of derivatives of the Dawson integral, with the dual twist and its phase determined by a quadratic Gauss sum. The formula gives the finite radial values of the moments at roots of unity as nonzero cyclotomic integers and yields congruences between them. Inside the unit disc we consider the quotient of $D$ by the theta series with terms $(-1)^{T_k}q^{T_k}$. Each nonconstant coefficient of this quotient is minus twice a positive integer that counts divisors and restricted partitions. These counts give a Lyndon-word formula for the exponents in the formal Euler product of $D$. The factorization also identifies the unique real zero in $(-1,1)$. A comparison with a cubic polynomial shows that this simple zero is the only zero in $|q|<1/2$.

papers.title: PlainMap: a lightweight, restartable mapping pipeline for ancient and modern DNA
papers.abstract: Mapping sequencing reads to a reference genome requires preprocessing and alignment choices that can vary with library type, fragment length, sequencing platform, and reference genome. These considerations are particularly important for ancient and historical DNA, where short and damaged fragments complicate read mapping. We present PlainMap, a lightweight and restartable mapping pipeline for modern and degraded DNA sequencing data. PlainMap accepts a simple manifest of FASTQ files, identifies single-end and paired-end data from read headers, supports heterogeneous sequencing inputs, and provides alternative mapping strategies for modern and degraded DNA. Optional pilot subsampling allows users to rapidly compare mapped fragment recovery across different settings using identical subsets of raw data, without attempting to determine the most accurate mapping strategy. Chunking and checkpoint-based execution support processing large datasets and resuming interrupted analyses, allowing users to balance memory requirements, runtime, and restartability. PlainMap produces duplicate-filtered BAM files together with fragment-aware mapping and coverage statistics. Evaluation using heterogeneous Japanese sea lion and short-fragment cave hyena datasets demonstrated successful processing across mapping modes, consistent trimmed and merged read counts across chunk sizes, and recovery from interrupted analyses without repeating completed mapping steps. PlainMap is implemented as a single Bash script and is freely available at this https URL .

papers.title: A Single-Loop Method with Optimal Leading-Order Oracle Complexity for Optimization and Game Stationarity in Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Optimization
papers.abstract: We develop a single-loop first-order framework for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax optimization, with matching leading-order upper and lower bounds for optimization and game stationarity in a projected zero-respecting oracle model. We propose a single-loop projected damped extragradient method coupling projected extragradient updates with dual momentum and a moving proximal center. Each iteration uses at most three gradient evaluations, without nested subproblems. For game stationarity, a deterministic best iterate has first-order residual below $\varepsilon$ with leading oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(L^{3/2}D_Y^{1/2}\Delta_\phi\varepsilon^{-5/2})$, where $L$ is the gradient Lipschitz constant, $D_Y$ bounds the dual feasible-set diameter, and $\Delta_\phi$ is the initial-point-dependent value-function gap. For optimization stationarity, a uniformly selected iterate has expected squared Moreau-envelope gradient norm at most $\varepsilon^2$ with leading oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(L^2D_Y\Delta_\phi\varepsilon^{-3})$. Matching lower bounds are $\Omega(L^{3/2}D_Y^{1/2}\Delta_\phi\varepsilon^{-5/2})$ for game stationarity and $\Omega(L^2D_Y\Delta_\phi\varepsilon^{-3})$ for optimization stationarity over projected zero-respecting first-order methods. Under dual strong concavity, the same framework achieves leading first-order oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\kappa}L\Delta_\phi\varepsilon^{-2})$ under both criteria, where $\kappa$ is the dual condition number. Matching lower bounds hold for both criteria in the same oracle model. To our knowledge, this is the first work to close the oracle complexity gap for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax optimization under both stationarity criteria by simultaneously improving upper and lower bounds in the projected zero-respecting oracle model.

papers.title: On the clumpy nature of super-early galaxies
Self-Distilled Pronunciation and Accent Control for Neural Text-to-Speech
papers.abstract: Text-to-speech that reads raw text has no lexicon: a rare word is read as guessed, and a native Japanese listener accepts a word only if its reading and pitch accent are both right. A known remedy installs a reading-and-accent channel into a released model, but it needs many recordings. This paper removes the recordings: the frozen backbone reads a sentence containing a common word it already says correctly, and that output serves as the teacher for the same sentence with the word replaced by an annotated reading with its pitch accent. Screened raters judged the tag right on 0.80 to 0.93 of unseen difficult words on four backbones spanning autoregressive, diffusion, and encoder-decoder synthesis; plain kana, which cannot express an accent, got 0.38 to 0.60. On words needing no edit, naturalness is non-inferior on one backbone; on the other three, listeners prefer the unedited rendition by 0.19 to 0.26.

papers.title: Stripe-Like Superconducting Enhancement and Coexisting Magnetic Texture in an Infinite Layer Nickelate
Polarforming-Enabled Power-Splitting SWIPT: A GNN-Based Optimization Approach
papers.abstract: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) is a critical technology for the future of the Internet of Things (IoT). However, ensuring a stable power supply in such networks remains a significant challenge. This work introduces dynamic polarization control as an additional degree of freedom (DoF) in SWIPT systems. We propose a system where both the base station (BS) and the users can adjust their antenna polarization, a technique known as polarforming. In addition, each user device is capable of splitting the incident signal to perform simultaneous information decoding (ID) and energy harvesting (EH). The resulting non-convex optimization problem, which involves strongly coupled variables, is addressed using a graph neural network (GNN) that predicts the beamforming, polarization, and power-splitting variables. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed GNN-based dynamic polarforming optimization significantly outperforms fixed-polarization schemes, particularly under imperfect channel state information (CSI). Moreover, joint polarforming and GNN-based optimization maintains robust SWIPT performance under both polarization mismatch and imperfect CSI.

papers.title: Local-to-Global Isometries in Standard-Norm Generalized Gyrovector Spaces
papers.abstract: Every bijective gyrometric isometry between nonempty connected open subsets of simply connected generalized gyrovector spaces (GGVs) with real value-line structure extends uniquely to a global bijective isometry. The extension is a left gyrotranslation composed with an isometry preserving the identity, gyroaddition, and scalar multiplication. Gyromidpoints and point reflections give continuation of local isometry germs. Without assuming simple connectedness, a global bijective isometric extension exists exactly when the germs of the map and its inverse are fixed by their respective monodromy actions. Continuity of each fixed-scalar multiplication map implies contractibility and hence simple connectedness. We construct standard-norm GGVs for $t>0$ on positive invertible cones of nonzero unital JB-algebras and, in dimension greater than one, on their projective cones. Power maps relate their gyrometrics to Thompson's and Hilbert's metrics, respectively, with equality at $t=1$. Thus for both metrics, bijective isometries between nonempty connected open subsets extend uniquely to global bijective isometries. We give proofs of the known Thompson and Hilbert isometry classifications, together with their power-coordinate forms for every $t>0$, using the GGV Mazur--Ulam theorem and recovering the Jordan structures from infinitesimal gyrations. Applications include a new proof of Mankiewicz's theorem on connected open subsets of real normed spaces and a local extension theorem for hyperbolic balls in real inner product spaces, including incomplete and infinite-dimensional spaces. We also give constructions for products and function spaces.

papers.title: Controlled Islanding and Reconnection with Stability Guarantees via Submodular Optimization
papers.abstract: In large-scale networked dynamical systems, local faults or disturbances may propagate through the interconnections and compromise the stability of the entire network. Partitioning the network into disjoint subsystems, or islands, limits this propagation by isolating unstable portions of the network from those that remain stable. This paper studies a two-stage controlled islanding and reconnection problem. In the first stage, the network is partitioned into stable and unstable islands. In the second stage, selected stable islands are reconnected to recover connectivity lost during islanding while satisfying stability requirements. We derive Lyapunov-based sufficient conditions for both stages. To address the coupling between the islanding and reconnection decisions, we construct an augmented graph on which the bases of a graphic matroid induce exactly the admissible islanding and reconnection pairs. We further show that the resulting optimization problem admits an equivalent nonincreasing supermodular formulation. Based on this structure, we develop a local-search algorithm with counterexample refinement and establish a performance guarantee for its inner loop with fixed sample sets. Numerical studies on linear networked systems illustrate the proposed procedure, examine its sensitivity to fault locations, and compare the proposed method with a mixed-integer linear programming benchmark in terms of solution quality and computational performance.

papers.title: Physics as the label for measuring and correcting materials reasoning in multimodal models
Timelike Entanglement from Spacetime Density Matrices: A Lattice Realization
A Station-Based Evaluation of Machine Learning-based Weather Forecasting Models in Northern Norway
papers.abstract: Recent machine learning weather prediction (MLWP) models have demonstrated remarkable forecasting skill on global reanalysis-based benchmarks. However, their performance remains unclear in challenging environments such as Northern Norway, where narrow fjords and rapidly changing weather result in highly variable local wind conditions. In this case study, we evaluate FourCastNet3 (FCN3), GraphCast, and ECMWF High Resolution Forecast (HRES) for wind speed forecasting using multi-year station observations from Northern Norway, focusing on their relative performance, generalization beyond the training period, and performance under high-wind conditions. Our results show that HRES slightly outperforms FCN3 and GraphCast, with an overall RMSE of 2.89 $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, compared to 2.96 $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ for FCN3 and 2.94 $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ for GraphCast. Notably, the MLWP models maintain comparable performance beyond their respective training periods, with no clear evidence of noticeable degradation. FCN3 performs best under high-wind conditions, although all models substantially underestimate strong winds. Our findings suggest that MLWP has become competitive with NWP for local wind, but further refinements are still needed to capture complex terrain better.

papers.title: The density of long runs of non-$r$-free integers
papers.abstract: Fix $r\ge2$ and let $D_k$ be the natural density of the $n$ such that none of $n+1,\dots,n+k$ is $r$-free. We prove that $\log(1/D_k)=\frac{r-1}{\zeta(r)}k\log k+\frac{r}{\zeta(r)}k\log\log k-C_rk+o(k)$, where $C_r=\frac{1}{\zeta(r)}((r-1)\log\zeta(r)+r-1+r\log\frac{\pi}{r\sin(\pi/r)})$; for $r=2$ this is $C_2=\frac{6}{\pi^2}(1+\log\frac{\pi^4}{24})=1.4595513\dots$. This determines Mirsky's constant $\alpha(h)$, the density of the $n$ with $s_{n+1}-s_n=h$ in the squarefree numbers, to the same precision. Previously the only known estimate was $\log\alpha(h)\le-\frac54 h\log\log h+O(h)$; ours improves this by a factor of order $\log h/\log\log h$, and is two-sided. The upper bound rests on the observation that the primes $p\le z$ with $\prod_{p\le z}p^r\le\sqrt k$ sieve a window of length $k$ with no freedom of alignment, so that at least $(1/\zeta(r)+o(1))k$ positions must be covered by $r$-th powers of distinct primes exceeding $k^{1/r}$. The resulting sum over injections is $m!e_m$ with $m\sim k/\zeta(r)$, evaluated by a saddle point. For the lower bound the Chung-Erdos inequality recovers the full contribution of $m!e_m$ rather than merely its largest term, which is what makes the linear coefficient explicit. As a consequence the first-moment threshold for gaps between $r$-free numbers is $\frac{\zeta(r)}{r-1}\frac{\log x}{\log\log x}(1-\frac{(1+o(1))\log\log\log x}{(r-1)\log\log x})$; for $r=2$ the constant is $\pi^2/6$, that of Erdos's 1951 lower bound. We also prove that every covering system of length $k$ has modulus at least $\exp((\frac{r}{\zeta(r)}+o(1))k\log k)$, so the Chinese remainder construction yields only $\zeta(r)/r$, half of $\pi^2/6$ when $r=2$. Erdos's bound is thus equivalent to the assertion that the first run of $k$ consecutive non-$r$-free integers occurs at the first-moment threshold, not at the scale set by the minimal modulus of a covering system.

papers.title: Effects of Interaction Range on Fluid Multicriticality: A Computational Study of an Interconverting Lattice Model
Positive Temperature Coefficient of Anisotropy due to $d^6L$ Groundstate in $ε$-Fe$_2$O$_3$
The phase coordinates transformation in Moyal noncommutative framework 2-dimensional harmonic oscillator and Painlevé second equation
papers.abstract: This work aims to explore the physical application of Moyal noncom- mutative formalism with the the presentation of new transformations which connect the old canonical coordinates to purly noncommuting phase coordi- nates through the parameters describe the Moyal noncommutative deforma- tion. These transformations are consistent with the Moyal noncommunica- tive brackets and build sixteen components traceless anti-symmetric tensor. This formalism incorporates space-space and space-momentum noncommu- taivity rather then noncommutativity (Heisenberg quantum commutation ) only for the canonical coordinates. The transformations imply to construct noncommutative analogs of 2-dimensional harmonic oscillator with its superintegrability and Painlevé second equation. The associated deformed Hamiltonians additionally involve some extra symmetries and reveal a deep physical understanding of about the additional symmetries with noncommunicative structure. The Painlevé second noncommutative coordinates transformation are also efficiently applied to generate the first Yablonskii Vorobev polynomial with Painlevé second parameter transformation.

papers.title: Thresholdless IBW Emission and Alpha-to-Thermal-Ion Energy Channeling via Pole Resonance of Fusion-Product Ions
papers.abstract: Fusion reactions can release a substantial fraction, and in aneutronic reactions nearly all, of their energy as the kinetic energy of fusion-product ions. In magnetized plasmas, these energetic ions can form ring distributions in velocity space. Such distributions can drive Dory-Guest-Harris (DGH) electrostatic instabilities, but these self-instabilities require a finite energetic-ion density and can be stabilized by a thermal background. We show that the same background can instead enable a distinct instability mechanism: a cyclotron pole of the minority energetic-ion susceptibility destabilizes a stable ion Bernstein wave (IBW) eigenmode. When the energetic-ion harmonic is distinct from the thermal-ion harmonics, exact root-pole resonance is thresholdless in the ideal collisionless limit. A species-resolved power balance shows that the energetic ions supply the free energy while the thermal plasma receives it. In the LAPD proton--alpha example, $99.96\%$ of the alpha-particle power loss enters the coherent proton response. This self-excited, ion-directed transfer provides a possible linear building block for alpha-particle energy channeling in proton-Boron11 fusion.

papers.title: Bounded Ratios of Lorentzian Polynomials II: Quadratic Derivatives
papers.abstract: We study bounded monomial ratios for Lorentzian polynomials. We prove that, in degree $d\geq2$ and $n$ variables, the bounded ratios from quadratic derivatives generate all bounded ratios for every $M$-convex support if and only if $n\leq3$, $d=2$, or $(n,d)=(4,3)$. For four-variable cubics, the proof uses a decomposition into $M$-concave functions. We construct explicit counterexamples with full support for four-variable quartics and five-variable cubics, then extend these two examples to all remaining pairs.

papers.title: Testing PPN by the Rotation of S301 Star
The LQ Digital Mode Family: Protocol Architecture and Reference Specification for Weak-Signal Communications
papers.abstract: This paper introduces LQ8, an open-source weak-signal digital mode for amateur radio that completes structured two-way contacts in 4 transmissions (60 s), achieving a 1.50x speedup over canonical 6-transmission exchanges (90 s) and 1.25x over 5-transmission RR73 exchanges (75 s) while preserving complete bidirectional exchange of Maidenhead grid locators, signal reports, and mutual acknowledgments. By replacing fixed-width message-type headers with variable-length prefix codes matched to physical-layer bit budgets, LQ8 packs the answering station's grid locator and measured signal report into a single 77-bit reply. In multi-station pileup operations, LQ8 confirms up to two answering stations simultaneously within a single-carrier 50.0 Hz transmission with a 0.0 dB RF power-splitting penalty, achieving a peak rate of 240 QSOs/h in continuous pileup (4x over single-carrier FT8; 480 QSOs/h dual-carrier) while retaining -21.0 dB SNR sensitivity. The protocol family also defines three extended profiles (LQ16, LQ4, and LQ2) tailored for extreme sensitivity, VHF/UHF contesting, and fast-burst channels.

papers.title: Seismic P- and S-wave attenuation inversion in time-frequency domain based on Kramers-Kronig relations
papers.abstract: Seismic attenuation (inverse quality factor) inversion is important for gas reservoir prediction. Two key issues in seismic attenuation inversion are the development of a physically consistent reflection coefficient equation and stable inversion of seismic attenuation from seismic data. To address these issues, this study, within the framework of isotropic linear viscoelastic media, starts from the Kramers-Kronig relations and expresses the viscoelastic stiffness matrix as a function of seismic attenuation. Under the assumptions of weak attenuation and small elastic and attenuation contrasts across the interface, a frequency-dependent PP-wave reflection coefficient equation explicitly containing P- and S-wave attenuation terms is derived using scattering theory. The derived equation not only satisfies the causality constraint but also preserves a compact mathematical form. Based on this equation, P- and S-wave attenuation are estimated by a time-frequency domain Bayesian inversion. To improve resolution and stability, the inversion adopts a recursive frequency strategy with half-power overlapping Gaussian windows, in which the result at the previous frequency serves as the prior model for the next frequency, and prior models are built from well-log rock-physics modeling to provide low-frequency constraints. Synthetic seismic data tests show that the inversion resolution and accuracy improve as the inversion frequency increases and that the method remains robust at a signal-to-noise ratio of 10 dB. Application to field seismic data further demonstrates that the P-wave attenuation anomalies effectively identify gas reservoirs, whereas S-wave attenuation is insensitive to gas reservoirs. This study provides a new approach for extracting P- and S-wave attenuation information from seismic data and achieving high-resolution prediction of gas reservoirs.

papers.title: A complete characterization of sequential testability and change detectability in i.i.d. models
papers.abstract: We give qualitative and quantitative necessary and sufficient conditions for sequential testing and change detection in an i.i.d. composite problem. A level-\(\alpha\) test with power one against every alternative exists if and only if the alternatives are separated from the null by a countable family of finite-block events. Equivalent conditions use randomized tests, bounded scores, e-processes, reduced-filtration test supermartingales, and a countable cover with positive finite-block weak-$*$ convex-hull separation. The construction gives pointwise expected sample size \(O_Q(\log(1/\alpha))\). Quantitatively, one e-process attains the intrinsic pointwise growth rate \(\Gamma(Q)\) at every alternative if and only if a countable family of bounded block bets recovers these rates. The same condition characterizes simultaneous attainment of the sharp expected-sample-size coefficient \(1/\Gamma(Q)\); arbitrary attainable lower rate profiles admit an analogous characterization. Total-variation separability of the alternatives suffices for recovery. Weak lower semicontinuity of the KL projection, in particular weak compactness of the null, also identifies \(\Gamma(Q)\) with \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathrm{KL}(Q\|P)\). The qualitative and quantitative conditions also characterize change detectability under fixed-time false-alarm bounds \(\Prob_{P^\infty}(T_\gamma\le n)\le n/\gamma\), together with ordinary ARL control. Whenever countable rate recovery holds, for any \(\eta>0\) one calibrated e-detector has robust Lorden delay asymptotic to \((\log\gamma)/\Gamma(Q)\) at finite positive rates, while satisfying the stronger optional-horizon inequality and placing every null ARL in \([\gamma,(1+\eta)\gamma+1]\). Examples exhibit a strict cost of simultaneous optimality and show that ordinary ARL alone supports neither characterization, even with finite, tightly calibrated null means.

papers.title: Comment on "Space-time shifted solitons and solution interactions for a generalized nonlocal nonlinear Schrödinger equation"
papers.abstract: Zhou and Yu [Appl. Math. Lett. 178 (2026) 109937] studied the space-time shifted NLS equation $iq_t(x,t)=q_{xx}(x,t)-2\sigma q^2(x,t) \bar{q}(x_0-x,t_0+\lambda t),\,\, \lambda=\pm 1$. They claimed that for both choices of $\lambda$ the equation is integrable. For $\lambda=-1$, however, the equation is not compatible with the standard NLS system and hence is not an integrable reduction of that system. The Hirota expansion used in the commented article does not truncate as stated; consequently the given one-soliton solution is not a solution for $\lambda=-1$. For $\lambda=1$, consistency of the shifted reduction of NLS system requires $t_0=0$ as a mandatory condition. This condition is not reported; instead $t_0$ is incorrectly treated as an arbitrary constant in the paper. The notation used in the Hirota form is misleading, and we provide a corrected form. Additionally, the equivalence between nonlocal equations with real shifts and their unshifted counterparts under translation of independent variables is clarified.

papers.title: Planetary gas gaps and kinematic signatures in the planet forming disk around WISPIT 2
Classification of abstract Bose field models
papers.abstract: We classify a class of abstract Bose field models in quantum field theory up to unitary equivalence. The class includes abstract free Bose field models, abstract van Hove--Miyatake models, and infrared-renormalized van Hove--Miyatake models. Moreover, as an application of our classification, we classify quadratic interaction models. In particular, our results answer a question of A. Arai concerning the classification of infrared-renormalized van Hove--Miyatake models.

papers.title: Joint Laws of Maximum Drawdown and Maximum Drawup for Spectrally Negative Lévy Processes
papers.abstract: Let X be a spectrally negative Lévy process observed up to an inde- pendent exponential time T with parameter {\gamma} > 0. We study the joint law of the maximum drawdown and the maximum drawup of X on [0, T ]. The path is decomposed according to the two possible orderings of its in- fimum and supremum. Conditional on the values of these extrema and on their ordering, the resulting pre-, intermediate, and post- components are independent. We identify their laws as Doob h-transforms of killed spec- trally negative Lévy processes and express the corresponding distribution functions explicitly in terms of the {\gamma}-scale functions W ({\gamma}) and Z({\gamma}) and their derivatives. Combining the conditional laws with the joint densities of the extrema yields integral representations of the joint distribution and moments.

papers.title: On the interpretation of the kinetics of ligand-receptor binding
papers.abstract: When the rates of ligand binding are measured by methods such as surface plasmon resonance, it is common practice to use the observed rate constants for the onset and offset of binding to estimate an equilibrium constant for ligand binding. If this agrees with the equilibrium constant found as the EC50 for binding at equilibrium, this is taken as validation of the measured rates. This is correct only when binding produces no conformation change in the receptor, and ligand binding follows a single exponential time course. Here, we investigate a simple 3 state model in which binding is followed by a conformation change in the receptor. Three special cases of this model in which the time course of onset and offset of ligand binding are close to being single exponentials are analysed. These cases are (1) when binding is much faster than the conformation change, (2) when the conformation change is much faster than binding, and (3) when the rates of ligand dissociation and receptor activation are both fast. It is concluded that the measured rates will often yield an estimate of the equilibrium constant for ligand binding that is close to the effective, or macroscopic, equilibrium constant, the EC50 found by measuring binding at equilibrium, which depends on both of the underlying microscopic equilibrium constants describing ligand binding and the conformation change. The exception to this conclusion is the case when binding is much faster than the subsequent conformation change, though the estimate of the equilibrium constant for ligand binding still depends on both of the underlying microscopic equilibrium constants.

papers.title: Requirements for Synthetic-Frequency Switching in Integrated Photonic Fabrics
papers.abstract: Electro-optic synthetic-frequency coupling can coherently transfer light between the frequency modes of an integrated resonator, but its value in a multiport photonic switch depends on how connections share spatial paths, frequency channels, and control signals. Here we identify two distinct architectural roles of synthetic-frequency coupling in switching fabrics and the device requirements associated with each. As a channel-assignment resource, it cannot increase the number of orthogonal channels per port, but it recovers connections blocked by fixed input frequencies or unavailable output channels. A short coupling range is sufficient. In an 8x8 fabric with eight channels per port, coupling over the first three frequency spacings achieves 95.2% of the blocking reduction of unrestricted inter-mode coupling, and the range of coupled separations matters more than the specific choice of radio-frequency tones, consistent with limited-range wavelength conversion in wavelength-division-multiplexed networks. As a spatial-switching resource, frequency control can reduce the number of spatial switching elements only through a nonseparable joint element whose spatial state is programmable for each frequency channel, whereas a separate frequency-conversion stage cannot replace missing spatial connectivity. Finally, a thin-film lithium niobate resonator model with experimentally reported coupling and decay rates, embedded in a multistage Mach-Zehnder interferometer fabric, shows that with a single shared drive the power redistributed to non-target modes and the reduced transmission of frequency-preserving paths outweigh the added connectivity. These results define the through-channel transmission, mode selectivity, and control requirements for useful synthetic-frequency switching.

papers.title: A 21-Coloring of the Plane Without Monochromatic Unit-Area Rectangles
papers.abstract: Erdős and Graham asked whether every finite coloring of the plane must contain a monochromatic rectangle of any prescribed area. Kovač gave a negative answer by constructing a $25$-coloring with no monochromatic rectangle of area $1$. We reduce the number of colors to $21$ by replacing the square cells in his construction with regular hexagons.

papers.title: Physiological Information Reliability: Contextual-Bandit Allocation of Coding Redundancy and Computation in Multimodal Cardiovascular Sensing
papers.abstract: A packet can arrive intact and still be nearly worthless. On a body-worn node the radio and processor share one small battery, yet ECG and photoplethysmography (PPG) windows differ widely in how much an estimator can recover from them. We propose Physiological Information Reliability (PIR): a hand-designed window-value proxy, PIV, built from signal quality and cross-modal heart-rate agreement, joins channel, energy and compute telemetry in one state vector, and a LinUCB bandit chooses coding redundancy and processing site. Over 25 paired seeds on a synthetic burst-erasure testbed, PIR-LinUCB used 4.3% less energy than a hand-written rule, with lower error and higher delivery. A rule that also reads PIV matches it on error and delivery but spends 3.7 mJ more per window. On five real fetal ECG recordings, PIV tracked heart-rate error better than signal quality alone (mean within-record Spearman $\rho = -0.50$ against $-0.40$). The evidence is simulated, small and non-clinical.

papers.title: Auslander correspondence for higher stable dg categories and cluster Morita theory
papers.abstract: We prove a cluster Morita theorem: every pretriangulated dg category with a $d$-cluster tilting subcategory is realized as the $d$-cluster dg category of that subcategory regarded as a connective dg category. Reversing the Amiot--Guo construction, this yields a bijection between $d$-stable dg categories and pretriangulated dg categories with a chosen $d$-cluster tilting subcategory. Our Auslander correspondence characterizes $d$-stability by coherence, weak global dimension at most $d+1$, and a $(d+1)$-shifted duality on finitely presented modules. For a locally finite $d$-stable dg algebra over a field, right $(d+1)$-Calabi--Yau structures on its perfectly valued derived dg category correspond bijectively to right $d$-Calabi--Yau structures on its $d$-cluster dg category. In characteristic zero, this removes the pseudo-compact enhancement hypothesis from Keller--Liu's theorem on Amiot's conjecture. Via Koszul duality, we characterize $d$-stability over any field for locally finite minimal completed dg path algebras (and their analogues for graded species) by explicit conditions on the graded arrows and the quadratic differential. For $d=1$, these are deformed derived mesh algebras of Dynkin type; for $d=2$, they are complete twisted Ginzburg dg algebras, yielding via cluster Morita theory a twisted analogue of Amiot's conjecture in arbitrary characteristic without a Calabi--Yau hypothesis.

papers.title: Derivation of a linearly elastic elliptic membrane shell theory in the framework of magnetoelasticity
papers.abstract: Starting from a three-dimensional model of linearized magnetoelasticity, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of a thin shell as its thickness approaches zero. Our analysis focuses on a family of linearly elastic elliptic membrane shells. Using $\Gamma$-convergence, we rigorously derive a two-dimensional linear magnetoelastic shell model and establish its relationship to the original three-dimensional model in terms of the convergence of minimizers.

papers.title: Sturm--Liouville-Type Parity and Oscillation of a Cubic Spline Eigenbasis
papers.abstract: We study the eigen-structure of the kernel matrix arising from cubic smoothing splines on equally spaced knots. Using matrix-theoretic methods, we show that its positive eigenvalues are simple, that the associated eigenvectors alternate between even and odd, and that the eigenvector for the $k$th largest positive eigenvalue has exactly $k+1$ sign changes.
