Building on established results on oscillatory and centrosymmetric matrices, we provide a more explicit proof of the known oscillation property of the eigenvectors and establish their alternating parity. We then verify, by a separate argument, that both properties extend to the associated continuous cubic spline eigenfunctions, showing that the resulting spline basis exhibits both an alternating parity structure and an oscillation pattern analogous to that of classical Sturm--Liouville eigenfunctions.

papers.title: Evaluating LLM-based AI agents integrated with materials synthesis tools: the case of atomic layer deposition
Strangeness, entropy, and chemical non-equilibrium from p+p to Pb+Pb: the $K^+/π^+$ horn on the system-size axis
papers.abstract: The maximum ("horn") of the $\langle K^+\rangle/\langle\pi^+\rangle$ excitation function in central Pb+Pb collisions near $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 7.6$ GeV is interpreted as the competition between strangeness production and the faster rise of entropy production at the onset of deconfinement. Statistical hadronization analyses by Letessier, Rafelski, and collaborators have shown that the horn is described quantitatively only if the light-quark phase-space occupancy $\gamma_q$ is free, with $\gamma_q$ near the pion condensation limit from 30$A$ GeV upward. We carry this analysis along the system-size axis provided by NA61/SHINE (p+p, Be+Be, Ar+Sc, preliminary Xe+La) and NA49 (Pb+Pb). Our main new result is the first non-equilibrium analysis, to our knowledge, of the Be+Be and Ar+Sc $4\pi$ multiplicities, published in 2021 and 2024: in Ar+Sc, chemical equilibrium of light quarks ($\gamma_q = 1$) is disfavored, but through the $K^+/K^-$ asymmetry rather than the pion yields, while the Be+Be data do not discriminate. For central Pb+Pb, our fits to the final NA49 data confirm the earlier result, most robustly at 30$A$-80$A$ GeV; the preference rests on the excess of produced hadrons per net baryon and on the Bose-Einstein enhancement of pions. Decomposing $\langle K^+\rangle/\langle\pi^+\rangle$ into strangeness and pion yields per wounded nucleon, we find that the step between Be+Be and Ar+Sc is carried by a doubling of strangeness per participant, whereas the horn appears only in Pb+Pb, where the pion yield per participant is suppressed at 20$A$-40$A$ GeV. Parton-hadron transport (PHSD) reproduces the Pb+Pb horn but predicts one also in Ar+Sc and Xe+La, where none is observed.

papers.title: Formation of black hole stars via star--black hole collisions
Dynamical formation of high-eccentricity compact binaries through BH--BH*/TZO collisions
Cycle Counting and Character Expectations Using Alternating Structures
papers.abstract: Recently, three related papers [ arXiv:2412.13941 , arXiv:2009.00897 , arXiv:2409.03626 ] found a connection between two subjects: the w-cycle theorem, which is a theorem about counting appearances of cycles reading out a word w in certain graphs, and character expectations on word measures. The w-cycle theorem was proven independently by [ arXiv:1410.2540 ] using stackings and by [ arXiv:1410.2579 ] using bislim structures. In the current work, we generalize stackings and bislim structures to alternating stackings and alternating bislim structures. We show how this significantly strengthens the w-cycle theorem for words admitting such alternating structures, and as a result, also strengthens the recent results of [ arXiv:2412.13941 ] and [ arXiv:2409.03626 ]. We show that generic words admit alternating bislim structures, and therefore, the strengthened results hold for generic words. Using our new machinery, we address conjectures of Wilton, of Hanany--Puder and of Puder--Shomroni. We prove that all three conjectures hold for generic words, but we also find counterexamples for the first two.

papers.title: Orbits of submaximal dimension for Sylow $p$-subgroups of finite classical orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup in a classical orthogonal group over a finite field with $q$ elements of characteristic $p$ large enough. The coadjoint orbits of the group $U$ play the key role in the description of irreducible complex characters of $U$. In the paper, we provide a classification of such orbits of pre-maximal dimension. As a corollary, we compute the number of all orbits mentioned above. It turned out that each of these numbers is a polynomial in $q - 1$ with integer non-negative coefficients, which agrees with the Isaacs' conjecture.

papers.title: Exact pair density wave in topological moire flat bands and universal superfluid stiffness
Probing Dirac Dark Matter in Composite Higgs Models with Xenon and Argon targets
Approximating thermodynamic equilibrium observables of quasi one-dimensional magnetic molecules and chains by thermal DMRG - a user perspective
Time-Window Noise2Noise: Self-Supervised Blind Denoising of Mechanical Vibration and Impact Signals
papers.abstract: Vibration and impact measurements in mechanical systems are invariably corrupted by noise, which degrades every quantity derived from them, such as modal parameters and contact forces. Classical filters rely on assumptions about the noise or the signal, and linear filters cannot remove the noise that shares the frequency band of the structural response. This work presents Time-Window Noise2Noise (TWN2N), a self-supervised method for blind denoising of signals produced by deterministic mechanical systems. The method requires neither a clean reference signal nor paired noisy observations, nor a measured noise variance or distribution: by reconstructing each time instant from its temporal neighborhood while masking the instant itself, a compact autoencoder-based network is encouraged to exploit the coherent temporal and multichannel structure of the measurement rather than the noise. The formulation requires no model of the system and is assessed on two benchmarks with exactly known ground truth: the impulse response of a linear 3-degree-of-freedom system and a nonlinear Hunt-Crossley impact. Over repeated realizations, TWN2N exceeds a zero-phase low-pass filter at low and moderate input signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and gives the largest gain inside the structural band, which a linear filter largely preserves, among the Savitzky-Golay and wavelet references; the advantage vanishes at high input SNR and under brown noise. The benefit propagates to identification: the damping ratio of the weakest mode, overestimated several-fold on the raw signals, is recovered close to its reference value after denoising.

papers.title: Geometric Propulsion of a Scallop with Control-Dependent Hydrodynamics
Direct, Collision-Operator-Free Simulation of Electron-Ion Transport in Magnetized and Unmagnetized Plasmas
papers.abstract: Accurate electron-ion collision models are central to predicting transport in fusion and space plasmas, yet collision operators and Monte Carlo collision models assume that a charged particle meets one partner at a time and that its successive encounters are independent. However, an electron that turns back along the magnetic field passes the same ions again. We solve the Newton-Lorentz equations for test electrons among static ions with a prescribed Debye-screened potential. The method combines force summation within an interaction radius, a time-symmetric particle pusher, and adaptive time stepping, enabling stable and scalable simulations in unmagnetized and magnetized plasmas. Using simulation-based measures of momentum relaxation and cross-field diffusion, we compare the simulations with a reference in the same model that treats every encounter as independent. Without a magnetic field the scattering rate reproduces the binary-collision rate for the same potential to within 2%. When the gyroradius is smaller than the Debye length, the scattering rate stays within 10% of the reference, but the cross-field diffusion coefficient exceeds it by a factor that grows with the field, up to 17. The excess comes from repeated passes of the same ions, whose guiding-center displacements add up: when the ions are replaced by new random ones many times per scattering time, so that a returning electron meets different ions, most of the excess disappears. The framework therefore provides a computational benchmark for testing and improving reduced collision operators and transport models.

papers.title: Native-Space 3D CarveMix for Multi-Site T1w Stroke Segmentation
papers.abstract: Segmenting ischemic stroke lesions on T1-weighted (T1w) MRI acquired across different scanners and protocols without intensity standardization is difficult because lesions are subtle and share intensity characteristics with cerebrospinal fluid. Standard deep learning architectures trained across multiple centers plateau around Dice 0.66, with acute lesions ($\le 7$ days post-stroke) performing substantially worse due to severe sample scarcity. We combine a MedNeXt-L ($k=5$) backbone with on-the-fly 3D CarveMix augmentation that pastes real lesion patches into recipient training patches. By generating synthetic lesion placements dynamically within each fold with subject-level split isolation, the model sees more diverse lesion patterns without requiring pre-generated copies on disk. We evaluate on 1,453 native T1w scans from 55 clinical centers in the ISLES 2026 challenge. MedNeXt-L with CarveMix achieved a mean five-fold cross-validation Dice of 0.648 after 500 epochs. For comparison, the estimated Dice for plain MedNeXt-L at epoch 500 was 0.630, obtained by interpolation from its 1,000-epoch training trajectory.

papers.title: Brans Dicke scalar-tensor gravity and unimodular FRW cosmology with Coleman-Weinberg potential
Pinchoff by surface diffusion
papers.abstract: Since Nichols and Mullins analysed the instability of cylindrical wires in 1965, numerical and asymptotic studies have predicted a self-similar neck at pinchoff under surface diffusion. Yet even the existence of a finite-time singularity for the flow of a smooth closed surface has remained open. We construct the first such examples, and establish their stability, modulo a finite-dimensional space. The same shrinking neck closes the central hole of an embedded torus in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and separates the lobes of a genus-zero dumbbell. In both cases the surface remains embedded until the singular time $T$ and converges smoothly away from the pinching point. Writing $A(t)$ for the waist radius and $r(z,t)$ for the radius near the neck, we prove that $A(t)=\{4\mu(T-t)\}^{1/4}(1+o(1)), \quad A(t)^{-1}r(A(t)\zeta,t) \longrightarrow U(\zeta) \quad\text{in }C^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}).$ The profile $U$ above is also for the first time rigorously constructed here. It was numerically computed by Wong-Miksis-Voorhees-Davis, and identified by Bernoff-Bertozzi-Witelski as the ground state of a family of conical shrinkers. Our proof also yields a general compactification and stability criterion for fourth-order geometric flows that admit positive symmetric conical shrinkers.

papers.title: Polynomial permutation stability, soficity, and universal polynomial groups
papers.abstract: We introduce polynomial permutation stability for maps between groups, extending ordinary permutation stability from homomorphisms to polynomial maps defined by iterated finite differences. We show that a group $G$ is polynomially permutation stable in degree $s$ if and only if its universal polynomial group $\operatorname{Pol}_s(G)$ is permutation stable. While every finite group is polynomially permutation stable in degree two, we prove that the cyclic group of order six is not stable in degree three. More precisely, we construct a finite-index direct-product subgroup of $\operatorname{Pol}_3(C_6)$ to which an instability theorem of Ioana applies. We also show that polynomial sofic approximations characterize the usual class of sofic groups. In degree two, we obtain a split exact sequence relating $\operatorname{Pol}_2(G)$ to a restricted wreath product, with applications to soficity and property $(T)$. A quotient-transfer principle yields infinite, finitely presented, nonperfect groups that are polynomially permutation stable in every degree. Finally, we obtain nonamenability and largeness results for higher-degree universal polynomial groups of finite groups.

papers.title: Fujiki Class $\mathcal C$ Varieties and a Kähler Criterion
papers.abstract: In this article, we show that flips and divisorial contractions preserve the Kähler condition (for strongly $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial compact Kähler generalized klt pairs with $B+\beta_X$ big), and we give a criterion for varieties in Fujiki's class $\mathcal C$ to be Kähler. We also prove the existence of small $\mathbb Q$-factorializations for generalized klt pairs and of dlt modifications for generalized pairs.

papers.title: Exact Algebraic Computation of Learning Coefficients for Two-Dimensional Singular Models
papers.abstract: Classical information criteria such as the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) rely on regularity assumptions that break down for singular models, leading to incorrect model selection in settings such as deep learning. The Widely Applicable Bayesian Information Criterion (WBIC) relies on local learning coefficients $\lambda$, which in the analytic case coincides with local Real Log Canonical Thresholds (RLCT) of the Kullback-Leibler divergence of the model, to capture correct marginal likelihood asymptotics. Exact computation of the learning coefficients has been limited to special cases, and only sampling-based estimation methods are generally applicable. We present the first deterministic algorithm that computes local RLCTs exactly for any two-dimensional model whose Kullback-Leibler distance is contact equivalent to a polynomial, derive a bound on its complexity, and demonstrate its effectiveness for a broad class of models, with applications including polynomial neural networks. Beyond providing ground truth to calibrate sampling-based estimators, exact computation reveals algebraic structure in learning coefficients that sampling cannot and out-speeds it in the shallow regime.

papers.title: Geometry-Encoded Multireceiver Fluorometry Affords Full-Range Nonlinear Quantification under the Primary Inner Filter Effect
papers.abstract: The inner filter effect (IFE) transforms the nominally linear fluorescence-concentration relationship into a geometry-dependent and often nonmonotonic response, resulting in reduced sensitivity, concentration ambiguity, and inaccurate underestimation at high optical densities. Here, we introduce a spatially encoded multireceiver fluorometric strategy that does not eliminate or correct the IFE, but instead harnesses the spatial fluorescence attenuation induced by IFE as an additional quantitative encoding dimension. Fluorescence generated along the excitation axis is integrated over independently positioned receiver windows, and concentration is recovered by nonlinear optimization of the joint fluorescent intensity vector. Tryptophan was selected as a biomedically relevant model fluorophore to validate the proposed strategy. Single-window calibration exhibited vanishing-gradient boundary and two-valued concentration inversions, whereas two spatially separated receiver windows restored global identifiability across the full concentration range. Screening of 35 two-receiver geometries identified the minimum-uncertainty configuration, achieving an average 95% error half-width of mean E_95= 0.884 mg/L, and the maximum-sensitivity configuration, reaching a noise-normalized response sensitivity of mean S_N=3.832 a.u./(mg/L). By converting spatial attenuation into a multidimensional concentration coordinate, this approach extends quantitative fluorescence analysis without dilution, a separate absorbance measurement, or piecewise calibration and provides a general metrology framework for fluorescence metrology even under strong IFE conditions.

papers.title: 3D trapping of a meta-atom in an intensity minimum
papers.abstract: High-refractive-index particles have recently attracted a growing interest in optical manipulation, enabling to engineer optical forces through electromagnetic Mie resonances. Unlike standard silica particles, which exhibit trap frequencies mainly determined by material density, resonant meta-atoms formed by high-index particles enable qualitatively new trapping behaviors. In this work, we experimentally investigate the trapping of resonant silicon particles in an optical standing wave. A direct comparison of silicon and silica highlights the fundamental differences in their optical force scaling and trapping dynamics. Beyond conventional trapping at intensity-maxima, we demonstrate deterministic and stable three-dimensional trapping of silicon nanoparticles in optical intensity minima, a regime that remains inaccessible for silica particles. Drawing a mesoscopic analogy with blue-detuned atom trapping, our results establish meta-atoms as a versatile approach to further extend the optical manipulation tool box towards accessing novel trapping regimes e.g. in close proximity to a surface.

papers.title: Entrywise Positivity Preservers on Green Matrices
papers.abstract: We classify entrywise functions preserving positive semidefiniteness on Green matrices with positive parameters. For each fixed \(n\ge2\), PSD preservation is equivalent to \(f\) being nondecreasing and \((f(tr^{i+j}))_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) being PSD for all \(t>0,r>1\). For \(f\in C^{2n-2}\), this is equivalent to \(f'\ge0\) and positive semidefiniteness of \(((t\,d/dt)^{i+j}f(t))_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) at every positive \(t\). These fixed-order classes strictly decrease with \(n\); their intersection consists exactly of \(f(t)=\int_{[0,\infty)}t^\alpha\,d\mu(\alpha)\), where \(\mu\) is a finite positive measure and the integral is finite for every \(t>0\). At each fixed order, entrywise Loewner monotonicity is equivalent to \(f\in C^1\) and \(f'\) belonging to the corresponding PSD preserver class. In all orders, monotonicity itself implies smoothness. Nonnegative minors of orders one and two on every strict three-by-three Green input already force \(f\equiv0\) or \(f(t)=ct^\alpha\), with \(c>0\) and \(\alpha\ge0\). They give TN output in every order; the nonzero members also preserve PSD Green structure. We also classify PSD, TN, and Loewner-monotone extensions to the closure allowing zero entries. No regularity is assumed except in the differential criterion.

papers.title: High-Harmonicity Planar Penning Traps for Single-Electron Qubits
papers.abstract: We present a detailed account of the design choices required for planar Penning traps that feature a highly harmonic confining potential. High harmonicity is indispensable for a number of applications, particularly for confinement of single electrons as qubits in quantum-information processing. The present work extends previous studies [J. Goldman and G. Gabrielse, Phys. Rev. A 81, 052335 (2010)] by a fully analytic treatment of finite electrode gaps and their relevance for small traps on the millimeter size scale and below, when relative gap sizes are non-negligible. We derive the overall trap potential with a particular focus on different models of finite-gap potentials and show how to find the optimum trap geometry and electrode voltages to minimize anharmonicities. The analytic calculations are compared with detailed finite-element simulations.

papers.title: Removability criterion for radiative corrections to the Starobinsky attractor in weakly nonlocal gravity
Boundary Layers and Finite-Section Asymptotics for Small Polygons
papers.abstract: In large even polygons of unit diameter, computed angle profiles oscillate near the vertex carrying the pendant diameter. We study the half-line variational problem behind this observation of Bingane and Mossinghoff. Its unique positive equilibrium approaches the regular state with alternating multiplier $(-3+\sqrt5)/2$. We determine the sharp energy errors for two ways of closing a finite section and enclose the limiting cubic coefficient in a rational interval of width below $9.4\times10^{-29}$. An explicit scaling identifies these energies with the cubic coefficients of the finite polygon constructions. Transferring the profile to unrestricted area maximizers is a further, conditional result: under the stated geometric hypothesis, the profile gives the $n^{-3}$ term of their maximal area. The recurrence, its finite-section estimates and the enclosure can be checked independently of that hypothesis.

papers.title: Social Learning with Selective Sampling
papers.abstract: This paper studies social learning when some types of actions are more likely to be sampled by successors than others. We show that Bayesian agents can achieve learning even without expanding observations, because the endogenous observation network itself carries information and agents can correct for selection bias. For nonanonymous sampling, we establish sufficient and pairwise necessary conditions of the sampling procedure for learning, which coincide in the binary state-matching model to yield an exact characterization. We also show that stationary anonymous sampling permits asymptotic learning, as agents can correct for selection bias using inverse-probability weighting. Finally, we demonstrate that asymptotic learning can fail under arbitrarily small misspecification of the sampling procedure.

papers.title: Reference-free logged energy-oracle recovery for neural approximations of symmetric coercive variational problems: conforming Riesz reconstruction and archive-level selection
papers.abstract: Neural PDE training yields a finite checkpoint archive, yet its logged energy errors are inaccessible without the exact solution, while loss-based selection does not necessarily recover the logged energy oracle. For admissible neural approximations of symmetric coercive variational problems, we introduce a reference-free selection rule based on minimizing a computable conforming Riesz monitor. The exact residual-energy identity and conforming projection make the monitor an unconditional lower bound converging monotonically to each logged energy error under nested conforming refinement; under saturation, hierarchical enrichment yields a computable upper estimate and hence a lower-upper bracket. A key finding is that archive selection is order-sensitive: unresolved checkpoint-dependent components can reverse the oracle-non-oracle ranking at finite resolution, so checkpointwise recovery alone is insufficient. For finite archives, we prove uniform recovery, yielding convergence to the logged-oracle error and, without saturation, logged-oracle selection at sufficiently fine auxiliary resolution. Under saturation, the bracket gives a computable near-oracle bound and certifies unique logged-oracle selection upon interval separation. We also bound logging-resolution loss and certify oracle inclusion over prescribed comparison trajectories. Experiments on diffusion and elasticity, including a non-manufactured perforated plate, demonstrate energy-scale calibration, oracle-level selection, and modest post-processing cost. This work frames neural checkpoint selection as an ordering problem, establishes projection-based reliability guarantees beyond checkpointwise error estimation and loss-error equivalence, and opens directions for variational loss design and more general selection theory.

papers.title: History-Dependent Mode Selection in a Driven Holographic Superfluid
papers.abstract: We study finite-rate mode selection among competing Landau-unstable modes in a holographic superfluid. The first mode to reach a prescribed amplitude need not be the instantaneously fastest-growing one. Time-dependent linear evolution on the driven homogeneous background closely reproduces the modal amplitudes obtained from full bulk evolution. Protocols with identical present driving conditions can reverse the relative ordering of two modes. For the controlled histories studied here, the change in their logarithmic amplitude ratio is well approximated by the excess accumulated differential QNM gain.

papers.title: Micromotion and topological constraints on Floquet-state quantum geometry
Comeager hereditary families of compact sets are big
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Polish space and let $\mathcal K(X)$ be its Vietoris hyperspace. A family $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal K(X)$ is hereditary if it is downward closed under inclusion. Matheron and Zelený asked whether every comeager hereditary family in $\mathcal K(X)$ contains a dense hereditary $G_\delta$ subfamily. We give an affirmative answer in ZFC.

papers.title: Equivariant learning of a transferable three-dimensional classical density functional
Portfolio Choice of Spouses with Heterogeneous Risk Preferences over Shared Household Consumption
papers.abstract: A number of recent empirical papers rely on a collective model to analyze the portfolio choice of spouses, their heterogeneous risk preferences, and intra-household bargaining. I show that although Pareto-Efficient, this approach generates a counterintuitive result with constant Pareto weights: an increase in the risk aversion of a household member can lead to an increase in household risk-taking. Moreover, household wealth affects the preferred risky portfolio share even under CRRA preferences and can make the household insensitive to preferences of a spouse. I offer an alternative approach based on the concept of risk premia and show that it always generates a Pareto-efficient and monotonic household level solution. I derive an intuitive normalization to the Pareto weights in the collective model which generates an approximately equivalent solution. Finally, I discuss multiplicative aggregation of utilities previously used in this literature and show that it is also approximately equivalent to the suggested approach.

papers.title: Satellite Infrastructure Sharing: Orbit-Structured Stochastic Geometry Modeling and Connectivity Analysis in Heterogeneous Satellite Networks
papers.abstract: This paper develops an analytical framework to evaluate the feasibility and performance of satellite infrastructure sharing among multiple low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite operators. Motivated by the growing demand for universal connectivity under limited satellite resources, the proposed model captures uncoordinated deployments where independently operated constellations coexist without predefined orbital agreements. To describe such heterogeneous configurations, the spherical Cox point process is employed to jointly generate orbital structures and satellites. Then, each satellite is further assigned a random communication range, reflecting variations in coverage capability across operators. The overall coverage region is modeled through a spherical Cox-Boolean model that captures the spatial overlap of individual satellite spherical footprints on Earth. Using the proposed framework, the feasibility and benefits of satellite infrastructure sharing are mathematically analyzed, and closed-form expressions are derived for key performance metrics such as the connection probability, connection number, and downlink signal characteristics including the nearest serving distance, total received signal power, and the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) distribution in the interference-limited regime. The analytical results, validated through system-level simulations, provide a tractable characterization of how orbital geometry governs coverage, connectivity, and interference, and reveal the inherent trade-offs induced by coverage overlap in heterogeneous satellite constellations.

papers.title: Random close packing at extreme size ratios with an Adam-based inflation protocol
False-vacuum bubbles in sphaleron scattering
papers.abstract: We investigate the collision dynamics of two bright sphalerons in a (1+1)-dimensional deformed $\phi^6$ scalar field theory with a symmetric potential possessing false vacua. Two one-parameter realizations of the model, referred to as the barrier and well models, are considered and their static and linear instability properties are first reviewed. We then study head-on collisions of boosted sphalerons over a broad range of initial velocities and deformation parameters. The scattering dynamics exhibit a rich variety of final states, including the production of kink-antikink pairs, long-lived oscillons in true and false vacuum, multiple oscillons propagating in false-vacuum regions, and radiative decay. A particularly remarkable outcome is the emergence of a long-lived bubble of the false broken vacuum bounded by a kink-antikink pair, which repeatedly collapses and re-expands before eventually decaying into an oscillon. These results demonstrate that deformed $\phi^6$ theories with false vacua exhibit considerably richer sphaleron dynamics than previously known and provide new insight into the role of unstable localized configurations in nonlinear field theories.

papers.title: Spin-coherent quantum designs
papers.abstract: Coherent states bridge the gap between quantum and classical physics, but their overcomplete and nonorthogonal nature makes it difficult to identify finite sets that represent spin observables exactly. Finite spin-coherent tomography and discrete coherent-state operator bases already exist. Here we address a more specific problem: preserving the canonical contravariant-symbol representation. For a spin-$J$ system, the canonical finite coherent-state formula reconstructs every operator in the rank-$S$ irreducible tensor sector exactly if and only if the sampling directions form a spherical $(2J+S)$-design and the corresponding coherent-state projectors then form a spin-coherent quantum design. We also give an explicit Gauss-Legendre construction which leads to weighted spherical designs. These results provide a systematic way to determine spin-operator moments from finite coherent-state POVMs without full state tomography, with practical protocols for polarimetry and magnetometry. Presented construction can be extended to other compact symmetry groups.

papers.title: Quantum Theory of Third-harmonic Generation in Epsilon-Near-Zero Materials
papers.abstract: We present a theoretical framework, based on the Green's tensor quantisation method, to describe third-harmonic generation in epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) materials and derive analytical, closed-form solutions for the generation efficiency. We validate our model against experimental measurements of wavelength- and angle-resolved third-harmonic generation efficiency from 30 nm-thin ITO nano layers at low pump intensity, described under the undeleted pump approximation. Our results provide a local and scalar model for quantum nonlinear processes in dispersive and lossy ENZ media, and establishes a simple and reliable framework for investigating a variety of nonlinear optical phenomena with applications to quantum sensing, quantum information, and quantum non demolition measurements.

papers.title: An asymptotic Liouville-type theorem for systems of Lane-Emden equations on RCD*(-K,N) spaces via gradient estimates
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish elliptic gradient estimates for positive solutions of the Lane-Emden system on metric measure spaces satisfying the synthetic Ricci curvature-dimension condition $\mathrm{RCD}^*(-K,N)$. Our approach combines the weak differential calculus and the Bochner inequality available in the $\mathrm{RCD}^*(-K,N)$ setting with suitable auxiliary function arguments, extending classical gradient estimate techniques to nonsmooth spaces. The resulting estimate is valid for all exponents $\alpha,\beta>0$ and all $N\in[1,\infty)$, with no dimensional case distinction and with explicit constants. As an application, we prove a quantitative, asymptotic Liouville-type theorem on $\mathrm{RCD}^*(0,N)$ spaces: for positive solutions that are bounded above and below by fixed positive constants, the normalized gradients $|\nabla f|/f$ and $|\nabla h|/h$ are bounded by a quantity that is of order $\max\{\alpha,\beta\}$ and hence tends to zero as the exponents tend to zero (with comparable size). We also explain why the method gives no rigidity for large exponents, which is consistent with, but does not prove, the existence of nonconstant solutions there. These results generalize corresponding results from the smooth Riemannian setting and contribute to the study of nonlinear elliptic systems on spaces with synthetic Ricci curvature lower bounds.

papers.title: Resolving the Gibbs Paradox through Local Free Space and Collision Potential
Autonomous Optimization of Complex Oxides for Thermochemical Fuel Production
Newton's Second Law: A Structural Necessity of Mechanics Constrained by Excluded Perpetual Motion and Universal Free Fall
papers.abstract: For over three centuries, Newton's second law (F = ma) has governed mechanics with extraordinary success, while its epistemic warrant has remained empirical. That merely empirical contingency vanishes once mechanics is constrained by two principles: the principle of excluded perpetual motion (PEPM) with its pre-Newtonian phenomenological content and the weak equivalence principle (WEP) with universal free fall as its primitive content. The PEPM secures the applicability of Suppes' measurement-theoretic framework to gravitational mass and force, exposing the formal structure latent in their empirical manifestations and establishing both as independent primitives. Gravity bridges statics and kinematics in Stevin's and Galileo's inclined-plane arguments, where the common sine factor in force and acceleration cancels in F/a. Cycle arguments under the PEPM extend this result to arbitrary force mechanisms, establishing F/a as object-intrinsic and securing inertial mass as a well-defined physical quantity. Further constrained by universal free fall, the resulting quantitative structure compels the equivalence of inertial and gravitational mass, with Newton's second law as the operational expression of that equivalence. Direct implications include constraints on modified-inertia MOND that follow from the PEPM alone. The PEPM also places free-fall and torsion-balance experiments on equal footing as tests of the WEP. Together with the WEP, the derivation further grounds both the dimensional reduction of mechanics and the location-invariance of the Kibble-balance realization of the SI kilogram. Deeper still, Newton's second law derives its necessity from exclusion and invariance principles whose scope extends beyond mechanics itself.

papers.title: Hypothesis Testing with Conditional Queries: Learnability and the Value of Interaction
papers.abstract: Model evaluations may fix all tests before observing any responses or select later tests using earlier responses. We study this choice in a conditional-query model on a finite outcome space $\mathcal{X}$ with $|\mathcal{X}|=N$. We first ask which pairs of distribution classes can be reliably distinguished. We then ask how many additional queries are required to match an adaptive tester when all queried events must be fixed in advance. We show that learnability holds if and only if the two classes have positive separation in their pairwise conditional probabilities. When this separation is zero, the optimal worst-case error is exactly $1/2$ at every finite query budget. For any $T$-query adaptive policy and any $\rho \in (0,1)$, we construct a randomized non-adaptive procedure using $O(N^2(T + \log(1/\rho)))$ pair queries chosen before any response is observed. Its simulated transcript is within $\rho$ in total variation of the adaptive transcript, uniformly over all distributions in the model. We also construct a matching family with constant adaptive query complexity and $\Omega_\varepsilon(N^2)$ non-adaptive query complexity. Consequently, the worst-case fixed-error adaptivity gap is $\Theta_\varepsilon(N^2)$. Thus interaction can reduce the required number of tests by a quadratic factor, but the apparent exponential branching of an interactive evaluation does not yield an exponential query advantage.

papers.title: Rotational spectra and de-perturbation analysis for ground state ytterbium oxide, YbO
papers.abstract: A combination difference analysis of Fourier transform microwave spectroscopy (FTMW) measurements of $^{174}$YbO combined with earlier near-infrared chemiluminescence data have resulted in much improved YbO rotational and centrifugal distortion constants. These have been confirmed in a multi-isotopologue analysis of further FTMW measurements of $^{172}$YbO and $^{176}$YbO and an analysis of nuclear-size-dependent Born-Oppenheimer breakdown effects in the molecule. Multiple excited electronic states overlap with low-lying excited vibrational levels of the electronic ground state leading to irregularities in its vibrational spacings and other previously observed electronic manifolds. This has been modeled with a matrix of the vibrational levels of the ground and multiple interacting states assuming Morse potentials and including electronic Hamiltonian matrix elements mixing the states. Vibrational level overlaps were calculated numerically assuming Morse vibrational wavefunctions. The resulting de-perturbed potentials for the states inform continuing experimental and theoretical work on this and other ytterbium-containing molecules.

papers.title: Topological Charge-Transfer Excitons
Equivalence of mapping gravitational wave background anisotropy across bases at equal information content
The Loss Does Not See the Basis, but Adam Does
papers.abstract: Different optimization algorithms can find very different solutions to the same problem. Gradient descent (GD) exhibits a low-rank bias in overparameterized problems when initialized near zero, while Adam does not. GD is rotationally equivariant: rotating both factors of a factored model $W = UV^\top$ by an orthogonal matrix leaves the loss unchanged, and GD's solution rotates accordingly. In contrast, Adam is not. We show that any algorithm using only the current gradient and respecting rotational symmetry amounts to a left-preconditioner depending only on the gradient's Gram matrix. This gives a norm-based test, which passes for the spectral norm in Muon and fails for Adam's $\ell_\infty$ norm. Empirically, nine optimizers fall into groups consistent with the test on underdetermined matrix sensing. Sharing Adam's second moment across coordinates gradually recovers a low-rank bias, and its solutions approach GD's as the stepsize decreases. On four hyperspectral scenes, Adam's solutions are hundreds to thousands of times further from GD's than two GD runs with different step sizes are from each other. In transformers and LoRA adapters, Adam separates two rotationally equivalent models from the first iteration, and learns higher-rank attention updates. Overall, recovering particular solutions depends on the optimizer's invisible coordinate basis, as well as how fast it grows small singular values relative to large ones.

papers.title: Dirichlet symbols and the nonlinear wave equation
papers.abstract: We develop the geometry of conformal mappings through Dirichlet operator symbols and the nonlinear wave equation. These symbols, introduced in the work of Hedenmalm and Shimorin (2020), are holomorphic functions on the bidisk associated with contractions on $L^2(\mathbb{D})$. For Grunsky operators, the nonlinear wave equation and the related Riccati equation induce a hierarchy of of differential relations along the diagonal. We use this jet hierachy to obtain alternative coordinates and a characterization of the manifold $\Sigma/\mathbb{C}$ of normalized exterior univalent functions modulo translations, without an explicit univalence test. This manifold may be viewed as an extension of the universal Teichmüller space beyond the quasicircle boundary setting. The diagonal jets also give rise to a hierarchy of \emph{diagonal series Schwarzian derivatives}. Already the fourth Schwarzian $S_4(\psi)$ leads to differential equations connected with the Weierstrass elliptic $\wp$ function and Painlevé I, revealing a comparison between the geometry of conformal mappings and that of complex tori. As a quantitative application of the framework, we interpret asymptotic variance through the Littlewood-Paley formula as an asymptotic density of quadratic nonlinearity energy under logarithmic averaging. We introduce Schwarzian asymptotic variance and obtain the lower bound $5.686\ldots$ and the upper bound $12.566\ldots$ for its averaged squared hyperbolically normalized amplitude, in comparison with the classical pointwise bound $36$. Note that the lower bound shows that the Nehari sufficient squared bound $4$ does not hold on average.

papers.title: A note on some upper bounds for the Frobenius norm of the $q$-deformed commutator
papers.abstract: For two square complex matrices $A,B,$ and a real number $q$, the $q$-deformed commutator of $A$ and $B$ is defined as $AB-qBA$. We give some upper bounds on the Frobenius norm of the $q$-deformed commutator in the case $q\ge0$. All of the inequalities derived in this paper generalize the Böttcher-Wenzel inequality.

papers.title: Fidelity-Based Robustness Margins for Quantum Control
papers.abstract: We develop certified lower bounds on structure-specific fidelity-threshold robustness margins for finite-dimensional closed quantum systems under piecewise-constant coherent control. A scalar physical parameter may perturb the drift, a control Hamiltonian, or another declared Hamiltonian component across the control horizon. A differential sensitivity bound for the trace-amplitude gate fidelity yields a threshold-dependent Lipschitz constant on the nominal connected safe parameter component and hence a certified finite perturbation radius. Recentering this certificate produces an iterative one-dimensional method whose finite runs return lower bounds on the distance to the first threshold contact. The fidelity may touch the threshold without falling below it. A three-qubit gate-control example shows that the returned bounds vary by up to a factor of three across controllers of comparable nominal fidelity and contain structure-dependent information not captured by nominal differential sensitivity alone.

papers.title: Modified Expansion and the JWST CMB Optical Depth Tension in Cosmology inspired by Self-Interaction Gravity
The One-Loop Power Spectrum of Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measures
Proper-Score Observation-Driven Filters: Tracking Efficiency, Estimation, and Continuous-Time Limits
papers.abstract: Observation-driven filters usually update a time-varying parameter with the score of the predictive log density. Replacing the logarithmic score by another proper scoring rule changes both the target the filter tracks and the precision with which it tracks it. These filters form a subclass of the PRADA models of de Punder (2026), and we study their properties at the level of the filtered path. In an in-fill framework, the local tracking error is an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process. Optimised over the gain, its invariant variance is the geometric mean of the target's volatility and an effective observation noise determined by the scoring rule. Tracking efficiency is the squared correlation between the scoring-rule driver and the true score at the rule's own target. In scale models it equals the asymptotic relative efficiency of the corresponding static minimum-score estimator. The resulting frontier quantifies the robustness--efficiency trade-off. Under Gaussian innovations, density-power and CRPS volatility filters raise minimal tracking risk by 3% and 11%. Under Student-$t_5$ innovations, the Gaussian log-score filter raises it by 58% in the limit, and by more at daily frequency. We also give primitive conditions for bounded scale-invariant drivers, a matrix version, a population self-tuning result for the gain, minimum-score estimation theory whose invertibility conditions hold at the fitted values, and diffusion limits. An international equity application separates the roles of the predictive density and the scoring rule.

papers.title: Nanohertz Loss in a Pendulum for Macroscopic Entanglement under Structural Damping
papers.abstract: Pendulums are attractive for macroscopic quantum control because gravitational dissipation dilution lowers the modal loss, while the $1/f$ force noise of structural damping allows nearly lossless trapping to suppress the noise at an upshifted resonance. The same $1/f$ spectrum, however, produces a low-frequency tail that penalizes entanglement. To overcome this penalty, we realize a 7-mg pendulum suspended by a stepped fused-silica fiber. Ring-down measurements give an energy-decay rate $\Gamma/2\pi=361(39)$ nHz at the bare resonance $\omega_0/2\pi=2.63$ Hz. The reduction in $\omega_0\Gamma$ relative to the previous uniform suspension more than offsets the penalty. Although both suspensions support entanglement in the error-free model, only the stepped one allows robust verification in the multimode model with experimental uncertainties.

papers.title: Quantum resetting with memory
The TNG50-SKIRT Atlas: Spatially resolved synthetic galaxies from the ultraviolet to the submillimetre (DR2)
Data-Driven Domain of Attraction Estimation via Convergent Koopman-Zubov Approximation
papers.abstract: This paper considers the problem of estimating the domain of attraction (DOA) of an asymptotically stable equilibrium, which is characterized by the support of a Zubov function. A Zubov--Koopman operator, i.e., a Koopman operator weighted by an accumulated cost, is defined and shown to be exponentially stable on a space of functions that vanish at the origin at least linearly (whenever the cost is sufficiently large away from the equilibrium). Consequently, the Zubov function is the unique invariant element on this space augmented with constants. Hence, by learning the Zubov--Koopman operator on a suitable reproducing kernel Hilbert space from snapshot data, an explicit kernel expression of the estimated Zubov function and an explicit DOA estimation algorithm are obtained. Such an estimation procedure is a highly efficient convex, closed-form regularized least-squares one, with a provable error bound proportional to the distance from the equilibrium and decreases with the fill distance of the sample. Numerical examples illustrate the accuracy and computational efficiency of the approach in comparison with existing neural network and dictionary-based methods.

Mechanism-Dependent Descriptors for Oxygen Capacity in Perovskite Oxides

papers.title: A Lower Bound on the Sliced Wasserstein Comparison Constant for Translated Measures
papers.abstract: We provide closed-form expressions for standard 1-Wasserstein distance ($W_1$) and Sliced 1-Wasserstein distance ($SW_1$) for translated probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Furthermore, we construct an explicit lower bound for the constant $c_d$ established by Carlier, Figalli, Mérigot, and Wang between $W_1$ and $SW_1$ [1] for translated probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Sliced Wasserstein distances are computationally efficient and used in image generation and other applications, which raises natural questions in computational efficiency versus theoretical correctness. A lower bound on the constant $c_d$ gives information about the cost of that efficiency.

papers.title: On the Kähler MMP and the transcendental base-point-free theorem
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish the minimal model program for big gklt Kähler pairs, and in particular we prove Tosatti's transcendental base-point-free conjecture.

papers.title: CFT-Inspired Two-Horizon Thermodynamics as a Diagnostic for the Bi-Hair Organization of NUT Charge
Comparative qualification of advanced plasma-facing materials for fusion pilot plants through public- and private-sector experiments in DIII-D
Evolution of the electronic and superconducting properties of Re-based quinary high-entropy alloys under chemical and physical pressure
Investigating planar Proca metamaterials in nonlinear (2+1)-Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: The present work pursues the investigation of the physics of a planar electromagnetic system incorporating nonlinear effects, as well as de Broglie-Proca and Chern-Simons mass terms in vacuum, which can be tuned to describe new planar metamaterials (MTMs) potentially suitable for technological applications. As a result, we observe interesting effects generated by a spatially dispersive profile that emerges from non-linearity. This characterizes the three-dimensional QED vacuum as a nonlocal metamaterial. The constitutive relations are derived, and the dielectric function of the metamaterial (MTM) exhibits spatial dispersion due to the Chern-Simons mass. The dispersion relations are analyzed in terms of applied external electromagnetic fields and both the de Broglie-Proca and Chern-Simons mass parameters. We also notice that, in the special case in which only a background magnetic field is present, this field gives no contribution neither to the dielectric function nor to the spatial dispersion profile, as is the case when both the electric and magnetic fields are present.

papers.title: Quantum transport in Cooper pair splitters using hierarchical equations of motion
Neilson's Weak vs. Strong Loss Aversion: A Characterization and a Generalized CPT-Utility Function
papers.abstract: In multi-objective and multi-criteria decision-making under risk, especially in settings involving individual behavior, risk-aware analysis based on subjective evaluation has become increasingly important. Moving beyond risk-neutral modeling and the constraints of Expected Utility Theory (EUT), Cumulative Prospect Theory (CPT) provides a behaviorally grounded framework for capturing how individuals perceive and evaluate risky prospects. This paper conducts a rigorous theoretical analysis of Neilson's definitions of aversion. We provide a gamble-based interpretation, sharpen key conceptual distinctions, and make explicit the conditions under which the weak and strong notions coincide as well as when they diverge. Furthermore, we examine the Kobberling-Wakker utility function and related standard CPT specifications, highlighting structural limitations and inconsistencies that arise when these forms are required to satisfy Neilson-type aversion conditions. To address these issues, we propose a generalized CPT-utility function that retains the canonical reference-dependent shape while offering additional flexibility. This generalization extends the descriptive scope of CPT and provides an explicit functional form that is useful for sensitivity analysis and utility function-based optimization.

papers.title: Formation and scaling of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ strings for global $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry
On Leray's Theoreme de Structure for a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations: an improvement of the result
papers.abstract: In this note we furnish a new result concerning the well known théorème de structure by Leray related to a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations. We are able to furnish a new estimate on the left endpoint of the unbounded interval of regularity.

papers.title: A multi-band radio flux density catalog of ICRF3 sources using the Onsala Twin Telescopes
A wormhole with two black holes
Strictly paired ${\rm CR}$ linear automorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^4$
papers.abstract: This paper studies real-linear automorphisms of $\mathbb C^2$ through the ranks of their complex-linear and conjugate-linear blocks. Particular emphasis is placed on strictly paired CR (SPCR) automorphisms of $\mathbb R^4$, for which both blocks have rank $1$. Such a map is complex-linear on one complex line and conjugate-linear on a complementary complex line. Equivalently, the SPCR automorphisms form the double coset ${\rm GL}(2,\mathbb C)\,\sigma_0\,{\rm GL}(2,\mathbb C)$, where $\sigma_0(z_1,z_2)=(z_1,\bar z_2)$ is a mixed real-linear involution whose fixed locus is a real hypersurface. We show that the SPCR locus is a $12$-dimensional submanifold of $M_2(\mathbb C)^2$ and carries a CR structure of CR dimension $4$ and CR codimension $4$ on an explicit open dense subset. We also construct canonical diagonal and genuinely non-diagonal examples.

papers.title: Non-Square UPA-Enabled XL-MIMO Systems: Anisotropic Near-Field Characterization, Fundamental Limits, and Channel Estimation
papers.abstract: Extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) is crucial for next-generation communication systems. In practice, the deployment of non-square uniform planar arrays (UPAs) fundamentally alters wavefront characteristics and induces anisotropic beamfocusing capability along different axes due to the aperture disparity originating from the non-square array geometry. To fully uncover the performance impact of such non-square geometry and thus unleash the potential of the non-square UPAs, we investigate the anisotropic near-field characteristics, fundamental limits, and channel estimation for non-square UPA-enabled XL-MIMO systems. First, we derive the effective beamfocusing distances for the long and short axes of the array. Interestingly, the radiation space of a non-square UPA can be partitioned into three regions, i.e., the fully near-field, the anisotropic near-field, and the far-field regions, and the anisotropic region asymptotically dominates the overall near-field space as the array aspect ratio increases. Then, the asymptotic effective degree of freedom for non-square UPA-enabled XL-MIMO systems is provided, which reveals that distance-domain multiplexing is governed by the long-axis aperture in the large array aspect ratio regime. Furthermore, the closed-form Cramer-Rao bound for distance estimation and the three-dimensional (3D) position error bound (PEB) are derived to reveal the geometry-induced performance trade-offs among distance, azimuth, and elevation estimation, based on which the optimal array aspect ratio that minimizes the 3D PEB is determined. Finally, by exploiting the anisotropic wavefront properties, we design a 3D anisotropic near-field codebook to facilitate low-complexity channel estimation for non-square UPAs. Numerical results validate that the proposed codebook achieves comparable accuracy to the 3D polar-domain codebook at reduced complexity.

papers.title: Robust Signal Maximization in Spillover Experiments
papers.abstract: We study the optimal design and analysis of experiments for estimating spillover effects. Assuming a known (e.g., linear) exposure mapping, we characterize the treatment-assignment distribution and regression-based estimator that minimize worst-case approximate variance against a broad class of distributions of unobservables. The design problem yields an intuitive solution in which the planner trades off spillover signal strength against dispersion of spillover variation. The analysis problem yields a simple recentered instrumental variable estimator to best leverage this variation. This framework produces natural solutions in several benchmark cases - such as clustered exposure - and suggests computationally tractable approximations for general networks, including bipartite settings. We illustrate these new tools in semi-synthetic experiments based on three applications from development economics. Our approach yields large standard error reductions in these experiments, increasing effective sample sizes by 44-266%.

papers.title: National-scale scheduling of long-distance electric vehicle charging under plug capacity
papers.abstract: Can today's U.S. public charging network serve long-distance trips by electric vehicles (EVs), and at what cost to travelers? We plan the charging stops of 2.2 million long-distance trips that need en-route charging, from a 1% sample of a one-month simulation, through the contiguous U.S. fast-charging network. Plans value detour, charging, and waiting time. Charging to a fixed battery level makes each trip's problem a shortest path, solved exactly; common modeling shortcuts can reverse the cost comparison. For trips competing for plugs, we compare four coordination methods, from none to reservations by departure time; the best two come within 2.2% and 6.1% of the best known solutions on small cases. First, if every plug serves every EV, existing fast chargers can reach 98.5% of the trips that need to charge, excluding those with an overly long link, with under four stops and about seven minutes of detour. Second, charging speed and electricity price decide the cost comparison: at \$0.15 per kWh, the EV is cheaper only for travelers valuing their charging time below \$11 per hour with 50 kW, or \$111 per hour with 350 kW chargers; at \$0.45 per kWh, it costs more at either speed. Third, without coordination, long queues form at several hundred small stations at 50 kW while nearby larger ones are less busy. If every trip books a plug, almost all waiting disappears on all trips at 350 kW for under a minute of extra detour, and at \$0.15 per kWh the EV trip stays about 21% cheaper.

papers.title: Supply Chain Networks: Equilibrium, Sensitivity, Dynamics and Shortage Games
papers.abstract: We model production in a supply chain network in which every node sets a Newsvendor order target, upstream demand is the sum of downstream orders routed through a substochastic matrix, and every node has a capacity. The clearing vector of production quantities is the unique Nash equilibrium of the ordering game and the unique optimal solution of a linear program, and it has the form of the Eisenberg--Noe interbank clearing model. Nodes that produce their order target are hedged; the others are unhedged. We give comparative statics and a closed form for the stationary covariance of node demands. Inventory drawdown after a capacity shock is a Skorokhod reflection problem with a closed-form solution: the network and the unhedged nodes determine who is eventually rationed and by how much, and inventories determine when. When rationed nodes can inflate their orders, the equilibria never lower aggregate deliveries and can make suppliers with no physical shortage unhedged. With endogenous prices, a per-epoch price equilibrium exists and, under mild conditions, is unique when supply is price-elastic. We illustrate the model on global crude-oil trade.

papers.title: Growing Hypergraphs with Homophily
papers.abstract: There are many extant models of hypergraphs with interactions governed by attribute-based homophily between nodes, but most assume independence between edges conditional on node parameters. Relaxing this assumption, we study a mechanistic model of growing hypergraphs in which edge formation is influenced by both previous edges and binary node labels. Edges form in this model as noisy copies of previous edges, where the transmission of nodes from one edge to the next depends on multiple homophilic mechanisms between labels. These homophilic mechanisms give rise to tunable assortative structure in the hypergraph. We derive a power law for the degree distribution in this model and describe the long-term dynamics of the joint distribution of labels contained in edges. Our model defines a likelihood over a labeled hypergraph, allowing us to use standard maximum-likelihood techniques to structure algorithms. We estimate the model parameters on synthetic and real data via (stochastic) expectation maximization. These estimates give statistically-principled descriptions of the operation of homophily in empirical polyadic systems. We also demonstrate an approach to community detection via simulated annealing which, though computationally expensive, achieves competitive results on both synthetic data and certain empirical data sets known to be challenging to community detection techniques based on the edge-independence assumption. Our findings highlight the benefits of incorporating edge- and label-dependence in higher-order modeling and data analysis, and point to several directions for future work.

papers.title: Dynamic Constraint Reconstruction Based Control Barrier Functions for Safety-Critical Control of High-Dimensional Manipulators
papers.abstract: Control barrier functions (CBFs) provide formal safety guarantees for constrained nonlinear systems, but their effectiveness relies on accurate system dynamics. In high-dimensional manipulators subject to unknown disturbances and model uncertainties, fixed safety constraints constructed from nominal dynamics may become inconsistent with the actual system behavior, leading to safety degradation or excessive conservatism. This paper proposes a dynamic constraint reconstruction based control barrier function (DCR-CBF) framework for safety-critical control of disturbed robotic manipulators. An extended state observer is employed to estimate lumped disturbances online, and the estimated disturbance is incorporated into high-order control barrier functions to reconstruct safety constraints according to the estimated true dynamics. To address estimation inaccuracies, a safety margin is introduced, and a sufficient condition is derived to guarantee forward invariance under bounded estimation errors. Simulation studies on a 4-DOF excavation manipulator demonstrate that the proposed DCR-CBF method achieves zero safety violation under strong unknown disturbances while significantly improving trajectory-tracking performance compared with standard and robust CBF methods.

papers.title: Uncovering Hierarchical Sub-Population of Binary Black Holes
Singular limit for nonlocal conservation laws with non-locality in density and velocity
papers.abstract: We study the singular limit of a generalized nonlocal conservation law intro- duced in [18]. The nonlocal equation incorporates non-locality both in density and velocity. We derive entropy solutions of the underlying Burgers equation as a singular limit. The main ingredient of the proof is a nonlocal Oleinik type estimate, extending the method of [7]. The nonlocal Oleinik estimate provides uniform bounds on the total variation, thereby enabling to pass to the limit in the regularization parameter.

papers.title: Microscopically informed constitutive framework for stress overshoot, yielding, and strain hardening in amorphous materials
Learning Forced Multibody Dynamics on Lie Groups
papers.abstract: We introduce an architecture for learning the dynamics of forced mechanical systems evolving on Lie groups, based on discrete forced Euler-Lagrange equations. The proposed method, termed Lie Group Discrete Forced Euler-Lagrange Neural Network (LieDFLNN), learns mechanical dynamics directly from discrete configuration observations, without requiring velocity measurements. This formulation allows the simultaneous identification of unknown mechanical properties and forcing terms, while ensuring that the predicted configurations remain on the underlying Lie group. We develop explicit formulations for rigid body dynamics on $SO(3)$ and $SE(3)$, extend the framework to interacting multibody systems, and introduce a method for learning unknown control forces when the Lagrangian is known. Finally, we evaluate the method through numerical experiments involving rigid body dynamics, nonlinear external forces, controlled systems, and real-world human motion capture data. The numerical results confirm the advantages of incorporating Lie group geometry and discrete variational structure into data-driven modeling of forced mechanical systems.

papers.title: Lattice Configuration Generation with a Self-Learning Diffusion Model
Genus and Gonality of Small Curves, Dynamical Uniform Boundedness, and Bifurcation
papers.abstract: We prove that a complex one-parameter algebraic family of endomorphisms of $\mathbb{P}^N$ has a non-empty bifurcation set if and only if the genus grows superlinearly in degree along every generic sequence of dynatomic curves. In this case, gonality also tends to infinity. In particular, for non-isotrivial families on $\mathbb{P}^1$, gonality tends to infinity along distinct dynatomic curves, while superlinear genus growth holds for every such sequence exactly when the family is not a flexible Lattès family. We also establish analogous results for generic sequences of small curves. As applications, we prove uniform boundedness results for iterated preimages over number fields and geometric uniform boundedness results for preperiodic points over function fields. The proof combines arithmetic equidistribution, woven currents, and bifurcation theory. The bifurcation mechanism is what forces the growth of genus and gonality.

papers.title: Shifted-Binomial Coordinates of Dilated Binomial Polynomials: Multinomial Decimation and Arithmetic Structure
papers.abstract: For integers $m\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, let $d=m+r-1$ and consider the unique expansion \[ \binom{mn}{d}=\sum_{k=1}^{d+1}T_{m,r,k}\binom{n+k-1}{d}. \] By a standard multisection of a rational generating function, the coordinates are a residue-class subsequence of multinomial coefficients: \[ T_{m,r,k}=[x^{mk-1}](1+x+\cdots+x^{m-1})^{m+r}. \] From this representation we obtain the exact support, a counting interpretation by words by drops (Theorem~\ref{thm:drops}), a reflection criterion (the nonzero row is palindromic precisely when $r\equiv2\pmod m$), and log-concavity, hence unimodality, of the nonzero row. An integer-valued polynomial argument gives the universal divisor $m/\gcd(m,r-1)$ of each row, and a prime-adic computation of the fixed divisor of $\binom{mX}{d}$ gives the exact greatest common divisor of each row, a sharpness criterion, and a family of rows in which the universal divisor is arbitrarily far from sharp. We also obtain the row sum $m^{m+r-1}$, a Catalan-number specialization, and explicit coefficient arrays for $m=2,3,4,5$. The methods are finite differences, multisection of rational generating functions, and fixed divisors of integer-valued polynomials.

papers.title: A few remarks on the Baez-Duarte Criterion
papers.abstract: We study exponentially damped Möbius approximants in $\mathscr H=L^2([1,\infty),dt/t^{-2})$. With \[ \gamma_n(t)=\left\lfloor\frac tn\right\rfloor -\frac{\lfloor t\rfloor}{n},\qquad f(u)(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)e^{-nu}\gamma_n(t),\] we compute the relevant scalar products, characterize the Möbius coefficients as the unique coefficients giving pointwise convergence to the constant function, and prove $\langle1 \mid f(u)\rangle\to1$. Vasyunin's formula expresses $F(e^{-u})=\|f(u)\|_2^2$ as an arithmetic cotangent sum. In the final section we give a criterion that would help in the analysis of asymptotics of $F(x)$ as $x\uparrow 1$.

papers.title: Analyzing Image Encoder Choices and Graph Homophily in GCN Frameworks for Breast Ultrasound Classification
papers.abstract: Breast ultrasound is widely used for screening, yet automated analysis remains challenging due to speckle noise, acquisition variability, and weak separation of benign and malignant cases in standard ultrasound imaging. Graph convolutional networks (GCNs) have recently emerged as a promising approach by leveraging relationships among similar patient samples. However, it remains unclear how the choice of image encoder influences graph construction and downstream classification performance. In this work, we systematically evaluate five image encoders spanning convolutional and transformer-based architectures for GCN-based breast ultrasound classification. Image embeddings are used to construct cosine similarity k-nearest-neighbor graphs, which are classified using a single-layer GCN with a linear classification head. Across three patient-wise cross-validation folds, higher-capacity encoders consistently improve graph homophily and downstream classification performance, yielding gains in accuracy, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score. Moreover, test-set graph homophily exhibits a strong linear correlation with classification accuracy (R-squared = 0.875), with higher-capacity encoders consistently occupying the high-homophily, high-accuracy region, suggesting that encoder-driven improvements in graph structure are a key mechanism underlying the observed performance gains. On 798 images from two external sources, the encoder ordering was preserved, but accuracy was 0.13-0.21 lower than in cross-validation and the homophily-accuracy association was weaker (R-squared = 0.759). These findings establish encoder selection as a critical factor in graph-based breast ultrasound classification and identify graph homophily as a key indicator linking representation quality to downstream classification performance.

papers.title: Modeling the Evolution of Protoplanetary Disks: Two Pathways from Gravitational Instability to MHD Wind-Driven Accretion
Fuss-free cumulative universes: theory and practice
papers.abstract: Universes are central to dependent type theory, and they are notoriously difficult to handle in a way that is both correct and usable. We propose a new "fuss-free" generalised algebraic presentation for polymorphic cumulative universes that dispenses with the intricate theory of coherent universe coercions in favour of a simpler formulation, which we prove equivalent by means of a normalisation theorem for the former. We study the fuss-free formulation by means of (1) an abstract specification of its bidirectional elaboration algorithm, and (2) a concrete implementation in Haskell. We also describe and implement an extension of the fuss-free universe hierarchy with a judgemental notion of datatype description from which prior notions of cumulative inductive type may be derived.

papers.title: Group action-stabilizer graph of group actions of a group on a set
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce the group action-stabilizer graph $GAS(G)$ of a group $G$ on a set $X$. Its vertex set is the collection of all non-trivial group actions of $G$ on $X$, and two vertices $\phi$ and $\psi$ are adjacent if and only if the normal subgroups $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^\phi$ and $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^\psi$ of $G$ intersect non-trivially, where $G_x^\phi$ and $G_x^\psi$ are the stabilizers of $x$ with respect to the actions $\phi$ and $\psi$, respectively. We show that $GAS(G)$ is obtained from the intersection graph of those normal subgroups of $G$ that occur as kernels of actions on $X$ by replacing each vertex by a clique of twin vertices, and we characterize a special subgraph $gas(G)$ of $GAS(G)$ in which the vertex set contains the actions $\phi$ of $G$ on $X$ such that the kernels $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^\phi$ are distinct. We determine the number of group actions within some specific groups and find certain conditions under which $GAS(G)$ is equal to $gas(G)$. We also show that, for a finite nilpotent group $G$ with at least two prime divisors, $gas(G)$ is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^3p_2$, and its complement is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^2p_2^2$.

papers.title: Penalized hyperviscous Navier-Stokes flows: well-posedness, incompressible limit and sharp decay
papers.abstract: We study a three-dimensional Navier--Stokes system obtained by Temam's penalty method in the presence of a biharmonic viscosity: the pressure and the divergence constraint are replaced by the term $-\varepsilon^{-1}\nabla\,div\,u$, and the convection term is written in skew-symmetric form. We prove global well-posedness in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and global regularity for data of arbitrary size in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, with bounds uniform in $\varepsilon$ and in time. For data in $L^1\cap L^2$, the energy decays like $t^{-3/2}$, with a constant independent of $\varepsilon$; for data in $L^1\cap H^2$, the first two derivatives decay at the corresponding heat rates. We identify the leading asymptotic profile and show that $t^{3/2}\|u(t)\|_{L^2}^2\to\gamma_\varepsilon(8\pi\nu)^{-3/2}|m_\infty|^2$, where $m_\infty$ is an asymptotic momentum and the explicit factor $\gamma_\varepsilon\in(\frac23,1)$ measures the energy removed by the penalization. Consequently, the decay rates are optimal in $L^1\cap H^2$ under an explicit non-degeneracy condition. Finally, as $\varepsilon\to0$, the solutions converge globally in time to those of the incompressible hyperviscous Navier--Stokes equations at the rate $\sqrt\varepsilon$, up to an explicit initial layer, and $-\varepsilon^{-1}div\,u$ converges to the pressure.

papers.title: Single-Photon Detection via Enhanced Cross-Phase Modulation in Topology-Optimized Epsilon-Near-Zero Dual-Wavelength Nanocavities
papers.abstract: We use the Green's tensor quantization theory for open resonant nanostructures with absorption losses to study cross-phase modulation (XPM) at the single-photon level in nanoscale Kerr-type epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) materials with an effective nonlinear susceptibility integrated inside dual-wavelength nanocavities. We obtain analytical formulas for the XPM frequency shifts in hybrid nanocavities that simultaneously trap a classical probe beam at 1.5 $\mu$m and single-photon pump at 3 $\mu$m wavelengths. We present a comprehensive analysis of the fundamental limits for mid-infrared single-photon detection in the quantum nondemolition modality for nanostructured cadmium oxide (CdO) regions with ENZ-enhanced nonlinearity embedded in a silicon (Si) environment inversely designed by free-form topology optimization. We numerically implement our theoretical results using finite element simulations within the rigorous framework of quasi-normal modes, demonstrating a single-photon XPM frequency shift $\Delta f_s \approx 5.71 \text{ GHz}$ with fractional shift (i.e., frequency pulling) $\Delta f_s / f_s \approx 2.85 \times 10^{-5}$ and addressing the feasibility of detection in the hybrid Si-CdO dual-wavelength nanocavity, either with a classical probe beam or a squeezed probe state, including the contributions of traditional limitations from self-phase modulation noise, thermorefractive noise, shot noise, and free-carrier absorption effects. Finally, we present a comparative size scaling analysis of the XPM phase shift and phase noise contributions for dual-wavelength nanocavities based on CdO and indium tin oxide (ITO) nonlinear ENZ materials. This work establishes a robust benchmark for the engineering of mid-infrared single-photon nonlinear devices such as nondemolition quantum detectors, sensors, and all-optical gates on a solid state photonic platform.

papers.title: Harmonic weights in inverse central binomial series
papers.abstract: We study how the partial fraction coefficients of an inverse central binomial series change when the harmonic weight $H_{pn}$ is replaced by $H_{qn}$. For positive integers $p<q$, every coefficient increases. As the index $k$ grows, the increase tends to $2\log(q/p)$ uniformly over all angles $0<\phi\le\pi$, even when the angle approaches either endpoint. The increase is above the limit at every odd index and below it at every even index. We give the first correction, of order $k^{-2/q}$ for $q>2$ and of order $k^{-2}$ for $(p,q)=(1,2)$. For the normalized transforms, subtracting $c$ times the first from the second gives a Stieltjes function exactly when $c\le1$. We also determine which real dilations $0<p<q$ satisfy the same sign law. For $p\ge1$ it holds exactly when $q\ge2$. For $0<p<1$ it holds above a threshold $Q(p)$, and at the threshold it holds precisely on one interval $0<p<p_*$. Finally, we give angle identities at every odd weight from three onward and determine which Dirichlet $L$-terms cancel at angle $\pi/3$.

papers.title: Universal swelling of tangentially driven ring polymers in two dimensions
Impact of Channel Dynamics on Higher-order Interactions of Oscillators
papers.abstract: Modeling higher-order interactions (HOIs) in nonlinear networks with static topologies is often physically restrictive. We demonstrate that standard 3-body Kuramoto couplings are mathematically equivalent to pairwise connections modulated by latent variables of transmission channels. While standard HOI topologies emerge in the adiabatic limit of these variables, relaxing this constraint reveals that latent channel timescales dictate collective macroscopic states. Specifically, transmission inertia drives bistability for symmetric interaction tensors and anti-phase cluster synchronization for antisymmetric ones. Furthermore, dynamically induced clustering in global topologies emerges as a finite-size effect of the dynamics of the local channels. Ultimately, we show that relying exclusively on static topologies restricts interaction modeling. Integrating latent variables captures the transient inertia and fundamental asymmetry of physical networks, bridging the analytical utility of higher-order functions with the reality of the underlying transmission medium.

papers.title: The Stability of the Backward Problem for Photoacoustic Imaging in Attenuating Media via Carleman Estimates
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the backward problem in time for photoacoustic tomography (PAT) in attenuating media. It is well-established that photoacoustic imaging in attenuating media can be accurately modeled by spatial fractional-order damping. This inverse problem is ill-posed in the sense of Hadamard. In this work, we construct a novel class of Carleman estimates independent of spatial variables, and by virtue of these estimates, we establish conditional stability estimates for this problem for the first time. Building upon this, we propose a Tikhonov-type regularization functional and derive its associated adjoint system. Furthermore, leveraging the established conditional stability results, we derive the convergence rate of the proposed regularization approach. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of our theoretical findings through extensive numerical experiments.

papers.title: Probing Extended Recognition Sites in Zn-Metalloproteins via Quantum Chemistry and Polarizable Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Zn-metalloproteins play vital roles in numerous metabolic processes, making them high-value targets for structure-based drug design. To advance these efforts, it is useful to unravel the individual components of the intermolecular interaction energies ($\Delta E$) that stabilize the Zn-binding cavity, both in the absence and presence of bound protein ligands. Here, we utilize quantum chemistry (QC) to decompose $\Delta E$ into distinct physical contributions. The relative magnitudes of these components vary significantly depending on the coordination number (four to six) and the chemical nature ('hard' vs. 'soft') of the Zn-coordinating ligands. These high-level QC analyses serve to calibrate and validate polarizable molecular mechanics potentials, effectively extending the accurate description of electronic effects beyond the immediate Zn-binding cavity to enlarged recognition sites and, ultimately, entire protein systems over long molecular dynamics (MD) simulation timescales. We focus here on a QC-grounded molecular mechanics procedure, denoted as SIBFA. Following a concise overview of our QC methodology used for its calibration, we present validation studies on complexes containing up to 300 atoms and discuss the prospects of applying this framework to large-scale simulations of Zn-metalloprotein-ligand complexes. Finally, the structural and energetic roles of discrete, highly polarizable water molecules are highlighted.

papers.title: XRISM Reveals a Kinematically Coherent Core System of the Nearby Cool-Core Cluster Abell 2199
Connecting Microseismicity to Lithology via a Model of Slip Avalanches
