papers.abstract: We develop an energy-decreasing algorithm for the finite element approximation of two-dimensional ferronematic equilibrium states. The problem is formulated as the minimization of the harmonic energy of two two-dimensional vector fields, both with prescribed length, together with an additional nonlinear relation on the orientation of the two vectors. The finite element setting is based on piecewise continuous finite elements on a weakly acute triangulation. The numerical realization of the energy-decreasing algorithm employs a decomposition-coordination framework and a Uzawa-like iteration. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the computational performances of the algorithm.

papers.title: Mitigating residual foregrounds and systematic errors in SKA1-Low AA* EoR observations via Bayesian Gaussian Process Regression
On the global convergence of gradient flow for wide shallow models beyond homogeneous nonlinearities
papers.abstract: A surprising phenomenon in the training of neural networks is the ability of gradient descent to find global minimizers of the training loss despite its non-convexity. Following earlier work, we investigate this behavior for wide shallow models. Existing global convergence results primarily concern models with positively one-homogeneous nonlinearities, such as ReLU activations, and models with scalar output weights and bounded nonlinearities, such as sigmoid activations. We study a broader class of models, including multi-head attention layers and two-layer fully connected networks with bounded or asymptotically positively one-homogeneous activations and vector output weights. Building upon (Chizat and Bach, 2018), we prove that, in the limit of infinitely many hidden neurons or attention heads, non-minimizers of the training loss are unstable under the mean-field gradient flow dynamics by constructing "escape regions" in the parameter space. Our global convergence statements are conditional in the following sense: if the mean-field gradient flow converges for the Wasserstein 2-distance, then its limit must be a global minimizer. We revisit the bounded nonlinearity, scalar-output setting of (Chizat and Bach, 2018), giving an escape region construction adapted to unbounded nonlinear parameter domains. We also propose new constructions for nonlinearities with at most linear growth under a non-degeneracy assumption and for asymptotically positively one-homogeneous nonlinearities. Finally, we show the well-posedness and stability estimates for the mean-field training dynamics under sub-Gaussian initializations.

papers.title: Dynamically Reconfigurable Optical Skyrmions Enabled by a Silicon Microring Optical Phased Array for Robust Free-Space Communication
papers.abstract: Optical skyrmions can encode information in the skyrmion number for free-space communication through atmospheric turbulence. However, programming both the skyrmion number and type on a compact chip remains challenging. Here, we propose and numerically demonstrate a skyrmion generator based on a silicon optical phased array with optimized inner- and outer-grating microring emitters. The two emitter types provide orthogonal circularly polarized components and generate optical skyrmions through coherent superposition. The on-chip phase shifters configure the azimuthal phase distribution, enabling the $4\times4$ array to generate states with target skyrmion numbers of $-2$, $-1$, 1, and 2. Adjustment of the relative phase bias continuously switches states with target skyrmion numbers of $\pm1$ between the Néel and Bloch types. Increasing the array size to $12\times12$ extends the target range from $-8$ to 8. Laser wavelength tuning and calibration of the microring input phases and amplitudes recover target states within a range of simulated fabrication errors, which shows the robustness of the generator. Furthermore, we evaluate four-symbol communication using skyrmion-number decoding over a simulated 100 m turbulent link and observe no symbol errors in $10^4$ trials at Rytov variances up to 0.12. These results demonstrate the potential of this generator as a compact, programmable transmitter for turbulence-tolerant free-space optical communication.

papers.title: The Geometric Wall: Manifold Structure Predicts Layerwise Sparse Autoencoder Scaling Laws
papers.abstract: SAEs operationalise the linear representation hypothesis: they reconstruct model activations as sparse linear combinations of dictionary atoms hypothesised to represent meaningful linear directions. Their reconstruction error varies sharply across layers in ways that existing scaling laws, fitted at a single layer, do not explain. We contend that this variation is the empirical trace of the changing geometric structure of activation manifolds across depth: as their intrinsic dimension and curvature vary from layer to layer, so does the difficulty of approximating them with sparse linear dictionaries, and SAE width-sparsity scaling becomes a layer-dependent function of manifold structure rather than a single universal law. We conduct the first cross-layer SAE scaling study, fitting per-layer scaling-law surfaces to 844 residual-stream Gemma Scope SAE checkpoints spanning all 68 layers of Gemma 2 2B and 9B, and relating the fitted scaling parameters to four geometric summaries of the activation manifold. We find that manifold geometry predicts the per-layer width-scaling exponent in both models, explaining variation that cannot be reliably captured by layer depth alone. A controlled experiment on 150 synthetic manifolds, where intrinsic dimension and curvature vary independently, further reveals two distinct geometric contributions: intrinsic dimension governs the rate at which reconstruction improves with dictionary width, while curvature governs the residual error at the largest trained width. At the six Gemma showcase layers where richer width grids permit identification of an asymptotic floor, the fitted floors follow the same geometric ordering, consistent with the second-order residual that sparse linear approximations of curved manifolds can leave behind. SAEs thus encounter not merely a finite-resource ceiling but a geometric wall set by the manifold they are trying to reconstruct.

papers.title: Homotopy exponents of polyhedral products
papers.abstract: We study Moore's conjecture and homotopy exponents for polyhedral products. For $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ where each $A_i$ is finite and has torsion-free homology, we prove that if $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ is rationally hyperbolic, then it has no homotopy exponent at any odd prime. Under the additional hypothesis $\Sigma A_i$ is homotopy equivalent to a finite-type wedge of simply-connected spheres, we show Moore's conjecture holds for $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$. We also give criteria such that, for a large family of polyhedral join products, the associated polyhedral products are rationally hyperbolic, mod-$p^r$ hyperbolic for all but finitely many primes, and have no homotopy exponent at all but finitely many primes.

papers.title: Embodied Communication: Sensing-Induced Reliability Fields and Capacity Bounds
papers.abstract: This paper introduces embodied communication, a new wireless communication modality in which information is imprinted onto environmental states and recovered by the receiver through sensing. No dedicated communication transmitter is activated, and no additional communication spectrum is occupied; instead, the sensed environment itself becomes the carrier of information. The key insight is that sensing must be reinterpreted for communication. Rather than asking how accurately an unknown physical state can be estimated, embodied communication asks how reliably two states can be distinguished. We formalize this idea through a multi-snapshot radio frequency (RF) sensing model and derive a sensing-induced reliability field that quantifies the distinguishability between physical states. This field turns embodied symbol design into a geometric packing problem shaped by the sensing resolution of the infrastructure. For this embodied channel, we characterize the finite-snapshot $\epsilon$-capacity through achievable designs and converses. We develop lattice-based codebooks, obtain a closed-form hexagonal design under a main-lobe approximation, and establish information-theoretic and geometric upper bounds. We further investigate the sensing-duration tradeoff: more sensing snapshots improve reliability, but also lengthen each embodied symbol, leading to a finite optimal sensing time. These results expose a latent communication pathway in sensing-enabled infrastructure and show how the environment can be transformed from a passive backdrop into an active information carrier.

papers.title: Structural and Lagrangian properties of analogue ensembles to characterize multifractality of stochastic processes
papers.abstract: We present a framework for the scale-invariance characterization of stochastic processes in reconstructed finite-dimensional spaces. This framework analyses the structural and dynamical properties of the reconstructed space and is based on a Takens embedding reconstruction followed by the definition of ensembles of analogue states. First, we specify a collection of target states densely sampling the full embedding space. For each target state, we search for the ensemble of its k-nearest neighbors, its k-best analogues, and we analyze its volume and dynamics. On the one hand, we study the probability distribution of the volumes and relate its mean and variance to the scale-invariance properties of the stochastic process. On the second hand, we study the Lagrangian properties of the analogues by characterizing how they disperse in time. More particularly, we study the volume occupied by the analogue's successors in function of time and of their initial volume. The main contribution of this paper is to highlight the link between these dynamical properties and the scale-invariance features of the process. We analyze two types of stationary and dissipative 1-dimensional scale-invariant processes: regularized fractional Brownian motion and regularized multifractal random walk. For both processes, the structure and dynamics of the embedding space are determined by their scale-invariant properties.

papers.title: Advance warning of $γ$-ray blazar flares from Fermi-LAT light curves: a strictly causal machine-learning backtest
Bootstrapping ground state properties of classical frustrated magnets
A High-Precision Statistical Analysis of the SN1987A Neutrino Temporal Distribution
Characterizing electronic scattering rates with transport in multiterminal devices
A CV-TMLE global test approach to improve power in rare disease clinical studies with multiple-component endpoints
papers.abstract: Rare disease trials face unique statistical challenges due to limited patient populations and heterogeneous clinical manifestations among patients. Multiple endpoints are often necessary to comprehensively capture treatment benefits. A global test is an approach for evaluating whether a treatment has any beneficial effect across multiple endpoints. We propose a new global test based on a weighted composite endpoint. The proposed global test employs shrinkage-based cross-validated targeted maximum likelihood estimation (CV-TMLE) to learn data-adaptive weights that maximize power while maintaining Type I error control. Shrinkage can be tailored to incorporate existing domain knowledge, such as anticipated relative effect sizes. In simulation studies designed to reflect real rare disease trial settings, the proposed procedure demonstrated improved power over standard multiplicity adjustments and classical global tests (such as the O'Brien test), while maintaining nominal Type I error, when effects are heterogeneous across endpoints. The proposed method simultaneously learns an optimal weighted composite outcome and provides an unbiased and efficient targeted maximum likelihood estimator (TMLE) for the average treatment effect (ATE) on that weighted outcome, with valid inference taking into account that the ATE is data dependent.

papers.title: Factorization and monotonicity methods for reconstructing an impenetrable obstacle in inverse biharmonic scattering
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of an impenetrable obstacle with a Dirichlet or Neumann boundary condition from far-field measurements. The associated data-to-pattern operators are noninjective, because the biharmonic scattered fields can be decomposed into propagative and evanescent components. We derive new symmetric factorizations of the far-field operator and analyzie the middle operators on the closures of the ranges of the adjoint data-to-pattern operators to establish range identities. These identities yield factorization criteria for the support of the obstacle when the wavenumber is not an associated transmission eigenvalue. Furthermore, we derive monotonicity criteria without excluding transmission eigenvalues. Numerical experiments for Dirichlet obstacles illustrate the reconstruction methods and show their performance with noisy data and for wavenumbers near a clamped transmission eigenvalue.

papers.title: Estimation and Inference for the $τ$-Quantile of Heterogeneous Individual-Specific Coefficient
papers.abstract: We study quantiles of heterogeneous coefficients across the $n$ observed units of a panel. Treating the coefficients as deterministic, we estimate each from $T$ observations, then use the estimates and their standard errors to construct a smoothed quantile estimator and estimate its variance. When $T^{1/2}\ll n\ll T^{3/2}$, the estimator is asymptotically normal around a deterministic center. A feasible bias correction relaxes the sample growth restriction to $n/T^{3/2}\to c\in[0,\infty)$, accommodating panels with large $n$. Normal inference extends to the target quantile when the difference between the deterministic center and the target is negligible relative to the standard error. Without this restriction, we establish an impossibility result that the distribution of the studentized error relative to the target cannot be estimated uniformly consistently. For practical inference in this case, we construct a conservative interval whose coverage tends uniformly to one and whose length attains the optimal worst-case rate in probability. We give primitive conditions for smooth GMM. Mortgage data show widespread but uneven declines in delinquency across credit scores.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Optimal Group Selection via the Double-Commutator Eigenvalue Problem
papers.abstract: The algebraic diversity framework generalizes temporal averaging over multiple observations to algebraic group action on a single observation for second-order statistical estimation. The central open problem in this framework is $\textit{group selection}$: given an $M$-dimensional observation with unknown covariance structure, find the finite group whose spectral decomposition best matches the covariance. Naive enumeration of all subgroups of the symmetric group $S_M$ requires exponential time in $M$. We prove that this combinatorial problem, restricted to a basis of $d$ candidate generators, reduces to a generalized eigenvalue problem derived from the double commutator of the covariance matrix, with complexity $O(d^2M^2 + d^3)$ for sparse (permutation-type) generators and $O(d^2M^3 + d^3)$ in general. The minimum eigenvector gives the optimal generator in the span of the basis in closed form, with no iterative optimization. The minimum eigenvalue is zero if and only if a generator in the span commutes exactly with the covariance, and its magnitude is a certifiable optimality gap otherwise. The problem does not appear in the standard catalog of Garey and Johnson (1979) and links group theory, matrix analysis, and statistical estimation. We relate it to independent component analysis (JADE), structured matrix nearness, and simultaneous diagonalization, and show that the double-commutator form is the unique objective, up to scale, built from a unitarily invariant quadratic norm of the commutator. We extend the framework to non-Abelian symmetry recovery via a Sequential GEVP with deflation, which is sound but not always complete, give canonical generator sets whose direct testing is complete for five named group families, and add two identifiability theorems on the commutant-lattice ambiguity and on whether $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbf{R})$ recovers a generative subgroup or only a supergroup.

papers.title: VCBench: Benchmarking virtual cell models for in-the-wild perturbation response
papers.abstract: Virtual cell (VC) models aim to predict cellular responses to diverse perturbations in silico, offering great promise for drug discovery and precision medicine. However, although models routinely report strong performance on existing benchmarks, whether these predictions translate to practical biological utility remains unclear. Current evaluations often rely on overly simplified or inconsistent setups that fail to capture the complexity and variability of real biological systems. Here, we present a standardized, modular benchmarking framework that evaluates nine VC models under challenging, in-the-wild scenarios spanning unseen cell lines and donors, novel genetic and chemical perturbations, and cross-study transfer. Across these evaluations, complex models do not consistently surpass simple linear baselines on broad transcriptional trends, while fine-grained, perturbation-specific effects remain difficult to recover. Moreover, different evaluation metrics emphasize distinct biological properties, resulting in markedly different model rankings. Consequently, model selection and data integration strategies should be tailored to specific downstream tasks rather than applied uniformly. Together, this framework establishes a more biologically grounded benchmark to guide model development, evaluation, and deployment in real-world settings.

papers.title: Structural Classes for Chollet's Permanent Conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1982, Chollet conjectured that $\operatorname{per}(A\circ B)\le \operatorname{per}(A)\operatorname{per}(B)$ for Hermitian positive semidefinite matrices $A,B$, where $\circ$ denotes the Hadamard (entrywise) product. In this paper, we study natural structural classes for which the conjecture holds. We first show that a stronger inequality holds for a broad class of matrices with bipartite support. We then introduce a simple way of joining positive semidefinite matrices and give conditions under which Chollet's inequality is preserved under this operation. For graph Laplacians, this operation corresponds to vertex coalescence and gives larger structured graph families satisfying Chollet's inequality from simpler graph classes.

papers.title: Extracting Exact Lie Derivatives Without Backpropagation: A Dual Compiler for Neural Control Barrier Functions
papers.abstract: A safety filter based on a neural control barrier function (CBF) evaluates, at each control cycle, the trained network and its Lie derivatives along the system vector fields. This paper presents a compiler whose emitted C++ code performs this evaluation on embedded processors by forward-mode differentiation with dual numbers. The derivatives are exact in the sense of automatic differentiation, which means that they are free of truncation error and subject to floating-point roundoff. One evaluation of the network in this arithmetic, called a dual pass, returns the barrier value and its Lie derivative along one vector field, and an extension to hyper-dual numbers returns the second-order Lie derivatives of CBFs of relative degree two. Apart from scalar variables, the memory that a dual pass writes is at most four floating-point numbers per neuron of the widest layer and does not depend on the network depth. On an ESP32-S3 microcontroller, we compare the emitted code with code for reverse-mode differentiation (i.e., backpropagation), which is also generated before the program runs and uses fixed-size arrays. In three experiments, the reverse-mode code has a lower execution time than the dual and hyper-dual passes executed one after the other. For single-input networks, the measurements do not establish such an ordering between the reverse-mode code and a variant of the dual pass that propagates the real part once. For networks of increasing depth, the working memory of the dual passes is constant, whereas that of the reverse-mode code increases. While the emitted code runs, no dynamic allocation is recorded. We report the maximum observed execution time of the complete filter step, which includes the dynamics and a breakpoint search for the quadratic program with input bounds and one affine constraint. The compiler and the experiments are open source.

papers.title: Deep Learning of Solver-Aware Turbulence Closures from Nudged LES Dynamics
papers.abstract: The differentiable physics paradigm may be leveraged as an a-posteriori approach for discovering turbulence closure models by embedding a neural network parameterization directly inside the solver and optimizing it given potentially sparse target data. This addresses a key limitation of a-priori learning where direct numerical simulation (DNS) data is used to approximate the subgrid stress with the assumption of a low-pass filter. Closures trained in this a-priori manner frequently lead to unstable deployments due to the mismatch between the assumed filter and the effect of numerical discretizations and coarse-graining. In comparison, while typically stable during deployment, a-posteriori learning incurs high computational costs due to the need to backpropagate through a large eddy simulation (LES) solver. Furthermore, a-posteriori methods are challenging to apply broadly since they require significant modification of existing solvers. Finally, both approaches are limited when generalization is desired across different numerical schemes with their implicit filtering characteristics. In this work, we present a deep-learning approach for turbulence closure modeling built on the continuous data assimilation framework. Our approach enables the a-priori training of closures using DNS data observed only at coarse-grid points without modifying or differentiating through the LES solver, while preserving stability during deployment for the recovery of long-term statistics. We focus on the model's ability to adapt to different discretizations by explicitly conditioning it on the numerical scheme. We use two- and three-dimensional canonical cases to test our framework and show that the learned correction systematically tracks the discretization error of the coarse solver.

papers.title: Convolution invertibility for constructible sheaves and functions
papers.abstract: We characterize convolution-invertible, compactly supported piecewise-linear sheaves on a finite-dimensional real vector space. We show that they factor, up to a shift, as convolutions of constant sheaves on two bounded convex sets, one closed and the other relatively open. To this end, we first establish a more general characterization of convolution invertibility for compactly supported constructible functions. In the piecewise-linear case, this yields a convex factorization which lifts to sheaves. The key step is a geometric characterization of invertibility in the dual projective space via the Radon transform.

papers.title: Rotating End of the World
papers.abstract: We study the thermodynamics and interior structures of dynamical end of the world (EoW) branes in the rotating BTZ black hole. By mapping the induced metric of the branes to an effective Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) system, we derive the first law of thermodynamics for the boundary conformal field theory (BCFT), incorporating boundary degrees of freedom. To construct this thermodynamics, we adopt two frameworks of black hole chemistry and the duality between the JT black hole and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model. In addition, we verify that the shadow entropy is equivalent to the boundary entropy via Hubeny-Ryu-Takayanagi (HRT) surfaces. Furthermore, we explore the possible interior configurations of the EoW brane inside the horizon. Two representative configurations, namely single and double-joint EoW branes, are considered. These disparate configurations share the same exterior brane configuration outside the horizon. By comparing their energies, we show that a transition could occur within the horizon.

papers.title: Temporal connection probabilities in real networks
papers.abstract: Principled prediction of when and where links form in complex networks is a fundamental problem. We derive a closed-form non-Markovian expression for next-step connection probabilities that unifies latent hyperbolic geometry with long-range memory of past interactions. This expression yields interpretable forecasts governed by a small set of parameters. Applied to large-scale real networks, the framework explains how interaction history changes the distance dependence of connectivity: repeated interactions can remain probable at large distances, whereas first-contact probabilities are consistent with a nonmonotonic distance dependence. The framework's predictions agree quantitatively with empirical connection probabilities. These results provide a common probabilistic description of first contacts and repeated interactions, linking the latent geometry of networks to their temporal connectivity.

papers.title: Thin-Film AlN Microbolometer for Very-Long-Wave Infrared Detection
papers.abstract: We demonstrate a suspended thin-film aluminum nitride (AlN) microbolometer for narrowband very-long-wave infrared detection. The device uses a 100 nm-thick AlN membrane suspended above a Pt back reflector by a 1 $\mu$m air gap. Resonant absorption near 15.4 $\mu$m is set by the AlN transverse optical phonon and is strengthened by suspension above the reflector. A periodic perforation pattern reduces membrane thermal mass, facilitates release, and tunes the effective optical thickness without requiring a thinner deposited film. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) reflection measurements on the released bolometer show approximately 95% peak cavity absorptance near 15.4 $\mu$m with a 0.772 $\mu$m FWHM. DC resistance measurements under tunable infrared illumination verify bolometric operation, with a peak normalized resistive responsivity of 252 ppm/mW at 15.48 $\mu$m. This platform can enable compact wavelength-selective thermal detectors for multispectral imaging, on-chip infrared spectroscopy, and chemical sensing.

papers.title: Composition operators and Rational Inner Functions on the bidisc: A geometric approach
papers.abstract: We study composition operators acting on the weighted Bergman spaces on the bidisc, i.e. $C_{\Phi}:A^2_{\beta}(\mathbb{D}^2)\to A^2_{\beta}(\mathbb{D}^2)$ where $\Phi$ is induced by rational inner functions (RIFs) or a RIF and a smooth function (mixed case). Our approach is geometric. Our main result is a uniform criterion for all $\beta\in(-1,0]$ that can be summarized as follows: Boundedness of the composition operator is equivalent to transversal intersection of the level sets for non-smooth symbols, under the assumption that if any tangential intersection occurs on the singularity it must be of high order. This extends the characterization of Bayart-Kosiński to the non-smooth self maps of the bidisc. To reach our conclusions, we utilize results obtained by Anderson, Bergqvist, Bickel, Cima and Sola on Clark measures associated to RIFs and Puiseux factorizations.

papers.title: The Pentagon Graph Operator
papers.abstract: The pentagon graph $C_5(G)$ of a finite simple graph $G$ is the edge-intersection graph of its induced cycles of length five. We prove that the dodecahedral graph is mapped to the icosahedral graph $I$, which is a fixed point of the operator. Our principal result classifies every graph obtained by adjoining one vertex to $I$: it is eventually fixed if the added vertex belongs to no induced pentagon, and it is expanding otherwise. The proof shows that every new pentagon gives rise to a tadpole hat within at most two iterations. More generally, an induced icosahedral core with $h$ tadpole hats gives the lower bound $12+h2^k$ on the orders of the iterates. We also establish a replication principle and construct two vertex-disjoint induced copies of the Shrikhande graph in its pentagon graph, yielding the bound $16\cdot2^k$. The general vanishing--periodic--expanding trichotomy is included as background.

papers.title: Coordination-number dependent universality in Mixed Wet Percolation
Visual Characteristics of a Rotating Black Hole in $4$D Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity with Thin Accretion Disk Under EHT Constraints
Rare Event Analysis via Stochastic Optimal Control
papers.abstract: Rare events, from biomolecular conformational changes and phase transitions to chemical reactions, are central to many physical systems, yet extremely difficult to study computationally because unbiased simulations seldom produce them. Transition Path Theory provides a rigorous statistical framework for analyzing such events: it characterizes the ensemble of reactive trajectories between two metastable states (reactant and product), and its central object, the committor function (the probability that the system next reaches the product rather than the reactant), encodes essential kinetic and thermodynamic information. We introduce a framework for committor estimation that builds on stochastic optimal control, with a principled formulation that grounds committor learning on capped hitting-time trajectories. In this framework the committor defines a feedback control, proportional to the gradient of its logarithm, that steers trajectories toward the reactive region, enabling sampling of reactive paths. As practical algorithms, we develop two training losses: a heuristic on-policy direct backpropagation loss and a principled off-policy Value Matching loss, for which we establish first-order optimality guarantees. Being off-policy, Value Matching can leverage simulated trajectories from alternative sampling processes and reuse them from a replay buffer, which enables efficient learning. In particular, we derive a reactive current-preserving sampling process that can accelerate exploration. On reversible and non-reversible dynamics, the framework yields more accurate committor estimates, reaction rates, and transition path samples than existing methods.

papers.title: On Higher-Order Geometric Refinements of Classical Covariance Asymptotics: An Approach via Intrinsic and Extrinsic Information Geometry
papers.abstract: Classical Fisher-information asymptotics describe the covariance of regular efficient estimators through the local quadratic approximation of the log-likelihood, and thus capture first-order geometry only. In curved models, including mixtures, curved exponential families, latent-variable models, and manifold-constrained parameter spaces, finite-sample behavior can deviate systematically from these predictions. We develop a coordinate-invariant, curvature-aware refinement by viewing a regular parametric family as a Riemannian manifold \((\Theta,g)\) with Fisher--Rao metric, immersed in \(L^2(\mu)\) through the square-root density map. Under suitable regularity and moment assumptions, we derive an \(n^{-2}\) correction to the leading \(n^{-1}I(\theta)^{-1}\) covariance term for score-root, first-order efficient estimators. The correction is governed by a tensor \(P_{ij}\) that decomposes canonically into three parts, an intrinsic Ricci-type contraction of the Fisher--Rao curvature tensor, an extrinsic Gram-type contraction of the second fundamental form, and a Hellinger discrepancy tensor encoding higher-order probabilistic information not determined by immersion geometry alone. The extrinsic term is positive semidefinite, the full correction is invariant under smooth reparameterization, and it vanishes identically for full exponential families. We then extend the picture to singular models, where Fisher information degenerates. Using resolution of singularities under an additive normal crossing assumption, we describe the resolved metric, the role of the real log canonical threshold in learning rates and posterior mean-squared error, and a curvature-based covariance expansion on the resolved space that recovers the regular theory as a special case. This framework also suggests geometric diagnostics of weak identifiability and curvature-aware principles for regularization and optimization.

papers.title: The Dedekind completion of an Archimedean ordered vector space as a reflector
papers.abstract: We consider the category $\mathbf{AOVS}$ of Archimedean ordered vector spaces with linear maps which preserve all existing nonempty suprema, and its full subcategories $\mathbf{DAOVS}$, $\mathbf{DVL}$ and $\mathbf{UVL}$, consisting of directed spaces, Dedekind complete vector lattices and universally complete vector lattices, respectively. We deduce from some results in the literature that $\mathbf{DVL}$ and $\mathbf{UVL}$ are reflective subcategories of $\mathbf{DAOVS}$, with the usual Dedekind completion being the reflector in $\mathbf{DVL}$. In contrast to these facts, we show that a non-directed Archimedean ordered vector space of dimension greater than $1$ has no reflector in either $\mathbf{DVL}$ or $\mathbf{UVL}$. In particular, there are no free Dedekind complete vector lattices over a set with more than one element. We also use the occasion to show that a free vector lattice with $\alpha$ generators embeds into a free vector lattice with $\beta$ generators if and only if $\alpha\le\beta$, and explore the concept of the free completion of an Archimedean vector lattice with a strong unit.

papers.title: The Schwarzian Derivative for Convex Holomorphic Mappings in Several Complex Variables
papers.abstract: We study the two components of Oda's Schwarzian derivative, the tensor $S_f$ and the quadratic form $S^0_f$, for convex holomorphic mappings of the polydisk and for Roper--Suffridge extensions of convex functions to the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^n$, with norms taken in the Bergman metric. For the polydisk we obtain the sharp bound $\|S_f\|\le\gamma_n$, where $\gamma_n$ is the maximum of an explicit quartic form on the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^n$, with $\gamma_2=2$ and $\gamma_n\to2\sqrt2$, and the sharp bound $\|S^0_f\|\le 4/(n+1)$, $n\ge2$, in both cases the extremal mappings are products of half-plane mappings. For Roper--Suffridge extensions both norms are computed exactly in terms of the Schwarzian derivative of the one-variable function. In particular $S^0_f$ reduces to the classical Schwarzian derivative, and the theorem of Chuaqui, Duren and Osgood yields the sharp bounds $\|S_f\|\le1/\sqrt{n+1}$ and $\|S^0_f\|\le 1/(n+1)$, with equality for the parallel strip.

papers.title: Iterative approach for high-quality binary intensity hologram generation in augmented reality applications
papers.abstract: Binary amplitude spatial light modulators, such as digital micromirror devices (DMDs), are increasingly relevant for computer generated holography due to their high refresh rates, low cost, and due to the emergence of subwavelength pixel architectures. However, the binary constraint limits the reconstruction quality, as conventional approaches rely on a binarization applied as a final step after hologram computation which leads to reduced efficiency and contrast. We introduce an iterative estimation approach for the generation of off axis binary amplitude holograms, in which the binarization constraint is applied at each iteration. We validate the approach through numerical simulations and experimental reconstruction using a DMD based optical setup. Quantitative and qualitative comparisons with random superposition and Gerchberg Saxton methods demonstrate significant improvements in image contrast, light efficiency, and reconstruction fidelity, with comparable computational cost. The proposed method provides a practical route toward high quality CGH using binary modulators and supports emerging applications requiring high speed and high resolution holographic projection.

papers.title: Koszulity in the category $\mathcal{O}$ of the periplectic Lie Superalgebra $\mathfrak{pe}(2)$
papers.abstract: The main result of this paper is to establish precisely which blocks in the Category $\mathcal{O}$ of the periplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{pe}(2)$ are Koszul. It is known that $\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{pe}(2))$ has three blocks up to equivalence; one generic block and two integral blocks. The generic block is known to be Koszul, and the principle integral block is verifiably not Koszul. In this paper, we prove that the remaining of the three blocks of $\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{pe}(2))$ is Koszul. Consequently every non-principal block of $\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{pe}(2))$ is Koszul, which is the category $\mathcal{O}$ analogue, in the smallest case, of a known result for finite-dimensional modules over semisimple extensions of Takiff superalgebras. This is done by explicitly computing the endomorphism algebra of projective modules in this block and then proving that it is Koszul inductively. Along the way, we compute all $\mathrm{Ext}$ groups between simples in this block. To compute the endomorphism algebra we are aided by a computer algebra tool developed in Mathematica, inspired by a post on Stack Exchange.

papers.title: Spectral Dehn Functions: Hyperbolicity, Filling Geometry and Diffusion
papers.abstract: We show that Dirichlet eigenvalues of van Kampen diagrams can distinguish groups whose Dehn functions have the same order. The Dehn function bounds the least filling area in terms of word length. We use the random walk on the faces, stopped at the exterior. For each null word we take the infimum, over its fillings, of the reciprocal of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, then maximize over words of length at most $n$. We call this the spectral Dehn function. Its coarse growth is a quasi-isometry invariant for presentations whose generators form a word ball and whose relators are all null words of length at most three. In such a presentation of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, the boundary word of a square can have a filling with more faces and a larger first eigenvalue than any of its least-area fillings. For two groups with quartic Dehn functions, it is at most $Cn^4$ for one and at least $cn^6/(\log n)^2$ for the other. The spectral Dehn function is bounded exactly for word-hyperbolic groups. For other finitely presented groups it grows at least as fast as $n^2/(\log n)^2$. In these presentations the bound is sharp for non-hyperbolic automatic groups and for non-hyperbolic groups acting properly and cocompactly by isometries on proper geodesic Lipschitz $1$-connected spaces. For the face walk we maximize the expected absorption time over starting faces. In these classes its supremum over least-area fillings of cyclically reduced null words of length at most $n$ has order $n^2$. Taking the infimum over all fillings of each null word before maximizing over words of length at most $n$ gives order $n^2/\log n$ in these presentations. Under a quadratic isoperimetric inequality, every non-hyperbolic group has, for each sufficiently large $n$, a null word of length at most $n$ whose least-area fillings have, for the face and vertex walks, $j$th Dirichlet eigenvalue of order $j/n^2$ for $1\le j\le cn^2$.

papers.title: Sensor Placement for Tsunami Early Warning via Large-Scale Bayesian Optimal Experimental Design
papers.abstract: Real-time tsunami early warning relies on distributed sensor networks to infer seismic sources and seafloor motion. Optimizing these networks via Bayesian optimal experimental design (OED) is exceptionally challenging for systems governed by hyperbolic partial differential equations, which lack the spectral decay required by standard low-rank approximations. We present a scalable Bayesian OED framework for linear time-invariant systems. By reformulating the inverse problem in the data space, we transform OED into dense matrix subset selection. We propose a multi-GPU, Schur-complement-update-based, greedy algorithm that solves the OED problem using a pipelined approach that fully overlaps I/O with GPU computations. Our framework achieves near-perfect weak and strong scaling across hundreds of GPUs on Perlmutter and Frontier. Applied to the 2025 Gordon Bell Prize-winning digital twin for tsunami forecasting in the Cascadia Subduction Zone, we optimize a 175-sensor network, minimizing the uncertainty of a parameter field with over one billion degrees of freedom.

papers.title: Axionlike Particles and Lepton Flavor Violation in Muonic Atoms
One-sided certification of surrogate near-minimizers: exact worst-case envelopes under strong convexity and smoothness
papers.abstract: We study target suboptimality for points that approximately minimize a surrogate objective. Unlike standard uniform perturbation estimates, the available comparison is one-sided, thresholded at a certified lower target level, and restricted to the entire surrogate-selected sublevel set. We first show that selected comparison alone cannot yield a finite worst-case guarantee, even for strongly convex quadratics with identical Hessians. A single scalar upper bound on the surrogate minimum closes this information gap and leads to a sharp general estimate. For pairs of $\mu$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth objectives, we then solve the associated worst-case information problem exactly. We obtain a sharp feasibility barrier and a dimension-free envelope; in its nontrivial regime, the value reduces to a scalar maximization over a compact interval. Explicit one-dimensional piecewise-quadratic objectives attain the bound while satisfying the one-sided constraint on the full selected set. We characterize when curvature strictly improves the general certificate and provide a threshold-preserving finite-net validation procedure. The results identify the best guarantee permitted by the prescribed partial information, independently of any particular optimization algorithm or additive perturbation model.

papers.title: Duality of operator Frobenius algebras and solution of Eisenhart-Stäckel problem in the non-diagonal case
papers.abstract: We study Frobenius algebras of operator fields and introduce a novel notion of duality for them. We show that, under the assumption that the operator fields forming the Frobenius algebra are mutual symmetries, the operator fields in the dual Frobenius algebra are also mutual symmetries. This result allows one to construct new infinite-dimensional integrable systems of hydrodynamic type starting from a given one. As the main application, we solve the long-standing Eisenhart--Stäckel problem for any Segre characteristic and in arbitrary dimension: namely, we describe all nondegenerate finite-dimensional integrable systems whose integrals are quadratic in momenta such that the corresponding $(1,1)$-tensors commute as operator fields.

papers.title: A family of groups extending McLain's
papers.abstract: Given a strict partial order $\Delta$ on a set $\Lambda$ and an arbitrary ring $R$ with $1\neq 0$, the corresponding McLain group $M(\Delta)$ has been studied in depth. We construct a larger family of McLain groups $G(\Delta)$, where $\Delta$ need be neither asymmetric nor transitive, while satisfying two weaker axioms. Structural properties common to all members~$G(\Delta)$ of this new family are investigated, including a group presentation, a description of the factors of its descending central series, a canonical form for its elements relative to any total order on~$\Delta$, and a recursive determination of its upper central series. In addition, we prove the natural isomorphism $G(\Delta)/G(\Gamma)\cong G(\Delta\setminus\Gamma)$, where $\Gamma$ is a normal subset of $\Delta$, and $G(\Gamma)$ and $G(\Delta\setminus\Gamma)$ are extended McLain groups on their own right. This result has no parallel in the classical context.

papers.title: Phase separation by polar active transport
An intertwined short and long $γ$-ray burst with a 4-minute separation
Amortized Inference for Correlated Discrete Choice Models via Equivariant Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Discrete choice models are fundamental tools in management science, economics, and marketing. Logit models dominate applied work because they yield closed-form choice probabilities, but IID Gumbel errors impose restrictive substitution patterns. We propose an amortized inference approach based on a neural network emulator that approximates choice probabilities under general, potentially correlated, error distributions. We develop a specialized neural network architecture respecting the invariance properties of discrete choice models and provide group-theoretic foundations for universal approximation from a minimal set of invariant features. Using Sobolev training, the emulator learns choice probabilities and their derivatives, enabling rapid likelihood and gradient evaluation. We show that emulator-based maximum likelihood estimators are consistent and asymptotically normal under mild approximation conditions. Simulations show substantial gains over the GHK simulator in accuracy and speed. Using NielsenIQ data on household laundry-detergent purchases, we estimate correlated-probit and correlated-Gumbel models with rich household-level random effects. The IID period-error restriction---and hence the conditional-IIA restriction underlying conventional mixed logit---is strongly rejected. The Bayesian information criterion (BIC) selects a correlated-Gumbel model with a three-factor period-error covariance structure. We find that allowing correlated period errors materially changes predicted product substitution patterns.

papers.title: Geometry of Critical Couplings, Quartic Binding, and Spectral Shift for Concentric $δ$-Shells
papers.abstract: We study the first zero-energy resonance of finitely many attractive concentric spherical $\delta$-shells with fixed radii and variable strengths. The positive critical strengths form a smooth hypersurface in coupling space. For every nonzero tangent redistribution we calculate its second fundamental form as an explicit strictly positive quadratic form $C_a$ in cumulative weighted coupling changes. Along the straight perturbation $g_*+\varepsilon a$, the same coefficient determines the unique emerging bound state, $E_b=-C_a^2\varepsilon^4+O(|\varepsilon|^5)$, for either sign of $\varepsilon$, and the crossover of the canonically normalized total spectral shift on the scale $k\asymp\varepsilon^2$. We also give a global smooth parametrization of the positive critical surface by probability weights, determine the exact attainable interval of effective ranges, and reconstruct all critical strengths from individual threshold-pole responses. An exact coupling coordinate gives a uniform $O(k^3)$ spectral-shift normal form and a differentiated $O(k^2)$ estimate without a restriction on the ratio of coupling distance to wave number. The scattering determinant and general threshold exponents are established inputs. Our results give the model-specific curvature coefficient, its spectral consequences, and a complete local and global description of the first-critical configurations.

papers.title: Modeling the Disjunction Effect within Classical Probability: A New Decision Process Model and Comparison with Quantum-like Models
papers.abstract: In a Prisoner's Dilemma experiment, participants defected less often when the opponent's move was unknown than when they were told that the opponent had defected or that the opponent had cooperated. This disjunction effect has often been interpreted as a violation of the classical law of total probability and has motivated quantum-like models of decision making. We re-examine this interpretation and identify a strong assumption implicit in the conventional classical model. The conventional model uses the two informed conditions to represent the full range of participants' expectations and thus treats every participant as certain of the opponent's move even when that move is unknown. We relax this premise by introducing a continuous parameter for each participant's degree of expectation that the opponent will defect. Participants are grouped by expectation level, with the intermediate groups representing ambiguous expectations. A standard quantum-like model offers a different account of this same uncertainty about the opponent's move. In that model, ambiguity arises through superposition, and ambiguous pure states are generic (dense and of full unitarily invariant measure on the unit sphere), so certainty states are mathematically exceptional. Despite this difference in how ambiguity is represented, the proposed classical model can reproduce the observed strong disjunction effect while satisfying the classical law of total probability. More generally, we prove that it can exactly reproduce any triple of defection rates strictly between zero and one, including every such triple generated by the quantum-like model. The proposed model is therefore no less expressive than the quantum-like model for these three observable rates while remaining entirely within classical probability, and the substantive difference between the two lies in how they represent ambiguity and interpret events.

papers.title: Origin of the tetragonal-to-hexagonal phase transitions in Fe-doped BaTiO$_3$
On CR manifolds of CR dimension 1
papers.abstract: We classify all maximal symmetry models of CR dimension 1, depending on their Bloom-Graham and Tanaka types, give coordinate realization to some of those models and prove a general extension principle.

papers.title: Precision Spectroscopy of a Trapped Ion Using a Bath of Ultracold Atoms
papers.abstract: We perform laser spectroscopy of a trapped ion that is not directly laser cooled. An ultracold atomic bath continuously cools the internal degrees of freedom of the ion to its hyperfine ground state via spin-exchange collisions, while a cotrapped $^{174}$Yb$^+$ ion sympathetically cools the external degrees of freedom. Successful laser excitation is detected via state-selective charge transfer following a collision with an atom and subsequent ion loss. As a demonstration of this spectroscopic technique, we probe the $6^2S_{1/2}\rightarrow 6^2P_{3/2}$ transition at 329 nm in $^{173}$Yb$^+$ and measure the magnetic and electric hyperfine interaction constants for the $6^2P_{3/2}$ state to be A = -241(1) MHz and B = 1460(8) MHz, respectively. Our results are in agreement with a previous measurement obtained in a hollow-cathode discharge experiment but are a factor of 6-9 more precise. The techniques demonstrated in this work may be extended to perform precision spectroscopy on ions with complex level structures, with applications in fundamental physics.

papers.title: The AI Layoff Trap
papers.abstract: If AI displaces workers faster than the economy can reabsorb them, it risks eroding the consumer demand firms depend on. We show that knowing this is not enough for firms to stop it. In a competitive task-based economy, each firm captures the full cost saving from automation but bears only a fraction of the demand loss it creates in the product market; the rest falls on rivals. This demand externality traps rational firms in an automation arms race, displacing workers beyond what is collectively optimal. The mechanism harms both workers and firm owners and can survive in general equilibrium. More competition and higher AI productivity can amplify the excess. Wage adjustment, free entry, transfers, worker equity, and Coasean bargaining need not eliminate it. A Pigouvian automation tax implements the cooperative optimum. Policy should address not only the aftermath of automation but also the competitive incentives driving it.

papers.title: Continuity of almost commutative manifolds for the spectral propinquity
papers.abstract: We prove that the canonical metric spectral triples of a fixed compact connected spin manifold depend continuously, for the spectral propinquity, on the Riemannian metric endowed with the $C^1$ topology. This continuity extends to almost commutative spectral triples, allowing the Riemannian metric and the Dirac operator of a fixed finite dimensional factor to vary simultaneously. We also establish continuity for metric spectral triples arising from ergodic actions of compact connected Lie groups as the inner product on the Lie algebra varies. Our proofs use a common continuity criterion involving graph norms and commutator seminorms. As a consequence, eigenvalues in any compact interval whose endpoints avoid the limiting spectrum converge with multiplicity. These results relate classical variations of metric data to the geometry of metric spectral triples.

papers.title: An OASIS of Lyman-$α$ within a neutral intergalactic desert: reaffirmed line and blue continuum reveal efficient ionising agents at $z = 13$
Origin of Reduced Coercive Field in ScAlN: Synergy of Structural Softening and Dynamic Atomic Correlations
Cache-Aided Asymmetric MIMO Communications: Achievable DoF Analysis
papers.abstract: Integrating coded caching (CC) into multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications significantly enhances the achievable degrees of freedom (DoF). This paper investigates a practical cache-aided asymmetric MIMO configuration with cache ratio $\gamma$, where a server with $L$ transmit antennas communicates with $K$ users. The users are partitioned into $J$ groups, and each user in group $j$ has $G_j$ receive antennas. We propose four content-aware MIMO-CC strategies: \emph{min-$G$} enforces symmetry using the smallest antenna count among users; \emph{Grouping} maximizes intra-subset spatial multiplexing gain at the expense of some global caching gain; \emph{Super-grouping} aggregates users into optimized \emph{min-$G$}-based super-sets with identical effective receive multiplexing gains before applying \emph{Grouping} across them; and \emph{Phantom} redistributes spatial resources assuming "phantom" antennas at the users to bridge the performance gains of \emph{min-$G$} and \emph{Grouping}. We develop these asymmetric strategies under three reference symmetric CC placement-delivery policies with guaranteed linear decodability: a finite-search DoF-optimized policy attaining the best single-shot achievable DoF lower bound, and two closed-form policies, namely combinatorial and linear cyclic low-complexity constructions, with the cyclic policy attaining DoF performance close to the others in many operating regimes. Analytical and numerical results demonstrate significant DoF improvements across various system configurations, and that policy-strategy combinations offer flexible trade-offs between DoF and subpacketization complexity.

papers.title: On the size of $\{a: 1\leq a<n, n|a^2-1, a|n^2-1\}$ for number $n$: Connections to Fibonacci-like Sequences and Twin Primes
papers.abstract: For a positive integer n, let $\mathcal{A}(n)$ denote the set of integers $a$ satisfying $1 \leq a < n$ subject to the simultaneous modular conditions \(n \mid a^2 - 1\) and \(a \mid n^2 - 1\). In this paper, we investigate the structural properties and cardinality of \(\mathcal{A}(n)\). By establishing a precise algebraic correspondence between the elements of \(\mathcal{A}(n)\) and the integer evaluations of a family of Fibonacci-like sequences defined by a second-order recurrence, we prove that \(\vert{}\mathcal{A}(n)\vert{} < \log_2 n +2\) for all composite $n > 1$. Trivially, $|\mathcal{A}(n)| = 2$ when $n$ is an odd prime power. Furthermore, we analyze the global distribution of these cardinalities, demonstrating that the asymptotic average of \(\vert{}\mathcal{A}(n)\vert{}\), for $n\leq x$, approaches $2 + o(1)$ as $x \to \infty$. Guided by the properties of the underlying algebraic mapping and supported by computational verification for all $n < 10^{15}$, we formulate the conjecture that $|\mathcal{A}(n)| \le 3$ uniformly for all $n$. In connection with this conjecture, we show that every integer $N$ that is the product of a pair of twin primes satisfies $|\mathcal{A}(N)| = 3$, providing an explicit family of integers $N$ with $|\mathcal{A}(N)| = 3$.

papers.title: On Big-M Reformulations of Bilevel Linear Programs: Hardness of A Posteriori Verification
papers.abstract: A standard approach to solving optimistic bilevel linear programs (BLPs) is to replace the lower-level problem with its Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) optimality conditions and reformulate the resulting complementarity constraints using auxiliary binary variables. This yields a single-level mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model involving big-$M$ parameters. While sufficiently large big-$M$s that preserve at least one bilevel-optimal solution can be computed in polynomial time, verifying a priori that given big-$M$s do not cut off any feasible or optimal lower-level solutions is known to be computationally difficult. In this paper, we establish two complementary hardness results. First, we show that, even with a single potentially incorrect big-$M$ parameter, it is coNP-complete to verify a posteriori whether a given optimal solution of the resulting MILP model is bilevel optimal. In particular, this negative result persists for min-max problems without coupling constraints and applies to strong-duality-based reformulations of mixed-integer BLPs. Second, we show that verifying global big-$M$ correctness remains computationally difficult a posteriori, even when an optimal solution of the MILP model is available.

papers.title: Pooled Inverse Optimization: Learning the Unique Optimal Decision from Repeated Observations
papers.abstract: Inverse optimization infers a decision-maker's objective from observed decisions. We study repeated noisy observations of one decision. Classical formulations impute a separate optimum for each observation, so their size grows with the sample, and may return one of many equally compatible objectives. With a bounded polyhedral feasible set and a cost vector drawn from a distribution with a density, the optimum is almost surely a unique vertex. Its compatible costs form a full-dimensional cone that repeated observations of the same decision cannot shrink. Pooled inverse optimization fits one optimum to all observations and reports its compatible cost cone. Under squared loss, the optimization model has fixed size after aggregation, the decision estimate has a finite-sample error bound, and guarded rounding recovers the true vertex and its full cone with probability tending to one. A single convex program sufficed in every linear scaling run. With 50 variables and 10,000 observations, median runtimes were 8 milliseconds under squared loss and 8 seconds under absolute loss. The standard mixed-integer formulation reached its time limit at 100 observations. At 10,000 observations, the remaining two exact formulations under absolute loss and two convex baselines reached their 10- to 60-minute limits. Using national survey data on women with hypertension and diabetes or prediabetes, the method finds in milliseconds the diet closest to each woman's mean reported intake subject to DASH-based nutrient bounds in a food-group model and identifies which bounds bind.

papers.title: A Dyadic Frequency Law for a Perturbed Hofstadter $Q$-Recursion
papers.abstract: We study the parity-perturbed Hofstadter $Q$-recursion defined by $$Q(1)=Q(2)=1,\qquad Q(n)=Q(n-Q(n-1))+Q(n-Q(n-2))+(-1)^n \quad(n\ge3).$$ for $n\ge3$. Cloître proved that the recursion is globally well-defined and encoded its odd- and even-indexed subsequences by binary arches and canonical plane forests. Let $F(s)=\#\{n\ge1:Q(n)=2s-1\}$, and let $\nu_2(j)$ denote the exponent of $2$ in $j$. For every integer $k\ge0$, we prove the multiset identity $$ \{F(s):2^k\le s<2^{k+1}\}=\{3+\nu_2(j):1\le j\le 2^k\}. $$ The proof expresses frequencies as sums of plateau lengths and folds reflected gap pairs to identify the excess frequencies $F(s)-3$ with the outdegrees of a canonical plane tree. For $k\ge2$, the maximum $k+3$ occurs at $s_k=\lceil 2^{k+2}/3\rceil$, and the second-largest frequency $k+2$ occurs at $s_k+1$. As a corollary, the sum with marks $z^{F(s)-3}$ and dyadic block weights $2^{-ku}$, multiplied by the Dirichlet eta function $\eta(u)$, has the Euler product of $\zeta(u)$ with its factor at $2$ replaced by $(1-z2^{-u})^{-1}$. Finally, we prove that the dyadic defect $Q(2n)-2Q(n)$ attains order $n/\sqrt{\log n}$ in absolute value along a subsequence.

papers.title: From description to design: Automated engineering of complex systems with desirable emergent properties
papers.abstract: Across the sciences, researchers have developed hundreds of statistics that describe the collective behavior of complex systems. These statistics are typically used passively, to describe a system after the fact, so it is rarely learned whether the patterns captured actually matter. The problem of engineering systems that display desirable emergent properties is a less developed area, as the very nature of emergent phenomena challenges the typical bottom-up approach to engineering. Here we propose a top-down approach, re-purposing the large number of descriptive statistics as objective functions in an optimization pipeline. Since this method lets a collective property instantiated directly, it makes long-standing correlational questions amenable to experimentation. We demonstrate this concept on four models taken from four different areas of science: a Kuramoto coupled-oscillator model (physics), a Wilson-Cowan network of excitatory and inhibitory processes (neuroscience), an SIRS pandemic spread model (epidemiology), and an echo-state network (machine learning). In each case, we take measures commonly used to describe behavior and feed those descriptive statistics back into the system to sculpt desirable macro-scale properties into the fundamental generative dynamics. We find that this approach is successful across domains and systems, and the inclusion of ``emergent" measures can actually improve the ability of some systems to perform tasks. We argue these threads can be unified into a general practice of emergent engineering that combines traditional task-oriented, bottom-up approaches to engineering with top-down guidance of collective, emergent properties to build resilient, capable, complex systems.

papers.title: The Lee-Huang-Yang energy for a dilute gas of hard spheres: an upper bound
papers.abstract: We consider a quantum gas consisting of $N$ hard spheres with radius $\frak{a} > 0$, obeying bosonic statistics and moving in the box $\Lambda = [0;L]^3$ with periodic boundary conditions. We are interested in the ground state energy per unit volume in the thermodynamic limit, with $N, L \to \infty$ at fixed density $\rho = N / L^3$. We derive an upper bound for the ground state energy density, matching the famous Lee-Huang-Yang formula, up to lower order terms, in the dilute limit $\rho \frak{a}^3 \ll 1$.

papers.title: What is a minimum work transition in stochastic thermodynamics?
A Trust-Region Interior-Point Stochastic Sequential Quadratic Programming Method
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a trust-region interior-point stochastic sequential quadratic programming (TR-IP-SSQP) method for solving optimization problems with a stochastic objective and deterministic nonlinear equality and inequality constraints. In this setting, exact evaluations of the objective function and its gradient are unavailable, but their stochastic estimates can be constructed. In particular, at each iteration our method builds stochastic oracles whose estimates of the objective value and gradient satisfy proper adaptive accuracy conditions with a fixed probability. To handle inequality constraints, we adopt an interior-point method (IPM), in which the barrier parameter is taken from a prescribed decreasing sequence and is reduced once a stochastic stationarity test is passed. Under standard assumptions, we show that, almost surely, the KKT residual vanishes along the iterations at which the barrier parameter is reduced, and every limit point of these iterates is a KKT point. We implement the method on a subset of problems from the CUTEst test set, as well as on constrained logistic regression problems, to demonstrate its practical performance.

papers.title: Fluctuation imaging of disorder in monolayer semiconductors
The Marked Power Spectrum as a Practical Bispectrum Measure for Galaxy Redshift Surveys
Mixed-state Phases from Higher-order SSPTs with Kramers-Wannier Symmetry
Econometric vs. Causal structure learning for time-series data: Implications for policy interventions using COVID-19 data
papers.abstract: This study compares regression-based and causal structure-learning approaches to recovering temporal dependencies in UK COVID-19 data and assesses their suitability for policy analysis. We evaluate four econometric methods and eleven structure-learning algorithms using a common lag-expanded dataset that permits edges only from past to current variables. The dataset comprises 866 daily observations and 45 variables, represented by 55 numeric series after categorical encoding. Maximum lags of 1, 7, 14, 17 and 21 days are examined; all four econometric methods and ten structure-learning algorithms successfully return structures at every lag specification. We compare graph structure, complexity, fit and temporal-edge stability across lag specifications. The resulting graphs vary substantially in density, complexity, fit and stability. Agreement with the knowledge graph is limited, while low structural Hamming distance sometimes reflects sparsity rather than recovery of known relationships. Edge recurrence also varies markedly by method, revealing sensitivity to the allowed history window. Diagnostics for VAR models using all lagged predictors indicate residual dependence, non-normality and instability; estimation becomes infeasible at longer lag orders. Policy evaluation raises further concerns: few mobility-to-infection links emerge, few meet the empirical coverage criterion, and none do so in longer-lag analyses. Common temporal constraints therefore do not resolve methodological disagreement. Learnt dependency structures should not be treated as policy-ready causal models without stronger identification assumptions, robustness checks and sufficient empirical support for the interventions assessed.

papers.title: Modeling individual nearby radio galaxies as ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray accelerators
Quantile-Based Skewness for Fuzzy Numbers With Probabilistic Foundations: An Application in Portfolio Optimization
papers.abstract: This article quantifies asymmetry under imprecision by introducing a probabilistic interpretation for fuzzy numbers and a non-moment based skewness coefficient derived from it. The coefficient adapts classical quantile-based skewness measures (Bowley, Kelley, and Groeneveld-Meeden) to the $\alpha$-cut representation of fuzzy numbers. Existing studies typically modify the classical Fisher-Pearson formula heuristically, substituting membership functions for probability densities without a rigorous semantic bridge between the two. Our coefficient, in contrast, is grounded in an explicit probabilistic interpretation, making it both mathematically meaningful and aligned with the semantics of fuzzy set theory. We interpret a fuzzy number's left and right membership function components as cumulative and survival probability functions of associated two random variables $X_L$ and $X_R$. This yields a reading of its $\alpha$-cuts as generalized quantiles, i.e., intervals of values that are "at least $(1-\alpha)$-probable", highlighting a duality between probability and possibility theory. As a quantile-based measure, the coefficient is invariant under scale and location transformations. Its point-based variant needs only a fixed number of quantile evaluations, constant time in the $\alpha$-discretization, compared with the linear cost of moment-based alternatives. The coefficient comprises two complementary constituents: an "inner" measure quantifying the intrinsic skewness of the underlying probabilistic distributions, and an "outer" measure capturing the fuzzy number's overall profile asymmetry. We illustrate the measures within a fuzzy mean-variance-skewness portfolio optimization framework on historical equity data, comparing their performance with two of the most highly cited moment-based fuzzy skewness coefficients from the literature.

papers.title: An Alternative Proof of an Erd\H os-Rényi Law for the Longest Consecutive Monotone Block in a Random Permutation
papers.abstract: $\{X_j\}_{j=1}^\infty$ of i.i.d.~($p$) coin-tosses, the longest run $L_n$ of heads in the first $n$ coin tosses approaches $\log_{1/p}n$ almost surely. In this paper we explore a formulation of this result in the case of random permutations and prove an Erd\H os-Rényi law for the longest consecutive monotone block in a random permutation. This problem has been studied before by several authors, and we offer a Poisson approximation viewpoint on this issue using the Stein-Chen method.

papers.title: Pricing with an Informed Buyer
papers.abstract: We study prior-independent pricing for a single seller and a single buyer when the seller has access to only one sample from the buyer's value distribution, whereas the buyer knows the distribution. Existing robust-pricing approaches either rely on distributional statistics, which may require many samples to estimate, or use realized samples to determine a price or mechanism before the buyer decides whether to purchase. We bridge these regimes by exploiting the buyer's informational advantage: policies that ordinarily require the seller to know a statistic such as the mean, an $L^\eta$-norm, or a superquantile can be implemented with a single private sample. We introduce sample-contingent mechanisms: the seller commits ex ante to a transfer rule, and the buyer participates and reports before observing the sample. Subject to standard regularity conditions, every concave pricing policy is implementable in this way. To evaluate performance, we reduce the worst-case analysis of any monotone pricing policy over $\alpha$-regular distributions to two parametric boundary families. This reduction allows us to characterize the optimal monotone sample-contingent mechanism; for monotone hazard rate (MHR) distributions, it attains an approximation ratio between $0.791$ and $0.796$. We also establish impossibility results for concave pricing policies. Finally, the same framework applies to statistic-based robust pricing, unifying the statistic-based and sample-based approaches.

papers.title: Fast, High-Accuracy, Randomized Nullspace Computations for Tall Matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop RLOBPCG, an efficient method for computing a small number of singular triplets corresponding to the smallest singular values of large, tall matrices. The algorithm combines randomized preconditioner from the sketch-and-precondition techniques with the LOBPCG eigensolver: a small sketch is used to construct a high-quality preconditioner, and LOBPCG is run on the Gram matrix to refine the singular vector. Under the standard subspace embedding assumption and a modest singular value gap between the two smallest singular values, we prove that RLOBPCG converges geometrically to the minimum singular vector. In numerical experiments, RLOBPCG achieves near-optimal accuracy on matrices with up to $10^6$ rows, outperforming classical LOBPCG and Lanczos methods by a speedup of up to $12\times$ and maintaining robustness when other iterative methods fail to converge.

papers.title: Universal electrical transport of composite Fermi liquid to Metal transition in Moiré systems
Pulsar Timing Array in the past decade
Dark Energy Survey Year 6 Results: Cosmological Constraints from Cosmic Shear
authors: DES Collaboration : T. M. C. Abbott

papers.title: Uniform Property (S)
papers.abstract: We introduce and investigate a quantitative version of Steinhaus' property$(S)$ for Banach spaces, called the \emph{uniform property$(S)$}. A Banach space$X$ is said to have uniform$(S)$ if for every pair of distinct unit vectors $x,y\in X$ and every $a>0$, the difference of the perturbed norms $$ \sup_{\|z\|\le a}\big|\|x+z\|-\|y+z\|\big| $$ is bounded below by a positive function of$a$ and$\|x-y\|$. We compute this modulus exactly for the spaces $L_1(\mu)$ with atomless measure$\mu$, $$ U_{L_1(\mu)}(d;a)=\Big(\tfrac{4a}{2+d}\wedge 1\Big)d. $$ The class of spaces with uniform$(S)$ is stable under ultrapowers, Bochner-$L_1$ constructions, and contains all Gurari\uı spaces as well as Banach lattices of almost universal disposition. In particular, every Banach space embeds isometrically into a non-strictly convex Banach space of the same density having uniform$(S)$. We further exhibit an explicit equivalent renorming of$\ell_1(\Gamma)$, $$ \|x\|_S=\big(\|x\|_1^2+\|x\|_2^2\big)^{1/2}, $$ which endows$\ell_1(\Gamma)$ and all its ultrapowers with uniform$(S)$. These results settle, in ZFC, several open questions about the quantitative geometry of property$(S)$ posed by Kochanek and the second-named author.

papers.title: On the Meta-Design of Allocation Problems
papers.abstract: There is an extensive literature that studies how to find optimal policies in resource allocation problems, taking the underlying design parameters that define the allocation, such as what data is collected, how many people can be served, and quality of service as fixed constraints. Yet, from a planner's perspective, these design parameters are themselves optimization variables that are just as important in determining overall welfare as selecting the optimal targeting rule for a given set of constraints. This realization motivates a rich set of meta-design questions exploring how planners should make principled decisions about investments in prediction, capacity constraints, and treatment quality, all of which lie upstream of classical policy optimization. Building on initial theoretical work in this space, our paper has three main contributions. First, we formally define the broad meta-design space of resource allocation problems. Second, we develop empirical tools that enable practitioners to reliably navigate it. Third, we demonstrate the framework in two real-world case studies on German employment services and targeted cash transfer programs in Ethiopia.

papers.title: GKM Theory for Manifolds of Isospectral Matrices in Lie Type D
papers.abstract: We study the manifold $Q_{\Gamma, \lambda}$ of isospectral real skew-symmetric matrices with a prescribed sparsity pattern determined by a graph $\Gamma$. The compact torus $T^n$ acts naturally on $Q_{\Gamma,\lambda}$ by conjugation, and this action can be studied using GKM theory. We prove two results about this manifold and its GKM graph. The first theorem describes how the GKM graph of $Q_{\Gamma, \lambda}$ is obtained from the GKM graph of the corresponding manifold $M_{\Gamma, \lambda}$ of isospectral Hermitian matrices. The second theorem shows that equivariant formality of $Q_{\Gamma,\lambda}$ implies equivariant formality of $M_{\Gamma,\lambda}$, whereas the converse fails.

papers.title: Correlation Calibration: A Hybrid Calibration Technique for Radio Interferometric Arrays
How much perceived-stress signal is in the maternal ECG? An exclusion bound across deep-learning and heart-rate-variability representations in pregnancy
papers.abstract: Deep learning can read physiological states from the electrocardiogram (ECG), prompting attempts to detect psychological stress. We asked how much information about perceived stress the maternal ECG carries. In 144 pregnant women, with every cross-validation split taken over participants, across 94 arms spanning 21 self-supervised, foundation-model, and heart-rate-variability architectures, the best discrimination of moderate-to-high stress (PSS-10 >= 19) was AUC 0.604 (95% CI 0.511-0.696), and AUC >= 0.70 was rejected in all eleven arms tested. Three pre-registered tests in a second cohort from the same center, recorded on different hardware, were null, at 30% power. Which of the three simultaneously recorded ECG channels was analyzed accounted for 96% of the predicted score's variance, against 4% between women; across 20 combinations of channel rule, label variant, and visit, the external correlation with perceived stress ranged from r = -0.095 to r = +0.307, a spread no larger than such a search produces by chance (raw one-sided p of the maximum 0.011; calibrated max-statistic p = 0.583). Hair cortisol was not predicted either. In the second cohort, PSS-10 scores were not stable across administrations spanning pregnancy and the postpartum period (ICC 0.06-0.16), so one administration is a weak measure of a woman's stress level at another visit. A single-recording ECG screener for perceived stress is excluded in this population, and multi-channel studies must pre-register their channel rule.

papers.title: Physics-Based Learning of the Wave Speed Landscape in Complex Media
papers.abstract: The propagation of waves through complex, inhomogeneous media is a fundamental challenge across scales, from optics to geophysics. In such environments, the waves reflected by the medium are typically dominated by a random speckle pattern, a complex interference resulting from multiple scattering by fine-scale heterogeneities. While this speckle is traditionally viewed as a source of noise that blurs the medium's structure, it contains rich information about the underlying wave speed landscape. Here, we introduce a physics-based learning framework that reconstructs the velocity distribution from the reflection matrix of the medium. We show how the speckle wave-field can be exploited to probe the focusing quality, serving as an intrinsic guide star to evaluate the local consistency of the velocity model. By representing wave propagation as a differentiable multi-layer network, we leverage optimization tools to solve the inverse problem and infer the wave speed map. We validate this approach through ultrasound experiments in highly scattering tissue-mimicking phantoms and human breast tissues, demonstrating its potential for tumor detection and characterization where standard methods fail. This synergy between wave physics and gradient-based optimization provides a general paradigm for non-invasive tomography in any complex environment where reflection data is available.

papers.title: Gradually opening Schrödinger's box reveals a cascade of sharp dynamical transitions
A single field inflationary model consistent with recent observations: reheating and radiative stability
Beyond First-Order: Learning Riemannian Geometries for Invariant Visual Place Recognition
papers.abstract: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) demands representations robust to drastic environmental and viewpoint shifts. Existing aggregation paradigms either depend on extensive supervised training or rely on first-order pooling, often struggling to preserve structural correlations under extreme shifts or incurring high adaptation costs. In this work, we propose Riemannian Invariant Aggregation (RIA), a unified geometric framework that explicitly models second-order scene structure on the Symmetric Positive Definite (SPD) manifold.
