Bonferroni emerges as the $\gamma \to 0$ limit and becomes overly conservative under asymptotic dependence. These results provide theoretical support for using truncated Cauchy or Pareto combination tests, offering a principled approach to enhance power while controlling false positives under complex dependence.

papers.title: Distributed Constraint-coupled Resource Allocation: Anytime Feasibility and Violation Robustness
papers.abstract: This paper considers distributed resource allocation problems (DRAPs) with a coupled constraint for real-time systems. Based on primal-dual methods, we adopt a control perspective for optimization algorithm design by synthesizing a safe feedback controller using control barrier functions to enforce constraint satisfaction. On this basis, a distributed anytime-feasible resource allocation (DanyRA) algorithm is proposed. It is shown that the DanyRA algorithm converges to the exact optimal solution of DRAPs while preserving feasibility of the coupled inequality constraint from a feasible initialization. To address constraint violations caused by external disturbances, we develop a recover-after-violation mechanism using a virtual queue with a minimum buffer, enabling feasibility recovery within a prescribed number of iterations. We characterize the trade-off between convergence accuracy and violation robustness for a fixed positive buffer and establish exact convergence with a suitably decaying buffer. DanyRA is further specialized to coupled equality constraints, with constraint preservation and an explicit linear convergence rate established. Finally, a numerical example is provided for verification.

papers.title: Finite element conformal complexes in three dimensions
papers.abstract: This paper develops three-dimensional finite element conformal Hessian and conformal elasticity complexes through a local-bubble Bernstein-Gelfand-Gelfand (BGG) construction parameterized by smoothness vectors. These complexes incorporate higher-order differential operators, including the linearized Cotton-York operator, and require conformal tensor spaces (i.e., symmetric and traceless tensor spaces) with nontrivial smoothness and trace conditions. We apply the discrete BGG framework at the level of local bubble complexes parameterized by vertex, edge, and face smoothness vectors, together with geometric bubble decompositions and a reduction operation. This yields exact bubble complexes over explicit admissible regularity ranges, together with the face-bubble exactness needed to assemble families of global conforming complexes with varying vertex, edge, and face smoothness. The construction recovers known conformal Hessian and conformal elasticity complexes as particular choices, while producing broader smoothness-parameterized families, including new exact conformal elasticity complexes with strictly weaker interelement continuity. The resulting complexes provide structure-preserving finite element building blocks for applications in relativity, Cosserat elasticity, and fluid mechanics.

papers.title: SpA2V: Harnessing Spatial Auditory Cues for Audio-driven Spatially-aware Video Generation
papers.abstract: Audio-driven video generation aims to synthesize realistic videos that align with input audio recordings, akin to the human ability to visualize scenes from auditory input. However, existing approaches predominantly focus on exploring semantic information, such as the classes of sounding sources present in the audio, limiting their ability to generate videos with accurate content and spatial composition. In contrast, we humans can not only naturally identify the semantic categories of sounding sources but also determine their deeply encoded spatial attributes, including locations and movement directions. This useful information can be elucidated by considering specific spatial indicators derived from the inherent physical properties of sound, such as loudness or frequency. As prior methods largely ignore this factor, we present SpA2V, the first framework explicitly exploits these spatial auditory cues from audios to generate videos with high semantic and spatial correspondence. SpA2V decomposes the generation process into two stages: 1) Audio-guided Video Planning: We meticulously adapt a state-of-the-art MLLM for a novel task of harnessing spatial and semantic cues from input audio to construct Video Scene Layouts (VSLs). This serves as an intermediate representation to bridge the gap between the audio and video modalities. 2) Layout-grounded Video Generation: We develop an efficient and effective approach to seamlessly integrate VSLs as conditional guidance into pre-trained diffusion models, enabling VSL-grounded video generation in a training-free manner. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SpA2V excels in generating realistic videos with semantic and spatial alignment to the input audios.

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Decentralized Stochastic Minimax Optimization
papers.abstract: We study decentralized stochastic nonconvex Polyak--Łojasiewicz minimax problems. Motivated by local SGD in federated learning, we improve communication efficiency by allowing agents to perform several local updates before the communication stage. Existing work gives a communication bound of $\mathcal{O}\Big(\frac{\kappa^3\varepsilon^{-2}}{(1-\lambda)^2}\Big)$ for local decentralized gradient descent--ascent using $\mathcal{O}\Big(\varepsilon^{-2}+\frac{\kappa^2\varepsilon^{-2}}{K(1-\lambda)}\Big)$ local updates per round. Here $\varepsilon$ is the target accuracy, $1-\lambda$ is the spectral gap and $\kappa\ge1$ is the condition number. However, too many local updates can leave available communication resources underused and increase local drift, as agents follow their own objectives for longer before exchanging information. We therefore pursue improved communication efficiency while keeping the number of local steps small. To this end, we propose DiMA, a structured local--global learning strategy that uses local updates to build an accelerated momentum and perform decentralized learning through either standard gossip or accelerated mixing. By exploiting the positive semidefiniteness of the mixing matrix, we derive complexity bounds for DiMA under different updating strategies. Experiments on robust logistic regression demonstrate improved performance over several existing baselines.

papers.title: Dirac reduction algebra
papers.abstract: There is a homomorphism of associative superalgebras from the enveloping algebra of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ to the Weyl-Clifford superalgebra $A(2n|n)$ with $2n$ even Weyl algebra generators and $n$ odd Clifford algebra generators. Under this homomorphism, the positive odd root vector $x\in\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ is sent to the Dirac operator $\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu\in A(2n|n)$ and generates a left ideal $I$. The corresponding reduction (super)algebra, denoted $Z_n$, is the normalizer of $I$ in $A(2n|n)$ modulo $I$. By construction, $Z_n$ acts on the space of all Clifford algebra-valued polynomial solutions to the (massless) Dirac equation. This setting goes back to Zhelobenko, who described generators of this reduction algebra and commutation relations among them. In this paper, we find a complete presentation of (a localization of) this so-termed Dirac reduction algebra, with full proofs. We give a closed formula for products of the raising operators in the reduction algebra and use it to write down explicitly the polynomial solutions to the Dirac equation in $n$-dimensional flat spacetime that they generate. Finally, we show that for $n\neq 2$ the space of polynomial solutions is irreducible over the reduction algebra tensored with the opposite Clifford algebra when $n$ is even, and is a direct sum of two irreducible submodules when $n$ is odd.

papers.title: Chirp-Permuted AFDM: A Versatile and Multifunctional Waveform for 6G
papers.abstract: We present a novel multicarrier waveform, termed chirp-permuted affine frequency division multiplexing (CP-AFDM), which introduces a unique chirp-permutation domain on top of the chirp subcarriers of the conventional AFDM. Rigorous analysis of the signal model and waveform properties demonstrates that the proposed CP-AFDM waveform preserves all core characteristics of affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) - including robustness to doubly-dispersive channels, peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), and integrated sensing and communications (ISAC)-enabling full delay-Doppler representation - while introducing a new degree-of-freedom without any loss of these properties. Given this, by exploiting the vast chirp-permutation domain, two selected exemplary multifunctional applications are presented: an index modulation (IM) technique over the permutation domain which achieves significant spectral efficiency gains, and a physical-layer security scheme that ensures practically perfect security through permutation-based keying, without requiring additional transmit energy or signaling over-head. In all, these characteristics establish CP-AFDM as a highly attractive candidate for emerging sixth generation (6G) use cases demanding reliability, sensing-awareness, and multifunctionality.

papers.title: CMB constraints on $U(1)$ axion warm inflation
Stable and Fair Benefit Allocation in Mixed-Energy Truck Platooning: A Coalitional Game Approach
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the benefit allocation in a mixed-energy truck platoon composed of fuel-powered and electric trucks. The interactions among trucks during platoon formation are modeled as a coalitional game with transferable utility. We first design a stable payoff allocation scheme that accounts for truck heterogeneity in energy savings and platoon roles (leader or follower), establishing core-stability conditions to ensure that no subset of trucks has an incentive to deviate for greater benefit. To enhance payoff fairness, we then propose a closed-form, Shapley value-based allocation approach that is computationally efficient and independent of the platoon size. Sufficient conditions under which the allocation is both fair and core-stable are provided. In scenarios where the Shapley value falls outside the core, we develop an alternative allocation based on the stable payoff that minimizes the mean relative deviation from the Shapley value while preserving core stability. This deviation is further proved to be upper-bounded by $1$, showing a favorable trade-off between stability and fairness. Finally, extensive numerical studies validate the theoretical results and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in facilitating stable, equitable, and sustainable cooperation in mixed-energy truck platooning.

papers.title: Prescribed Time Higher Order Control Lyapunov-Barrier Functions
papers.abstract: We propose a framework based on Repeated-Root Prescribed Time Higher-Order Control Lyapunov- Barrier Functions (RR-Pxt-HOCL-BF) that guarantees convergence to a safe set/ goal set within user-specified time. Unlike conventional Higher-Order Control Barrier Functions, which does not provide any guarantee on reaching the safe set if the system is initially not in safe set, the proposed method enforces convergence within a prescribed time horizon. This is achieved through a structured differential constraint derived from repeated roots of the characteristic polynomial, leading to closed-form polynomial solutions that ensure convergence at the desired time. Analytical conditions for forward invariance and prescribed-time reachability are derived, with explicit formulations for second-order systems. The approach is validated on an acceleration-controlled unicycle and an inverted pendulum and compared with existing HOCBF methods. Simulation results demonstrate reliable convergence within the desired time horizon, even in scenarios where conventional approaches fail.

papers.title: Interaction-enhanced quantum to classical transport crossover temperature in a Luttinger liquid
Exact Solutions to the Klein--Gordon Equation via Reduction Algebras
papers.abstract: Reduction algebras (also known as generalized Mickelsson algebras, Zhelobenko algebras, or transvector algebras) are well-studied associative algebras appearing in the representation theory of Lie algebras. In the 1990s, Zhelobenko noted that reduction algebras have a connection to field equations from physics, whereas Howe's study of dual pairs in the 1980s signifies that the link originated even earlier. In this paper, we revisit the simplest case of a massless scalar field, in arbitrary spacetime dimension $n\ge 3$ and arbitrary flat metric $\eta_{ab}$; the field equation then specializes to the Laplace equation and to the massless Klein--Gordon equation. The relevant reduction algebra comes from a representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ (technically, $\mathfrak{sp}_2$) by differential operators. We give a complete presentation of this reduction algebra. Its raising operators produce bosonic states $|a_1a_2\cdots a_\ell\rangle$, polynomial solutions of degree $\ell$ to the field equation, and we show that the natural bilinear form on these states is computed by symmetrizers built from the rational dynamical R-matrix. Along the way we give explicit formulas for the states, and a self-contained proof, for a general metric, of Zhelobenko's results that they span the polynomial solutions and that the solution space is an irreducible module over the reduction algebra.

papers.title: Hall--Littlewood expansions of chromatic quasisymmetric functions using linked rook placements
papers.abstract: In this work, we obtain a Hall--Littlewood expansion of the chromatic quasisymmetric function arising from a natural unit interval order and describe the coefficients in terms of linked rook placements. Applying the Carlsson--Mellit relation between chromatic quasisymmetric functions and unicellular LLT polynomials, we also obtain a combinatorial description for the coefficients of the unicellular LLT polynomials expanded in terms of the modified transformed Hall--Littlewood polynomials.

papers.title: The Hamilton cycle space of random graphs
papers.abstract: The cycle space of a graph $G$, denoted $\mathcal{C}(G)$, is a vector space over ${\mathbb F}_2$, spanned by all incidence vectors of edge-sets of cycles of $G$. If $G$ has $n$ vertices, then $\mathcal{C}_n(G)$ denotes the subspace of $\mathcal{C}(G)$, spanned by the incidence vectors of Hamilton cycles of $G$. A classical result in the theory of random graphs asserts that for $G \sim \mathbb{G}(n,p)$, asymptotically almost surely the necessary condition $\delta(G) \geq 2$ is also sufficient to ensure Hamiltonicity. Resolving a problem of Christoph, Nenadov, and Petrova, we augment this result by proving that $\mathcal{C}_n(G) = \mathcal{C}(G)$ holds asymptotically almost surely for $G \sim \mathbb{G}(n,p)$, with $n$ being odd and $p := p(n) \geq (\log n + 2 \log \log n + \omega(1))/n$. That is, not only does $G$ typically have a Hamilton cycle, but its Hamilton cycles are typically rich enough to span its cycle space. It is known and easy to show that if $p := p(n) \leq (\log n + 2 \log \log n - \omega(1))/n$, then a.a.s. $\mathcal{C}_n(G) \neq \mathcal{C}(G)$ unless $G$ is a forest.

papers.title: orGAN: A Synthetic Data Augmentation Pipeline for Simultaneous Generation of Surgical Images and Ground Truth Labels
papers.abstract: Deep learning for surgical image analysis is constrained by limited data diversity, ethical restrictions, high acquisition costs, and the scarcity of accurately annotated bleeding datasets, making reliable bleeding localization particularly challenging. To address these limitations, we propose orGAN, a modular framework that generates realistic, fully annotated synthetic surgical bleeding images together with recoverable point-level supervision. To overcome the ethical and cost barriers of real surgical data, the pipeline is trained on silicone-based mimicking organs that reproduce tissue properties, using an enhanced StyleGAN3 generator coupled with Relational Positional Learning to embed bleeding coordinates, a Surgical Label Detection Algorithm to recover coordinate and mask labels, and a fine-tuned LaMa inpainting network to restore clean image-label pairs. To compensate for scarce annotations, Bleeding Alert Map (BAM) localization models are trained on a blend of synthetic and mimicking-organ images. The enhanced StyleGAN3 attains an Inception Score of 2.24, and the inpainting network preserves realism at a mean SSIM of 0.98. The blended model outperforms both single-source baselines, reaching a Dice coefficient of 0.635 on paired bleeding frames. With a stronger Pix2PixHD backbone, Dice rises to 0.893 with a centroid error of 6.3 pixels. On real Hamlyn surgical video, the blended model achieves a frame-level accuracy of 0.858 and a bleeding-frame detection rate of 0.998 on Hamlyn 2, where all 500 frames were annotated as bleeding-positive. These results show that combining realistic synthetic images with mimicking-organ data is an effective, ethical, and economical strategy for developing surgical AI under limited annotated data.

papers.title: Fractional Sobolev spaces and fractional $p$-Laplace equations on locally finite graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first define a discrete version of the fractional Laplace operator $(-\Delta)^{s}$ through the heat semigroup on a stochastically complete, connected, locally finite graph. Moreover, we introduce a fractional Sobolev space, which is necessary when we study problems involving $(-\Delta)^{s}$. Thirdly, we define the fractional divergence, and then give another form of $(-\Delta)^s$, which leads to a formula of integration by parts. Finally, using the mountain-pass theorem and the Nehari manifold, we obtain multiplicity solutions to a discrete fractional Schrödinger equation. We caution the readers that though these existence results are well known in the continuous case, the discrete case is quite different.

papers.title: Quantum cosmological perturbations in bouncing models with mimetic dark matter
An Introduction to Algebraic Combinatorics
papers.abstract: This is an introduction to algebraic combinatorics, written for a quarter-long graduate course. It starts with a rigorous introduction to formal power series with some combinatorial applications, then discusses integer partitions (proving Jacobi's triple product identity), permutations (Lehmer codes, cycles) and subtractive methods (alternating sums, cancellations and inclusion-exclusion principles, with a particular focus on sign-reversing involutions and determinants). The last chapter introduces symmetric polynomials and proves the Littlewood--Richardson rule using Bender--Knuth involutions (a la Stembridge). The appendix contains over 200 exercises (without solutions).

papers.title: Distribution free M-estimation
papers.abstract: The basic question of delineating those statistical problems that are solvable without making any assumptions on the underlying data distribution has long animated statistics and learning theory. This paper characterizes when a convex M-estimation or stochastic optimization problem is solvable in such an assumption-free setting, providing a precise dividing line between solvable and unsolvable problems. The conditions we identify show, perhaps surprisingly, that Lipschitz continuity of the loss being minimized is not necessary for distribution free minimization, and they are also distinct from classical characterizations of learnability in machine learning.

papers.title: FGAS: Fixed Decoder Network-Based Audio Steganography with Adversarial Perturbation Generation
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) has made high-fidelity generated audio widely available across the Internet, driving the advancement of audio steganography. Benefiting from advances in deep learning, current audio steganography schemes are mainly based on encoder-decoder network architectures. While these methods achieve promising perceptual quality, they typically require network pre-training, and maintaining anti-steganalysis performance at high payloads remains challenging. To address these issues, we propose Fixed Decoder Network-Based Audio Steganography with Adversarial Perturbation Generation (FGAS). Adversarial perturbations carrying a secret message are embedded into the cover audio to generate stego audio. The sender and receiver independently construct the same fixed decoder from a shared architecture and initialization key, avoiding the transfer of trained decoder parameters. In FGAS, we propose an Audio Adversarial Perturbation Generation (A2PG) strategy with an optional robust extension and design a lightweight fixed decoder. The fixed decoder guarantees reliable extraction of the hidden message, while adversarial perturbations are optimized to keep the stego audio perceptually and statistically close to the cover audio, thereby improving anti-steganalysis performance. The experimental results show that FGAS significantly improves stego audio quality, achieving an average PSNR gain of over 10 dB compared to SOTA methods. Furthermore, FGAS demonstrates strong robustness against common audio processing attacks. Moreover, FGAS exhibits superior anti-steganalysis performance across different relative payloads; under high-capacity embedding, it achieves a classification error rate about 2% higher, indicating stronger anti-steganalysis performance than current SOTA methods.

papers.title: Learning mechanical systems from real-world data using discrete forced Lagrangian dynamics
papers.abstract: We introduce a data-driven method for learning the equations of motion of mechanical systems directly from position measurements. This is particularly relevant in system identification tasks where only positional information is available, such as motion capture, pixel data or low-resolution tracking. Our approach takes advantage of the discrete Lagrange-d'Alembert principle and the forced discrete Euler-Lagrange equations to construct a physically grounded model of the system's dynamics. We decompose the dynamics into conservative and non-conservative components, which are learned separately using feed-forward neural networks. In the absence of external forces, our method reduces to a variational discretization of the action principle naturally preserving the symplectic structure of the underlying Hamiltonian system. We validate our approach on a variety of synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness compared to baseline methods. In particular, we apply our model to (1) measured human motion data and (2) latent embeddings obtained via an autoencoder trained on image sequences. We demonstrate that we can faithfully reconstruct and separate both the conservative and forced dynamics, yielding interpretable and physically consistent predictions

papers.title: Fourier inequalities and sign uncertainty
papers.abstract: Motivated by inequalities in Fourier analysis, we present an improvement on the lower bound for the sign uncertainty principle of Bourgain, Clozel and Kahane in high dimensions. Additionally, our methods can be used to match the existing Torquato-Stillinger lower bounds for the Cohn-Elkies linear program for sphere packing.

papers.title: Regular polygons
Channel coding against quantum jammers via minimax
papers.abstract: We study classical communication over fully quantum arbitrarily varying channels, in which a jammer can prepare an arbitrary state entangled across channel uses. We formulate assisted codes as joint input-output maps and apply Sion's minimax theorem to exchange optimization over codes and jamming states at fixed message size. Combining this reduction with one-shot coding bounds and a generalized quantum asymptotic equipartition property yields a single-letter formula for the entanglement-assisted classical capacity, a single-letter formula for the shared-randomness-assisted capacity of classical-quantum channels, and a regularized formula for general quantum input channels. For entanglement assistance and for shared-randomness-assisted classical-quantum channels, we extend the capacity formulas to arbitrary jammer Hilbert spaces while keeping the sender and receiver systems finite-dimensional. The extension uses finite-dimensional approximations at each blocklength, a uniform bound on the change in coding error, and compact closures of finite-dimensional output-state sets. These arguments avoid de Finetti reductions and establish equality with the corresponding compound-channel capacities in these two settings.

papers.title: A Generalization of Ramanujan's Sum over Finite Rings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generalization of Ramanujan sums over finite rings and derive an explicit formula for these sums. These generalized Ramanujan sums coincide with the eigenvalues of the unitary Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(R,R^{\times})$, as follows from Babai's result on Cayley graph spectra. This provides a useful approach to determining the spectrum of the unitary Cayley graph. Moreover, under a certain independence condition on the maximal left ideals, we show that our formula extends the classical formula for Ramanujan sums to finite rings.

papers.title: Strange correlator and string order parameter for non-invertible symmetry protected topological phases in 1+1d
Towards Higher Order Oscillatory Ising Machines
papers.abstract: Ising machines as hardware solvers of combinatorial optimization problems (COPs) can efficiently explore large solution spaces due to their inherent parallelism and physics-based dynamics. Many important COP classes such as satisfiability (SAT) assume arbitrary interactions between problem variables, while most Ising machines only support pairwise (second-order) interactions. This necessitates translation of higher-order interactions to pair-wise, which typically results in extra variables not corresponding to problem variables, and a larger problem for the Ising machine to solve than the original problem. This in turn can significantly increase time-to-solution and/or degrade solution accuracy. In this paper, considering a representative CMOS-compatible class of Ising machines, we propose a practical design to enable direct hardware support for higher order interactions. By minimizing the overhead of problem translation and mapping, our design leads to up to 4x lower time-to-solution without compromising solution accuracy.

papers.title: Conjugate continuous-discrete projection filter via sparse-Grid quadrature
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the continuous-discrete projection filter for exponential-family manifolds with conjugate likelihoods. We first derive the local projection error of the prediction step of the continuous-discrete projection filter. We then derive the exact Bayesian update algorithm for a class of discrete measurement processes with additive Gaussian noise. To control the stiffness of the natural parameters' ordinary differential equations, we introduce a regularization method via projection to the Fisher information metric's eigenspace. Lastly, we apply the proposed method to approximate the filtering density of a modified Van der Pol oscillator problem and a coupled stochastic FitzHugh--Nagumo system. The proposed projection filter shows superior performance compared to several state-of-the-art parametric continuous-discrete filtering methods.

papers.title: Strong convergence of uniformly random permutation representations of surface groups
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. Consider the composition of a uniformly random element of $\mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma,S_n)$ with the $(n-1)$-dimensional irreducible representation of $S_n$. We prove the strong convergence in probability as $n\to\infty$ of this sequence of random representations to the regular representation of $\Gamma$. As a consequence, for any closed orientable hyperbolic surface $X$, with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$, a uniformly random degree-$n$ covering space of $X$ has near optimal relative spectral gap --- ignoring the eigenvalues that arise from the base surface $X$. To do so, we show that the polynomial method of proving strong convergence can be extended beyond rational settings. To meet the requirements of this extension we prove two new kinds of results. First, we show there are effective polynomial approximations of expected values of traces of elements of $\Gamma$ under random homomorphisms to $S_{n}$. Secondly, we estimate the growth rates of probabilities that a finitely supported random walk on $\Gamma$ is a proper power after a given number of steps.

papers.title: Amenability of group actions on compact spaces and the associated Banach algebras
papers.abstract: For a topological group $G$, amenability can be characterized by the amenability of the convolution Banach algebra $L^1(G)$. Here a Banach algebra $A$ is called amenable if every bounded derivation from $A$ into any dual--type $A$--$A$--Banach bimodule is inner. We extend this classical result to the case of discrete group actions on compact Hausdorff spaces in our main theorem Theorem 5.2. By using a Banach algebra naturally associated with the action and adopting a suitably weakened notion of amenability for Banach algebras, we obtain an analogous characterization of amenable actions. As a lemma, we also proved a fixed--point property for amenable actions in Theorem 4.4 that strengthens the theorem of Dong and Wang (2015).

papers.title: Feasible Regions of GB phenomenon in Extended Proca-Nuevo Gravity
Solvable Structures for Hamiltonian Systems
papers.abstract: We develop a geometric framework connecting solvable structures and integrable Hamiltonian systems. For a completely integrable Hamiltonian system with $n$ degrees of freedom, we construct a solvable structure consisting of $2n$ Hamiltonian vector fields that allows us to integrate Hamilton's equations by quadratures. Explicit expressions are derived for the associated Pfaffian forms whose integration yields both the solutions of Hamilton's equations and action-angle variables. This provides a novel interpretation of the Arnold-Liouville theorem in the context of solvable structures. We illustrate the theory by deriving explicit solutions and canonical variables of action-angle type for the open Toda lattice and the rational Calogero-Moser system.

papers.title: Coarse chain recurrence and Morse graphs with finite errors
papers.abstract: This paper provides a unified framework connecting dynamical systems with tools from topological data analysis and geometric topology and inspires new interactions among dynamical systems, topology, and nonlinear analysis. To this end, we introduce a one-parameter family of ``chain recurrences'' that generalizes chain recurrence and induces a natural filtration on the underlying metric space of a dynamical system. In particular, the forward directions of the filtrations characterize the level of control required to return to the original position, and the backward directions capture the robustness of the recurrence. The resulting filtrations yield potentials and bifurcation diagrams of dynamical systems that encode the evolution of recurrent sets under bounded total or stepwise perturbations. In addition, we extend Morse graphs to one-parameter families of ``coarse Morse graphs,'' which evolve through vertex collapses reflecting coarse recurrence transitions. These constructions not only refine Conley's decomposition but also reveal singular limit behaviors as the perturbation level vanishes. Furthermore, we establish analogous filtrations for difference equations to bridge the theoretical framework with numerical analysis.

papers.title: Glued tree lattices with only compact localized states
Blanket representation for spin networks with n-body interactions
A Majorana Relativistic Quantum Spectral Approach to the Riemann Hypothesis in (1+1)-Dimensional Rindler Spacetimes
papers.abstract: We present a Hilbert--Pólya approach to the Riemann zeta function via a Mellin--Barnes integral for massive Majorana modes in $(1+1)$-dimensional Rindler spacetime. The boost spectrum is continuous on the full wedge and discrete with a reflecting wall. Summing positive momentum modes on a transverse circle yields $\zeta(2s)$ in the radial Mellin transform. Building on our one-sided Cesàro criterion for additive correlations of $\Lambda(n)-1$, we assign each prime $p$ a chiral channel of optical length $\tfrac12\log p$. Its $k$th return at $u=k\log p$ carries weight $\log p$. The centered correlation obeys $C(u)\le C(0)$ for all real $u$ exactly when the Riemann hypothesis (RH) holds. For a Majorana oscillator with linear mass profile, a bounded self-adjoint function of its Hamiltonian assigns period $kT_1$ to mode pair $k$. The first $n$ pairs have least common period $T_n=T_1\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,n)$, so $\log(T_n/T_{n-1})=\Lambda(n)$ for $n\ge2$. Set $m=\lceil\sqrt{x}\rceil$, $N=\lfloor mx\rfloor$, and $\psi(y)=\sum_{n\le y}\Lambda(n)$. The signed revival mean $A(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}(N/j-\psi(N/j))$ satisfies $A(x)=R(x)+o(\sqrt{x})$, where $R(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\Lambda(n)(x/n-1)-x\log x+(1+\gamma_{\mathrm E})x$. At each zeta zero $\rho$ of multiplicity $d$ with $\Re(\rho)>1/2$, the meromorphic continuation of $\int_2^\infty A(x)x^{-s-1}\,dx$ has a simple pole of residue $d/[\rho(1-\rho)]$. For fixed $\lambda>1$, $1/2<\theta<\Re(\rho)$ and $K>0$, the Kaczorowski--Pintz theorem gives $A(x)>Kx^\theta$ at some $x\in[Y,Y^\lambda]$ for all large $Y$. Thus RH follows if for each $\varepsilon>0$ there is a $C_\varepsilon$ with $A(x)\le C_\varepsilon x^{1/2+\varepsilon}$ throughout $[Y,Y^\lambda]$ for arbitrarily large $Y$. For $\lambda=3/2$, the independent theta-lift estimate reported by Alpöge and Claude for $G=R$ gives this bound for $A$.

papers.title: Lyapunov Exponent Bounds for Random Products of Relaxed Projections
papers.abstract: Current performance bounds for randomized iterated projections, such as the Kaczmarz method, are often considered tight under per-iteration analyses, yet they are notoriously loose in practice. We derive asymptotic performance bounds that narrow this theory-practice gap, leveraging a new technique for bounding the spectral radii of operators arising in the Lyapunov exponent analysis of randomized iterations. The asymptotic analysis also uncovers the previously unexplained role of relaxation in improving performance, thereby resolving an open problem posed by Strohmer and Vershynin in 2007.

papers.title: Bridgeland Stability of Sheaves on del Pezzo Surface of Picard Rank Three
papers.abstract: We study the stability of line bundles and torsion sheaves under divisorial Bridgeland stability conditions. On the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^2$ at two general points, we characterize stability and semistability of a line bundle, or of its shift in the tilted heart, in terms of the three $(-1)$-curves. We also prove that, on any smooth projective surface, the pushforward of a torsion-free sheaf of rank $1$ on an integral curve of nonpositive self-intersection is stable for every divisorial stability condition.

papers.title: New Lower Bounds for Stochastic Non-Convex Optimization through Divergence Decomposition
papers.abstract: We study fundamental limits of first-order stochastic optimization in a range of nonconvex settings, including L-smooth functions satisfying Quasar-Convexity (QC), Quadratic Growth (QG), and Restricted Secant Inequalities (RSI). While the convergence properties of standard algorithms are well-understood in deterministic regimes, significantly fewer results address the stochastic case, where only unbiased and noisy gradients are available. We establish new lower bounds on the number of noisy gradient queries to minimize these classes of functions, also showing that they are tight (up to a logarithmic factor) in all the relevant quantities characterizing each class. Our approach reformulates the optimization task as a function identification problem, leveraging divergence decomposition arguments to construct a challenging subclass that leads to sharp lower bounds. Furthermore, we present a specialized algorithm in the one-dimensional setting that achieves faster rates, suggesting that certain dimensional thresholds are intrinsic to the complexity of non-convex stochastic optimization.

papers.title: Primitivity Testing in Free Group Algebras via Duality
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field and $F$ a free group. By a classical result of Cohn and Lewin, the free group algebra $K\left[F\right]$ is a free ideal ring (FIR): a ring over which the submodules of free modules are themselves free, and of a well-defined rank. Given a finitely generated right ideal $I\leq K\left[F\right]$ and an element $f\in I$, we give an explicit algorithm determining whether $f$ is part of some basis of $I$. More generally, given free $K[F]$-modules $M\le N$, we provide algorithms determining whether $M$ is a free summand of $N$, and whether $N$ admits a free splitting relative to $M$. These can also be used to obtain analogous algorithms for free groups $H\le J$. As an aside, we also provide an algorithm to compute the intersection of two given submodules of a free $K\left[F\right]$-module. A key feature of this work is the introduction of a duality, induced by a matrix with entries in a free ideal ring, between the respective algebraic extensions of its column and row spaces.

papers.title: Lagrangian Attention Tensor Networks for Velocity Gradient Statistical Modeling
papers.abstract: Direct numerical simulation of turbulence at realistic Reynolds numbers is still beyond current computational capability, necessitating models that reduce the number of resolved spatial scales. Improving these models requires better models of the statistical dynamics of the Velocity Gradient Tensor (VGT) at the Kolmogorov scale. Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML) has found considerable success in exploiting large datasets generated from direct numerical simulation (DNS) of Navier-Stokes to improve models for the evolution of the VGT. Using the intimate connection between VGT evolution and fluid deformation, we augment a Tensor Basis Neural Network (TBNN) closure with learned Lagrangian memory kernels, and name the result Lagrangian Attention Tensor Networks (LATN). Trained on single-time (tangent) data, Lagrangian memory is strongly predictive: it lowers the error of the pressure Hessian by 43% and markedly improves its eigenvector alignment, with the most useful history spanning about half a Kolmogorov time. These \textit{a-priori} gains, however, do not translate into improved \textit{a-posteriori} prediction. We therefore inject the memory features into the first layer of a frozen, pre-trained TBNN and train \textit{only the memory} on model rollouts, against a distributional objective. We integrate the model for nine Kolmogorov times from DNS initial conditions and evaluate it with single- and multi-time statistics of the DNS. The resulting LATN retains the trunk's single-time accuracy while improving the long-time statistics: the topology, magnitude and tail distributions of the VGT, and the alignment of vorticity with the strain rate.

papers.title: Coresets for Density-Based Clustering via Bayesian Predictive Partition Matching
papers.abstract: Density-based clustering identifies groups as connected high-density regions, accommodating irregular shapes and reflecting their geometry, but this reliance on density estimation introduces uncertainty into the resulting partitions, which is often costly to quantify. To represent this uncertainty efficiently, we construct a compact representation of the data, or coreset, designed to preserve the distribution of predictive density-based partitions. We sample observations from a Dirichlet process surrogate, smooth them to estimate densities, and use the resulting level sets to partition a common reference set. Starting from a uniform subsample, we learn an affine transformation that improves agreement with full-data partitions by minimizing a tractable approximation to paired expected variation of information. Fresh, independent predictive simulations then guide the selection of the final transformation. Our analysis provides approximation and selection guarantees and establishes consistency for ideal fixed-resolution partitions under geometric conditions. Simulations and an application to mass cytometry show improved partition agreement over uniform subsampling, often matching substantially larger supports.

papers.title: Localisation for the second-order Beckmann problem: bimartingale couplings and leaf decompositions
papers.abstract: We develop a second-order localisation theory for optimal transport based on leaf decompositions and bimartingale couplings, which impose martingale constraints in opposite directions on complementary orthogonal subspaces. It provides a second-order analogue of the classical decomposition of optimal transport into transport rays and monotone couplings: transport rays are replaced by the leaves of the $1$-Lipschitz derivative map $Du$ of an optimal dual potential $u\in C^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)$, while monotone couplings are replaced by bimartingale couplings. We apply this framework to the three-marginal optimal transport problem introduced by Bolbotowski and Bouchitté, whose relaxation is the second-order Beckmann problem. We characterise the existence of bimartingale couplings through a convex-concave order condition. This yields a generalisation of Strassen's theorem from convex order to the convex-concave setting. Equivalently, the dual problem associated with the second-order Beckmann problem admits an optimiser whose derivative is an isometry. For absolutely continuous measures with common barycentre, assuming the existence of an optimal plan with absolutely continuous third marginal, we prove that every optimal plan decomposes into a family of problems on the leaves of $Du$. On each leaf, all optimal plans are completely described by bimartingale couplings between the corresponding conditional measures. Without this absolute continuity assumption on the third marginal, we show that the leaf decomposition persists in a more general form: optimal plans are mixtures of plans concentrated on triples $(x,y,z)$ satisfying $x\in \mathcal{S}_1$, $y\in \mathcal{S}_2$, and $z\in \mathcal{S}_1\cap \mathcal{S}_2$, where $\mathcal{S}_1$ and $\mathcal{S}_2$ are neighbouring leaves of $Du$.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of twisted maps to smooth pairs
papers.abstract: We study moduli spaces of twisted maps to a smooth pair in arbitrary genus, and give geometric explanations for the known comparisons between orbifold and logarithmic Gromov--Witten invariants. We classify the irreducible components of the space of twisted maps to the universal target in terms of tropical data, and show that each is built from torsors under semi-abelian varieties coming from Jacobians of the domain curves. Natural morphisms between these spaces for different rooting parameters measure how each component grows: for rooting parameters sufficiently large and divisible, the growth is monomial, with exponent between $0$ and $\max(0,2g-1)$, and the main component is the only one with exponent $0$. In genus $1$ the virtual class is the fundamental class, which recovers the polynomiality results of Tseng and You. We conclude with geometric examples, beginning with Maulik's original genus $1$ example.

papers.title: Range-Only Dynamic Output Feedback Controller for Safe and Secure Target Circumnavigation
papers.abstract: The safety and security of robotic systems are paramount when navigating hostile targets. This paper addresses the problem of circumnavigating an unknown target by a unicycle robot while ensuring it maintains a desired safe distance and remains within the sensing region around the target throughout its motion. The proposed controller design is based on a composite Lyapunov framework consisting of: (i) a quadratic Lyapunov function characterizing the target-circumnavigation objective, and (ii) a barrier Lyapunov function-based potential term enforcing the prescribed safety and sensing constraints. A notable feature of the proposed approach is that it relies exclusively on local range measurements between the robot and the target, achieved through a dynamic output-feedback controller that treats the range as the only measurable output. Using Lyapunov-based stability analysis together with an equivalent autonomous reformulation of the closed-loop dynamics, we establish asymptotic stability of the desired equilibrium while guaranteeing satisfaction of the prescribed safety and sensing constraints under the proposed controllers. Restrictive bounds on the post-design signals are also derived, and numerical simulations are presented to validate the proposed approach.

papers.title: Incoherent Diffraction Imaging with a Pseudo-Thermal Light Source
papers.abstract: Incoherent Diffraction Imaging - IDI - is a diffraction-based imaging technique that has been recently proposed to exploit the partial coherence of incoherently scattered light to retrieve structural information from the scattering centers. Similar to the stellar intensity interferometry of Hanbury Brown and Twiss, the signal builds up on the second-order spatial correlations of the emitted light. The complex spatial distribution of the target is thereby encoded in the spatial intensity fluctuations of the scattered light. The first experimental realisations of this imaging technique have been realised using the fluorescence excited by an ultra-short X-ray pulse at Free Electron Laser (FEL) facilities. Here, we propose an alternative set-up based on a table-top Pseudo-Thermal Light Source. This set-up allows us to explore IDI under a wide range of physically relevant conditions as well as to benchmark numerical and analytical models currently used to determine the imaging capabilities of this technique.

papers.title: Fusion-pMT: Biological Sequence Modeling for Tri-Molecular Binding in Immunogenicity Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurately modeling the tripartite interaction among peptides, major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules, and T cell receptors (TCRs) is essential for understanding T-cell-mediated immunity and informing immunogenicity prediction. A key challenge is to connect peptide-MHC binding knowledge with TCR specificity while retaining the residue-level context needed to model their interactions. In this paper, we propose Fusion-pMT, a biological sequence modeling framework that (1) learns representations of the three molecular inputs through a shared amino acid projection and molecule-specific encoders, and (2) combines peptide-MHC pretraining with two-stage cross-attention, retaining MHC-conditioned peptide tokens for subsequent interaction with TCR sequences. By aligning sequence fusion with the stepwise nature of immune recognition, Fusion-pMT effectively supports both pairwise and tripartite interaction modeling. To validate its effectiveness, we conduct comprehensive experiments covering both pairwise and tripartite interactions and demonstrate the advantages of Fusion-pMT over strong baselines while validating its core design choices.

papers.title: Classification of torsion of elliptic curves over quartic fields
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a quartic field $K$. By the Mordell-Weil theorem, $E(K)$ is a finitely generated group. We determine all the possibilities for the torsion group $E(K)_{tor}$ where $K$ ranges over all quartic fields $K$ and $E$ ranges over all elliptic curves over $K$. We show that there are no sporadic torsion groups, or in other words, that all torsion groups either do not appear or they appear for infinitely many non-isomorphic elliptic curves $E$. Proving this requires showing that numerous modular curves $X_1(m,n)$ have no non-cuspidal degree $4$ points. We deal with almost all the curves using one of 3 methods: a method for the rank 0 cases requiring no computation; the Hecke sieve, a local method requiring computer-assisted computations; and the global method, an argument for the positive rank cases also requiring no computation. We deal with the handful of remaining cases using ad hoc methods.

papers.title: K-moduli with real coefficients
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop an algebraic K-stability theory (e.g. special test configuration theory and optimal destabilization theory) for log Fano $\mathbb R$-pairs, and construct a proper K-moduli space to parametrize K-polystable log Fano $\mathbb R$-pairs with some fixed invariants (e.g. dimension, volume, coefficients). All of these are well-known for log Fano $\mathbb Q$-pairs, and the strategy in this paper is trying to reduce the problems (in many cases) to $\mathbb Q$-coefficients case rather than rebuilding the whole program as in $\mathbb Q$-coefficients case.

papers.title: Duality for Arithmetic $p$-adic Pro-étale Cohomology of Analytic Spaces
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove that the arithmetic $p$-adic pro-étale cohomology of smooth partially proper spaces over $K$ satisfies a duality, as conjectured by Colmez, Gilles and Nizioł. We derive it from the geometric duality on the Fargues-Fontaine curve by Galois descent techniques of Fontaine.

papers.title: Differential forms and Brauer classes in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We study $p$-torsion Brauer classes in positive characteristic arising from differential forms. We relate this construction to the Brauer group of supersingular K3 surfaces and analyze the contribution of these classes to the Brauer-Manin obstruction. As an application, we examine the Brauer-Manin set of supersingular K3 surfaces and of varieties admitting many differential forms.

papers.title: Self organisation of invasive breast cancer driven by the interplay of active and passive nematic dynamics
Financial Volatility and Risk Forecasting Incorporating a Larger Number of Realized Measures
papers.abstract: High-frequency data have led to the development of numerous realized volatility measures, while standard Realized GARCH models typically rely on a single measure. This paper proposes three approaches to incorporate information from multiple realized measures within the Realized GARCH framework. First, we develop an autoencoder-enhanced Realized GARCH model that constructs a synthetic realized measure through nonlinear dimensionality reduction. Second, we propose a linear weighted Realized GARCH model that jointly estimates convex aggregation weights and model parameters. Third, we introduce a functional weighted Realized GARCH model based on parsimonious Beta weighting functions. Using approximately 22 years of data for 29 international equity indices, we evaluate the proposed methods in volatility, Value-at-Risk, and Expected Shortfall forecasting. Compared with benchmark models based on single realized measures, equal weighting, and linear dimension reduction, the proposed methods consistently deliver more accurate volatility and risk forecasts.

papers.title: Shortest Path Lengths in Poisson Line Cox Processes: Approximations and Applications
papers.abstract: We study street-constrained ($\ell_1$) shortest paths in a Poisson line Cox process (PLCP), where Poisson points of linear intensity $\mu$ lie on the lines of an underlying Poisson line process (PLP) of density $\lambda$. Under a one-turn restriction, we derive closed-form expressions for the distribution of the nearest-neighbor path length from (i) the typical PLCP point and (ii) the typical PLP intersection, by explicitly evaluating the relevant void probabilities via a geometric decomposition of the feasible path-length set. For the intersection case, we further provide analytically tractable upper and lower bounds that capture the impact of $\lambda$ and $\mu$. Allowing two turns from the typical point, we obtain a computable upper bound using a feasible-set shrinking argument and identify regimes in which it is tight. We also delineate parameter ranges where a one-turn route from a typical intersection can outperform a two-turn route from a typical point. Finally, we discuss how the results enable statistical performance characterization of ride-hailing services in terms of service guarantee, trip time, and consequently, derive dimensioning insights. We also illustrate qualitatively, how the results can be employed to study vehicle-to-vehicle communication broadcast messages near intersections.

papers.title: Scaling Structure-Aware Virtual Screening to Billions of Molecules with SPRINT
papers.abstract: Virtual screening of small molecules against protein targets can accelerate drug discovery and development by predicting drug-target interactions (DTIs). However, structure-based methods like molecular docking are too slow to allow for broad proteome-scale screens, limiting their application in screening for off-target effects or new molecular mechanisms. Recently, vector-based methods using protein language models (PLMs) have emerged as a complementary approach that bypasses explicit 3D structure modeling. Here, we develop SPRINT, a vector-based approach for screening entire chemical libraries against whole proteomes for DTIs and novel mechanisms of action. SPRINT improves on prior work by using a self-attention based architecture and structure-aware PLMs to learn a co-embedding space for drugs and targets, enabling efficient binder prediction, search, and retrieval. SPRINT achieves competitive enrichment factors in virtual screening on LIT-PCBA, DTI classification benchmarks, and binding affinity prediction benchmarks, while providing interpretability in the form of residue-level attention maps. In addition to being both accurate and interpretable, SPRINT is ultra-fast: querying the whole human proteome against the ENAMINE Real Database (6.7B drugs) for the 100 most likely binders per protein takes 16 minutes. SPRINT promises to enable virtual screening at an unprecedented scale, opening up new opportunities for in silico drug repurposing and development.

papers.title: P-adic numbers and kernels
Lightweight Detection and Model Attribution of Synthetic Speech via Residual Statistical Fingerprints
papers.abstract: As speech generation technologies advance, so do risks of impersonation, misinformation, and spoofing. We present a lightweight, training-free method for synthetic speech detection and source model attribution. Our method builds on model-specific fingerprints that are computed as the average of the differences between audio signals and their filtered versions, referred to as residuals. Leveraging the Mahalanobis distance of the residual for a given audio signal to these model-specific fingerprints allows to identify the source model as well as to distinguish real from fake audio. A broad set of experiments across multiple synthesis systems and languages demonstrate a supreme performance of the proposed approach on four tasks: open-world single-model attribution, closed-world multi-model attribution, real vs. synthetic speech classification, and out-of-domain detection.

papers.title: High-temperature superconductivity from kinetic energy
Extremely amenable automorphism groups of countable structures
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the isomorphism relation of extremely amenable non-Archimedean Polish groups from the point of view of descriptive set theory. Our main result is that this relation is more complex than any isomorphism relation of countable structures in the Borel reducibility hierarchy.

papers.title: Enhancing Diabetic Retinopathy Detection with CNN-Based Models: A Comparative Study of UNET and Stacked UNET Architectures
papers.abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy DR is a severe complication of diabetes. Damaged or abnormal blood vessels can cause loss of vision. The need for massive screening of a large population of diabetic patients has generated an interest in a computer-aided fully automatic diagnosis of DR. In the realm of Deep learning frameworks, particularly convolutional neural networks CNNs, have shown great interest and promise in detecting DR by analyzing retinal images. However, several challenges have been faced in the application of deep learning in this domain. High-quality, annotated datasets are scarce, and the variations in image quality and class imbalances pose significant hurdles in developing a dependable model. In this paper, we demonstrate the proficiency of two Convolutional Neural Networks CNNs based models, UNET and Stacked UNET utilizing the APTOS Asia Pacific Tele-Ophthalmology Society Dataset. This system achieves an accuracy of 92.81% for the UNET and 93.32% for the stacked UNET architecture. The architecture classifies the images into five categories ranging from 0 to 4, where 0 is no DR and 4 is proliferative DR.

papers.title: Identification of Heterogeneous Peer Effects
papers.abstract: We develop a peer effects model in which each peer's influence depends on their outcome rank within the peer group. Unlike existing models, it allows non-monotonic effects across ranks. The model admits a unique equilibrium, and its parameters can be identified using peers' exogenous characteristics. We introduce a parsimonious quantile-dependent specification and develop a specification test to guide model selection. Applying the model to student outcomes in Add Health reveals heterogeneous, often non-monotonic spillovers. Counterfactual analysis shows that allowing for non-monotonic peer effects changes the rankings of influential students relative to existing models. Our R package, QuantilePeer, implements these methods.

papers.title: Incentivizing Information Acquisition
papers.abstract: I study a principal-agent model in which a principal hires an agent to collect information about an unknown continuous state. The agent acquires a signal whose distribution is centered around the state, controlling the signal's precision at a cost. The principal observes neither the precision nor the signal, but rather, using transfers that can depend on the state, incentivizes the agent to choose high precision and report the signal truthfully. I identify a sufficient and necessary condition on the agent's information structure which ensures that there exists an optimal transfer with a simple cutoff structure: the agent receives a fixed prize when his prediction is close enough to the state and receives nothing otherwise. This condition is mild and applies to all signal distributions commonly used in the literature.

papers.title: Arthur packets for metaplectic groups
papers.abstract: For metaplectic groups over a local field of characteristic zero, we define the Arthur packet attached to any Arthur parameter $\psi$ as a multi-set of unitary genuine irreducible representations, characterized by endoscopic character relations. Over number fields, we obtain a multiplicity formula for the genuine discrete $L^2$-automorphic spectrum in terms of global Arthur parameters and $\epsilon$-factors, by leveraging the trace formula for metaplectic groups. This confirms a conjecture of Gan, and extends earlier results of Gan-Ichino on the Shimura-Waldspurger correspondences, whereas their works play a critical role in our proof. Furthermore, all these are shown to be compatible with existing results in rank one (Waldspurger) and two (Gan-Ichino).

papers.title: Iwasawa theory for unitary groups via Eisenstein congruences and its applications
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime number. In this article, we study automorphic aspects of Iwasawa theory for unitary groups, focusing on the $p$-primitivity of Klingen Eisenstein series and their $p$-adic families on $\mathrm{U}(m+1,n+1)$, which is a key component in establishing lower bounds for Selmer groups in Iwasawa theory for $\mathrm{U}(m,n)$. First, we compute the Gan--Gross--Prasad period integral of a Klingen Eisenstein series on $\mathrm{U}(m+1,n+1)$ against a cuspidal automorphic form on $\mathrm{U}(m+1,n)$, and relate it to special Rankin--Selberg $L$-values. We then interpolate these period integrals $p$-adically as both forms vary in Hida families, thereby producing a Rankin--Selberg type $p$-adic $L$-function for $\mathrm{U}(m,n) \times \mathrm{U}(m+1,n)$ as a byproduct. This method is designed to replace the computation of Fourier--Jacobi coefficients used in the existing literature to establish the $p$-primitive property of Klingen Eisenstein series, which so far treats only cases where $m+n \leq 2$. As an application, we consider the case $\mathrm{U}(m,n)=\mathrm{U}(1,0)$ and obtain a new proof of M.-L. Hsieh's Iwasawa main conjecture for CM elliptic curves over a totally real field $F$ with CM field $M$ and good ordinary reduction at all places above $p$, for all primes $p \geq 5$ unramified in $F$. Our approach removes the assumption in Hsieh's original work that $p$ does not divide the relative class number of $MF/F$.

papers.title: Inferring behind-the-meter demand components from net load via inverse optimization
papers.abstract: Understanding and forecasting electricity demand responses to price signals is essential to support the operational decisions of system operators, retailers, and regulators. Traditional time series and machine learning approaches have performed well under stable consumption patterns. However, the rise of active consumers with flexible assets, such as solar-plus-storage systems and electric vehicles, introduces new complexities. These consumers exhibit behind-the-meter behavior that is generally unobservable to system operators and retailers, who can typically only measure net demand at the boundary meters which are located at the connection points to the grid. Net demand reflects the aggregate of baseload consumption, flexible load shifting, and self-generation, all of which may respond nonlinearly to market prices. As these unobservable components grow, existing forecasting models may fail to capture the true dynamics of consumer behavior. This work develops and implements a data-driven inverse optimization framework to reveal behind-the-meter consumption patterns using only net demand data. By analyzing net demand as revealed at the grid connection point, we estimate parameters for a latent optimization model, enabling predictions that infer the unobservable components. This enables more accurate point and probabilistic forecasting of electricity demand under varying price signals. Thus, it provides actionable insights for system operators to improve local congestion management and flexibility extraction, as well as for retailers and aggregators, who could thereby optimize operations and tariffs to leverage consumer flexibility. We validate the methodology using real-world data, demonstrating improved forecasting accuracy over leading machine learning and time-series benchmarks.

papers.title: The ring of stable characters over $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$
papers.abstract: For a fixed prime power $q$, let $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$ denote the family of groups $\text{GL}_N(q)$ for $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. In this paper we study the $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of "stable" class functions of $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$, and show it admits four different linear bases, each arising naturally in different settings. One such basis is that of stable irreducible characters, namely, the class functions spanned by the characters corresponding to finitely generated simple $\mathrm{VI}$-modules in the sense of [ arXiv:1408.3694 , arXiv:1602.00654 ]. A second one comes from characters of parabolic representations. The final two, one originally defined in [ arXiv:1803.04155 ] and the other in [ arXiv:2110.11099 ], are more combinatorial in nature. As corollaries, we clarify many properties of these four bases and prove a conjecture from [ arXiv:2106.11587 ].

papers.title: Parahoric reduction theory of formal connections (or Higgs fields)
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the parahoric reduction theory of formal connections (or Higgs fields) on a formal principal bundle with parahoric structures. This generalizes the reduction theory due to Hukuhara-Levelt-Turrittin and Babbitt-Varadarajan in the case without parahoric structures [7], and Boalch's result in the case of regular singularity [14]. As applications, we first prove that a formal connection is intrinsically regular if and only if it is a parahoric formal connection, in combination with the works of Bremer-Sage [45] and Chen-Kamgarpour [20], providing various criteria for the regularity of formal connections. We then introduce a notion of relative regularity for formal connections and give criterions. Finally, we demonstrate a parahoric version of Frenkel-Zhu's Borel reduction theorem of formal connections [33].

papers.title: DeepVoting: Learning and Improving Voting Rules with Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Recently, social choice theory has been found broadly useful for AI alignment and evaluation, often based on the axiomatic properties for combining preferences provided by social choice functions. However, for many sets of axioms, functions which never violate the axioms are known to not exist, e.g., Arrow's Impossibility Theorem. Recent work on learning novel rules to minimize axiom violations shows the effectiveness of machine learning but explores a limited class of axioms. In this work we show the effectiveness of standard social choice data structures as features for learning existing voting rules, resulting in networks that have better accuracy than past approaches while using an order of magnitude fewer parameters. Subsequently, we develop a process for adding axiomatic properties to existing voting rules. By building novel axiomatic loss functions we are able to use transfer learning to fine-tune existing voting rules in a way that quantitatively preserves their original behaviour while also exhibiting strong adherence to previously absent axiomatic properties, resulting in novel voting rules that are closer to the impossibility frontier than those in the machine learning or theoretical literature.

papers.title: Complexity as Axiomatic Incompleteness
papers.abstract: IInformation theory has long sought to uncover the universal laws governing complex systems. Yet information is not merely quantified; it is also interpreted by this http URL formalize this cognitive aspect through a Generalized Incompleteness Theory (GIC), which integrates axiomatic logic, Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning, and Gödel's incompleteness theorem to establish a connection between complexity and formal incompleteness. We introduce the notions of interpreter-based information and PAC complexity, demonstrating that certain outputs can be PAC-learnable even when their corresponding interpreters cannot be constructed. We further show that every nontrivial formal system contains a PAC-learnable incompleteness space of dimension \(2^n-n-1\). The GIC framework unifies several foundational results-including Cantor's diagonal argument, Gödel's incompleteness theorem, and the Turing halting problem-within a categorical and topological framework. We further show that physical models, including four-dimensional spacetime in relativity and the 11- and 26-dimensional spaces arising in string theory, admit natural correspondences with incompleteness spaces, while critical states can be understood in terms of symmetry-breaking selections of axioms. Our framework identifies incompleteness as a universal feature underlying complexity, criticality, and observability, thereby revealing fundamental limits on description and cognition in any axiomatizable theory.

papers.title: Surface elevation errors in finite element Stokes models for glacier evolution
papers.abstract: The primary data which determine the evolution of glaciation are the bedrock elevation and the surface mass balance. From this data, which we assume is defined over a fixed land region, the glacier's geometry solves a free boundary problem which balances the time derivative of the surface elevation, the surface velocity from the Stokes flow of the ice, and the surface mass balance rate. This problem can be posed in weak form as a variational inequality over a cone of admissible surface elevation functions, those which are above the bedrock topography. After some preparatory theory for the Stokes problem, we conjecture that the corresponding continuous-space, implicit time-step variational inequality problem is well-posed if the surface kinematical equation is appropriately regularized. This conjecture is supported by physical arguments and numerical evidence. We then prove a general theorem which bounds the numerical error made by finite element approximations of nonlinear-operator variational inequalities in Banach spaces. This bound is a sum of error terms of different types, special to variational inequalities. When it is applied to the implicit time-step glacier problem there are three terms in the bound: an error from discretizing the bed elevation primarily near the glacier margin, an error from numerically solving for the Stokes velocity, and finally a Céa-type best-approximation error for the finite element space representation of the surface elevation. The design of glacier models is then reconsidered based on this mostly a priori error analysis.

papers.title: Fractional Laplace operator and related Schrödinger equations on locally finite graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first define a discrete version of the fractional Laplace operator $(-\Delta)^{s}$ through the heat semigroup on a stochastically complete, connected, locally finite graph $G = (V, E, \mu, w)$. Secondly, we define the fractional divergence and give another form of $(-\Delta)^s$. The third point, and the foremost, is the introduction of the fractional Sobolev space $W^{s,2}(V)$, which is necessary when we study problems involving $(-\Delta)^{s}$. Finally, using the mountain-pass theorem and the Nehari manifold, we obtain multiplicity solutions to a discrete fractional Schrödinger equation on $G$. We caution the readers that though these existence results are well known in the continuous case, the discrete case is quite different.

papers.title: Primordial B-mode sensitivity forecasts for northern-sky cosmic microwave background surveys
Mahler's problem and Turyn polynomials
papers.abstract: Mahler's problem asks for the largest possible value of the Mahler measure, normalized by the $L_2$ norm, of a polynomial with $\pm1$ coefficients and large degree. We establish a new record value of approximately $0.951$ in this problem by analyzing certain Turyn polynomials, which are defined by cyclically shifting the coefficients of a Fekete polynomial by a prescribed amount. Recently, Klurman, Lamzouri, and Munsch established that the distribution of values over the unit circle of Fekete polynomials of large degree is effectively modeled by a particular random point process. We extend this analysis to the Turyn polynomials, and determine expressions for the asymptotic normalized Mahler measure of these polynomials, as well as for their normalized $L_q$ norms. We also describe a number of calculations on the corresponding random processes, which indicate that the Turyn polynomials where the shift is approximately $1/4$ of the length have Mahler measure exceeding $95\%$ of their $L_2$ norm. Further, we show that these asymptotic values are not disturbed by a small change to make polynomials having entirely $\pm1$ coefficients, which establishes the result on Mahler's problem. We also estimate that the limiting value of the normalized $L_1$ norm of these polynomials exceeds $0.977$, in connection with a question of Newman.

papers.title: An upper bound for the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of relative Sullivan algebras
papers.abstract: This paper addresses a question posed by Félix, Halperin and Thomas. We prove that the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of a relative Sullivan algebra is finite if such invariants of the base algebra and fiber algebra are both finite. Furthermore, we provide a similar estimation for the Toomer invariant.

papers.title: Operator dependent para-controlled calculus, periodic homogenisation and singular PDEs
papers.abstract: We develop a variant of the para-controlled distributions framework based on operator dependent (generalised) Besov spaces. This in particular covers the class of oscillatory operators from periodic homogenisation. We then apply the framework to study periodic homogenisation problems for a class of singular stochastic PDEs. One novel viewpoint is to measure regularity via the geometry induced by the operators at hand rather than classical Fourier basis. The generalised Besov spaces were introduced by Kerkyacharian-Petrushev. In contrast to the Fourier decomposition in the classical setting, they are built from spectral decomposition of general self-adjoint elliptic operators. A major difference is that products of two spectrally localised functions in general have ``frequencies" spread over the whole spectrum. We obtain a decay estimate on ``high frequency" component of the product of two spectrally-localised functions. This enables us to obtain uniform bounds for the naturally associated para-product and commutator operations over a class of operators. This in particular includes the family of periodic homogenisation operators uniform in the oscillation parameter. Next, we show convergence properties of these operations in the periodic homogenisation setting. A key ingredient is a sharp quantitative convergence of the generalised Littlewood-Paley block operators. The proof utilises the Helffer-Sjöstrand's formula for self-adjoint operators. Finally, we apply this framework to periodic homogenisation problems for dynamical $\phi^4_3$, $2$D gPAM, and $1$D KPZ. Assuming the convergence of stochastic objects to their homogenised limits, we show that the solutions and fluxes also converge to the corresponding limits. The convergence of the explicit stochastic terms with suitable renormalisations will be treated in a separate note.

papers.title: Resolving Gilbert's Conjecture: Dimensional Dependencies in Hardy Spaces Valued in Clifford Modules
papers.abstract: This article provides a thorough investigation into Gilbert's Conjecture, pertaining to Hardy spaces in the upper half-space valued in Clifford modules. We explore the conjecture proposed by Gilbert in 1991, which seeks to extend the classical principle of representing real $L^p$ functions on the real line as boundary values of Hardy holomorphic functions to higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces valued in any Clifford module. We present a complete resolution to this conjecture, demonstrating that its validity is contingent upon the dimension $n$, specifically holding true when \(n \not\equiv 6, 7 \mod 8\) and failing otherwise. The pivotal discovery that Gilbert's conjecture can be reformulated as a set of algebraic conditions is underscored in this work. To navigate these conditions, we employ a novel strategy that leverages the octonions, revealing their instrumental role in addressing issues related to Clifford modules and spinors. This innovative approach not only provides explicit realization through the generalization of the Hilbert transform to the Riesz transform but also establishes a significant advancement in the understanding of Hardy spaces within higher dimensions.

papers.title: Examples of Ricci limit spaces with infinite holes
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq 3$, $\lambda \in \mathbb{R} $, and $(X,h)$ be an $n$-dimensional smooth complete Riemannian manifold with ${\rm Ric}_h > \lambda $. In this paper, we construct, for each given $\epsilon >0$, a sequence of $(n+2)$-dimensional manifolds $(M_{i} ,g_i ) \stackrel{GH}{\longrightarrow} (X_\epsilon ,d_\epsilon ) $ with ${\rm Ric}_{g_i} > \lambda $, such that $d_{GH} (X,X_\epsilon ) \leq \epsilon $, and $X_\epsilon $ is homeomorphic to the space obtained by removing an infinite number of balls from $X$. Hence $X_\epsilon $ has dense boundary with an infinite number of connected components. Moreover, $X_\epsilon $ has no open subset which is topologically a manifold. This generalizes Hupp-Naber-Wang's result (arxiv: 2308.03909 ) from $4$-dimensional case to the general case of dimension $n\geq 3$. Our construction differs from that of Hupp-Naber-Wang. In their approach, Hupp-Naber-Wang considered doing an infinite number of blow-ups on the local complex surface structure of $X$, thus relying on the $4$-dimensional condition. However, our method involves removing an infinite number of balls from $X$, allowing us to construct in the general case of dimensions greater than or equal to $3$. As a corollary, we provide a solution to an open problem posed by Naber in the $3$-dimensional case.

papers.title: Combatting Fraud in Artificial Currency Based Government Benefits Programs
papers.abstract: Benefits programs are policy tools for providing targeted aid, such as food assistance or transit subsidies. However, these programs are often susceptible to misreporting fraud, wherein users misreport private attributes to obtain excess aid. To address this problem, we introduce a two-stage audit game between an administrator and users in which the administrator can audit users at a cost and levy fines on misreporting users, with player payoff structures designed to reflect real-world benefits programs. We show that the administrator's least-favorable Bayesian Stackelberg equilibria can be computed tractably via linear programming and derive prescriptive bounds on the administrator's excess payments and users' misreporting probability as functions of audit costs and fines. We further establish that, with an appropriately chosen budget level, the reduction in excess payments in any least-favorable Bayesian Stackelberg equilibrium offsets the audit budget required to sustain the mechanism, yielding total costs no greater than those of a baseline without an auditing authority, which we corroborate through a case study of Washington D.C.'s federal transit benefits program.

papers.title: A convergence result for a local planning problem for mean field games and rigorous proof of a Freidlin-Ventchel-type Large Deviations Principle for the $1+1$ KPZ equation
papers.abstract: We study an innovative connection between a very singular optimal transport variational problem with a congestion term connecting two Dirac measures, which is related to the planing problem in mean field games or gases with negative pressure, and a large deviation principle for the KPZ equation. The main result proves a limit of a singular approixmate problem with vanishing diffusive flux and a relaxed initial condition. The paper also provides a rigorous justification for the informal analysis of the ad hoc large deviation principle for the KPZ equation appearing in the physics literature.

papers.title: Depth-multiplexing spectral domain OCT for full eye length imaging with a single modulation unit
papers.abstract: Clinical measurement of a patient's axial eye length is emerging as a crucial approach to track progression and monitor management of myopia. However, the preferred method for such measurements is swept-source OCT, whose cost prohibits broad use, especially in lower-income communities.
