Spectral domain (SD) OCT is a more affordable option, but it has limited imaging depth range, so is not suitable for full eye length measurement. Depth-multiplexing (DM) techniques for SD-OCT provide a workaround by capturing images at multiple depths within the eye. However, these methods typically require multiple light modulation units or detectors for simultaneous imaging across depths, adding complexity and cost. In response, we propose a novel DM-SD-OCT approach that utilizes a single light modulation unit for depth encoding. We capture images at multiple depths within the eye simultaneously with a single line scan camera, then computationally demix the contributions from different depths. Here, we demonstrate acquisition and demixing of signals from three distinct depths within the eye and validate experimentally in human subjects. Our method thus offers a cost-effective solution for comprehensive eye length measurement in clinical myopia research.

papers.title: The universal Euler characteristic and Burnside group for definable groupoids
papers.abstract: We introduce the universal Euler characteristic of orbit space definable groupoids, a class of groupoids containing cocompact proper Lie groupoids as well as translation groupoids associated to proper definable group actions. We show that every additive and multiplicative invariant of orbit space definable groupoids with an additional local triviality hypothesis arises as a ring homomorphism applied to the universal Euler characteristic. This in particular includes the $\Gamma$-orbifold Euler characteristic introduced by the first and third authors when $\Gamma$ is a finitely presented group. For definable groupoids, where the object and arrow spaces as well as the structure maps are definable, we also introduce a Burnside group which is an analog of the classical Burnside ring associated to compact Lie groups and, for a transitive groupoid with compact isotropy, admits a partial multiplication.

papers.title: Optimal Rate of Kernel Regression in Large Dimensions
papers.abstract: We perform a study on kernel regression for large-dimensional data (where the sample size $n$ is polynomially depending on the dimension $d$ of the samples, i.e., $n\asymp d^{\gamma}$ for some $\gamma >0$ ). We first build a general tool to characterize the upper bound and the minimax lower bound of kernel regression for large dimensional data through the Mendelson complexity $\varepsilon_{n}^{2}$ and the metric entropy $\bar{\varepsilon}_{n}^{2}$ respectively. When the target function falls into the RKHS associated with a (general) inner product model defined on $\mathbb{S}^{d}$, we utilize the new tool to show that the minimax rate of the excess risk of kernel regression is $n^{-1/2}$ when $n\asymp d^{\gamma}$ for $\gamma =2, 4, 6, 8, \cdots$. We then further determine the optimal rate of the excess risk of kernel regression for all the $\gamma>0$ and find that the curve of optimal rate varying along $\gamma$ exhibits several new phenomena including the multiple descent behavior and the periodic plateau behavior. As an application, For the neural tangent kernel (NTK), we also provide a similar explicit description of the curve of optimal rate. As a direct corollary, we know these claims hold for wide neural networks as well.

papers.title: Metric-Measure Concentration and Strong Cosmic Censorship in Vacuum Gowdy Spacetimes
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth vacuum $T^3$-Gowdy maximal globally hyperbolic development is $C^2$-inextendible if its asymptotic velocity differs from one on a dense subset of the singular circle. This is the implication posed in Section~14.2 of Ringström's 2010 review. The proof compares the spacetime volume of a timelike boundary collar with that of a shrinking angular cone, using Killing transport and the Einstein constraint. We connect this criterion to Gromov's observable distance: the physical spatial mm-spaces satisfy the lower bound $d_{\rm conc}(X_\tau,*)\ge L(\tau)/(4+L(\tau))$, where $L(\tau)$ is the length of the orbit circle. If $L(\tau)\to0$, then $v_\infty\ge1$ everywhere, the critical set $\{v_\infty=1\}$ has Lebesgue measure zero, and the development is $C^2$-inextendible. Thus physical point concentration is sufficient for inextendibility, but is not necessary. We also give explicit, non-perturbative subcritical characteristic conditions on vacuum Cauchy data ensuring quantitative Kretschmann blow-up without using Gowdy asymptotic theorems in the curvature estimate. The exact volume-transfer identity yields predictive monotonicity criteria and distinguishes coordinate localization from intrinsic metric collapse. In the transversely expanding regime, observable rescalings with an extended transverse-length limit are classified as a point, a measured circle, or the maximal pyramid; a uniform spectral estimate eliminates all nontrivial toroidal Fourier sectors, including in the presence of spikes. The geometric framework is completed by quantitative tube estimates, a local CMC redistribution theorem, and constrained variational descriptions of the reduced energy current and normalized-volume flow.

papers.title: Soft photon corrections in $B \to K^{(\ast)} \ell^+ \ell^-$ and $Λ_b \to Λ^{(\ast)} \ell^+ \ell^-$ decays
papers.abstract: We calculate QED corrections to the semileptonic decays $H_1\to H_2\ell^+\ell^-$ where $\ell=e, \mu$ and $H_{1,2}$ are hadrons. The soft and/or collinear divergences are regulated in a gauge-invariant manner and demonstrably cancel, leaving behind a finite residue that depends on the (infrared) momentum cutoff below which a photon is considered to be indistinguishable. On resumming, the said sensitivity reduces drastically, {\em i.e.}, for the NLL result as compared to the NLO one. The overall correction is negative and its magnitude is larger for a lighter lepton. The corrections are presented for $B\to K^{(*)}$ and, for the first time, for $\Lambda_b\to\Lambda^{(*)}$ decays. Given that QED final-state radiation is routinely incorporated in experimental Monte Carlo simulations, for example through PHOTOS, our results provide an important theoretical framework for assessing the accuracy and limitations of these simulations and their impact on LFU observables such as $R_{K^{(*)}}$.

papers.title: The complete dynamics description of positively curved metrics in the Wallach flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$
papers.abstract: The family of invariant Riemannian manifolds in the Wallach flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$ is described by three parameters $(x,y,z)$ of positive real numbers. By restricting such a family of metrics in the \emph{tetrahedron} $\cal{T}:= x+y+z = 1$, in this paper, we describe all regions $\cal R \subset \cal T$ admitting metrics with curvature properties varying from positive sectional curvature to positive scalar curvature, including positive intermediate curvature notion's. We study the dynamics of such regions under the \emph{projected Ricci flow} in the plane $(x,y)$, concluding sign curvature maintenance and escaping. In addition, we obtain some results for positive intermediate Ricci curvature for a path of metrics on fiber bundles over $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$, further studying its evolution under the Ricci flow on the base.

papers.title: Inference in clustered IV models with many and weak instruments
papers.abstract: This paper studies inference in instrumental variable models with many, weak instruments and clustered data. It first examines how clustering affects identification strength, showing how to adapt the concentration parameter to account for within-cluster dependence. The adapted concentration parameter may be smaller and may grow more slowly asymptotically than the concentration parameter that ignores the dependence, thereby weakening identification. Next, the paper extends the identification-robust jackknife Anderson--Rubin and jackknife score statistics for independent data to clustered data by removing clusters rather than individual observations from the statistics. These statistics converge jointly to a normal distribution under many-instrument asymptotics, such that scaling with cluster cross-fit variance estimators yields identification-robust tests. Simulations show that the cluster jackknife tests achieve close to nominal size and have good power. A reanalysis of a study on the effect of queenly reign on war shows the empirical relevance of the new tests.

papers.title: Sensitivity Analysis in Unconditional Quantile Effects
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a framework to analyze the effects of counterfactual policies on the unconditional quantiles of an outcome variable. For a given counterfactual policy, we obtain identified sets for the effect of both marginal and global changes in the proportion of treated individuals. To conduct a sensitivity analysis, we introduce the quantile breakdown frontier, a curve that $(i)$ indicates whether a sensitivity analysis is possible or not, and $(ii)$ when a sensitivity analysis is possible, quantifies the amount of selection bias consistent with a given conclusion of interest across different quantiles. To illustrate our method, we perform a sensitivity analysis on the effect of unionizing low income workers on the quantiles of the distribution of (log) wages.

papers.title: The pro-$\mathcal{C}$ anabelian geometry of number fields
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and $\mathcal{C}$ a nontrivial full class of finite groups. Write $K^{\mathcal{C}}/K$ for the maximal pro-$\mathcal{C}$ Galois extension of $K$ and $G_K^{\mathcal{C}}$ for its Galois group. Write $\Sigma(\mathcal{C})$ for the set of prime numbers $p$ such that $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}\in\mathcal{C}$. We prove that, for two such pairs $(K_i,\mathcal{C}_i)$, every isomorphism $G_{K_1}^{\mathcal{C}_1}\simeq G_{K_2}^{\mathcal{C}_2}$ is induced by a unique isomorphism between $K_2^{\mathcal{C}_2}/K_2$ and $K_1^{\mathcal{C}_1}/K_1$, provided that $\Sigma(\mathcal{C}_i)$ has positive upper Dirichlet density for at least one $i$. As a consequence, we generalize reconstruction results of Uchida and Sueyoshi to Galois extensions $\Omega_i/K_i$ such that $\Omega_i$ has no nontrivial abelian pro-$\Sigma$ extension, where $\Sigma$ has positive upper Dirichlet density. We also prove a relative version of the first result without a density assumption: the same conclusion holds if the group isomorphism is compatible with the canonical restriction maps to the maximal abelian pro-$\Sigma(\mathcal{C}_1)$ quotient of the absolute Galois group of $\mathbb{Q}$, and if $2\in\Sigma(\mathcal{C}_1)$ or at least one of $K_1,K_2$ has a complex prime. This relative result applies, in particular, to maximal pro-$p$ quotients under these conditions.

papers.title: Isoparametric functions on Finsler space forms
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that each connected regular level hypersurface of a transnormal function on a Finsler space form $(N(c),F)$ has constant principal curvatures under suitable conditions. This result extends Miyaoka's refinement of Q. M. Wang's classical theorem on transnormal functions in Riemannian space forms to the Finsler setting. On forward Finsler space forms $(\overrightarrow{N}(c),F)$, we discuss the relationship between umbilic hypersurfaces and isoparametric hypersurfaces, and construct global and local isoparametric functions using the distance function.

papers.title: Uniformly Expanding Coupled Maps: Self-Consistent Transfer Operators and Propagation of Chaos
papers.abstract: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation, uniformly in time, for systems of $N$ deterministic uniformly expanding heterogeneously coupled maps. The local dynamics and interactions may vary between coordinates, so exchangeability is not required. Under assumptions (independent of the dimension) on expansion, regularity, and weak-coupling, we construct self-consistent transfer operators whose product evolutions approximate every fixed finite marginal. For a class of weakly dependent initial laws (containing products), the error is $O(N^{-1})$ on fixed time intervals and $O(\log N/N)$ uniformly in time. The finite-time rate is optimal within this class. An explicit family exhibits error of order $\sqrt{\log N}/N$ at times of order $\log N$, proving that a uniform $O(N^{-1})$ bound is impossible in general; the optimal correction remains open. The proof is based on ergodic theory: expansion preserves classes of regular, weakly dependent densities, while transfer-operator contraction controls error accumulation. These classes yield concentration estimates and allow direct comparison of densities, giving strong propagation of chaos without external noise. Under additional assumptions, we also obtain Gaussian approximation for empirical observables on fixed time intervals and invariant neighbourhoods of stable fixed points of the self-consistent operator.

papers.title: Topological Frobenius algebras
papers.abstract: We define in a graded and topologized setting the notions of unital/counital/biunital infinitesimal anti-symmetric bialgebras and coFrobenius bialgebras and discuss their algebraic properties. We also define in this setting the notion of a 2D open-closed TQFT. We illustrate these structures with old and new examples of geometric origin that arise in contexts as varied as symplectic topology, string topology, manifold topology, and quantum homology. The underlying vector spaces, which are typically infinite dimensional, belong to a class of topological vector spaces known as Tate vector spaces.

papers.title: Functional equation, upper bounds and analogue of Lindelöf hypothesis for the Barnes double zeta function
papers.abstract: The functional equations of the Riemann zeta function, the Hurwitz zeta function, and the Lerch zeta function have been well known for a long time, and there is great importance in studying these zeta functions. For example, fundamental properties such as the upper bounds, the distribution of zeros, and the zero-free regions in the Riemann zeta function derive from functional equations. In this paper, we consider the functional equations for the Barnes double zeta-function $ \zeta_2 (s, \alpha ; v, w ) = \sum_{m=0}^\infty \sum_{n=0}^\infty (\alpha+vm+wn)^{-s} $. Additionally, by applying this functional equation and the Phragmén-Lindelöf convexity principle, we obtain some upper bounds for $ \zeta_2(\sigma + it, \alpha ; v, w) $ with respect to $ t $ as $ t \rightarrow \infty $. Furthermore, we prove that an analogue of the Lindel"of hypothesis for the Barnes double zeta-function is equivalent to suitable upper bounds for its positive even moments on vertical lines in the critical strip.

papers.title: A note on split extension classifiers of perfect objects
papers.abstract: It is well known that the automorphism group of a perfect group has trivial center. This is a consequence of the fact that for a perfect group the centralizer of the normal subgroup of inner automorphisms of its automorphism group is trivial. We find a categorical explanation for this fact by showing that for a semi-abelian category $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying (WNH), if $X$ is a perfect object in $\mathbb{C}$ such that the split extension classifier $[X]$ exists, then the centralizer of the \emph{conjugation} morphism $c_X : X\to [X]$ is trivial and hence the center of $[X]$ is trivial. Our proof depends on the following fact, which we show holds in an arbitrary semi-abelian category satisfying (WNH). If $f:X\to Y$ is a central extension and $\theta_1$, $\theta_2$ and $\phi$ are internal object actions of $B$ on $X$, $X$ and $Y$, respectively, such that $f:(X,\theta_i)\to (Y,\phi)$ is an internal $B$-action morphism, then $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ restrict to the same action on $[X,X]$. Using this latter fact we also prove that (UCE) is a consequence of (WNH) alone (rather than of (WNH) together with (SH) as previously known).

papers.title: Direct electron cooling at millikelvin temperatures with quantum-well heat pump
Cohomology of SL(3,Z) with coefficients in the standard representation
papers.abstract: This paper is a natural continuation of a joint paper with Bajpai, Harder and Moya Giusti \cite{BHHM}, even though it began as an answer to Goncharov's question. It that paper, we had complete description for all representations except for odd symmetric powers and their dual ones. For those representations we were left with two options: certain one dimensional module is a ghost space or not. Here we find the $H^2(SL_3(\Z),V_3)$ has ghost classes. It means that it is generated by a class from the cohomology of the Borel subgroup. With the techniques developed here, we show that the $d_2$ map of the spectral sequence for the boundary cohomology of $GL_4(\Z)$ is non-trivial if and only if there is a ghost class in $GL_3(\Z)$ (see Propositions 11 and 12.) We use a result of Elbaz-Vincent, Gangl and Soule to show that a spectral sequence related to $GL_4(\Z)$ does not degenerate at $E_2$-level. Then $d_2$ is non-trivial. Therefore, we obtain that $H^2(SL_3(\Z),V_3))$ is a ghost space, where $V_3$ is the standard representation.

papers.title: Orthosymplectic Satake equivalence, II
papers.abstract: This is a companion paper of arXiv:1909.11492 and arXiv:1912.01930 . We prove an equivalence relating representations of a degenerate orthosymplectic supergroup with the category of twisted $Sp(2n,{\mathbb C}[\![t]\!])$-equivariant $D$-modules on the so called mirabolic affine Grassmannian of $Sp(2n)$. We also discuss (conjectural) extension of this equivalence to the case of quantum supergroups and to some exceptional supergroups.

papers.title: Twisted light affects ultrafast demagnetization
Local Statistics of Random Permutations from Free Products
papers.abstract: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be uniformly random permutations of orders $2$ and $3$, respectively, in $S_{N}$, and consider, say, the permutation $\alpha\beta\alpha\beta^{-1}$. How many fixed points does this random permutation have on average? The current paper studies questions of this kind and relates them to surprising topological and algebraic invariants of elements in free products of groups. Formally, let $\Gamma=G_{1}*\ldots*G_{k}$ be a free product of groups where each of $G_1,\ldots,G_k$ is either finite, finitely generated free, or an orientable hyperbolic surface group. For a fixed element $\gamma\in\Gamma$, a $\gamma$-random permutation in the symmetric group $S_{N}$ is the image of $\gamma$ through a uniformly random homomorphism $\Gamma\to S_{N}$. In this paper we study local statistics of $\gamma$-random permutations and their asymptotics as $N$ grows. We first consider $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$, the expected number of fixed points in a $\gamma$-random permutation in $S_{N}$. We show that unless $\gamma$ has finite order, the limit of $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$ as $N\to\infty$ is an integer, and is equal to the number of subgroups $H\le\Gamma$ containing $\gamma$ such that $H\cong\mathbb{Z}$ or $H\cong C_{2}*C_{2}$. Equivalently, this is the number of subgroups $H\le\Gamma$ containing $\gamma$ and having (rational) Euler characteristic zero. We also prove there is an asymptotic expansion for $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$ and determine the limit distribution of the number of fixed points as $N\to\infty$. These results are then generalized to all statistics of cycles of fixed lengths.

papers.title: Wavescan: Multiresolution Time-Frequency Transform of Gravitational-Wave Data
Approximating TSP walks in subcubic graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that every simple 2-connected subcubic graph on $n$ vertices with $n_2$ vertices of degree 2 has a TSP walk of length at most $\frac{5n+n_2}{4}-1$, confirming a conjecture of Dvořák, Král', and Mohar. This bound is best possible; there are infinitely many subcubic and cubic graphs whose minimum TSP walks have lengths $\frac{5n+n_2}{4}-1$ and $\frac{5n}{4} - 2$ respectively. We characterize the extremal subcubic examples meeting this bound. We also give a quadratic-time combinatorial algorithm for finding such a TSP walk. In particular, we obtain a $\frac{5}{4}$-approximation algorithm for the graphic TSP on simple cubic graphs, improving on the previously best known approximation ratio of $\frac{9}{7}$.

papers.title: Can Satellite Mega-Constellations Justify Their Impact on Astronomy?
Hyperbolic Embeddings in Toric Geometry: Effectivity and Deformation Stability
papers.abstract: We study the deformation behavior of Kobayashi hyperbolic embeddings for complements of divisors in projective toric varieties. In the toric setting, the Zariski closure of an entire curve in a torus complement is a translate of an algebraic subtorus contained in that complement. This translates hyperbolicity questions into combinatorial conditions on lattice-point configurations of Newton polytopes. Building on a theorem of Tiba, which guarantees hyperbolic embedding for a general divisor under suitable facewise lattice conditions, we develop an effective refinement of his argument. We construct an explicit constructible bad locus in the coefficient parameter space, characterized by the presence of translated subtori in the divisor or its complement on a torus stratum, and use its proper Zariski closure as an exceptional locus. This description makes the exceptional set amenable to computation. Using this effectivity, we prove a deformation stability result: along any algebraic one-parameter family of divisors whose initial member avoids the exceptional locus, hyperbolic embedding fails for at most finitely many parameters. Under strengthened lattice-point hypotheses, we further exhibit distinguished one-parameter families for which hyperbolic embedding persists without any exceptional parameters. We also analyze deformations arising from diagonal torus reparametrizations. If the initial divisor lies outside $\mathcal Y$, the inverse image of $\mathcal Y$ under the similarity family is empty on the nondegenerate parameter domain, while the smallest possible degeneracy set of a rational similarity presentation is controlled by a multiplicative rank invariant of the scaling vector. Finally, we illustrate the theory through examples in projective spaces and Hirzebruch surfaces.

papers.title: On a Conjecture About the Sombor Index of Graphs
papers.abstract:
Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V(G)$ and edge set $E(G)$. A graph invariant for $G$ is a number related to the structure of $G$ which is invariant under the symmetry of $G$}. The Sombor and reduced Sombor indices of $G$ are two new graph invariants defined as $SO(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\sqrt{d_G(u)^2 + d_G(v)^2}$ and $SO_{red}(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\sqrt{ ig(d_G(u)-1 ig)^2 +  ig(d_G(v)-1 ig)^2}$, respectively, where $d_G(v)$ is the degree of the vertex $v$ in $G$. We denote by $H_{n,
u}$ the graph constructed from the star $S_n$ by adding $
u$ edge(s), $0\leq 
u\leq n-2$, between a fixed pendent vertex and $
u$ other pendent vertices. Réti et al. [T. Réti, T Došlić and A. Ali, On the Sombor index of graphs, 	extit{Contrib. Math.} 	extbf{3} (2021) 11--18] proposed a conjecture that the graph $H_{n,
u}$ has the maximum Sombor index among all connected $
u$-cyclic graphs of order $n$, where $0\leq\,
u\leq n-2$. In some earlier works the validity of this conjecture was proved for $
u\leq 5$. In this paper we confirm that this conjecture is true, when $
u = 6$. The Sombor index in the case that the number of pendent vertices is less than or equal to $n - 
u - 2$ is investigated and the same results are obtained for the reduced Sombor index. Some relationships between Sombor, reduced Sombor and first Zagreb indices of graphs are also obtained.

papers.title: Topological conjugacy and its relations for symbolic matrices
papers.abstract: In 1988 Boyle and Krieger defined sub-matrices for representation matrices of sofic shift. This paper presents some details of relations between integral sub-matrices and representation matrices. Besides, we express a new version of the Decomposition Theorem by sub-matrices. Generally, strong shift equivalence (conjugacy) of sub-matrices does not apply to representation matrices, but we show that this result can be achieved by the fixed diagonal integral sub-matrix.

papers.title: Gene ologs: a categorical framework for Gene Ontology
papers.abstract: The Gene Ontology (GO) is the most widely used resource for the functional annotation of genes and gene products. It unifies biological knowledge across species through a dynamic, controlled vocabulary, and it is now primarily represented in the Web Ontology Language (OWL), a logic-based language that supports automated reasoning. Ologs (ontology logs), introduced by Spivak and Kent, offer a different language for knowledge representation, grounded in category theory: concepts are types, functional relationships are aspects, and declared equalities between paths are facts. Ologs come with features that are not part of the standard use of GO: path equations, universal constructions (products, coproducts, pullbacks and pushouts), a database reading in which instance data are set-valued functors, and functors with which ontologies can be compared and merged. In this work we take an initial step towards Gene ologs, i.e. ologs for GO. We fix conventions for reading GO terms as olog types, examine which GO relations can be represented as aspects and which must instead be represented as spans, illustrate each olog construction with GO examples, show that standard GO annotations and GO Causal Activity Models (GO-CAM) can be represented as olog instance data subject to checkable constraints, and describe how functors and pushouts can be used to compare and merge Gene ologs. We also discuss what ologs do not provide relative to OWL. We regard Gene ologs as complementary to, rather than a replacement for, the OWL representation of GO.

papers.title: Chiral QCD phase in equilibrium with Hadron Gas and the location of the critical point
papers.abstract: We develop a description of the equation of state of QCD matter with restored chiral symmetry, which is in thermal and chemical equilibrium with the hadronic phase. The hadron gas is described with thermodynamically consistent volume corrections. The chiral phase is composed of a set of few quark condensates, each of which corresponds to a family of hadrons with specific quark content. On the boundary between the two phases we apply the requirement of conservation of particle numbers per family. We use lattice calculations for temperatures below the transition curve to determine hadronic volumes. We find that the pion system plays decisive role in the shift of the transition from higher order (crossover) to first order. For four volume models and five hadron sets we calculate the location of the critical point as function of critical temperature $T_c$ at vanishing baryon density. Among other acceptable solutions, if we additionally impose the equality between the densities of quarks contained in mesons and baryons, we find a critical point residing in the interval of baryon chemical potential $\mu_B \simeq$ 234-279 MeV and of temperature $T \simeq$ 148-156 MeV. We propose as signal of approach to the critical point the determination of the chiral pion mass through experimentally measured pion multiplicities in heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title: General Slit Stochastic Löwner Evolution and Conformal Field Theory
papers.abstract: This monograph is dedicated to a generalization of the Löwner equation in its stochastic form, known as SLE, and to its coupling with the Gaussian free field, with the ultimate aim of constructing a boundary conformal field theory with one free scalar bosonic field. The exposition aims to be a systematic, and hopefully concise, account and generalization of known elements of the theory of Löwner evolution. We also study the relation to singular representations of the Virasoro algebra, as well as methods of numerical simulation. The main results are proofs of the basic properties of the generalized SLE and general necessary and sufficient conditions for its coupling with the Gaussian free field. We also introduce a framework that allows one to treat all L"owner equations and known types of coupling as different manifestations of the same phenomenon.

papers.title: Newton's second law: not so elementary (as it may seem)
papers.abstract: Introductory courses present Newton's second law either as a definition of force or as a law of nature, and in both cases leave unexplained why it holds only in a special class of reference frames. We give an operational reading of the law built on a single instrument, the spring balance. Its reading is a local fact on which all observers agree; in a given laboratory it defines the masses of bodies and a vector {\gamma} characterising the laboratory. Laboratories with $\gamma$ = 0 are, by definition, inertial. The empirical content of the second law is then the statement {\gamma} = -KA, where A is the acceleration of the laboratory measured kinematically from any inertial laboratory, and K is a universal constant that the choice of the newton as unit of force makes invisible. In this reading a spring balance is an accelerometer and an accelerometer is a dynamometer: both measure the specific force a-g familiar from inertial navigation. We discuss the hypotheses involved (universality of free fall, absence of rotation, locality) and the relation with Newton's own formulation.

papers.title: A bordism theory related to matrix Grassmannians
papers.abstract: Matrix Grassmannians give finite-dimensional representatives for virtual bundles of rank one and vanishing first Chern class. We use them to study two groups of labelled manifolds. A choice of stable normal framing gives framed bordism of $\BSU_{\otimes}$ and an integral Pontryagin--Thom description. Forgetting the framing gives a quotient defined by the boundary relations for labelled, stably parallelizable manifolds. The forgetful map is surjective with torsion kernel. Both rational bordism rings are polynomial on explicitly labelled spheres, one generator in each even dimension at least four. We compute the characteristic numbers of their products and show that each sphere generator spans an integral direct summand in its own degree.

papers.title: Theories of bundles with additional homotopy conditions
papers.abstract: A homotopy between two amplified special unitary bundles and a trivialization of a tensor product give two different finite-dimensional classifying spaces. For coprime ranks $k,l>1$ the first space is a biquotient of $\SU(kl)$ and the second is a homogeneous matrix Grassmannian. We distinguish the two manifolds for every such pair by their first Pontryagin classes. For $(k,l)=(2,3)$ their eighth integral cohomology groups have orders $3$ and $21$, respectively. The same amplification maps define a dimension-drop algebra on a labelled simplex. Its skeletal filtration gives a weighted cellular complex and computes $K_0$, $K_1$ and the unit when the vertex labels have greatest common divisor one. We also compute both groups for triangles with arbitrary vertex labels.

papers.title: On Some Diophantine Parameters of the Cyclic Torsion Subgroups of Odd Order of Elliptic Curves over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: For elliptic curves $ E $ over the rational number field $ \Q, $ based on Mazur's classical result, we give in this paper some explicit Diophantine parameters for their cyclic torsion subgroups $ E(\Q)_{\text{tors}} $ of odd order. This work is a continuation of the ones in ([Q1], [QZ1$\sim $2]). Such explicit form of parameters might be useful in calculating torsion subgroups of elliptic curves over higher degree number fields.
